title: 2 hospitalized in large Detroit apartment fire
description: Two people have been hospitalized after a large apartment fire in Detroit, according to the Detroit Fire Department (DFD).
content: Two people have been hospitalized after a large apartment fire in Detroit, according to the Detroit Fire Department (DFD).The apartment fire broke out on Detroit's west side on Webb Street and Burlingame Street. Crews have been working for over an hour to put out the fire. The two injured people were transported to Detroit Receiving Hospital to be treated for smoke inhalation and minor burns.The Detroit Police Department, Detroit Fire Department and DTE responded to the scene.The cause of the fire is not clear yet.

title: Frosty mornings turn into sunny and comfortable afternoons in the Pittsburgh region
description: Over the next week or so, the mornings will be frosty and the daytime will be comfortable and sunny.
content: The stretch of cool mornings giving way to pleasant afternoons will continue for at least the next week and beyond. This is the time of year when morning traffic accidents start to tick up due to a couple of issues. Deer are on the move as they try to prepare for the lean winter months, sunrise times are late enough that it is still dark for parts of the morning commute, and frost can cause slick spots for motorists who aren't expecting it.You may not realize that when we put up a map with temperatures in the mid to upper-30s, that's the temperature at two meters above ground level. There's a whole bunch that can happen and occurs below two meters agl, and when it comes to driving, we are really only concerned about what is happening at road level. That's where a false sense of safety can occur, with people seeing the temperature on their cars showing a temperature well above 32°, but slick conditions are still possible on roads. The nice thing with newer cars is that they will ding from anywhere from 39° down to 37° to show that slick conditions are indeed possible. Getting into the forecast, highs today should hit the mid-60s. Yesterday's high was just 66° (I had us at 68°), and I am going to maintain my 66° forecast high for today. We will see plenty of sun with light winds coming in from the north. Noon temperatures should be in the low 60s. Friday will be interesting, as we will have a chance for maybe some drizzle during the morning as a back door cold front moves through. This should push Friday highs down to the low 60s. We will also see cloudy skies for the morning before sunshine returns in the afternoon. Friday morning temperatures will be up near 40° with noon temperatures in the upper 50s.The rest of the weekend is looking pleasant, with the cool mornings giving way to pleasant afternoons. Morning lows both Saturday and Sunday should tick down to the mid-30s, with afternoon highs hitting the mid-60s on Saturday and upper sixties on Sunday. Steelers in Paris: Game starts at 9:30 a.m. our time. 3:30 p.m. in Paris. Sunny skies are expected. Paris' sunset time will be near 6:40 p.m., so the game should be wrapping up with a beautiful golden hour glow. Skies will be clear for the game, with game-time temps in the mid to upper 50s. The next week will see a couple of mornings where these slick spots will be possible. Clear overnight skies with light winds and low humidity levels will allow rapid cooling, with hard road surfaces cooling fast. Where temperatures will remain well above 32 ° most mornings, frosty conditions are expected. Treat every morning, and every break, like ice may be near.

title: 2 decades before he joined the Sixers, LeBron James made headlines in Philadelphia
description: In 2002, LeBron James was the top-ranked high school prospect in the world and dropping 28 points on Philly's top high school team.
content: LeBron James is back in Philadelphia — this time as a Sixer. But his connection to the city began nearly 24 years ago, when he was still a high school star.On Dec. 22, 2002, James and his alma mater St. Vincent–St. Mary High School faced Strawberry Mansion at the Palestra.It was a game that featured Philly's best high school team, with star Maureece Rice chasing Wilt Chamberlain's career scoring record, and the 6-foot-8, 18-year-old James, the No. 1-ranked high school prospect in the country.Jeremy Treatman organized the game after watching James play in a tournament in Delaware."I think I just saw somebody as good as, if not better than Kobe," Treatman recalled telling Lower Merion coach Gregg Downer.Treatman had been an assistant coach at Lower Merion during Kobe Bryant's high school career. He said he knew Philadelphia had to see James play."All you had to do was see him play once and you knew he was going to be an NBA superstar," Treatman said. The Palestra game sold out. Treatman says the crowd was so large that about 1,000 more people got inside.James put up 28 points with eight rebounds, five assists and seven steals in an 85-47 rout of Strawberry Mansion.Allen Iverson was reportedly in attendance. James mentioned the Palestra game at the late-September press conference where he was introduced as a Philadelphia 76er.James said he was excited to be on the receiving end of the positive energy Philly fans can give, noting that as a visitor, the fans are like another adversary."It's been like, OK, we respect the way you play the game because we know the game and we know the history of the game and we've seen so many players play. But we hate you, you know like, you're not with us and we hate you. But I love that, I actually really thrive under that circumstance," James said. "I actually came here in high school as well and played at the Palestra my senior year. And it was that same type of atmosphere, you know. Happy to be on this side, though."Now, decades later, James is making his Sixers home debut Thursday night against the Cleveland Cavilers.

title: Fort Lauderdale proposes earlier closing times for downtown bars, facing pushback from business owners
description: Closing times would move up one hour, and a final commission vote is expected on Nov. 17.
content: Fort Lauderdale city officials are considering a plan to roll back bar closing times in the downtown entertainment area, a move that local business owners warn could severely impact their livelihoods.Under the proposal, closing times along Himmarshee Street would shift from 3 a.m. to 2 a.m. on weekdays and from 4 a.m. to 3 a.m. on weekends.Ian Lowe, owner of Original Fat Cats Bar, said late-night patrons, including hospital employees, night-shift workers, and hospitality staff, make up a major portion of his business."We're one of the only bars on the street that's open seven days a week till 4 a.m.," Lowe said, estimating that losing the final operating hour could slash his weekly revenue by 40% to 50%. "Taking care of our nighttime people, our night workers, our hospital workers, our local bar and restaurant people. We take care of them."Fort Lauderdale Mayor Dean Trantalis defended the proposed changes, arguing that the area has attracted a volatile crowd for too long and requires a shift in culture."People come from all over South Florida thinking it's a playground to act out their grievances," Trantalis said. "We want to do away with the Bourbon Street attitude; we want to do away with the idea of you can come here and… find yourself passed out on the sidewalk. Those days are gone."The initiative is part of a broader revitalization effort to give the entertainment district a facelift, including parklets and improved landscaping designed to create a family-friendly environment welcoming to patrons from the nearby Broward Center for the Performing Arts."Make it lovely so the people who leave our center won't be afraid to go down on 2nd to have a drink, have a hamburger, be involved with the city," one resident told the city commission.Lowe expressed hope for a compromise, such as a special permit option that would allow established businesses to maintain 3 a.m. operations."We deserve a chance at getting some sort of permit… to actually save the business," Lowe said.However, Mayor Trantalis indicated there is little support for exemptions among city leadership, stating he does not believe the commission currently has an appetite for permits or exceptions.A final vote on the proposed changes to the closing time is expected at the Nov. 17 commission meeting.

title: How and when to vote early in Maryland's 2026 midterm elections
description: Maryland voters are ready to cast their ballots in the 2026 midterm elections, as early voting starts Thursday.
content: Maryland voters are ready to cast their ballots in the 2026 midterm elections, as the early voting period starts Thursday. Voters are weighing in on key races, including all eight seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, as well as the state's next governor and some highly anticipated ballot questions.Use this tool to check your voter registration status.When does early voting start and end in Maryland?Early voting starts on Thursday, Oct. 22. It runs for eight days, ending the following week on Thursday, Oct. 29.Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. Anyone in line by 8 p.m. should be allowed to vote before the polls close.If you cast your ballot during the early voting period, you will not be allowed to vote by mail or in person on Election Day. Polls will close over the Halloween weekend, then reopen at 7 a.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3 for Election Day.Heads up: Polling sites for early voting sometimes differ from Election Day. Check this document to find your early voting location. What's on the ballot for the 2026 general election?All eight of Maryland's seats in the U.S. House of Representatives are up for election, as the midterms determine the balance of power in Washington. Seven of the eight seats are currently held by Democrats, while Rep. Andy Harris is the lone Republican. He represents District 1, covering the Eastern Shore and parts of Baltimore, Carroll and Harford counties.Another key race to watch is Gov. Wes Moore's reelection campaign against Republican challenger Dan Cox. This race also includes Green Party candidate Andy Ellis and Working Class Party candidate Cathy White.Voters will also decide:State Attorney General: Anthony Brown (D) vs. James B. Rutledge, III (R)State Comptroller: Brooke Elizabeth Lierman (D) vs. Sonya Dunn (R)State's Attorneys (county-by-county)State Senate (county-by-county)State House (county-by-county)State Supreme Court (county-by-county)In addition to elected officials, voters will also weigh in on three statewide ballot questions. The first involves whether the state budget should cover agreements stemming from arbitration between the state and its employees.The second is about appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities in the event that a member is no longer able to serve. Last but not least, Question 3 asks voters whether to change how the state defines its congressional districts, paving the way for redistricting in the coming years. The controversial measure was championed by Moore and the Democratic-led state legislature, but Republican groups sued to block it from appearing on the ballot. The fight reached the state's highest court, with the Maryland Supreme Court ruling it could appear before voters but it had to be rewritten to be more clear. A recent UMBC poll found a majority of likely voters opposed the measure, with 19% still undecided. Depending on where you live, your county may also have additional ballot questions. For a sample ballot with a closer look at your local races, use the state's Voter Lookup tool here.

title: NYC Council to vote on bill to ban horse carriage rides within 2 years
description: The New York City Council will vote Thursday afternoon on Romanch's Law that would ban horse-drawn carriage rides in the city by 2028.
content: The New York City Council is set to vote on a bill that would ban horse-drawn carriage rides in the city by 2028.Lawmakers will vote Thursday afternoon on Romanch's Law. The legislation is named after Romanch Mahajan, 18, who died during a carriage accident in June in Central Park.If passed, the law would end operations in June 2028, with a transition plan for workers and owners required in 2027. But it doesn't set specific compensation amounts for carriage owners. Carriage owners and their families are arguing that the plan doesn't go far enough. They rallied outside City Hall Wednesday to push back.One family said they have spent nearly a century building their business. "I invested $400,000 two years ago to expand my father's dream, and you're coming here to steal it," said owner Francesco Riccobono."We are asking for fairness. We are asking for compassion. We are asking for a seat at the table," said his wife, Natalie.Supporters of the legislation say the ban is long overdue and necessary to protect animals and public safety. The bill also calls for humane placement of animals and assistance for displaced workers."With a majority of the Council behind us, we have a historic opportunity to protect New Yorkers, visitors, workers, and animals, and we intend to finish the job," said Council Member Christopher Marte.The Transport Workers Union says it is prepared to challenge the ban in federal court if it passes.

title: Prosecutor seeking death penalty for Idaho mom who blamed vaccines for twin toddlers' deaths
description: Andrea Shaw, 23, has said the 18-month-old twins became sick and died after receiving flu shots and routine childhood vaccinations.
content: An Idaho prosecutor is seeking the death penalty against a woman charged with murder in the 2025 deaths of her twin toddlers. Andrea Shaw, 23, has pleaded not guilty and has said the 18-month-old twins became sick and died after receiving flu shots and routine childhood vaccinations. But Payette County Prosecutor Mike Duke wrote in court documents that an autopsy revealed symptoms consistent with smothering and wrote that suffocation "is the only conceivable explanation" for their deaths.In July, a grand jury indicted Shaw, on two counts of first-degree murder, according to court records and a statement from the Payette Police Department.Deputy prosecuting attorney Ryon Sirucek notified the court of his intent to seek the death penalty last week. In the court document, Sirucek said the state would try to show that four aggravating factors make capital punishment appropriate in the case: That more than one murder was committed at the time; that the killings were especially heinous, atrocious or cruel; that the defendant showed "utter disregard" for human life; and that she would likely pose a continuing threat to society. "That's outrageous," said Shaw's attorney, Joseph Filicetti. "They're not going to be able to prove the underlying case beyond a reasonable doubt, so there's not a chance the death penalty is going to come into play."Filicetti requested the court drop the indictment against Shaw due to alleged improprieties in front of a grand jury, CBS affiliate KBOI-TV reported.He said the grand jury that indicted Shaw wasn't told that the county coroner found the cause of death to be undetermined but consistent with hyperthermia, or overheating. The pathologists who examined the twins also said their causes of death were undetermined, Filicetti said."A prosecutor has a duty of candor, meaning that they have to be truthful in front of [the grand jury] and they have a duty to provide exculpatory evidence, which is evidence giving [the grand jury] any reason to believe that this person's not guilty - some other reason that these deaths could have occurred outside of murder - and the prosecutor did not do that," Filicetti told KBOI. The prosecutor's office wrote in court documents that the temperature in the twins' room would often reach 100 degrees, but that the children had survived high temperatures before and that their time of death didn't correlate to the peak temperature of the day. "They don't have any motive, they don't have any backstory, they don't have any confession ... She didn't do any of that, and they can't prove she did any of it," Filicetti said. The twins were found dead in their shared bed May 1, 2025, according to court records. They had been vaccinated eight days earlier, and the day after their vaccinations Shaw took them to the emergency room, reporting that they were lethargic and felt feverish. The doctor felt the symptoms were a reaction from the vaccinations, and the twins were given Tylenol and a popsicle and sent home, according to the court records.KBOI reported in May of 2025 that after the bodies of 18-month-old twins had been discovered, police said at the time, "Foul play is suspected, and the incident is being handled as a homicide at this time," but did not identify any suspects. A few days after the twins' deaths, Shaw went on an internet show produced by Children's Health Defense, an anti-vaccine group founded by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He has not been affiliated with the group since December 2024, when he formally resigned as chairman to join President Donald Trump's administration. Medical experts point out that the childhood vaccines at issue - hepatitis A, influenza and DTaP - are safe and effective for kids and recommended by various medical groups. Shaw is also a plaintiff in a federal lawsuit brought by Children's Health Defense and others against the American Academy of Pediatrics, accusing the organization of racketeering and lying about the safety of vaccinations. The American Academy of Pediatrics has asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit, calling it the "latest missive in a campaign targeting" the academy and its "use of science-backed evidence in vaccine policy." Shaw is being held without bond. A trial has been set for January.

title: "Door kick challenge" TikTok trend now a problem in Westboro, Massachusetts: "It's terrifying"
description: Police in Westboro, Massachusetts, are warning homeowners about an alarming TikTok trend​ called the "door kick challenge​."
content: Police in Westboro, Massachusetts, are warning homeowners about an alarming and potentially dangerous TikTok trend called the "door kick challenge."Investigators have had several reports in town recently of strangers trying to kick down doors in the middle of the night. No one has been hurt, but police are looking for the people responsible.Amy Dwyer was sleeping when she said someone tried to kick in her front door in the middle of the night Saturday."Literally like leapt out of bed like, 'What the heck was that?'" said Dwyer. "It's terrifying. I didn't know if somebody was trying to come in my house and hurt me or kill me or hurt my family."Police said the challenge is like "ding dong ditch," except it's taken to a dangerous extreme where pranksters nearly break in doors, leaving real damage.Dwyer's door is custom made. It will cost her $4,000 to replace it."Four thousand dollars for punk kids potentially thinking they're funny. I'm not amused at all. It's a major inconvenience. It's very unsettling. I haven't slept well the last couple of nights," said Dwyer.Just around the corner, another family was left shaken. Melissa Gonzalez said her door was damaged after someone tried to kick it in at 2 a.m. one night last month. She's since installed surveillance cameras around her home."I don't feel safe anymore," said Gonzalez. "It doesn't really matter if they're children or not. The fact of the matter is that somebody is out there trying to scare neighbors and that's terrorizing."Those who've been targeted want to know where the parents are while this is happening."Who is creating these challenges and asking kids to do this and why do they think it's a good idea, and why aren't the parents more involved in what their kids are looking at on social media?" said Dwyer.Police said it can also be dangerous to the pranksters if they try to kick in the wrong door and a homeowner believes they're under attack.Investigators are asking anyone who sees anything suspicious or has video of an incident in Westboro to call them.

title: 2026 Florida early voting guide for Miami-Dade and Broward: Dates, hours, locations and requirements
description: Early voting begins Oct. 19 across South Florida ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Here's what voters need to know about dates, hours, locations and requirements.
content: Early voting for the 2026 midterm elections began this Monday in several Florida counties, giving registered voters the opportunity to cast their ballots in person ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.Although early voting has begun in some parts of the state, the dates, hours and locations vary by county.Under Florida law, all counties must offer early voting from Saturday, Oct. 24, through Saturday, Oct. 31, but local election officials can extend that period.In Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties, early voting runs from Oct. 19 through Nov. 1, providing voters with 14 consecutive days to cast their ballots. In Monroe County, early voting runs from Oct. 19 through Oct. 31.Unlike Election Day, when voters must go to their assigned polling place, registered Floridians can vote at any designated early voting location within the county where they are registered.Here's what Florida voters need to know about early voting dates, identification requirements, polling locations and important deadlines.When does early voting start and end in Florida?Florida's early voting period for the Nov. 3 midterms officially begins Monday, Oct. 19, in counties that have chosen to offer additional voting days.According to the Florida Division of Elections, the statewide early voting schedule is:Oct. 19-23: Optional early voting days, depending on the county.Oct. 24-31: Mandatory early voting period in all Florida counties.Nov. 1: Additional optional early voting day.Nov. 3: Election Day.State law requires early voting locations to remain open for at least eight hours and no more than 12 hours per day during their scheduled voting periods.Because individual counties determine their specific schedules, voters should confirm the dates and hours with their local Supervisor of Elections before heading to the polls.The Florida Division of Elections provides a statewide directory of early voting locations and schedules. Where can I vote early in Florida?During early voting, registered voters can cast their ballots at any designated early voting site within their county of registration.That means voters are not restricted to the polling place assigned to them for Election Day.Early voting locations may include public libraries, community centers, government buildings and other designated facilities.To find an early voting location, voters can visit the Florida Division of Elections website, which provides information about early voting sites throughout the state.Voters can also use the state's county Supervisor of Elections directory to find their local elections office and access county-specific voting information.Election officials recommend checking locations and hours before leaving home because early voting sites may differ from regular Election Day polling places.What ID do I need to vote early in Florida?Florida voters must present a current and valid photo identification with a signature when voting in person, whether during early voting or on Election Day.According to the Florida Division of Elections, acceptable forms of identification include:Florida driver's license.Florida identification card issued by the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles.U.S. passport or passport card.Military identification.Veteran health identification card issued by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.Concealed weapon or firearm license issued under Florida law.Qualifying government-issued employee identification.If the photo identification does not include a signature, voters must provide another acceptable form of identification containing their signature.A voter information card is not an acceptable form of identification for voting.Voters who arrive without the required identification can still cast a provisional ballot. Election officials will determine whether that ballot can be counted after reviewing the voter's eligibility and other requirements.Voters can review the state's official voter identification requirements before heading to the polls.An important note: Florida's 2026 statute, Section 101.043, lists a narrower set of acceptable photo IDs than the Division of Elections FAQ, which still includes debit cards, student IDs and other categories. The list above follows the 2026 statute. Voters planning to use one of the disputed categories should confirm acceptance with their county Supervisor of Elections before voting. How can I check my Florida voter registration status?Floridians can verify their registration status through the state's online voter information lookup system.The Florida voter registration lookup allows voters to check whether they are registered and whether their information is accurate.To search, voters must enter their first name, last name and date of birth as they appear on their registration record.The state's online system also directs voters to their county Supervisor of Elections for information about their assigned polling place, sample ballot and vote-by-mail ballot status.Anyone who cannot locate their registration information should contact their county Supervisor of Elections or call the Florida Division of Elections' Voter Assistance Hotline at 1-866-308-6739.Can I still register to vote in Florida?No. The deadline to register to vote in Florida's Nov. 3 general election was Monday, Oct. 5.Florida requires voters to register at least 29 days before an election, meaning anyone who missed the deadline generally cannot register in time to participate in the November midterms.The state does not offer same-day voter registration during early voting or on Election Day.People who submitted their registration applications before the deadline should check their status online to confirm their registration has been processed.Florida residents can still submit new voter registration applications, but registrations submitted after the deadline will not qualify them to vote in the Nov. 3 election. Can I vote early if I requested a mail ballot?Yes. Florida voters who requested a vote-by-mail ballot but decide to vote in person can still do so.Voters should bring their mail ballot to the early voting location if they have it. Election workers can cancel the mail ballot and allow them to vote in person.If the voter does not bring the mail ballot, election officials must verify that it has not already been received before issuing a regular ballot. If they cannot verify its status, the voter may be required to cast a provisional ballot.Florida voters who prefer voting by mail should also keep these deadlines in mind:Thursday, Oct. 22, at 5 p.m.: Deadline for election officials to receive a request to mail a vote-by-mail ballot.Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m.: Deadline for completed domestic vote-by-mail ballots to be received by the county Supervisor of Elections.Mail ballots must arrive by the deadline. A postmark alone does not make a late-arriving ballot valid.Voters can also return completed mail ballots at designated secure ballot intake stations during authorized hours.More information is available through the Florida Division of Elections' vote-by-mail guide. What's on the ballot in Florida's 2026 midterm elections?Florida voters will decide several major races in the Nov. 3 general election, including contests for governor, a U.S. Senate seat and seats in the U.S. House of Representatives.Other statewide contests include attorney general and additional state Cabinet positions.Depending on where they live, voters may also see races for the Florida Legislature, county offices, judicial positions and local ballot questions.Constitutional amendments and other measures may also appear on the ballot.Because ballots differ by county and voting district, residents should review their personalized sample ballot before voting.Voters can find sample ballot information through their county Supervisor of Elections website.When is Election Day in Florida?Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.Polls across Florida will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time. Anyone waiting in line when the polls close at 7 p.m. will still be allowed to vote.Unlike early voting, voters casting their ballots on Election Day must go to their assigned precinct.Voters can find their assigned polling location using the state's voter precinct lookup tool or by contacting their county Supervisor of Elections. For additional assistance, voters can call the Florida Division of Elections' Voter Assistance Hotline at 1-866-308-6739.

title: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson to take 2027 budget proposal to residents
description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson to take 2027 budget proposal to residents
content: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson will take his 2027 budget pitch directly to residents Thursday, as some aldermen reject a key part of his plan.At noon Thursday, the mayor will host a virtual town hall to explain his plan and hear from residents. But he faces opposition from the same group of 29 aldermen who helped block his corporate head tax last year.The mayor brought back the proposal for a head tax in the $17.6 billion budget proposal he laid out on Wednesday. It would charge companies with 125 or more full-time employees $25 per worker per month. Companies whose employees work in parts of Chicago officially designated as Socioeconomically Disadvantaged Areas would qualify for credits to cover the cost of the tax for each employee in those areas.The mayor said the head tax would generate $101 million to help close the city's $882 million budget gap. Johnson argues large corporations should contribute more.Critics say the tax would hurt job growth and discourage companies from coming to Chicago. Some alders say the proposal won't pass.It was disingenuous for the mayor to put the head tax into the budget," Ald. Bill Conway (34th) said after Johnson's budget address. "Twenty-nine of us signed that letter. Clearly that part of is dead on arrival."But others see an opportunity to bring businesses into more Chicago neighborhoods."This is not exodus. This is not a threat to kick corporations out," said Ald. William Hall (6th). "It's an invitation for corporations to come closer to a base of employees."Hall pointed to the benefit of the mayor's plan for tax relief for companies in underserved neighborhoods.Meanwhile, Johnson also proposed a 15-cent packaging waste tax that would expand the city's existing retail bag tax to include all forms of packaging for carry-out or delivery, bringing in an estimated $9 million.He also wants sports betting companies to pay a 20% tax, up from 10.25% to bring in $37 million, although the city's sports betting tax is facing a court challenge, with opponents arguing only the state of Illinois is authorized to impose such a tax.The mayor also plans to increase personal property lease taxes from 15% to 20%. The tax rate for car leases would remain at 15%, while leases for film production equipment would see their tax reduced to 11%. The mayor's office estimates the changes to the personal property lease tax would generate $234 million.Residents can hear from the mayor and ask questions during the virtual town hall at noon Thursday.The City Council has until Dec. 31 to approve a budget.

title: Short on rent, $128,514 within reach: North Texas man's challenging choice caught on camera
description: A 37-year-old man struggling to pay his rent stumbled upon bags of cash left at a Lewisville ATM. Newly obtained police bodycam video reveals what he did next.
content: He was $100 short on rent. Then he stumbled upon $128,514 in cash.For one North Texas man, the find of a lifetime came on a day when he could barely make ends meet.Now, newly obtained police body camera video reveals what happened when the 37-year-old barber faced a six-figure temptation — and chose honesty over cash flow."Bro, you know what I felt when I seen it? I got scared, bro," the man told a Lewisville police officer. "I didn't get excited."The discovery happened Aug. 3 at a Bank of America ATM in Lewisville. Police say the man and his 42-year-old friend found two bags left behind, one containing $128,514.The cash had apparently been forgotten by a Brink's crew servicing the ATM.But the man wasn't looking for a windfall that day. He was looking for enough money to pay his rent."I'm arguing with her at the Walmart because I'm short on rent," he explained to the officer. "Go to the ATM, I'm short 100."Then came the money. And the fear."Bro, I got scared, man. I started shaking. I'm like, what do I do? I called the laws."The man, who asked CBS News Texas not to identify him, told police he has a felony on his record. Instead of taking the cash, he called the authorities and went searching for its rightful owner.A label on the bag led him to a nearby Chick-fil-A restaurant. The money wasn't the restaurant's, but the location offered a clue.A Lewisville Chick-fil-A owner explained that a nearby business, now operating as Hawaiian Bros, had once been a Chick-fil-A. The ATM apparently still carried the old restaurant's identification.The restaurant owner contacted the police."Literally, it's cash," the caller told a 911 dispatcher.When an officer arrived, even he struggled to believe the amount."When I saw the notes, I was like, you mean $128, right?" Officer J. Nazario recalled.Although the cash was considered abandoned property, Nazario explained that its identifying labels made clear it belonged to someone.The temptation wasn't lost on either man."I could have took off today. Spent it in Mexico," the barber admitted.Instead, he walked away without a dime of what could have been rent and then some."I didn't take a dollar, bro. I swear to God," he told the officer.Bank of America told CBS News Texas it expressed gratitude for the man's actions, but did not confirm whether he received a financial reward.The officer, however, made sure the man didn't leave without something valuable: recognition."It takes a lot to do the right thing. And I can't commend you enough," the officer said. "Especially, like you said, in this day and age, that's impressive."

title: Dallas Mavs fall to Houston Rockets 128-110 in season opener behind Durant, Smith's 30-piece game
description: Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr. scored 30 points apiece and the Houston Rockets used a big second quarter to build a huge lead and coast to a 128-110 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night in the season opener for both teams.
content: Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr. scored 30 points apiece and the Houston Rockets used a big second quarter to build a huge lead and coast to a 128-110 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night in the season opener for both teams.The Rockets led by six after the first quarter before outscoring Dallas 38-12 in the second to take a 32-point lead into halftime.Durant and Smith each scored 16 points each in the first half. The Rockets were up by 15 midway through the second before using a 19-2 run to make it 70-38 at halftime.Kyrie Irving had 15 points for Dallas in his first regular-season game since tearing his left ACL in March 2025. But it was a tough debut for Dallas coach Dusty May, who led Michigan to the NCAA championship before being hired to replace the fired Jason Kidd.Cooper Flagg, the 2025 No. 1 pick and last season's NBA Rookie of the Year, led the Mavericks with 32 points. P.J. Washington had 10 points and four rebounds.The Mavericks used a 9-0 run, with six points from Marcus Sasser, to cut the lead to 103-86 with about nine minutes remaining. But Houston used an 8-2 spurt with 3s from Durant and Fred VanVleet to push it to 111-88 about a minute later.Alperen Sengun added 23 points with 10 rebounds for the Rockets. VanVleet chipped in six points with 11 assists in his return after missing last season recovering from a torn ACL.Houston's Tari Eason was ejected with about three minutes left in the first quarter after receiving a flagrant foul 2 for shoving Washington to the court.Mavericks: Visit Indiana on Friday night.Rockets: Play San Antonio in Austin, Texas on Friday.

title: Trump rallying with Senate hopeful Ashley Hinson in Iowa as she pledges to push back on White House
description: President Trump is set to rally with Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa as he seeks to boost GOP candidates in a political environment that has dimmed for the party — prompting pushback from some candidates, including Hinson.
content: Sioux City, Iowa — President Trump is set to rally Thursday with Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa as he seeks to boost Republican candidates in a political environment that has dimmed for the party — prompting modest pushback from the very candidates he's supporting.Hinson, who is running for Iowa's open Senate seat, initially pledged to be the president's "top ally" in the upper chamber. But as she faces off against Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek in a contest that, like several in the Hawkeye State, has grown more competitive than expected, she's adjusted that commitment in recent weeks. When she and Turek went head-to-head at a debate earlier this month, the former local news anchor said she would be Mr. Trump's ally when it's "important for Iowa." But she said she would "push back on him" when it's needed — as she said she would regardless of who's in the White House. Last week, Hinson told Fox News: "If he's going to say something that's wrong, I'm going to challenge him on it." "I'm not afraid to say, 'hey, I disagree with you on this,'" she said. "But I'll be an ally to somebody when they're with me."For Republicans, the Senate race in Iowa is just one of several in which Democrats appear competitive despite Mr. Trump winning the state by double digits in 2024. Iowa has been hit hard by high energy prices and last year's U.S.-China trade war, which led Beijing to boycott American soybeans. It's a picture that appeared unthinkable at the outset of the cycle — and puts Republicans' Senate majority on the line. Hinson, who's represented the state in the House since 2021, said she would be at the rally on Thursday to welcome Mr. Trump to Iowa, "because I think this is a contrast election." As the nation experiences challenges, she posed the question: Who do Iowans want at the helm?"You want a mom, a minivan-driving mom who's common sense, who's driving that common sense back into Washington, D.C.," she said. "I think that's what Iowans want as their U.S. senator."Hinson has made the minivan motif central to her campaign. She connected the image to her emphasis on working with Mr. Trump for Iowans earlier this week, describing a recent call with the president. "I had just finished dropping off the boys, I was ready to run an errand," Hinson said at an event in Des Moines geared toward moms, alongside Sen. Katie Britt. "And I see pop up on my caller ID in my minivan, 'DJT.'"She continued, "'Ashley, it's your favorite president,' that's how he introduced himself."Hinson said the call lasted five minutes and that Mr. Trump was "just checking in on us here in Iowa." She said she thanked the president for his efforts to move forward on trade with China and asked about a deal for China to buy more soybeans.At the event, Hinson also delivered her latest break with the president, according to Semafor, telling reporters, "I don't think we need to be making any more deals with Russia," regarding Mr. Trump's waiver of sanctions against Moscow.The criticism follows Hinson's move to separate herself from the president's handling of the war with Iran late last month. Tucked within a post expressing support for methods to combat high prices, such as a pause on diesel exports, Hinson made one of the first splits by a GOP Senate candidate with the president over the war, writing: "The war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end."The statement appeared in contrast to Hinson's vote earlier in September, when the House considered a resolution aimed at reining in the president in Iran. While two other Iowa Republicans locked in tight races supported the resolution, Hinson opposed it.At the debate a couple weeks later, Turek pressed Hinson over those votes, saying during a discussion on energy costs: "We are in this situation because of this unnecessary war in Iran that Ashley Hinson voted in favor of continuing."Hinson clarified during the debate that she believes the war must be brought to an "immediate and successful end" by not allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon and by making sure that U.S. allies in the region are protected. Asked why she doesn't support the efforts to pass war powers resolutions in Congress, Hinson said, "I don't think we need another resolution." "And I certainly don't want to see the president not be able to do a orderly end to this war," she added. Thursday's rally marks the president's second visit to Iowa this year, after he kicked off campaigning in the midterms with a trip to the Des Moines area in January. Mr. Trump also announced plans last month for the largest steel plant in U.S. history to be built in Iowa, in an Oval Office event with Hinson in attendance. During the announcement, the president pledged to visit the state for a "great rally" to help get the Republican candidates elected. "We'll save you a good Iowa pork chop, sir," Hinson replied.

title: Mother, 4 children die in Van Zandt County house fire, sources confirm
description: The Van Zandt County Fire Marshal's Office said the fire broke out around 12:30 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 21.
content: An overnight house fire in Van Zandt County left four children and their mother dead, according to CBS News Texas sources. A news release from the Van Zandt County Fire Marshal's Office said the fire broke out around 12:30 a.m. Wednesday near County Road 4127 and County Road 4128. Crews reported that three people were able to get out, but firefighters had to breach an exterior wall to reach four children who remained inside.Three of the children, the fire marshal's office said, had already succumbed to the flames. While names were not released, the office said the children who died included an 8-year-old boy, a 5-year-old boy, and a 3-year-old girl. Two more victims were rushed to a Dallas-area hospital in critical condition; the office initially identified them as an adult and a 10-year-old boy. Late Wednesday, our CBS affiliate KYTX, confirmed that the boy was 9 and that he and the other victim, the children's mother, had both died from their injuries. The investigation into the fire remains ongoing. Crews from Canton, South Van Zandt, Ben Wheeler, and Wills Point tackled the blaze.

title: Cook County commissioner condemns racist, homophobic comments reported at Evanston-New Trier football game
description: Cook County Commissioner Scott Britton (D-14th) spoke out this week as the investigation continues into racist and homophobic comments​ made at a high school football game last Friday.
content: Cook County Commissioner Scott Britton (D-14th) spoke out this week as the investigation continues into racist and homophobic comments made at a high school football game last Friday.Evanston Township was taking on New Trier Township High School at Northwestern University's new Ryan Field on Friday, Oct. 16, in a massive rivalry matchup with more than 27,000 tickets sold.In a joint statement, Evanston Township High School District 202 and New Trier Township High School District 203 said on the sidelines, the Evanston marching band was subjected to racist and homophobic comments along with other offensive behavior by New Trier fans during the game.The Illinois High School Association is now investigating the allegations.In a letter to the New Trier Township High School Supt. Peter Tragos, Britton wrote that this was not the school's sports program's first allegation of bullying that has come to his attention, but he hopes it will be the last."I write to echo the voices in a call for real action, repair, and continued education," Britton wrote. "We know the cycle of violence escalates with each escaped consequence."Britton referenced the recent arrest of 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis of Palatine, who was recently arrested for an alleged mass shooting plot targeting a Hindu temple."We need look no further than just a few miles west in Palatine, to see hateful rhetoric radicalized to murderous ends — thankfully this time foiled," he wrote. "If those involved do not repair the harm, they will be more emboldened, and the next attack may be even more deadly."ETHS color guard members Kevin Watts and Kiro Tabor said they were just moments away from performing with their high school color guard and marching band when they noticed aggressive chants from the opposing student section for NTHS.They say it started with people shouting 'f- you,' but things escalated."Somebody was pointing Kevin out, called Kevin the f-slur and then a group of boys had looked at me, called me the N-word a couple of times," Watts said.In a statement released Tuesday, IHSA executive director Craig Anderson said the IHSA has been in contact with the administrations of both schools, and will work closely with them and determine what will happen next.

title: Family says Hall of Fame basketball coach Bob Huggins has a "progressive cognitive condition"
description: Huggins' family released a statement ahead of his induction into the University of Cincinnati's Hall of Fame.
content: Retired Hall of Fame basketball coach Bob Huggins has a "progressive cognitive condition" that has started to impact his memory "and aspects of his daily life," his family said.Huggins' family released a statement on his health in coordination with the University of Cincinnati Athletics Department ahead of the 73-year-old's induction into the school's Athletics Hall of Fame. The family kept the matter private over the past several months but believes now is "an appropriate time to share the news with the many people who have supported Bob throughout his remarkable career," the statement said.Cincinnati's Hall of Fame induction is Friday night. Other inductees include Jason Kelce and former Philadelphia Eagles' teammate Connor Barwin. The statement said Huggins was "looking forward to returning to Cincinnati this weekend, celebrating with former players and friends, and sharing in a moment that recognizes not only his accomplishments, but also the enduring bonds formed along the way.""Although Bob and his family recognize the challenges that lie ahead, they remain focused on the relationships, experiences, and moments that bring him joy," the statement said.Huggins compiled a 935-414 head coaching record at five colleges that included 16-year stints each at Cincinnati and West Virginia, where he took both schools to the Final Four. Former Huggins pupil Jerrod Calhoun was named Cincinnati's coach in March. Calhoun graduated from Cincinnati in 2004 and was a student assistant under Huggins during the 2003-04 season. He also spent five seasons on Huggins' staff at West Virginia from 2007-12.Huggins' teams were NCAA Tournament staples, and included all-Americans Danny Fortson and Steve Logan and 2000 AP national Player of the Year Kenyon Martin for the Bearcats. Cincinnati reached the Final Four under Huggins in 1992 before losing to Michigan in the national semifinals.At West Virginia, Huggins landed few high-profile recruits. The 2010 West Virginia team won the Big East tournament and defeated top-seeded Kentucky along its ride to the national semifinals before losing to Duke.Huggins was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in September 2022.Eight months later during an appearance on a Cincinnati radio station, Huggins used a homophobic slur to refer to Xavier fans while also denigrating Catholics. Under an agreement with West Virginia after the remarks, Huggins was suspended for three games at the start of the 2023-24 season, took a $1 million salary reduction and was required to undergo sensitivity training.Then, in June 2023, Huggins was arrested on suspicion of drunken driving in Pittsburgh. He resigned the next day and issued his second public apology in a month. It was his second drunken driving arrest. The other occurred in 2004 while he was at Cincinnati and led to his firing in 2005 in a power struggle with the school's president. After spending one season at Kansas State, Huggins took his dream job at West Virginia in 2007. He was born in Morgantown, West Virginia, grew up in Ohio where his father molded three state high school champion teams, and was a three-year letter winner in basketball at West Virginia.___Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP's full men's basketball coverage here

title: How to watch the New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears game on Thursday Night Football
description: Drake Maye and the New England Patriots take on Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears in primetime. Here's how to watch Thursday Night Football.
content: A showdown between young quarterbacks is on the docket for Thursday Night Football this week. The primetime game pits Drake Maye of the New England Patriots against the Chicago Bears' Caleb Williams, two quarterbacks selected in the top three of the 2024 NFL Draft. The Patriots got off to a rocky start to the season, struggling offensively in their first three games en route to two losses. But after bouncing back with an upset win over the Buffalo Bills, the Patriots started to find their rhythm and have now won three straight. Next, New England travels to take on the Bears, who have one of the NFL's most exciting offenses under head coach Ben Johnson.Both teams enter the matchup with 4-2 records. The Bears played without Williams for three of those games after he suffered a hamstring injury.There was plenty of star power at the top of the 2024 draft. Williams was selected first out of USC, then Jayden Daniels to the Commanders from LSU. The Patriots selected Maye with the third pick, and were rewarded with a run to the Super Bowl last year in Maye's first full season as a starter.After an up-and-down rookie campaign, Williams put together a stellar 2025 campaign and led the team to the playoffs in Johnson's first year as head coach. When Maye and Williams were both rookies in 2024, they squared off at Soldier Field. Maye threw the only touchdown pass between the two, and the Patriots left with a 19-3 win.Kickoff between the Patriots and Bears is set for 8:15 p.m. Eastern time at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois.Where can you stream the Patriots vs. Bears game?Prime Video, Amazon's streaming platform, is the home of Thursday Night Football.Because Thursday Night Football is exclusive to Amazon, the only other option for streaming is NFL+, the NFL's subscription service. Prime Video is a paid streaming service, but free trials are available. How can you watch the Patriots vs. Bears game on cable? Because the Patriots-Bears game is the standalone game, it will only be aired on cable in the Chicago and Boston television markets.In the Boston area, fans can find the game on WCVB-TV. In the Chicago market, the cable broadcast can be found on FOX32 Chicago. Legendary broadcaster Al Michaels will handle play-by-play duties, joined by Kirk Herbstreit as the color analyst. Kaylee Hartung will be the sideline reporter. Pregame coverage begins at 7 p.m. Eastern time on WBZ-TV in the Boston area. Once the game is over, tune in for reaction and analysis on Patriots 5th Quarter airing on WSBK-TV/myTV38. Coverage after the game will include news conferences from Mike Vrabel and Drake Maye.Fans in Illinois can watch live coverage from inside Soldier Field on CBS News Chicago starting at 4 p.m. Central time. Who is favored in the Patriots vs. Bears game? The Patriots took care of business last week against the New York Jets as heavy favorites. The Bears defeated the Falcons in Atlanta.New England is extremely banged up heading into the short week. Last week alone, the Patriots lost wide receiver Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury, and added several more offensive linemen to their growing list of injuries in front of Maye. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown are out for the game, while right tackle Morgan Moses was able to practice during the week after leaving Sunday's game. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada are also out.According to CBS Sports, the Bears enter the game as 3-point favorites at home, with the total set at 50.5 points. John Breech of CBS Sports is picking the Bears, 27-20.What is the rest of the Patriots schedule?Because of the Thursday game, New England has an extended break before heading to Miami. Here's a look at the remaining Patriots schedule.
