"WTF, Steve?" wrote North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis. "Look up the definition of 'humanitarian.' What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say. You should go back to Ukraine and ask the families of the children Putin has kidnapped and murdered whether they agree your friend Putin is a 'humanitarian.'"Republican Sen. John Cornyn of Texas responded to a video of Witkoff's comments: "No. Putin is a stone cold killer," he wrote on X. "Another embarrassment," said Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska, who has been critical of the Trump administration's handling of Russia and Ukraine. Republican Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, who has also been critical of the administration, was asked about the comment on the campaign trail and replied, "I would describe Putin as a warmonger, a thug. He's certainly not a humanitarian. He is the aggressor in the war against Ukraine."Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine William Taylor, who served during the Bush and Obama administrations, said in an interview with CBS News that it's "absolutely a good thing" Hubbard is coming home, "but he should never have been there in the first place." "We should not give the Russians any credit for releasing someone who should not have been in jail," Taylor said. "And to call Putin a humanitarian, that's cringeworthy."Republican Sen. Joni Ernst of Iowa said Putin is "not our friend.""Vladimir Putin is not our friend, and he is certainly no humanitarian," she posted on X. "His relentless attacks on innocent civilians in Ukraine show his total disregard for human life. Appeasement won't end this war. Pressure will."Witkoff's praise of Putin also comes as Mr. Trump made the surprise move last week to waive new U.S. sanctions on Russia two days before they were supposed to go into effect, defying Congress and his late friend, Sen. Lindsey Graham. The waivers came one week after Mr. Trump had eased sanctions on Russian diesel and announced a deal with Putin to import diesel to the U.S. market.Mr. Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and on Tuesday, said "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much."Before heading to Russia, Witkoff was in Oslo, Norway, where he met with and embraced Zelenskyy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio described that meeting as "positive."

title: Woman charged with shoving 73-year-old man off CTA bus in downtown Chicago
description: A woman has been charged with attacking a 73-year-old man as he was getting off a CTA bus earlier this month in downtown Chicago.
content: A woman has been charged with attacking a 73-year-old man as he was getting off a CTA bus earlier this month in downtown Chicago.Charne Sisson, 34, of Homewood, is charged with two felony counts of aggravated battery.Police said, around 12:30 p.m. on Oct. 5, she shoved a 73-year-old man onto the ground as he was getting off a CTA bus near Michigan Avenue and Randolph Street. The victim suffered a dislocated shoulder.Court records show Sisson has been arrested multiple times for hitting people, and has been convicted twice. In one case, she served a 20-day sentence in Cook County Jail.In this case, a judge has ordered her to be held at Cook County Jail while she awaits trial. She's due back in court on Tuesday.

title: Jerry Jones rules out more Cowboys coaching changes but leaves door open for roster moves
description: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones does not anticipate making any more coaching changes this season after adding longtime defensive assistant Mike Pettine to the staff earlier this month.
content: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones does not anticipate making any more coaching changes this season. Additions to the roster are another story.Jones said Wednesday at the NFL's annual fall meeting that the hiring of longtime defensive assistant Mike Pettine earlier this month was strategic and unique."(Pettine) had a background with our coordinators and was with us in the spring," Jones said. "It fit. He wanted to come help. That's a pretty significant qualifier for somebody that has that kind of background with everybody involved. So, it was as much about his uniqueness as it was about what we wanted to do to help us play better."The Cowboys rank 30th out of 32 teams on defense after bringing in Christian Parker to serve as the coordinator. They are 2-4 after losing back-to-back games in which they combined to score 29 points.Jones chalked up the struggles on offense to tactical concerns, not a lack of effort, after speaking with second-year coach Brian Schottenheimer."I've seen it not be what it's been in the last couple of games," Jones said. "Not only do I have expectations, I have a really sound basis of saying we're better than that and we can improve in the areas that have really frustrated us, especially last week."Personnel moves could be coming ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline."I'll be real clear: I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year," Jones said. "That's important."Saying he's frustrated and disappointed with his team's record, Jones does not envision selling, unless someone makes him an offer he can't refuse.The state of the NFC East, with the New York Giants in first place at 3-2-1, Philadelphia also 2-4, and Washington 1-4-1, means Dallas could go either way. The past two weeks were the first time since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger that every team in a division played twice, and all failed to register a win."It gives me a lot of promise," Jones said. "I see opportunity. And I see it legitimately because I know the things that we have the potential to do, both with our talent, both our schemes, adjustments I've seen us do in the spring — the kinds of adjustments that you might want to do between the halves."

title: Baltimore sues RentCafe and property manager over alleged hidden fees
description: Baltimore is suing RentCafe and one of the city's largest property managers over alleged hidden, or "junk," fees.
content: Baltimore is suing RentCafe, a property management platform, and one of the city's largest property managers over alleged hidden, or "junk," fees.The lawsuit names RentCafe and its partner, Yardi Systems, as defendants, along with the Pennrose Management Company, which owns and manages hundreds of low-income rental units in the city.Mayor Brandon Scott and the City Council announced the legal action Monday, accusing RentCafe and Pennrose of using "predatory practices to squeeze every last dollar out of economically vulnerable renters.""The complaint alleges that RentCafe steers tenants toward fee-generating payment options by obscuring the fees associated with each payment method behind multiple clicks, embedding fee information across several web pages in fine print, and failing to disclose the fee associated with a selected payment method until the last step of the payment flow," the announcement said. The announcement went on to say tenants are forced to pay these fees in order to pay their rent, and they do not receive any additional service in exchange. If tenants do not pay the fees, they risk being charged late fees or even evicted."These illegal junk fees effectively raise the rent for thousands of Baltimore residents," Scott said in a statement. "This is about holding these businesses accountable for their deceptive practices and protecting Baltimoreans' hard-earned money."Hidden fees, also known as "service fees," "administrative fees," or "processing fees," are illegal under Baltimore's Consumer Protection Ordinance. "Renters should not have to navigate a maze of web pages and fine print to understand what they are being charged," City Solicitor Ebony M. Thompson said in a statement. "When companies obscure the true cost of rent, we will use the City's consumer protection laws to hold them accountable.""Hard-earned money paid in fees to RentCafe means less money for groceries, transportation, or medical bills," said Tara K. Ramchandani, Co-Managing Partner at Relman Colfax. "We are proud to partner with the City of Baltimore to protect these consumers."

title: Neiman Marcus unveils 2026 Fantasy Gifts lineup. Here's what it includes.
description: A Star Wars experience, an Italian grand tour, and a hand-decorated foosball table are part of the luxury gifts this year.
content: Dallas-based luxury retailer Neiman Marcus is kicking off the 2026 holiday season in style, sharing its list of high-dollar items and luxury experiences in its annual Holiday Fantasy campaign.The 2026 Fantasy Gifts were announced Tuesday by Exemplar Luxury Group, the holding company for Neiman Marcus. A press release said this year's lineup showcases Neiman Marcus' commitments to service, car, and luxury."The 2026 Fantasy Gifts continue to redefine extraordinary luxury through one-in-a-lifetime experiences, unparalleled access, and boundless imagination," said Darcy Penick, president and chief commercial officer of Exemplar Luxury Group. "As an industry leader, Neiman Marcus' role extends beyond curating exceptional fashion—we are dedicated to creating rare, unforgettable moments for our most engaged customers. Holiday Fantasy celebrates this enduring legacy, uniting unmatched craftsmanship with the world-class service and personal care that have defined Neiman Marcus for over a century."It's also a milestone for Neiman Marcus; this year marks the 100th edition of the Holiday Book, which features the Fantasy Gifts. Cheryl Han, Exemplar's chief marketing and digital officer, said the in-store and online experiences are all about immersing clients."This season, we've designed Holiday Fantasy to meet our clients wherever they engage with us, seamlessly blending high-fashion inspiration with 360 immersive experiences across digital and stores," said Han. "From nostalgic red bow motifs in our store displays to immersive digital lookbooks, tailored gift guides, and dynamic social series, every touchpoint across our channels is curated to deliver." The announcement highlighted a handful of the gifts and experiences clients can select from. A $182,500 Star Wars Legacy Experience, for example, gets a customer a behind-the-scenes look at Lucasfilm and Industrial Light & Magic, a one-of-one lightsaber hilt prop from the upcoming second season of "Ahsoka" signed by series creator Dave Filoni, a private consultation to design custom-assembled lightsabers, and tickets to an upcoming Star Wars world premier and afterparty alongside the cast and creators.One item offered in the book is a foosball table. But, it's not just any foosball table; it's a $180,000 Dolce&Gabbana Casa Carretto Siciliano table. The announcement says it's hand-decorated and built out of solid wood, features galvanized steel hardware, includes a screen-printed glass field, and displays hand-painted Carretto Siciliano artwork.Beyond the 2026 Fantasy Gifts, Neiman Marcus is promising an elevated shopping experience, both in its stores and online. That includes curated gift guides, experiences at its flagship stores, localized menus, signature items, and specialized holiday dining. The retailer also notes that every Fantasy Gift purchase benefits the Heart of Neiman Marcus Foundation with a dedicated corporate donation, and a point-of-sale campaign for the Boys & Girls Club of America promises to extend the impact, both in-store and online, through January 31, 2027. Neiman Marcus notes that, since 2018, the point-of-sale campaign has generated nearly $2 million.

title: Randsburg, a remote Kern County "living ghost town," hoping to draw crowds with Halloween tours
description: A remote Kern County "living ghost town" is hoping to draw crowds this spooky season, thanks to the help of a ghost hunter offering tours of the historic, haunted halls.
content: A remote Kern County "living ghost town" is hoping to draw crowds this spooky season, thanks to the help of a ghost hunter offering tours of the historic, haunted halls. Randsburg, which was once a booming California Gold Rush town founded in 1895, has seen most of its residents leave over the years. But the nearly three dozen residents who still live there say the town is still filled with those who lingered after their deaths. "We have our madams. We have the shootouts, we have people that were shot in the street, we've had people who were lynched, we have it all," said Marie Mason, the ghost hunter leading tours of the historic town. With just 40 people still "living" in Randsburg, residents say the buildings appear empty, but are far from it. Though they say the spirits are still dancing, the town itself is dying. "It's gonna be dead out here," said David Wood, who owns the "Randsburg Rod Shop," which sells both souvenirs and bike parts for the off-roading community that typically frequents the Rand Mountains. This year, however, trails were closed to protect the desert tortoise, dealing a fatal blow to the town's crucial tourism industry. "We, maybe, had 10 visitors that came into the shop over a three-day weekend, and usually the town is packed," Wood said. Now, Randsburg locals hope their storied history, plus some horror, can bring a little boom back to the once-bustling town. Mason's tour includes stops in several of the town's allegedly haunted locations, during which she uses her paranormal equipment to hunt for residents past. "We pull out all the stops," Mason said. "We have a trolly ride, we have a local that tells you the history."Tickets for the Halloween Weekend can be found online.

title: Developer helps preserve stained glass, relics for neighbors of demolished West Town church
description: Santa Maria Addolorata is being demolished to make way for six new homes, but not before neighbors get to take home pieces from the church.
content: A church that's been part of a Chicago neighborhood for more than 60 years is coming down to make way for new homes.The Santa Maria Addolorata Church in West Town is being demolished to make way for six new homes. As demolition got underway, the construction crew helped remove pieces from the church, including a stained-glass window, neighbors say, that represent its history and are worth far more than their material value.The church has stood at Ohio and Ada since 1960, but it's coming down for good."To have such a sacred, holy place and to see a wrecking ball come in, it's actually really sad," said neighbor Claire Hogan. But before the building disappears, neighbors are finding a way to preserve part of its history. "I think I was only encouraged to make the effort through hearing all these stories of the love and the connection people felt towards the building," said neighbor Cathrine Witt. Witt, who lives across the street from the church, learned of the project and began reaching out to the developer and local officials, as well as talking with residents about what the church meant to them. "Starting in August, that they would just like a small piece that sort of gives them a lasting connection and a memory. So it's like gonna live on in their hearts and for who knows however many more years in the future," she said. Developer MK Construction says those requests were rolling in before the purchase of the church. This week they helped pull pieces of stained glass, crosses and relics from the building, giving them to neighbors. "It's a very, very close-knit community. A lot of people belong to the parish, so obviously they wanted to have a piece of the church," said Edita Topolska with MK Construction. Dozens of people came by to take a piece of history home. Former neighbors and community members are planning to collect pieces, too, including local artists who may give the salvaged materials a second life through their work. "I hope that this connection to the old building will make them feel, make people feel that all is not lost for them," Witt said.Neighbors still have a chance to stop by this week and pick up small pieces at the fence. They say It's a small way to preserve the historic building.

title: U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard released by Russia after 4 years in jail, and Trump says "no 'swap'"
description: Steve Witkoff lauded Vladimir Putin as "a humanitarian" as Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, an American deemed wrongfully detained by the U.S., after more than 4 years in prison.
author_name: Jennifer  Jacobs, Olivia  Gazis, Tucker  Reals
content: Stephen Hubbard, a U.S. citizen who was jailed in Russia for more than four years after being accused of fighting for Ukraine, has been released from custody, President Trump confirmed Wednesday. The release was announced during a meeting between U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. President Trump said in social media posts that Putin agreed to release Hubbard at his request, with "no 'swap' necessary," though he also said the American would not have been released had the White House not stopped new sanctions against Russia from taking effect last week.The news came as Trump administration officials, including Witkoff, were in St. Petersburg for talks with Putin and other senior Russian officials focused on the Ukraine war. Video of the meeting showed Witkoff thanking Putin for freeing the American — whom the U.S. government had declared wrongfully detained — and offering the Russian autocrat, who ordered the ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine almost five years ago, effusive praise, including calling him "a humanitarian." "I wanted to thank you very much. The president sends his thanks. Our whole nation sends it's thanks," Witkoff said. "Because of you, he's going home to his family." "You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian, you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that," Witkoff told Putin.Russian state news agencies, citing Putin, said Hubbard was at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport. Hubbard, a 74-year-old Michigan native, was the last American in Russia whom the State Department had formally declared wrongfully detained. As many as 10 other Americans, including dual nationals, remain in Russian custody.Hubbard, who is in poor health, was expected to be flown to Texas for treatment at a military hospital. Witkoff and President Trump shared a photo on social media showing Hubbard on a plane after his release.In a statement posted on his Truth Social platform early Wednesday, Mr. Trump said Hubbard "was just released from prison, at the request of President Donald J. Trump, made directly to President Vladimir Putin in a telephone conversation last week."Mr. Trump said in his post that Russia released Hubbard "out of respect for President Trump," and the U.S. "was not required to give anything in return — an unprecedented situation for Russia. There was no 'swap' necessary for this release."But on Wednesday afternoon, the president tied his decision to nix sanctions to Hubbard's release. "We were in the midst of negotiating," Mr. Trump told reporters on the White House South Lawn. "And a lot of stupid people said, and people that don't know how life works, they said, 'Why aren't you putting Russia sanctions and all this' in the midst of a negotiation to try to get a long-term hostage back from Russia. If I would have done that, you would not have Mr. Hubbard coming back."The American's release came five days after Mr. Trump announced that his administration would waive some sanctions on Russia just before they were due to take effect. That decision by the president was praised by Putin but criticized harshly by members of Congress, including some Republicans.In a subsequent post on Truth, Mr. Trump did link Hubbard's release to the easing of U.S. sanctions on Russia, claiming "numerous people" who had called for the sanctions to take effect as previously planned had "called to apologize to President Trump in that they didn't know that he was negotiating the release of Stephen Hubbard, a truly big and important deal for the U.S. If sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt."A retired school teacher who served in the U.S. National Guard and Air Force, Hubbard was captured in Ukraine shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of the country in February 2022. Russian authorities accused him of manning a checkpoint for mercenaries. He was sentenced in 2024 to almost seven years in a penal colony.Hubbard's family had little contact with him while he was detained, and they have maintained his innocence.Hubbard's release follows the return of American Robert Gilman, who was freed from Russian custody in August after his health deteriorated to a life-threatening condition. A former Marine who spent more than four years imprisoned in Russia, Gilman was granted a humanitarian pardon following a direct appeal by Mr. Trump to Putin. Early last year, Russia released American school teacher Marc Fogel, and in 2024 journalist Evan Gershkovich and Marine veteran Paul Whelan were among those released from Russian custody in a complicated multi-country prisoner swap.The State Department maintains a Level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory for Russia, warning U.S. nationals against all travel to the country due to the risk of wrongful detention, arbitrary enforcement of local laws and limited U.S. consular assistance. The Trump administration last year established a new designation for countries that are deemed "state sponsors of wrongful detention," CBS News previously reported. The measure gives the State Department expanded authority to impose sanctions, export controls and travel restrictions on countries that use detained Americans as political leverage.Despite its lengthy history of imprisoning Americans on questionable charges, Russia has not faced the designation, which was applied to Iran in February and Afghanistan in March.Some Americans jailed in Russia have not been declared wrongfully detained by the U.S. government, including Aleksandr Antonov, who was arrested in Russia last year and sentenced to six years in prison. His family argues that he was detained because he is a U.S. citizen, and they have urged the State Department to prioritize his case. CBS News reported earlier this year on an internal debate within the department over whether to designate him as wrongfully detained.

title: Driver dies in rollover crash northeast of Woodland, CHP says
description: One person died in a rollover crash in a rural area outside of Woodland in Yolo County, officials said Wednesday.
content: One person died in a rollover crash in a rural area outside of Woodland in Yolo County, officials said Wednesday.The California Highway Patrol's Woodland office said a single-vehicle crash happened shortly before 4 p.m. along County Road 17, just west of County Road 104. This is an area just northeast of Woodland and northwest of Sacramento International Airport.The driver was the only person in the vehicle and was declared dead at the scene. Investigators said the vehicle had gone off the roadway and overturned.According to the CHP, it was not immediately clear what caused the crash and whether the rain, which arrived in the region on Wednesday, was a factor.The driver has not yet been identified.

title: DOJ's inspector general declines to investigate prosecutors who falsely charged Olympian David Hearn in Reflecting Pool case
description: Hearn's lawyers complain the inspector general has referred the case to the Office of Professional Responsibility, a unit that was largely gutted and lacks independence.
content: The Justice Department's inspector general has declined to investigate allegations of misconduct against the prosecutors who brought an indictment against Olympian David Hearn that falsely accused him of vandalizing the Reflecting Pool.In an Oct. 8 letter to Hearn's attorneys seen by CBS News, Inspector General Don Berthiaume said he was bound by limitations in the law to refer the case to the Office of Professional Responsibility."The primary DOJ allegations in your letter fall within the categories of prosecutorial misconduct," he wrote, adding that his determination "rests on the nature of the allegations and the appropriate oversight forum."Established in the wake of the Watergate scandal, the Office of Professional Responsibility is charged with investigating certain categories of attorney misconduct. Unlike the inspector general, who is presidentially appointed and confirmed by the Senate, however, the head of the Office of Professional Responsibility is appointed by the Attorney General and is generally viewed as less independent than an inspector general's office.Last year, Justice Department leadership removed the career official in charge of the office, a maneuver that raised concerns among longtime department veterans about whether the office would be willing to hold Trump-appointed officials accountable.Lawyers for Hearn responded to the decision in an Oct. 21 letter, noting that the Office of Professional Responsibility has been depleted by roughly 50% since the start of the Trump administration. "The plain fact is that OPR is no longer a fully functioning entity capable of conducting rigorous oversight," they wrote in the letter, which was viewed by CBS News.The attorneys added that the declination from the inspector general's office means that an investigation "will simply not take place." On Oct. 6, Hearn's lawyers asked both the DOJ inspector general and the inspector general at the Interior Department to investigate the circumstances surrounding Hearn's arrest, indictment and the dismissal of the felony charge of destruction of property.The indictment was announced in a fiery press conference on July 2 with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, who accused him of ripping up a piece of the Reflecting Pool liner with his hands.She later dismissed the case, after she said new information had come to light showing the damage had been caused by a contractor's "botched installation," not vandalism. In their follow-up letter to the Justice Department's internal watchdog office, Hearn's lawyers said an investigation was warranted because the handling of the case by the Justice and Interior departments points to "numerous potential crimes, including witness tampering, subornation of perjury, obstruction of justice, and criminal civil rights violations.""The question presented here is not whether prosecutors exercised poor judgment in the course of litigation. Rather, the allegations concern potential criminal conduct, including witness tampering, subornation of perjury, obstruction of justice, and conspiracies against civil rights," said his lawyers, which include former DOJ Inspector General Michael Bromwich."Such allegations fall squarely within the OIG's traditional investigative function," they said. One such example of a possible crime, they said, was the fact that a key witness in the case abruptly changed the content of the testimony before the grand jury.At first, the witness told the grand jury that the Reflecting Pool was already in need of repairs. The witness also was unable to estimate the cost of the damage and did not know whether Hearn had caused it.After a 21-minute break, however, the witness returned and testified that the damage was "definitely" $1,000 or more, his lawyers wrote — a key figure that is necessary in order to indict someone on a destruction of property felony.Prior Justice Department inspectors general have long complained about the limitations to their authority to investigate certain types of attorney misconduct.The OPR is tasked with exclusive jurisdiction to investigate department lawyers in connection with their actions when they are litigating, investigating, or providing legal advice.Federal agents who are accused of misconduct in connection with conducting investigations, however, are subject to the jurisdiction of the inspector general.Despite those delineations, the DOJ inspector general's office has in the past conducted a number of high-profile investigations into conduct by department lawyers.For instance, in 2023, it investigated the former U.S. Attorney Rachael Rollins for the District of Massachusetts and referred her for possible prosecution, after concluding she had improperly used her position to meddle in a local district attorney election by leaking to newspapers dirt about a political rival.The Justice Department declined to pursue criminal charges in that case.In his Oct. 8 letter declining to take up the case, Berthiaume added that his decision should not be interpreted to mean that there was no merit to the allegations or that they should not be reviewed."This determination concerns the appropriate oversight forum and does not constitute a finding on the merits of your allegations," he wrote. "Nor do we regard the dismissal of the criminal case against your client as resolving the separate question of professional misconduct. Consistent with our principles of objectivity and fair process, the referral neither adopts nor rejects the factual assertions in your letter and does not prejudge OPR's assessment."

title: Macomb County outlines "ambitious" $100 million 2027 road construction season
description: Drivers across Macomb County can expect to see more orange barrels next year as county road officials prepare for what they're calling an ambitious 2027 construction season.
content: Drivers across Macomb County can expect to see more orange barrels next year as county road officials prepare for what they're calling an ambitious 2027 construction season.During Wednesday's State of Macomb County Roads presentation, officials outlined more than $100 million in planned road, bridge and traffic improvement projects while also highlighting major work completed throughout 2026.Among the projects expected to move forward next year are improvements to 10 Mile Road, Hayes and Kelly, in Eastpointe and Roseville; a five-mile resurfacing project on Jefferson Avenue in Chesterfield Township; reconstruction work on Joy Boulevard; and bridge work on 21 Mile Road and North River Road."We're talking over $100 million. We're going to be applying towards road improvement projects and traffic improvements here in Macomb County," said Macomb County Executive Mark Hackel.For residents like Mersades Burns, some of those projects can't come soon enough."My tire got busted driving down that road, so it's been out for a good month now," Burns said while discussing conditions on Joy Boulevard.She welcomed news that the roadway is expected to receive attention next year."Good. I'm glad it's getting fixed because that road is horrible and it's been horrible for a very long time," Burns said.County leaders say the planned work follows a busy 2026 construction season. According to officials, more than $119 million in road, bridge and traffic improvements were completed this year, including projects along Mound Road, Dequindre Road and Metro Parkway.Hackel said maintaining the county's transportation system is a significant undertaking. The county road system includes roughly 1,700 miles of roads, 226 bridges and more than 800 culverts."Right now, we see that about 52% of the roads are in good or fair condition. That's always a good thing to hear. But the bigger challenge we have is what's not in that good or fair condition," Hackel said. "It's the poor condition roads that we're talking about."Hackel said nearly half of the county's roadway system still needs work."Forty-eight percent of the roads need work," he said.While county leaders praised additional road funding approved by the state, they acknowledged there remains a substantial gap between available funding and the amount of work needed.Officials estimate it would take approximately $2.5 billion to address all current road repair needs within the county road system."We can't fix a road, a bridge or a culvert unless they fix the funding," Hackel said.In addition to major corridor projects, officials said they plan to invest more in neighborhood roads and pavement preservation efforts aimed at keeping roads in good condition longer.County leaders say those investments, combined with new state funding, should gradually improve road conditions in the coming years. For now, they say drivers should expect construction to remain a common sight throughout Macomb County as work continues on one of Michigan's largest county road systems.

title: Mike Rogers launches statewide bus tour ahead of midterm election
description: With less than two weeks before the election, Republican candidate Mike Rogers launched a statewide bus tour.
content: With less than two weeks before the midterm election, Republican Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers launched a statewide bus tour. "This is the race of our lifetime. This is no longer left versus right," Rogers said at the launch.The Rogers campaign team said he will start the bus tour in the Upper Peninsula after debating his Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, on Wednesday night in Detroit. The first day of the tour includes stops in Marquette and Cheboygan counties. "We're going to get our kids reading again; we're going to bring jobs back here; we are absolutely going to make sure that kids or young adults have the ability to get into a home before the age of 30. We have plans for all of these things, but we can't get to any of it if we don't get people to turn up and vote," he said. The campaign team said that through Nov. 2, they're planning get-out-the-vote-style stops, as well as opportunities to talk with voters at places like distilleries.Rogers encouraged attendees at the tour bus launch to inspire others to vote, too, with a story about a Detroit resident. "Will you vote for us? She said, ' No, I'm going to do something even better,' and I said, 'Oh, really. What's that?' 'I'm going to tell everyone in my neighborhood that you're 100% gangsta," Rogers said. Rogers didn't take any questions at the launch. His team said he wasn't made available because of Wednesday night's final debate with El-Sayed.

title: Subtropical Storm Josephine kicks up high surf while fantastic fall weather continues in Philadelphia
description: Mostly sunny skies will once again spread across the Philadelphia region as temperatures climb back into the mid-to-upper 60s.
content: Philadelphia's fantastic stretch of fall weather continues Wednesday with little change.Mostly sunny skies spread across the region as temperatures climb back into the mid-to-upper 60s. One thing you may notice through the day Wednesday will be a breeze picking up, especially closer to the coast from the newly named Subtropical Storm Josephine.Wind gusts inland will range from 15-25 mph, but near the coast they could reach around 40 mph.NEXT big weather changesThe region's next big change is the strengthening nor'easter — now named Josephine — passing offshore, although the greatest impacts should remain confined to the Jersey Shore and Delaware beaches.Low pressure strengthening off the Carolina coast will gradually move northward, while high pressure remains anchored to our north. The tightening pressure gradient between these systems will produce a prolonged period of northeast winds, pushing water toward the beaches and into the back bays.The duration of that onshore flow will be especially important, as several consecutive high-tide cycles could produce flooding.Coastal flood advisories are in effect through Wednesday evening, with widespread minor flooding expected in vulnerable shore communities. The highest coastal flooding risk is expected around the Wednesday evening high tide.Moderate flooding is possible on low-lying roads and in back bay communities, particularly where water doesn't fully drain between tides. Northeast wind gusts of up to 40 mph and seas reaching 7-12 feet could also produce dangerous marine conditions and additional beach erosion into Thursday.For Philadelphia and our inland suburbs, the forecast remains much quieter. Josephine will begin to pull away Thursday, allowing winds and water levels to gradually subside, with highs rebounding to the upper 60s inland.Another push of cooler air arrives Friday, bringing highs back into the lower 60s, followed by a chilly Friday night and Saturday morning with possible frost.The weekend looks mainly sunny and dry, with temperatures gradually moderating from the lower to mid 60s Saturday to near 70 degrees Sunday.The bottom line: beautiful fall weather continues inland, but several rounds of coastal flooding, strong winds and beach erosion concerns will affect the shore through midweek.Here's your 7-day forecast:Wednesday: Breezy, bright. High 67, Low 48Thursday: Sunny. High 70, Low 46Friday: Cooler. High 61, Low 46Saturday: Chilly a.m. High 64, Low 38Sunday: Sunny. High 68, Low 38Monday: Sunny. High 74, Low 41Tuesday: Partly cloudy.
