Case followed Trump executive orderThe dispute before the Supreme Court stems from a lawsuit the inmates filed against the Trump administration last year on behalf of incarcerated people diagnosed with gender dysphoria. The suit was filed after President Trump issued an executive order that barred the use of federal funds for medical procedures or treatments for transgender inmates who are in Bureau of Prisons custody.In response to Mr. Trump's directive, the Bureau of Prisons issued a new policy in February stating that it would not provide surgeries or hormone therapy to address gender dysphoria. Inmates who were receiving hormone treatments could be put on a tapering plan that would eventually lead to a discontinuation of the interventions.Under the new rules, the Bureau of Prisons will also no longer provide any social accommodations, such as breast padding, binders, wigs and makeup, to inmates with gender dysphoria.In a memo accompanying the policy, the Bureau of Prisons cited Mr. Trump's executive order and said it changed its rules to "reflect treatment for gender dysphoria that is more aligned with the latest scientific information, that is consistent with BOP's longstanding policy of providing medical care that is tailored to the unique needs of the inmate, and that accounts for the complex security and administration concerns in the correctional environment."In June, U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth issued an order preventing the Trump administration from enforcing the February policy. The judge required the Bureau of Prisons to continue providing medical interventions and social accommodations to a class of inmates with gender dysphoria."The court does not wade into the culture war being waged against transgender individuals," Lamberth, who was appointed by President Ronald Reagan, wrote in a 31-page decision. "The court simply concludes that the government violated [federal law] when it issued a new policy restricting the provision of gender-affirming care to inmates diagnosed with gender dysphoria."Lamberth issued an order in August that continued to block the policy.A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit then declined to lift the district court's injunction. In a 2-1 decision, the appeals court said the Bureau of Prisons "did not adequately consider its own experience providing gender-affirming care under its prior policy" and failed to make a strong showing that it is likely to succeed on the merits of the case.Appeal to Supreme CourtIn its emergency appeal to the Supreme Court, Solicitor General D. John Sauer argued that the district court's decision "prevents the application of the Executive's chosen policy" on a broad basis.Sauer defended the legality of the policy ending medical treatments for transgender inmates and said the Bureau of Prisons "seasonably considered its prior experience both in determining that such interventions are not medically necessary and in determining that security and prison-administration concerns independently justified a change in policy."But the challengers of the administration's new rules argued the Trump administration failed to put forth any evidence indicating whether healthcare providers for the Bureau of Prisons found the now-restricted medical treatments to be effective, ineffective or harmful."BOP cut off treatment that its healthcare providers had recommended for decades and replaced it with psychotherapy — which its own expert acknowledges is backed by no evidence demonstrating its efficacy as a treatment for gender dysphoria — and psychotropic medications — which BOP's Medical Director does not even claim treat gender dysphoria, only co-existing conditions," lawyers for the transgender inmates wrote.They also argued that the agency has not "pointed to a single security incident" relating to the provision of medical interventions to address gender dysphoria."Had BOP's doctors found this treatment unhelpful or harmful to patients or had the agency found that the treatment compromised security, surely BOP would have mentioned it in the administrative record," lawyers for the plaintiffs said. "That glaring omission, as well as the unreasonableness of its decision, make it clear that the rationales were contrived to support the demand President Trump made in the EO."

title: Crews investigate reports of gas leak at Dolphin Mall in Sweetwater, MDFR says
description: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said the gas company has been notified of the situation and no injuries have been reported.
content: An investigation took place at the Dolphin Mall in Sweetwater after officials received reports of a gas leak on Wednesday morning, according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue.Few details have been released, but MDFR told CBS News Miami that the call was handled by the first arriving units, and the gas company had been notified.The mall was not evacuated and no injuries were reported.No other information was released.

title: South Florida king tides, heavy rain and wind lead to concerns of flooding this weekend
description: A NEXT Weather Alert will go into effect in South Florida starting on Sunday and lasting through Tuesday.
content: It's finally feeling a bit more like fall out across South Florida on Wednesday morning with low temperatures that dropped into the upper 60s and low 70s.Expect a beautiful, breezy, and mainly dry day ahead with forecast high temperatures in the low 80s with plenty of sunshine.Get outside and enjoy the day while you can since our weather pattern will be changing later this week, and the weekend is looking very wet and windy.Wednesday won't be as blustery, but there is still a dangerous high risk of rip currents along our Atlantic beaches.Minor coastal seawater flooding will be possible along low-lying, vulnerable areas along the coast due to the king tides returning starting on Wednesday.A small craft advisory continues for boaters due to the choppy conditions on the bay.On Thursday morning, we'll wake up with low temperatures in the upper 60s and low 70s once again. The chance of rain will be low, but some spotty showers will be possible.High temperatures will rise into the 80s in the afternoon.Scattered showers will be moving into the region on Friday, and then even more wet weather is expected on Saturday and especially on Sunday.The Weather Prediction Center has already placed most of South Florida under a Level 2 risk of excessive heavy rainfall with a slight risk of flash flooding on Sunday.NEXT Weather Alert goes into effect SundayThe CBS News Miami NEXT Weather team will be issuing a NEXT Weather Alert from Sunday to Tuesday due to the potential for heavy rain, localized flooding, gusty winds and the higher-than-normal king tide flooding, which will peak late weekend into early next week.Moderate to major coastal flooding will be possible.In addition, wind gusts could reach 30 to 40 mph or stronger Sunday into Monday.

title: Maryland announces Blue Ribbon Schools for 2026-2027. These 23 made the list.

content: Maryland is honoring 23 schools with "Blue Ribbon" status for the 2026-2027 academic year, Gov. Wes Moore announced Tuesday. The honorees include 12 public schools, along with six from the Archdiocese of Baltimore and five from the Archdiocese of Washington."Here in Maryland we have the talent and the drive to have the best schools in the nation, and these exceptional institutions are leading our state in that effort, " Moore said in his announcement. "While our administration works to ensure every Maryland student has a world-class education, we are proud to honor a growing cohort of schools that embody the best of what our state has to offer."The schools were selected based on their performance on state and national tests, as well as their "success in closing achievement gaps" among groups of students, the announcement said. The honorees will receive a Maryland Blue Ribbon School banner, flag and an award citation, and they will be formally honored during the Maryland State Board of Education meeting on Dec. 8 and during the General Assembly legislative session next spring. title: Denver business owner calls for more police action after nearly $8,000 in tools stolen from work van
description: The owner of Peak HVAC Heating & Air Conditioning LLC said someone smashed the passenger-side window of his work van and stole the equipment he relies on to make a living.
content: A Denver small business owner is calling for more action from police after thieves broke into his work van and stole nearly $8,000 worth of tools, leaving his business unable to operate for several days.Elliot Charles, owner of Peak HVAC Heating & Air Conditioning LLC, said someone smashed the passenger side window of his work van and stole the equipment he relies on to make a living.Charles discovered the theft on the morning of Oct. 12."I put every single thing that I earn back into this company," Charles said. "They stole all of our tools that we were supposed to use for the job."Charles left his engineering career in Houston to return to Colorado with his family and start his own business, investing his life savings into the company."I mean, tens of thousands of dollars in order to get up and running," Charles said. "Obviously, I put my life savings into this business."Just months after launching the business, Charles said the theft forced him to temporarily shut down operations."We were out of business for pretty much a week," Charles said.Charles said he filed a police report, but no officer responded to the scene to investigate the break-in."The cop told me on the phone they don't have anyone to help me," Charles said.He also said his commercial auto insurance policy does not cover the stolen equipment, leaving him responsible for replacing the tools.Charles said he has spent thousands of dollars on security measures and insurance to protect his business, but the theft has left him questioning whether those protections are enough. He said he remains hesitant to restock his van because of ongoing security concerns.Beyond the financial loss, Charles said the experience has shaken his sense of safety in the community. He emphasized that he is not seeking donations. Instead, he wants police to investigate the theft and help recover his equipment."I need the police to do their job so that I could do my job," Charles said.Under Colorado law, theft of property valued between $5,000 and $20,000 is classified as a Class 5 felony.CBS Colorado reached out to DPD for comment and is waiting on a response.

title: NFLPA calls for full investigation into how Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' blood clots
description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the rest of the season after he was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs.
content: The NFL Players Association is calling for a full investigation into how the Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' blood clots. "The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," an NFLPA spokesperson said Tuesday. "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward." Meanwhile, the NFL staunchly defended the Eagles' handling of Hurts. A person with knowledge of the situation confirmed to The Associated Press that the Eagles were not being disciplined for their actions with Hurts. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because conversations between the league and team were to remain private.Dr. Allen Sills, the NFL's chief medical officer, offered a passionate defense of how the Eagles treated Hurts, following a statement from the league that said officials had been in contact with Philadelphia's medical personnel and the Cleveland Clinic in London throughout the process."I have complete confidence in the Eagles' medical staff and their handling of this situation, and I would characterize their work as very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded at every step," Sills said at the league's annual fall meeting. "I don't think you can take that outcome and say there was something flawed about the process. Sometimes in medicine, we do all the right things and diseases progress and other things develop. ..."In this case, everyone was incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant and was very quick to make diagnoses of these conditions that might not have been diagnosed in a nonathlete."Multiple NFL insiders reported Monday that Hurts was told not to sleep in London after receiving his first blood clot diagnosis. The report was later clarified, and the NFL also refuted it. "No one told Hurts not to go to sleep," an NFL spokesperson said. "All players and staff were told to try to stay awake later into Saturday evening as the Eagles didn't have a bye week following the game. The team was leaving after the London game and trying to stay on a regular sleep." Hurts is on injured reserve and expected to miss the rest of the season after a blood clot in his left calf traveled to his lungs. The Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn on Monday said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.His treatment involves blood thinners, and Hurts will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them.Hurts played in London against Jacksonville on Oct. 11, three days after informing medical staff of the injury after practice. He was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis.Hurts is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery. "We anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery," a joint statement from the Eagles and Lynn read in part. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni declined to get into specifics Monday about how the team handled Hurts' blood clots, including allowing him to play against the Jaguars and fly back from London. "Guys, I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni said. "I lean on our guys in all those situations. I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full faith and trust in them. It's not just me that has major care for our players; it's them as well. So, we are all there, and I'm glad to be part of an organization that cares about the guys the way our guys do."With Hurts out, the Eagles' season is heading in the wrong direction. They're 2-4, injury-riddled and have lost four straight for the first time since 2020, with the Dallas Cowboys coming to Lincoln Financial Field for a prime-time matchup on "Monday Night Football."

title: 2 dead, 1 injured in shooting near gas station in Northwest Baltimore
description: Two men died and another person was injured after a shooting near a gas station in Northwest Baltimore on Monday afternoon, according to police.
content: Two men died and another person was injured after a shooting near a gas station in Northwest Baltimore on Monday afternoon, according to police.Officers responded around 4:30 p.m. to the area near Fuel Motor Fuels in the 5200 block of Muth Avenue, where three men were found shot.A 24-year-old man and a 30-year-old man died, and a 21-year-old man was taken to the hospital in stable condition."I was so surprised and scared," Baltimore resident Suah Lee said.The shooting comes a day after eight people were shot in two separate incidents in West Baltimore. Two people were killed.Baltimore police said that as of Tuesday morning, 253 people have been shot in the city so far in 2026, compared with 247 at this point last year. The city has recorded 101 homicides this year, down from 105 during the same period in 2025."It doesn't make sense," another Baltimore resident said. "We shouldn't have to do this. When does it stop?"2 dead, 3 injured in West Baltimore gas station shootingA 34-year-old woman and a 20-year-old man were killed in a shooting at a gas station in the 2800 block of Edmondson Avenue in West Baltimore on Sunday night.Officers responded around 10:30 p.m. to the BP gas station, where they found a woman and three men suffering from gunshot wounds. Another man arrived at a hospital with gunshot wounds.The woman and one of the men died. The three other men are expected to survive.The victims in the shooting were identified as 20-year-old Dashawn McCoy and 34-year-old Layla Bailey.Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said there appeared to be two or three shooters and that high-powered rifles were used. No arrests have been announced.3 injured in shooting at Northwest Baltimore liquor storeEarlier Sunday night, three people were injured in a shooting at a liquor store in Northwest Baltimore, according to police.Officers responded around 8:30 p.m. to Pepper Liquor Store in the 5400 block of Reisterstown Road, where they found two women, ages 26 and 22, suffering from gunshot wounds.Both women were taken to a hospital in stable condition.While at the scene, officers were notified that a 27-year-old man had arrived at a hospital with non-life-threatening gunshot wounds.Recent shootings in BaltimoreBaltimore police have responded to at least four mass shootings over the past month, including a shooting earlier this month that killed a 12-year-old at a West Baltimore park.Another mass shooting in the Winchester neighborhood of West Baltimore left an 18-year-old and a 19-year-old dead and two other people wounded."It continues to be young people that indiscriminately fire weapons that they don't know how to shoot, they don't know how to control and multiple people are getting hit," Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said Sunday night. "It is frustrating. We are going to continue to push, try to solve this one and hold those accountable who took two lives."

title: DuPage County reports first measles case of 2026, with exposure at Chicago O'Hare Airport
description: DuPage County has reported its first measles case of 2026, and said the patient traveled through Chicago O'Hare International Airport.
content: DuPage County has reported its first measles case of 2026, and said the patient traveled through Chicago O'Hare International Airport.The count said the case is in a vaccinated resident who recently returned from an international trip DuPage health officials said anyone who was at O'Hare Terminal 5 on Thursday, Oct. 15, between 4:20 p.m. and 7 p.m. should contact their local health department to report they may have been exposed.Because the case is in a vaccinated person, DuPage health officials said the risk to the public is low. Vaccinated individuals who catch measles typically have a milder illness and are less likely to experience complication. They also may be less likely to spread the virus to othersThe MMR vaccine – which covers measles, mumps and rubella – is considered protection for life against measles and rubella, though the CDC says it may become less effective against mumps over time. If you've had two doses of the MMR or were born before 1957, you're considered protected.Breakthrough measles infections in vaccinated individuals are uncommon but possible, health officials said. If you may have been exposed to measles, you should monitor for symptoms for 21 days. Symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, red and water eyes and a rash that typically starts on the face and spread downwards. The rash typically appears three to five days after other symptoms start. So far in 2026, the Illinois Department of Public Health has confirmed 24 cases of measles, with the case in DuPage County being the only confirmed in the past week. Most of the cases are linked to an outbreak in Douglas County, which is south of Champaign and east of Decatur, where 11 cases have been confirmed. The rash appears as pink, red or reddish-brown flat spots and small raised bumps on light skin tones, and darker, dusky or purplish-brown areas on darker skin tones. The rash can be more subtle on darker skin tones, but a bumpy or textured feel is often present. If you have questions about whether a rash may be related to measles, call your doctor immediately. Cook, DeKalb and DuPage counties have all had one confirmed case of measles so far this year. Kane County has had two, Madison County has had three and Moultrie County has had five.

title: Vehicle struck by lightning south of Eddy Road in Colusa County, man taken to hospital
description: A man was taken to the hospital after he was struck by lightning Wednesday while he was sitting in his vehicle in Colusa County, officials said.
content: A man was taken to the hospital after the vehicle he was sitting in was struck by lightning Wednesday, the Arbuckle Fire Department said.The vehicle was in an open field roughly a mile south of Eddy Road when lightning struck the antenna of the vehicle, the fire department said, causing the man to suffer minor burns to his left leg. The man was not directly struck by the lightning bolt, but his injuries were caused by the strike, according to the fire department.It is not clear why the man had parked the vehicle in the field, although the fire department said that he was a farm laborer.

title: Atlanta police searching for suspects in apartment shooting that hospitalized 13-year-old boy
description: Police say the 13-year-old was inside the Atlanta apartment when a group opened fire into the building early Sunday morning.
content: Atlanta police are asking the public for help finding a group of suspects in a shooting that sent a 13-year-old boy to the hospital over the weekend.Officials say the shooting happened shortly before 4 a.m. on Sunday at the Capitol Vanira apartments on the 900 block of Hank Aaron Drive SE.Officers got to the scene and found the teenage victim shot at least once. Medics rushed the teen to a nearby hospital. He is expected to survive his injuries.Investigators say the victim was inside the home when a group opened fire, shooting multiple rounds into the apartment.The Atlanta Police Department shared surveillance video showing six people wearing hoodies walking into the complex less than 10 minutes before the shooting took place, identifying the group as suspects.After the shooting, the group left the area, heading northbound on Fraser Street SE, investigators said. Authorities have not released any information about a possible motive behind the shooting.The case remains under investigation. Officials are asking anyone who has information that could help with the investigation to call the Crime Stoppers tip line at 404-577-8477 or go to www.stopcrimeatl.org.

title: Boston police officer justified in shooting knife-wielding man to death inside Chick-fil-A, D.A. says
description: An off-duty Boston police officer was justified in shooting a knife-wielding man to death inside a Chick-fil-A ​last year, the district attorney said.
content: An off-duty Boston police officer was justified in shooting a knife-wielding man to death inside a Chick-fil-A last year, Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden announced Wednesday.The deadly shooting happened at the busy Copley Square restaurant on March 1, 2025. Hayden said 32-year-old Lemark Jaramillo had chased a 17-year-old boy into the restaurant and was trying to stab him in retaliation for a fight that happened moments before at a nearby Chipotle.The district attorney released police body camera footage and witness interviews alongside the investigation report. According to Hayden, witnesses confirmed that Jaramillo ignored commands from Officer Jose Valenzuela to drop the knife.Jaramillo was "literally about to plunge the knife into the youth's back" when the officer fired three shots, Hayden said."Officer Valenzuela fired his off-duty handgun in a lawful use of force that was necessary to prevent Mr. Jaramillo from killing or seriously wounding the younger male or anyone else," Hayden said in the report. "Therefore, I have determined that criminal charges against the officer are not warranted." Surveillance video from a neighboring liquor store showed panicked customers running out of the restaurant and onto Boylston Street as the incident unfolded. "It was scary," one teenage girl told WBZ-TV at the time. "He was like, 'put the knife down, sir.' Boom, that's when he shot him. It was fast."Another bystander said he was walking by the restaurant with his girlfriend and dog when everyone came running out."Somebody yelled gunshot, gunshot and we all ran away," Paul Andresen said. "Definitely scary; I live only a couple of blocks away."

title: Education sales tax renewal is on the ballot this November in DeKalb County: Here's what it would do
description: Voters in DeKalb County will decide whether to renew a one-cent E-SPLOST that goes toward improving schools across the county, in Atlanta, and in Decatur.
content: Voters in DeKalb County will decide whether to renew a special one-cent sales tax that goes toward improving schools. DeKalb County's E-SPLOST is a special local sales tax that goes toward improving the DeKalb County School District, Atlanta Public Schools, and City Schools of Decatur. "Things like roof repairs, HVAC replacement, school renovations of varying sorts and kinds, technology upgrades — significant technology upgrades, significant transportation equipment upgrades, those sorts of things," said DeKalb County School District Superintendent Norman Sauce. APS and CSD are included in DeKalb's E-SPLOST because both City Schools of Decatur and a portion of Atlanta Public Schools are in DeKalb County. The tax is on retail goods and services and is paid by anyone making a purchase in DeKalb County, not just residents. DeKalb County resident Al Bailey said he isn't a fan of the school board, but still supports E-SPLOST. "The school board gotta get their act together," Bailey said. "We're wasting too much money on our school board. Our school board, I mean, I don't like it, but it is what it is, but you still need that money for your children." For DeKalb County, this would be an E-SPLOST renewal. According to the district, E-SPLOST VI was approved by 81 percent of voters in November 2021 and took effect July 1, 2022. If approved, this next round would be E-SPLOST VII. "This would be a continuation of what the voters have passed, you know, going all the way back to E-SPLOST I, and so it's not anything new or different," Sauce said. E-SPLOST VI funding has been part of the conversation across the district in recent months. The district said City Schools of Decatur discovered that it and Atlanta Public Schools had not been receiving their correct share of E-SPLOST VI funds. During a July school board meeting, Sauce said a certificate of distribution containing the revenue split among all three districts had never been submitted back in 2022. According to the Sept. 14 DeKalb County school board meeting agenda, the district owed APS $2.9 million and CSD a little more than $9 million. Sauce said both APS and CSD have since been paid. "We put measures in place and given specific responsibility to individuals in our finance department to do so, and there won't be any issues with that," Sauce said. "Once E-SPLOST VII passes, we'll certainly have that submitted on time, on deadline, and then we'll be able to guarantee the public that that won't happen again." Sauce said the Georgia Department of Audits not only looks at the district's overall finances, but the E-SPLOST program as well. DeKalb resident Faye Garrett supports the E-SPLOST renewal but would like to see more transparency from the district. "Involve the community a little bit more about how they plan on spending the money, and then you know just have regular meetings informing taxpayers about where the dollars are actually going," Garrett said. Sauce said the district is also looking to hire a full-time auditor specifically dedicated to the E-SPLOST program. "We do have an internal department of audits and compliance," Sauce said. "This person, when we identify that person, this full-time auditor just for E-SPLOST programming would reside in that office to help us ensure a daily, regular, full-time commitment of reviewing, monitoring, and auditing our E-SPLOST programming and funding." E-SPLOST is on the ballot in other metro Atlanta counties, including Fulton and Athens-Clarke.

title: 3 injured in condo complex fire in McHenry, Illinois
description: Three people were injured and a garage was destroyed in a fire at a condo complex on Wednesday morning in northwest suburban McHenry.
content: Three people were injured and a garage was destroyed in a fire at a condo complex on Wednesday morning in northwest suburban McHenry.McHenry Township Fire Protection District officials said the fire started around 9:45 a.m. in a four-unit condo building in the 4900 block of West Oakwood Drive.When firefighters arrived, two people were trapped on a second floor balcony. Both were rescued and taken to the hospital for smoke inhalation. A third person who lives in the building was taken to the hospital after suffering an ankle injury while escaping the fire. None of the injuries were considered to be life-threatening.The fire appeared to have destroyed the attached garage of the condo complex, and at least four vehicles appeared to have been destroyed inside the garage.Fire officials said all four units of the condo complex were left uninhabitable due to the fire.The cause of the fire was under investigation.

title: 16-year-old boy shot and killed in Bellwood, Illinois; 3 in custody
description: Boy shot, killed in Bellwood, Illinois
content: A teenage boy was killed this week in a shooting in the west Chicago suburb of Bellwood.Bellwood police said at 3:21 p.m. Tuesday, they were called to the 1000 block of 22nd Avenue after someone was shot and thrown out of a car.Officers found a male juvenile who had been shot, police said. Bellwood fire crews took the boy to a local hospital, where he died.The Cook County Medical Examiner's office identified the boy as Alejandro Garcia, of Villa Park.Bellwood police detectives were investigating Wednesday morning, and said three people had been taken into custody. Police said the Cook County State's Attorney has been notified of the investigation.The West Suburban Crimes Task Force was helping to investigate, police said. No charges have yet been announced.

title: After 75 years serving Monticello and Buffalo, Stellis Health plans to join CentraCare
description: Stellis Health says its commitment to the communities it serves "isn't changing" as it plans to become part of CentraCare. Shareholders have voted to move forward.
content: Stellis Health plans to become part of CentraCare, the two organizations announced. They have a goal of completing the change with the arrival of the new year. For now, Stellis clinics and team members will continue operating as usual, and patients can keep seeing their current providers, the organizations said. Stellis shareholders have voted to move forward. The organizations still need to complete final agreements and get required regulatory review and approval. The announcement did not include financial terms. Stellis has provided care in Monticello, Buffalo and surrounding communities for 75 years. Under the proposed agreement, Stellis physicians, advanced practice providers and team members would join CentraCare. The organizations said the move would improve coordination between primary care, specialty care and hospital services. The two already work together, particularly in Monticello, where Stellis physicians provide care at CentraCare â Monticello Hospital. Both also use Epic, an electronic medical record system. CentraCare President and CEO Ken Holmen said the organizations need to be "thoughtful about how we position our organizations for the future" as health care changes rapidly. Stellis Health President Frank Anderson said Stellis "has been built on the simple idea of neighbors caring for neighbors," and called the partnership a chance to carry those values forward. Stellis Health CEO Brent Wilde said providers and employees have built lasting relationships with patients and families, and that the commitment to communities "isn't changing."

title: Ohio governor's race takes ugly turn with Ramaswamy attack ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother
description: Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar in a new Ramaswamy campaign ad. Acton's brother says the ad marks a "despicable low" and says their stepfather sexually abused Acton when she was a child.
content: A new attack ad from Republican Vivek Ramaswamy features the estranged mother of his opponent in the Ohio governor's race, Amy Acton, calling her a "liar." Acton's campaign and her brother denounced the ad as a "despicable low."Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, whose husband was accused of raping Acton when she was a child, says in the spot, "It's not easy for a mother to say this, but Amy was a serious problem. She is a liar; she lies about her past." Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, lashed out at Ramaswamy in response: "It's not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother's husband into a political talking point." He said that after their stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested and charged, he and Acton were removed from the Arthurs' custody and lived with their father. "Our birth mother stayed married to Amy's rapist until he died," Stearns said. "This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core â a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants."The origin of the ad, which circulated on social media Monday night, was initially unclear because it lacked the mandatory disclosure of who paid for and authorized the spot. But on Tuesday, Ramaswamy told reporters it was "an ad from our campaign," according to The Columbus Dispatch. He defended the content of the ad, saying: "Every person who appears to know her the best â¦ have told voters not to vote for her but to vote for me instead."Connie Luck, a spokesperson for Ramaswamy, said in a statement earlier Tuesday, "We don't know what happened between Amy and her mother, who first spoke out about Amy in 2020, but we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist who has some serious problems with the truth that the public needs to be aware of before deciding who to entrust as governor." The state Republican Party has not responded to a request for comment.Vice President JD Vance, who represented Ohio in the Senate before becoming vice president, said Wednesday that "whether the ad was appropriate or not is not really my concern" and that he was "a little bit disgusted" by fellow Republicans who are "whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America.""Politics is a tough business," Vance said. "And my message to my fellow elected Republicans is, if you actually believe in the things you say you believe in, stop whining about an advertisement and go win the race in 13 days."Acton, who served as the state's public health commissioner under GOP Gov. Mike DeWine during the pandemic, has previously talked about being abused by her now-deceased stepfather. According to court records provided by the campaign, in 1978, Arthur was charged with raping Acton, when she was between 10 and 12 years old. He entered a not guilty plea.Acton has also detailed struggles throughout her early childhood with poverty and homelessness, and records provided by her campaign show that the family lived in a tent for a year. Acton told the Youngstown Vindicator in 2019 that once she and her brother were able to go live with their father, their lives became more stable. "In the courthouse after they were charged, I went to give her a kiss, and she just turned her cheek away," Acton told The Vindicator seven years ago. "That was the last time I ever saw her." Her campaign says that court date remains the last time Acton saw her mother.Her mother and her stepfather, released on bond, left Ohio without facing charges, the news site said. Warrants were issued for Cledith Arthur's arrest at least twice in the next few years, according to court records. Donna and Cledith Arthur lived in Pennsylvania until Cledith's death in 2004. Ramaswamy's backers have launched other personal attacks against Acton, who has been leading in polls over the last month.Other aspects of Acton's personal life have also resurfaced during the election, including an incident when police were called to her home in 2019 during what was characterized as a domestic dispute.

title: Old Highway 6 in Colorado revealed as Lake Dillon Reservoir's water levels recede
description: The Old Highway 6 in Colorado has been revealed in recent weeks as Lake Dillon's water levels continue to recede. The highway has been submerged for six decades!
content: The Old Highway 6 in Colorado has been revealed in recent weeks as Lake Dillon, also known as Dillon Reservoir, continues to recede during drought conditions across the state. The old highway is typically submerged in the reservoir. The highway went through the middle of Old Dillon, but in 1962, the town moved to what is now Dillon, and the reservoir was filled with water. Portions of Interstate 70 replaced parts of Old Highway 6 as the interstate system was constructed across Colorado. "If you didn't move your building, it was torn down and burned... If someone tells you that if the lake gets low, you can see the structures... No. You might be able to see the road network, but you won't see any buildings," said Bruce Queen with the Summit Historical Society. According to Queen, the last time the water dropped this low, exposing part of Old Highway 6, was in the 1980s.

title: Woodie's Flat in Old Town has Malort wings in October
description: Chicago sports bar Woodie's Flat has a new wing flavor through the end of October, featuring Chicago's most well-known, and hotly debated spirit: Malort.
content: Chicago sports bar Woodie's Flat has a new wing flavor through the end of October, featuring Chicago's most well-known, and hotly debated spirit: Malort.The Old Town bar, which just won Best Overall Wings at Chicago's Wing Out for the fourth consecutive year, said their sauce blends a classic BBQ sauce with Malort for a "bold, unexpected" flavor.The bar's wings are smaller than some other bars â by design, they say, as they get a juicier cook that way â and are smoked over hickory and applewood for about two hours, coated in a signature spice rub, then double-fried.The Malort BBQ wings are the latest in the bar's Sauce of the Month series and will be available through Oct. 31.

title: Angels won't extend Kurt Suzuki's contract, begin search for new manager for 2027 season
description: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, which agreed to purchase the franchise from Arte Moreno, will lead the search for a replacement.
content: As the franchise wipes the slate clean ahead of a new era beginning in 2027, the Los Angeles Angels announced Wednesday that they'll have a new manager alongside new ownership.In a post to social media, the Angels announced that the club declined Kurt Suzuki's contract option for 2027 and will begin the search for a new manager."As we look toward 2027 and beyond, I have had thoughtful conversations internally and with Kroenke Sports & Entertainment's leadership about the future of Angels Baseball and the direction of our organization," said Baseball Operations Consultant John Mozeliak. "Those conversations have shaped the decision to seek a new manager and coaching staff for the 2027 season."Suzuki's stint as manager in Anaheim will end after just one season, which happened to be the worst in franchise history. The Angels, who were previously the only team in MLB to never have lost 100 games in a single season, went 62-100 in 2026.The team hired Suzuki last October after firing Ron Washington, who helmed the club for two seasons. The new manager in 2027 will be the franchise's sixth full-time manager since longtime skipper Mike Scioscia was fired in 2018. Suzuki played 16 seasons in Major League Baseball, including his final two in Anaheim with the Angels. After his 2022 retirement, he joined the team's front office as a special assistant to the general manager. "Kurt has earned tremendous respect in our clubhouse, and I've seen firsthand how much he cares about our players," Mozeliak said. "I do not believe our record this year was a true reflection of his abilities as a manager."Mozeliak said the franchise has offered Suzuki a role to stay on as a special assistant, "where his knowledge of our players and his perspective would continue to be valuable to the organization." It's unclear whether Suzuki will accept the offer.The Angels also said the managerial search would include a search for a new coaching staff.

title: Detroit Fire Department rescues woman from apartment fire
description: The Detroit Fire Department rescued a woman from an apartment fire on the 12700 block of Plymouth Road early Wednesday, the fire department says.
content: The Detroit Fire Department rescued a woman from an apartment fire on the 12700 block of Plymouth Road early Wednesday, the fire department says.The fire department received a call reporting a fire in an apartment at 12:34 a.m. Wednesday. Crews arrived to find the fire showing from two sides of the apartment, made entry and removed the occupant from the apartment with the help of Detroit Police officers.The resident, a woman in her mid-30s, according to the fire department, was suffering from smoke inhalation.The woman was transported to Sinai-Grace Hospital, where she was in critical condition per her last check, according to the fire department.Crews knocked the fire down and contained it to one unit.One Detroit police officer was evaluated by EMS on scene and refused transport.

title: Entire full-time police department resigns in Milner amid dispute with city leaders
description: Milner's entire full-time police department has submitted resignations, along with the city manager, who told council members Monday that a breakdown in trust had made her unable to do her job.
content: The City of Milner's entire full-time police department has submitted resignations, along with the city manager, who told council members Monday that a breakdown in trust had made her unable to do her job.City Manager Tausha Grose announced the departures at the Oct. 19 City Council meeting. She said the police department's last day would be Oct. 28 and hers would be Oct. 30."The trust is gone. I have been rendered ineffective in my position," Grose said. "There is no trust."The resignations include Police Chief Lamar Bunn and the department's full-time officers. Grose also said most of its part-time officers had resigned.Both Grose and Bunn rejected the suggestion that a dispute over officers' outside work was the reason for their departures. Grose said officers could continue working part-time jobs but had temporarily been barred from using city vehicles for that work.Bunn raised concerns about surveillance, saying officers could not trust that cameras or tracking devices would not be used without their knowledge."If I cannot do my job, if I'm not given an opportunity to do my job with character, I can't do it," he said.Bunn said he had not asked other officers to resign with him and was not the first to submit his resignation.Despite announcing his departure, he expressed interest in resolving the dispute before Oct. 28."So it's the trust issue. If it can be fixed, we need to fix it," Bunn said.Mayor Craig Timmons told The Herald Gazette he had not expected the resignations. Asked whether he had placed a tracker on Bunn's vehicle, the mayor declined to comment directly, the newspaper reported. Grose, who said she had devoted six years to the city, described leaving as painful."It breaks my heart to have to resign," she said.

title: Knicks championship ring maker on capturing New York City's DNA in his design
description: Jason Arasheben has designed championship rings for plenty of teams. When he was tapped to create one for the Knicks, he knew it needed to represent New York in a special way.
content: It took Jason Arasheben 22 carats of diamonds and blue sapphires, 180 grams of gold and nearly 800 individually set stones to capture New York City's DNA in the Knicks' championship rings, which he debuted last night at the team's home opener against the Philadelphia 76ers."I wanted something that really captured the essence, the grit, the energy of New York City," Arasheben said.While he's designed championship pieces for other professional teams, the Knicks were different."This is the mecca of basketball, arguably the greatest city on Earth," he said."The real DNA behind this," Arasheben explained, "was to capture Madison Square Garden, where this championship was won."The ring opens up to reveal a replica of "The World's Most Famous Arena." A 16-point diamond mounted on the tiny gold Larry O'Brien Trophy is meant to represent the 16-point deficit the Knicks overcame in their final game against the San Antonio Spurs."We want something that's not only amazing in design but robust in storytelling," the designer said.Squeezing all of those elements into a seven-week turnaround time is no small feat, but Arasheben works well under pressure — much like Jalen Brunson, he said, "I like to come through in the fourth quarter."He says he didn't sleep at all the night before the debut, but the players' reactions make it all worthwhile."When I see their eyes light up and their jaws drop, I know I did my job," Arasheben said.A limited number, 200 rings, are available at Jason of Beverly Hills for $20,000 each.

title: Man with machete steals teen's sneakers in the subway, police say
description: A man with a machete stole a teenager's sneakers on the subway Sunday night, police said. It happened on a northbound 2 train near Westchester and Intervale avenues at 11:18 p.m.
content: A man with a machete stole a teenager's sneakers on the subway Sunday night, police said. It happened on a northbound 2 train near Westchester and Intervale avenues at 11:18 p.m. Police said the suspect approached a 15-year-old on the train. The suspect, who was wearing a backpack, opened it and "displayed a machete," police said. He then removed the teen's sneakers. A 25-year-old good Samaritan on the train intervened, but the man with the machete punched him in the face and ran off, police said. The teen was not physically hurt. The 25-year-old who was punched refused medical attention at the scene. Police say the suspect is about 17-20 years old, has a light complexion, has a heavy build, black braided hair and brown eyes. He was wearing a black jacket, gray sweatpants, and carried a black backpack. The NYPD says crime in the transit system has ticked up slightly so far this year - crime statistics reflect a 1.7% increase year to date - but overall, 2026 has been the second safest year in the transit system in the past 15 years, excluding the pandemic. Anyone with any information is asked to call the NYPD's Crime Stoppers hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477), or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782). You can also submit a tip via the Crime Stoppers website or via DM on X, @NYPDTips. All calls are kept confidential.

title: North Texas highs remain in the low 80s to close the work week
description: By the end of the workweek, we'll see an uptick in our cloud cover and these clouds linger this weekend.
content: Wednesday morning temperatures were once again in the 50s in North Texas, providing another refreshing start. Be sure to grab a jacket for this morning and have the sunglasses handy for this afternoon. Highs today warm into the lower 80s.There is an Air Quality Alert in effect today due to elevated surface ozone levels. With high pressure in control, sinking air outside traps pollution at the surface instead of allowing it to rise. For the next couple of days, our weather pattern will remain quiet. Highs rise into the middle 80s tomorrow and stay there into Friday. By the end of the workweek, we'll see an uptick in cloud cover, and these clouds will linger this weekend. Highs this weekend stay above average in the lower 80s. With dry conditions, it will be perfect for any fall-like activities. Looking ahead to next week, a cold front approaches and should move through around Tuesday. As a result, we'll see small chances of rain and temperatures right around average.

title: Elon Musk signals Tesla and SpaceX could merge. Here's why he thinks it's a good idea.
description: Combining SpaceX and Tesla, whose stocks jumped after Musk said the companies are exploring a deal, would be the biggest corporate merger of all time.
content: Elon Musk on Tuesday said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger — a business combination that one Wall Street analyst said could be worth nearly $5 trillion, which would make it the largest deal in corporate history. "Both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea at the request of shareholders, and these special committees consist of independent directors," Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call with investors, adding that he sees "a lot of merit to combining the companies."Tesla's stock price rose $14.01, or 3.8%, to $387.72, while SpaceX shares jumped $14.62, or 9.9%, to $162.41 in morning trading. Here's what to know about a possible merger between the companies. How big would a SpaceX-Tesla merger be? The merger would likely be valued at close to $5 trillion, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at investment firm Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News. SpaceX is currently valued at $1.98 trillion, while Tesla's market capitalization stands at about $1.5 trillion. But Tesla shareholders would likely demand a premium for their shares to agree to the merger, Ives noted."For the merger to get passed by shareholders, it would have to be a higher price for Tesla — likely in the $500/$550 per share range in our view," he said.That would make the combined company one of the most valuable in the world, rivaling that of the most highly valued businesses like chipmaker Nvidia, worth $5.2 trillion, or Apple, valued at $4.95 trillion.What is the strategic rationale for merging the companies?The main reason for combining SpaceX, a space exploration and AI company, with an electric vehicle manufacturer is to position them for a future in which artificial intelligence, or what Musk terms "super intelligence," becomes increasingly essential to everyday life."There's a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing super intelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation," Musk said in Tuesday's earnings call. While Tesla's primary business remains manufacturing EVs, Musk has signaled that the company is shifting away from traditional motor vehicles. In January, the Tesla CEO said the company would phase out production of its Model S and Model X vehicles.Instead, the company is changing course to focus on developing autonomous products, such as self-driving taxis and humanoid robots. Musk said Tesla will eventually produce 1 million humanoid robots a year as the company transitions to an "autonomous future." The humanoid robot, called Optimus, could hit the market in 2027, Musk said in January.AI is essential to Optimus, allowing it to follow orders and take on various tasks, as well as to Tesla's push into self-driving robotaxis.Meanwhile, SpaceX owns xAI, Musk's AI unit that created Grok, the chatbot that is used in the social media app X and other Musk-owned products. Musk's planned Terafab chip factory will tie all the businesses together by manufacturing semiconductors for both SpaceX and Tesla.Combining the businesses makes sense for a "number of strategic AI and data-driven reasons, and this is the right move for Musk," Ives said in a research note.What are the hurdles to a merger?On Tuesday's conference call, Musk underlined that a merger of SpaceX and Tesla is far from assured, noting that a majority of Tesla shareholders would need to vote in favor of the combination."I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it," he said. Musk added, "At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this, and particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50% vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that's quite a high hurdle to try to achieve."Even so, Ives assigns an 80% to 90% chance that the merger will happen by the end of 2027.

title: Weiser, Marx in race to succeed Polis as Colorado governor
description: Here's where the candidates for Colorado Governor stand on some of the issues
content: Republican Victor Marx and Democrat Phil Weiser are the major-party nominees on Nov. 3. Both promise to make Colorado more affordable.Colorado voters will choose a new governor on Nov. 3 to replace Democratic Gov. Jared Polis. Polis is term-limited after eight years. The race is led by Democratic Attorney General Phil Weiser and Republican newcomer Victor Marx. Four other candidates are also on the ballot.Weiser has been the state's top prosecutor since 2019. He previously served as the dean of the University of Colorado Law School, worked in the Obama administration, and clerked for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg. Weiser beat U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet in the Democratic primary in June. His running mate is Jefferson County Commissioner Lesley Dahlkemper. Republican Victor Marx served as a Marine. He founded the Colorado Springs-based ministry "All Things Possible Ministries." He entered the race as a political unknown with a social media following of nearly 3 million. He defeated two sitting legislators, state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer and Rep. Scott Bottoms, in the GOP primary. His running mate is retired Marine Col. George Markert.Housing is at the center of both campaigns. Weiser's plan sets a goal of 40,000 new homes statewide. He says teachers and firefighters should be able to live in the communities they serve. Marx would cut regulations and review what he calls "cost-inflating mandates," and he would push for more property tax relief for families and seniors according to videos on his policy website. The next governor inherits a structural budget deficit. Weiser wants to overhaul the Taxpayer's Bill of Rights so that it could let the state keep more revenue in surplus years. In the near term, he proposes audits and performance reviews. He also points to lowering prison recidivism, which he says is 45% in Colorado against a 37% national average.Marx says the state has a spending problem. He would use zero-based budgeting, phase down the state income tax and end state fees and enterprises that he says skirt TABOR. He would prioritize public safety, water infrastructure and education. Weiser says his legal background is an asset. The attorney general's office says he has filed or joined 82 lawsuits against the administration since January 2025.Marx says he is "not a MAGA person." He says he wants to build relationships with the White House.Weiser has been receptive to business complaints about overregulation. He has called Colorado's 2026 AI consumer-protection law a mistake. Healthcare is among the top concerns he says he hears from voters. He also wants to look for savings and efficiencies in Medicaid. And Weiser wants to bring new ideas and efficiencies into state government by appointing a Chief Innovation Officer to boost the economy.Marx wants to slash red tape on home building and roll back cost-inflating mandates. And Marx wants to expand apprenticeship programs and create industry-aligned workforce pipelines in construction, technology, energy, manufacturing, and the skilled trades.The unaffiliated candidate with the most money is Greg Lopez. He is a former Republican who briefly served in Congress in 2024 and was Parker's mayor. He left the GOP in January. Lopez proposes a state "Department of Government Efficiency," 25,000 starter homes in four years at prices as low as $235,000, and help for rural hospitals. Also on the ballot are Stephen T. Hamilton (American Constitution Party), Eric Mulder (Libertarian), Jeff Peckman (Unity Party) and Erik Underwood (Approval Voting Party). Election Day is Nov. 3.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar says Trump is trying to intimidate her before midterms: "We're not gonna be silenced"
description: Omar said the administration is trying to intimidate her and "so many people" before the midterm elections. The Justice Department says the search was part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.
content: Rep. Ilhan Omar says she is not backing down after federal agents searched her home, vowing in a new Instagram video to keep campaigning in the weeks before the midterm elections."We're not gonna be intimidated. We're not gonna be silenced. We're not gonna be scared," the Minnesota Democrat said. "I'll be out there campaigning alongside all of you."Omar said the goal is to win the midterms, "win the House, win the Senate, and hold this administration accountable."Omar said President Trump and his administration are "trying to intimidate me and so many people right before the midterm elections." She did not mention the search or the investigation by name.Omar also thanked supporters who sent $5, $10 or $20 and asked them to keep giving. She said it will be "a very expensive and challenging time."Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C., home early Oct. 12. The Justice Department said the agents carried out a search warrant as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. Sources told CBS News that day that the investigation centers on Omar's immigration paperwork, which dates to her childhood and was completed by her late father, and that investigators are examining potential false statements and immigration fraud.Omar's office said she has done nothing wrong. Omar earlier wrote on X that the search was an attempt to target political enemies and that "I will not be silenced." Mr. Trump, who has frequently targeted Omar, told reporters he had nothing to do with the search.Supporters rallied in Minneapolis hours after the search, and Omar began fundraising off it that day. Her district is heavily Democratic, and she is heavily favored to win reelection.

title: Bones discovered at Horsch "house of horrors" in Philadelphia were animal bones, sources say
description: Soil was excavated around the property as part of the investigation into Raymond "R.C." Horsch, a suspected serial killer​ who died in 2025.
content: Bones discovered at the "house of horrors" under investigation in Philadelphia's Olney neighborhood have been determined to be animal bones, law enforcement sources tell CBS News Philadelphia.Last week, personnel from the FBI and Philadelphia police excavated around the property as part of their investigation into Raymond "R.C." Horsch, a suspected serial killer who died last year. The home on the 400 block of Chew Avenue has been linked to at least seven missing women, five of whom are feared dead.Investigative work last week included demolishing a shed in the backyard and digging through soil. The bones were found in the backyard, sources say.Testing has now shown the bones were animal bones. Relatives and people closely following the case for more on the missing women will have to continue waiting.As of Monday, investigators were more than 50% finished with the excavation in the backyard, sources said. Once complete, they will move to the front yard. Also last week, investigators sprayed luminol, a chemical that glows when it comes into contact with signs of human blood. The chemical spray test showed human DNA in several locations around the home that will now need further testing.Previous work at the property included the removal of two clogged sewer laterals, pipes that connected the home to the main sewer line in the street.Investigators have also removed drums containing an oily, sludge-like material from the property and have investigated the home for signs of wet cremation, when a mix of chemicals are used to break down human remains.Raymond Horsch, who once described himself as an "empathetic serial killer," directed and performed in pornographic films and wrote several books that have since been pulled from online marketplaces. Horsch in one book described strangling a woman and disposing of her body with a chemical process.The home has been under investigation since this summer, when Horsch's son, Eugene, was arrested in Center City after a traffic stop. Authorities said he had guns, drugs, and false law enforcement credentials, and was traveling with a woman carrying the ID of Blair Tonzelli, who had been missing since 2023.The woman later told investigators about the home and said she was scared of its basement, that "bad things happened in that basement to other people," sources said.

title: Cook County Board weighs measure to close loopholes in protections for immigrants
description: Cook County Board weighs measure to close loopholes in protections for immigrants
content: The Cook County Board on Wednesday was considering a measure to strengthen sanctuary protections, and close a loophole that could let federal immigration agents indirectly obtain information about immigrants.The board was considering an amendment to prevent private contractors from selling or sharing people's personal information with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.Immigrant rights activists claim LexisNexis sold DMV data, jail and court data, and other records to immigration agents.Activists joined Cook County Commissioners Alma Anaya (7th) and Jessica VÃ¡squez (8th) to call for the passage of the amendment 15 years after the county passed a sanctuary ordinance that restricts the Cook County Sheriff's office from complying with ICE when it comes to turning inmates over to ICE.The commissioners and activists appeared at a news conference Wednesday along with Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle."We live in a state of constant surveillance, and that technology unfortunately is not regulated," Anaya said. "As county commissioners, it is our duty to protect our residents from becoming the ever-evolving targets that we have seen us to become."County leaders said they are also considering measures to regulate Flock cameras and other automated license plate readers.

title: Pennsylvania Lottery scratch-off ticket worth $4 million sold in Westmoreland County
description: The ticket was sold at Live! Casino Pittsburgh in Hempfield Township.
content: A winning $4 million scratch-off lottery ticket was recently sold at Live! Casino Pittsburgh in Westmoreland County.The Pennsylvania Lottery didn't specify when the ticket was sold, but said that the casino will earn a $10,000 bonus for selling the winner.The winner was from the Cash Money game, a $50 ticket, the lottery said. Nearly a dozen winning tickets worth at least $1 million have been sold so far this year in western Pennsylvania.The lottery said scratch-off tickets are distributed randomly, so neither the lottery nor retailers know where winning tickets will be sold until a prize is claimed.Winners are advised to immediately sign the back of their ticket and contact the Pennsylvania Lottery at 1-800-692-7481. Scratch-off prizes expire one year after the game's end-sale date posted on the lottery's website.Since ticket sales began in 1972, the lottery has contributed more than $38.2 billion to programs including transportation, care services, prescription assistance, senior centers and meals.

title: Grand Rapids man sentenced for drug trafficking through U.S. mail
description: A Grand Rapids man was sentenced for his involvement in interstate drug trafficking through the U.S. mail, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office of the Western District of Michigan.
content: A Grand Rapids man was sentenced for his involvement in interstate drug trafficking through the U.S. mail, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office of the Western District of Michigan.Cordairo Aqravian Lambert, 39, was sentenced by District Court Judge Robert J. Jonker to 20 years in federal prison for possessing cocaine with the intent to distribute, according to the district attorney's office.According to the district attorney's office, investigations starting in July 2024 showed that Lambert had mailed a parcel containing over a half kilogram of cocaine from Arizona to Grand Rapids, seen on surveillance video.Evidence presented at trial showed that Lambert frequently traveled to Arizona, often crossing the border into Mexico, in conjunction with the dates that other suspected drug parcels were sent, the district attorney's office says.In July 2025, Lambert attempted to retrieve a parcel containing nearly two-thirds of a kilogram of cocaine from a residence in southeast Grand Rapids before local police attempted to arrest him, and he fled on foot and hid in a residential neighborhood before surrendering to police, the U.S. Attorney's Office says. The U.S. Attorney's Office says that Lambert had previous felony drug trafficking and firearm convictions in both federal and state courts. "Lambert is a recidivist drug dealer who refused to take any responsibility for his crimes," said U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey. "The sentence he received should serve as a warning to career drug dealers and those importing drugs into our communities of the severe consequences for dealing drugs in West Michigan." "We appreciate the work of the GRPD Vice Unit, along with our law enforcement partners, to focus on disrupting the flow of drugs into our area," said Grand Rapids Police Chief Joe Trigg. "Not only for the pain caused by drug addiction to individuals and families, but to stop the violence the drug trade frequently brings to our neighborhoods and the larger community."

title: Injuries reported in multi-vehicle crash on Bishop Ford Freeway
description: Injuries reported in multi-vehicle crash on Bishop Ford Freeway
content: The northbound Bishop Ford Freeway was disrupted Wednesday morning after a crash at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Drive in Chicago's Roseland neighborhood.Illinois State Police said at 9:41 a.m., troopers responded to the freeway (I-94) at King Drive for a multi-vehicle crash with injuries.A semi-trailer truck and three cars were involved in the crash.State police did not specify the extent of the injuries involved.State police said all northbound lanes of the Bishop Ford were shut down after the crash, but traffic still got by on the right shoulder.All lanes were back open by just before 11 a.m.Further information was not provided.

title: George W. Bush's brother Neil Bush says he voted for James Talarico in Texas Senate race
description: "My vote was motivated by two things: deep concern about Ken Paxton's record and genuine admiration for the character and principles I see in James Talarico," Neil Bush posted on Facebook.
content: Neil Bush, the brother of former President George W. Bush and son of former President George H.W. Bush, said Tuesday that he voted for Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race while criticizing President Trump and "those who have enabled him" for causing "enormous damage to the Republican Party." "My vote was motivated by two things: deep concern about Ken Paxton's record and genuine admiration for the character and principles I see in James Talarico," Bush wrote in a Facebook post.Talarico is currently facing Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in one of the country's most closely contested Senate races. Early voting started Monday.The Bush name is nearly synonymous with the rise of the Republican Party in Texas. Democrats dominated Texas politics for much of the 20th century, and George W. Bush's defeat of Democratic Gov. Ann Richards in 1994 helped cement the GOP's takeover. Within a decade, Republicans swept every statewide office, redrew the U.S. House map to enhance their advantage and took the majority in both houses of the state Legislature. George P. Bush, the son of Jeb Bush and nephew of Neil and George W. Bush, unsuccessfully challenged Paxton in a primary for attorney general in 2022.In his post, Neil Bush wrote that he is "deeply troubled by Paxton's conduct as Texas Attorney General, particularly his decision to challenge the results of the 2020 presidential election in other states in an effort to help Donald Trump remain in power."Most members of the Bush family have generally avoided criticizing the sitting president since George W. Bush left office in 2009.Neil Bush noted that he has been a "Republican for most of my life, and I still believe deeply in many traditional Republican principles.""But character matters more than party affiliation," he wrote. "Our democracy depends on leaders who respect our institutions, tell the truth, accept accountability, and seek to unite rather than divide."One of the more controversial candidates on the ballot this cycle, Paxton was indicted on securities fraud charges in 2015, which were later settled as part of a diversion agreement. He was impeached in 2023 by the GOP-controlled Texas House on separate accusations of bribery and abuse of office. He was acquitted in the state Senate trial. Paxton toppled incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in a bitter GOP primary earlier this year after receiving Mr. Trump's endorsement. The president has continued to vigorously back Paxton throughout the general election, making several trips to Texas to campaign for him. Although Texas hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988, Democrats are hopeful their fortunes will change this year. Talarico has had a narrow lead in most polls, including a recent CBS News poll. CBS News' Battleground Tracker rates the race as a toss-up.Neil Bush said in his post that his "vote today was about much more than opposition to Ken Paxton.""I've never met James Talarico, but I have been enormously impressed by the way he approaches complicated and controversial issues," Bush wrote. "He speaks with respect, seeks common ground, and seems genuinely interested in bringing people together rather than driving them apart."Bush praised Talarico, who is a seminarian, for his faith, and added that he sees "in him the qualities I admire most in public servants: integrity, civility, humility, and a willingness to listen to those with whom he disagrees."

title: Teen with knife, 6 others arrested after fight at Santa Rosa school, police say
description: Seven teenagers, including one who was allegedly armed with a knife, were arrested following a fight on a Santa Rosa high school campus, police said.
content: Seven teenagers, including one who was allegedly armed with a knife, were arrested following a fight on a Santa Rosa high school campus, police said.Around 1:10 p.m., police were called to Montgomery High School following multiple reports of a physical altercation involving several students. Callers reported seeing a knife and police received unconfirmed reports of a possible firearm.Police arrived on scene within several minutes and the school was placed on lockdown. Using video, school staff and officers identified students who were allegedly involved.According to a preliminary investigation, the fight was likely gang related. During the incident, a 15-year-old male student brandished a knife and attempted to "aggressively advance" towards another student, police said, before a school employee placed themselves between the two students to stop the confrontation."The employee's brave actions prevented the armed student from advancing further toward the other student, potentially preventing additional injuries," police said in a statement.The armed student left campus before the first officers arrived. Officers later found the student hiding behind a home across the street from campus.A knife with a 4-inch fixed blade was recovered "in close proximity" to where the student was found, according to officers. Police said several students sustained minor injuries during the fight and were treated at the scene. One student who suffered injuries to his face and hand was taken to the hospital.Officers did not locate a firearm or find evidence that a firearm was used in the incident. School officials lifted the lockdown shortly after 1:55 p.m. A 14-year-old male, three 15-year-old males and three 16-year-old males were arrested on suspicion of battery on school grounds. The 15-year-old who is accused of having a knife is also accused of brandishing a weapon and possession of a weapon on school grounds.Montgomery High School has been marred by previous violence, including a March 2023 stabbing that killed a 16-year-old student. Following the stabbing, the school's principal and assistant principal were placed on leave.Earlier this year, Santa Rosa City Schools settled with two of the families involved for $6.25 million.

title: Surveillance video captures burglars at gas station in Chicago's Uptown community
description: Surveillance video captures burglars at gas station in Uptown
content: Surveillance video released Wednesday captured a crash-and-grab burglary at a BP gas station in Chicago's Uptown neighborhood the morning before.Chicago police said a blue Jeep crashed into the gas station minimart in the 5100 block of North Broadway, at Foster Avenue, around 3:30 a.m. Tuesday.Police said a witness reported seeing three people get out of another sport-utility vehicle at the scene and enter the gas station. The witness said the group took an ATM and drove off in a black sport-utility vehicle with the driver of the Jeep.Surveillance video shows the driver crashing the blue Jeep into the minimart, and then the three burglars taking the ATM and leaving in the second vehicle.Crash-and-grab burglars also targeted a jewelry store on Clark Street in Rogers Park on Tuesday morning, and a 7-Eleven on Halsted Street at Milwaukee and Grand avenues on Wednesday morning.Burglars also struck at least four businesses on 95th Street in the Beverly, Washington Heights, and Roseland communities early Wednesday.

title: Crash-and-grab burglars hit 7-Eleven in Chicago's River West district
description: Crash-and-grab burglars hit 7-Eleven in Chicago's River West district
content: A 7-Eleven in Chicago's River West community became the latest shop early Wednesday to fall victim to a crash-and-grab burglary.Video shows the entire front window knocked out at the 7-Eleven at 504 N. Halsted St., at the six-way intersection with Milwaukee and Grand avenues.Police said at 4:33 a.m., at least one burglar crashed a sport-utility vehicle into the store, went in, and stole an ATM.The burglar or burglars then got into another car and fled, leaving the crashed SUV on scene.No injuries were reported in the burglary.Belmont Area detectives were investigating.Early Tuesday morning, crash-and-grab burglars hit no fewer than two stores — a jewelry store on Clark Street in Rogers Park, and a BP gas station on Broadway in Uptown.Early on Wednesday morning, burglars also struck at least four businesses on 95th Street in the Beverly, Washington Heights, and Roseland communities.

title: After prison and clemency, Georgia football great Runt Moon earns Hall of Fame honor
description: Ronald "Runt" Moon once made his name carrying the football for Commerce High School. Now, nearly a decade after receiving clemency and leaving prison, he is being recognized for the career that first made him a hometown standout.
content: Ronald "Runt" Moon once made his name carrying the football for Commerce High School. Now, nearly a decade after receiving clemency and leaving prison, he is being recognized for the career that first made him a hometown standout.Moon, a star running back for the Tigers in the early 1970s, has been elected to the Georgia High School Football Hall of Fame. His former coach, Ray Lamb, delivered the news before his death last month."When Coach Lamb called me and told me, I said, 'What?'" Moon recalled. "I was overjoyed."Moon set Georgia's career rushing record before playing at Louisville. There, the former high school standout found himself waiting behind experienced players."I get to Louisville and they got two players just as good as I am, and they're juniors and seniors, and I'm just a freshman," he said.Moon described struggling with alcohol and drug abuse, followed by a prison sentence on federal drug charges. After serving nearly 12 years, he received clemency from President Barack Obama in 2016.Since returning home, Moon has married, remained sober and spoken to young people about his experiences.Last Friday, he returned to the field at Commerce, where he was presented with his No. 47 jersey."It was overwhelming, you know, for them to do that," Moon said. "I never thought that would ever happen like that."The Hall of Fame recognition brought another moment he had not expected."It was something great for me," Moon said.

title: Trump weighs moving White House press corps out of building
description: Outside allies of President Trump have recently pushed the idea of moving the White House press corps to another building, including former Trump strategist Steve Bannon, one source said.
content: President Trump has discussed the possibility of moving the White House press corps to another building, according to two people close to the president — a move that could escalate Mr. Trump's clashes with news organizations over coverage and access.Outside allies of the president have pushed the idea in recent weeks, including former Trump strategist Steve Bannon, one source told CBS News.No final decisions have been made, according to both sources.The discussions were first reported by The New York Times.White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement: "America is rightly distrustful of the fake news media because they fabricate stories based off lies and sources who are not even privy to any type of information. … All options remain on the table, and we will make an announcement when appropriate."Reporters have had dedicated workspaces in the White House building for more than a century. The current press briefing room was constructed during the Nixon administration, replacing a swimming pool that dated back to Franklin D. Roosevelt's presidency.But late last month, Mr. Trump posted a before-and-after image to Truth Social that suggested the briefing room could be turned back into a swimming pool.Ahead of Mr. Trump's first term, administration officials floated the idea of moving the press corps out of the building, framing it as a bid to broaden access by using a roomier part of the White House complex rather than the small, cramped spaces in the West Wing.
