James and a fellow All-Star in Brown started alongside holdovers Embiid, Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.There are some questions about how that All-Star starting four plus Edgecombe will coexist when all have been the primary ballhandlers on their respective teams in the past. Who gets the ball in crunch time? Who has to sacrifice the most? Who has the most to gain?Watching the answers unfold in real time will be fascinating for the Sixers and their fans.The chemistry looked strong throughout the night. James hit Brown cutting to the basket to earn the assist on the former Celtics star's first points with the Sixers. The Sixers closed the third quarter with an 11-0 run, capped by Brown's second straight 3-pointer that came at the buzzer and gave Philadelphia an 83-76 lead."We did that on the fly," James said. The offseason all the way through the countdown to the Sixers' home opener Thursday against Cleveland has been a swirl of excitement in Philadelphia. James jerseys are flying off the racks. Murals of him have popped up all over the city. He drew more than 10,000 fans to a public scrimmage and preseason games were sold out. There's a fascination with his helicopter rides from the Sixers' facility in New Jersey to New York.Even his younger teammates admitted to being a bit awestruck when they first met James.The Sixers entered the Garden almost unrecognizable from when they played there in early May in a second-round playoff series. They lost twice in New York and the Knicks finished the sweep in Philadelphia.The Sixers loaded up with talent and pushed the payroll so they could challenge the Knicks."It's certainly been fun these first few weeks," coach Nick Nurse said. "These guys have been really great."There's not much left for James to accomplish, except win that fifth ring.Philadelphia is waiting.

title: Philadelphia mother pleads for return of son's stolen dog: "He needs his friend back"
description: Diane Newman alleges someone stole her son's dog, Cody, from outside a convenience store in North Philadelphia on Sunday.
content: A mother is pleading for the safe return of her son's dog, who was stolen outside a convenience store in North Philadelphia last weekend."I would really, really, sincerely wish somebody would bring my son his dog back," Diane Newman said. "He needs his friend back."Newman is pleading for the return of her son's dog, Cody. She says her boyfriend took Cody to a convenience store Sunday, and while inside, someone stole him."Dogs are not allowed in the store," Newman said, "so he put Cody on the pole, tied him to the pole right next to the store. Purchased whatever he was purchasing. When he came out of the store, Cody was gone. I have been looking for Cody ever since." Newman says her son is 47 years old and has cerebral palsy. When he was 6 years old, he was hit by a truck and was in a coma for a while. She says now he is in a wheelchair. "He don't have no friends. He can't really walk," Newman said. "He can talk, but nobody understands him. Only the people who love him understand him. He has nobody. That is his friend. Please bring his friend back."Newman said she rescued Cody and surprised her son Jamel Newman for Christmas. Now, the two have an inseparable bond."He looked like he needed a home," Newman said, "and we looked like we needed him. We brought him home, and it took a while for him to get connected and attached. Took us a while too. We did. We fell in love. Cody has been our baby since."Newman said the dog meant everything to her family and was her son's best friend and companion. She said she exhausted all options looking for him.""He keeps asking me every time I go outside and come back in, 'Did you find my dog yet, Ma, did you find my dog?' And I'm trying. I did all. I did everything a person can do to find this dog," Newman said. "Can you please, please bring my dog back home, please?"Newman said she hopes whoever took Cody will do the right thing and bring him home."I understand sometimes when you do the wrong thing," Newman said. "None of us are perfect. I am not perfect. Nobody in the world is perfect, but my son needs his dog."

title: Illinois U.S. Senate candidates Juliana Stratton, Don Tracy face off in first and only debate
description: Both candidates are vying for the seat to replace Dick Durbin, who announced his retirement from the position last year after nearly 30 years in the Senate.
content: The first and only forum between Democrat Juliana Stratton and Republican Don Tracy for the U.S. Senate in Illinois was held Tuesday evening.Both candidates are vying for the seat to replace Dick Durbin, who announced his retirement from the position last year after nearly 30 years in the Senate.Illinois Lt. Gov. Stratton and Tracy weighed in on topics from Iran to clean energy to the differing needs of northern and southern Illinois.The candidates are coming from opposite sides, with Tracy self-funding his campaign, while Stratton is largely funded by the Pritzker family. Tracy is seen as the underdog by 13-17 points according to the latest poll.Pat Brady, former head of the Republican Party in Illinois and currently with Mercury Public Affairs, shares what he believes Tracy needs to do to flip the script."I think Don actually helped articulate the conservative viewpoint in most instances or what the Republicans have historically and traditionally stood for. So I think he did a nice job presenting that. It was a nice contrast to Lt. Gov. Stratton, who is a gifted debater. She's very talented. She's very fluent in the way she or fluid, the way she delivers her message, but there was a contrast there which was nice to see."The candidates spoke on the subject of affordability, a top issue in almost every race for the midterms.Stratton says she wants to pass Medicare for everyone."It's important that everyone who wants to see a doctor can see a doctor. One of the biggest examples of how things are unaffordable is health care. And we have people in Illinois right now choosing between going to the doctor and paying their rent. That's a false choice. We need to make it more affordable and accessible, and that's what I'll do when I get to the Senate," she said."Medicare for all is a proposal to take one of the best health care systems in the world, maybe even the best, ditch it in favor in place of government health care at a cost of estimated of $30-50 trillion," Tracy responded. Brady says the Medicare for all approach won't cut costs for anyone."She's mixing up costs with accessibility and the history of Democrats leading with sweeping changes in our health care system. In ' 94, it cost them 43 seats in the House, and in 2010, 63. It's a bad issue because Americans, I don't think, are quite ready for that. And Don, I think, was effective on pointing out how much it was going to cost."During the debate, Tracy alleged Stratton is a democratic socialist, even though she doesn't claim to be one, while she pointed out Tracy would welcome an endorsement from President Trump.For the farmers and the consumers of Illinois, Mr. Trump's tariffs were a focal point of the forum â with the candidates giving two very different answers on the topic. "I think the jury is still out on tariffs and there's a lot of different types of tariffs â there's blanket tariffs, there's reciprocal tariffs. It takes a while for the results of that to happen," Tracy said. "About half the manufacturers say tariffs are helping them reshore jobs and work back the United States. The others are saying they cost them more money. That's why I say the jury is still out on tariffs""The jury is not still out. The Supreme Court has ruled that these tariffs are illegal. That is not the jury still being out, and with these illegal tariffs, refunds are owed, but guess who is getting them? Is it you, the people of Illinois? No. They are going to big corporations like Amazon," Stratton said.Brady says defending tariffs placed Tracy in a difficult spot. "The Federal Reserve said just a couple of months ago, they've added substantially to inflation in this country. And I think that's just something the hard, difficult spot he was in. He's got to defend some of Trump's positions that are kind of indefensible."With two weeks to go and the balance of power on the line, Brady says Election Day could be a rough night for Republicans. "I think it's going to be a rough night for republicans. But you know what? There's a lot of chatter about whether or not these polls are completely accurate. So, I'm not quite sure yet."

title: Scott Singer and Jared Moskowitz spar over attack ads at Boca Raton forum in Florida's 25th District race
description: Republican Scott Singer called it a turnout race, and Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz did not speak with reporters after the hour-long forum.
content: Republican Scott Singer and Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz traded barbs over campaign ads at a forum in Boca Raton for Florida's 25th Congressional District race, where some voters said they came to make up their minds.B'nai Israel's congregation hosted the forum, which lasted about an hour. Singer and Moskowitz discussed Cuba, Iran and Israel, topics tied to communities in the newly drawn district, which stretches from Palm Beach County to Miami Beach.Some ballots were still blank heading into the forum."That's an empty ballot right now, and I know I have to fill it out. I was waiting to hear this," voter Rene said.Singer acknowledged the race is tight and urged Republicans to vote."But this is a turnout race. This district has a 5-point Republican advantage," Singer said. He said that when Republicans turn out, he will win.Voters said the volume of campaign ads has left them looking for clarity."There have been so many negative advertisements on both sides that I couldn't imagine all that was true," Rene said.The ads became a point of contention between the candidates."All the ads call me corrupt. They say corruption," Moskowitz said.Moskowitz is seeking a third term. He did not speak with reporters after the forum.Singer stood by his ads and his position on stock trading by members of Congress. He also called for limits on the president's own branch of government."I believe we need stronger penalties against congressional stock trading and I think we need them in the executive branch too," Singer said.Rene said the forum helped."I had to hear in person what they had to say and how they presented themselves," Rene said.Speaking with reporters, Singer challenged Moskowitz to a televised debate. The two have another forum scheduled next week.

title: Jolly, Clinton visit Hollywood church as Donalds brings bus tour to Westchester 2 weeks before midterm elections
description: Democrat David Jolly appeared with former President Bill Clinton in Hollywood, and Republican Byron Donalds drew a standing-room crowd in Westchester.
content: With Election Day two weeks away, the major candidates for Florida governor made campaign stops across South Florida on Tuesday and Wednesday.Democrat David Jolly and Republican Byron Donalds offered contrasting platforms as both campaigns courted regional voters.Jolly appeared in Hollywood with former President Bill Clinton at an interfaith event at the Koinonia Worship Center."The message of our campaign, myself and Gwen Graham is really the same in every single community: housing, healthcare, education, and no data centers," Jolly said during a campaign stop in Orlando.Affordability is a central concern for voters such as Alex Weaver, a maintenance worker at the worship center who helped prepare the building for the visit. Weaver said he is struggling to afford living in his hometown and that Jolly's message resonates with him.For others, the issues go beyond economics. Koinonia Deacon James Sparks pointed to representation and history."I'm going to be honest," Sparks said. "I'm a black man from a black community, and when you tell me my history is no good [and] for Ron DeSantis to support [Donalds], that lets me know if he's with Donalds, then he's not for me and my history."Donalds brought his 50-stop bus tour to La Carreta restaurant in Westchester on Bird Road, where he arrived to a standing-room, RSVP-only crowd inside and outside. He entered to John Cena's theme song, "The Time is Now."Donalds, who is endorsed by President Donald Trump and outgoing Gov. Ron DeSantis, spent much of Tuesday answering voter questions."I could talk about the Democrats, but why?" Donalds said. "Why? Because what we stand for is common sense. What we stand for is family values."Supporters echoed his focus on conservative policy and security."We have seen what happened in New York, LA, all these areas that are Democrats, and we don't want that to happen in Florida," said Martha Mesa, president and founder of Latinos GOP. She said Donalds' platform fits her core values.Another supporter, identified only as Johnny, said: "He is all positive and he's backed up by my president."Both campaigns plan to stay in South Florida this week, with Donalds visiting a restaurant in West Miami-Dade and Jolly meeting voters across Broward County.

title: Hay Fire breaks out in Solano County east of Vacaville
description: Firefighters in Solano County battled a vegetation fire that broke out east of Vacaville Tuesday afternoon.
content: Firefighters in Solano County battled a vegetation fire that broke out east of Vacaville Tuesday afternoon.The incident, dubbed the "Hay Fire," was first reported near Hay Road and Dally Road shortly after 12 p.m., according to Cal Fire. By 12:50 p.m., the fire grew to about 8-10 acres in size, prompting a fourth alarm.In an update posted shortly after 1:10 p.m., Cal Fire said they were assisting crews at the incident. A battalion chief, four engines, two dozers, two crews, one helicopter, two tankers and one air attack were sent.Cal Fire said crews stopped the forward progress of the fire shortly after 1:30 p.m. No injuries or structural damage has been reported.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

title: Man accused of burglarizing 2 Miami Beach restaurants arrested after backpack links cases, police say
description: Police say surveillance footage and a matching backpack tied the man to break-ins at 7TYONE Restaurant & Coffee Bar and Big Joe Smash Burgers.
content: A 57-year-old man accused of burglarizing two Miami Beach restaurants two weeks apart was arrested Sunday after investigators used surveillance footage and a matching backpack to link him to both break-ins, police said.Miami Beach police released body camera video Tuesday night that shows the arrest of Kevin Reilly on the beach.Investigators say Reilly broke into 7TYONE Restaurant & Coffee Bar on Normandy Drive in the early hours of Oct. 16 and took about $500."He just took like 26 seconds, just entered, went straight to take the money," said restaurant owner Liliana Arguinzones.Arguinzones shared surveillance footage with CBS News Miami, along with cellphone video that shows her shattered door and the rock police say Reilly used to get inside."I received a call from my neighbor," she said. "And he told me that my door was broken."Miami Beach police spokesperson Christopher Bess said officers connected the break-in to an Oct. 2 burglary at Big Joe Smash Burgers on Collins Avenue. He said officers saw similarities between the two incidents and identified Reilly from the earlier investigation. Investigators also matched the backpack seen in footage from both burglaries.At Big Joe Smash Burgers, police say the suspect forcibly removed a lockbox. Surveillance footage from the owner shows a man using tools to remove the cash register. Police said about $1,000 in cash was taken.Bess said officers found Reilly, who was experiencing homelessness, on the beach early Sunday morning. He said Reilly has an extensive criminal record.Arguinzones said the break-in has left her uneasy."Now I'm feeling unsafe all the time," she said.Reilly remained in custody Tuesday night at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. He was scheduled to appear before a judge Wednesday.

title: Woman recounts brutal attack by 3 men in Central Park: "'Give me everything,' and then he punched me"
description: A Bronx woman is speaking out following a frightening attack last weekend in Central Park while she was on her way home from work.
content: A Bronx woman is speaking out following a frightening attack last weekend in Central Park while she was on her way home from work.The victim told CBS News New York it happened in seconds. The NYPD is now looking for three suspects.What started as a routine bike ride home turned into a terrifying fight for survival for Katherine Marroquin on Sunday night. The attack near West 93rd Street and West Drive just before 10 p.m. left the 32-year-old bruised, shaken, and in pain.She said she was riding through the park when her AirPods fell to the ground. She said she stopped to pick them up and that's when she felt the punch."'Give me everything,' and then he punched me and he punched me again and I punched him back," Marroquin said.She says before she could process what was happening, two other men grabbed her and she was outnumbered."They grabbed my book bag, they opened it, and they took everything out," Marroquin said. "They took my Stanley cup and they threw it right in front of me. The first reaction was they're going to kill me, so I grabbed the cup and hit the first guy. So they felt I was defending myself and they run."She said what's even harder to understand is the complete disregard for human life."Imagine if they would have done something to me, kill me, for what? Less than $500? Are you kidding me?" Marroquin said.The NYPD has released video of the men suspected in the attack, and Marroquin said she would recognize them immediately.She said she shared her story in the hope of preventing someone else from becoming a victim."I was strong enough to defend myself, but what if it would have been another person? It wouldn't be the same situation," she said.Marroquin said she's determined not to let the attack keep her from living her life.Anyone with any information is asked to call the NYPD's Crime Stoppers hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477), or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782). You can also submit a tip via their website or via DM on Twitter, @NYPDTips. All calls are kept confidential.

title: Nor'easter offshore keeps Maryland crisp, cool and comfortable this week
description: Stunning fall weather continues for several more days.
content: Sunshine, crisp and comfortably cool temperatures will continue through the weekend. Wednesday begins with sunshine and temperatures in the low to mid-40s in many areas. Plan on a temperature closer to 50Â° along the bay front. Sunshine sends temperatures into the mid and upper 60s by the middle of the afternoon. Breezy winds will are expected between mid-morning and late afternoon as a Nor'easter spins well offshore. Offshore storm keeps Maryland weather bright, crisp, and comfyA storm system is set to slowly and erratically meander across the northwestern Atlantic through the middle of the workweek.Direct impacts from rain and wind remain well out to sea this week. High tides along with a gusty breeze will impact communities along the Atlantic Ocean beginning Tuesday, continuing through early Thursday. Beach erosion is expected Tuesday into Wednesday extending from Assateague Island northward along the Maryland and Delaware beaches through Thursday, as well. While it won't change any local impacts, there is a medium chance that this Nor'easter could develop some subtropical characteristics and get upgraded, named by the National Hurricane Center. The next name on the list is Josephine. Crisp, comfortably cool, breezy and dry weather rule the workweek forecast across the Baltimore area. It will be breezy during the afternoons and early evenings. The windiest weather will stay along the beaches, where gusts up to 40 MPH are possible. Some minor coastal flooding is possible along the bay around times of high tide on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. More significant tidal flooding is expected in Ocean City, which will be closer to the storm. Temperatures will remain seasonable, with afternoons in the mid to upper 60s. Temperatures will bottom-out in the 40s to lower 50s early each morning. Plan for plenty of sunshine. Even cooler weather next weekend in BaltimoreAs the storm offshore pulls away, a fresh batch of chilly air will settle into Maryland. Another widespread frost is possible on Saturday or Sunday morning along with sunny and cool afternoons. Fall color will continue to increase across Maryland. It will end up being a great weekend to get out and see some color across the Baltimore metro, central, northern and northeastern Maryland.

title: Mandatory paid parental leave policy passed by Allegheny County Council
description: Allegheny County Council voted on a mandatory paid parental leave policy on Tuesday.
content: Most businesses in Allegheny County will soon be required to provide paid parental leave after Allegheny County Council voted to approve the historic policy. The bill advanced after an 11-4 vote on Tuesday night, after hours of testimony from residents and business owners.The policy has been championed by unions who say paid leave will support workers and families, but some businesses say that while they support the intention behind the policy, Allegheny County will require employers to fund the benefit, which could be difficult. How long is paid parental leave? The policy requires 12 weeks of paid parental leave, which was down from the 18 weeks originally proposed by the Allegheny County Health Department. After months of public comment, the policy was revised to shorten the length of leave, among other changes.If the legislation becomes a law, Allegheny County would become the first county in Pennsylvania to require paid parental leave countywide.Who is eligible? Employers with 15 or more full-time or part-time employees, excluding temporary and seasonal workers, are mandated to give paid leave. The original proposal included employers of all sizes, but the Board of Health amended the policy to exempt small businesses. Full-time workers are eligible after six months, and part-time employees qualify after 625 hours. The original proposal had a 30-day period before employees became eligible. It would apply to the adoption, legal permanent placement and birth of children within the first 12 months of their life. It also includes language for parents who experience stillbirths. When would it go into effect? The policy provides a six-month implementation period after the bill becomes law, with an extra six-month grace period for businesses that can't implement the change until their next fiscal year or budget cycle begins.Councilmembers reactCouncilmember Susan Filiaggi, who voted against the bill, said she is not against paid parental leave. She just does not agree wth how this is being handled. "The proponents of this paid leave mandate, and most notably the county executive, have chosen a cynical and politically convenient path rather than introducing a universal publicly-funded program that would require an honest conversation about raising county revenue," Filiaggi said.Councilmember Bethany Hallam, who voted for the bill, defended the move."It would be great if the state would do anything, or the feds would step in and make policies nationwide," she said. "But we all know that's not something that happens. Our job is not to constantly defer to higher governmental bodies, but instead it is to do the extent of what we are able to do."What's next?The bill now heads to Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato's desk. Innamorato has been an outspoken proponent of the bill. "I want to thank County Council for taking a bold step tonight and putting the health of Allegheny County's families first," she said in a statement after the vote. "By passing the first county-level Paid Parental Leave policy in the country, we're showing that we're serious about protecting workers and their families at one of the most economically and medically vulnerable times in their lives."

title: Harford County Humane Society urges adoptions, fosters as shelter reaches capacity
description: The Harford County Humane Society is pleading for help after an influx of dogs in October left the shelter at full capacity, with all 67 kennels occupied.
content: The Harford County Humane Society is pleading for help after an influx of dogs in October left the shelter at full capacity, with all 67 kennels occupied.The shelter is now facing difficult decisions as it struggles to make room for more animals."Basically, we're trying to keep our heads above water," said Erin Long, with the Harford County Humane Society. "Because we'll adopt one out and then we'll get a call almost immediately that someone has a dog that they found and they need to bring it in, so as soon as we're getting a kennel empty, we're filling it right back up."Call for adoption or fostering helpSeven-year-old Pac is one of more than 60 dogs currently housed at the shelter, which says it cannot take in any more animals until space becomes available.Long said the humane society has taken in more than 60 dogs so far this month but has adopted out only about half that number.She believes the struggling economy may be contributing to the problem.The shelter is asking the public to consider adopting or fostering a dog to help ease the overcrowding.Euthanasia is a last resortThe situation has left dogs like 2-year-old Maizie, who has been at the shelter for eight weeks, at risk of euthanasia if conditions do not improve."Euthanasia is always the absolute last thing that we consider," Long said. "People get really outraged when they hear that, but when people aren't adopting or fostering or when rescues aren't coming forward and pulling the animals, what else are we going to do?"Long said it has been more than a decade since the shelter last faced a decision like this.She is urging people to delay surrendering their dogs if possible, adopt if they can, or consider fostering â even for just a weekend.The shelter offers a weekend foster program that allows people to take a dog home Friday night and return it Sunday night or Monday morning."We have a weekend foster program so people can pick up a dog on a Friday night and they can spend the weekend loving on the dog and give them a really great weekend and bring them back Sunday night or Monday morning and tell us all about the dog so it helps us get more information so we can find them the right home," Long said.Other ways to helpThe shelter is also accepting donations of food, blankets, toys, treats and money as its resources become increasingly strained."It really does make a big difference and it uplifts our staff too when people come in and want to help in that way," Long said.The Harford County Humane Society will host a vaccine event at the Aberdeen Fire Department on Saturday, Oct. 24, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

title: Knicks raise championship banner, then fall to LeBron James and 76ers
description: The 76ers sent an opening-night message they'll be a contender for the Knicks' NBA title after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, rallying for a 106-100 victory Tuesday.
content: The Philadelphia 76ers sent an opening-night message they'll be a contender for the New York Knicks' NBA title after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, rallying for a 106-100 victory Tuesday.Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points and Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first game since being acquired from Boston. James began his NBA-record 24th season by finishing with 14 points, nine rebounds and six assists.The 76ers got three 3-pointers from Anfernee Simons and two from fellow newcomer Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, as the reserves took advantage of the open looks they got when the Knicks were caught focusing too much on the bigger names.Jalen Brunson scored 21 points but the NBA Finals MVP shot just 6 for 19 from the field.Brunson told fans inside Madison Square Garden in a pregame ceremony when the Knicks raised their NBA championship banner and received their rings that: "The joy that this city had this summer, we would love to replicate that again."Maybe they can, but they will have to play a lot better than they did Tuesday in shooting 37% overall and 33.3% on 3s. Karl-Anthony Towns had 19 points and 12 rebounds.The Knicks dominated the 76ers in a second-round sweep, early on during their streak of 13 straight victories as part of a 16-3 finish with the highest point differential in NBA postseason history.Philadelphia then went out and traded for Brown and signed James after the NBA's career scoring leader decided to leave the Los Angeles Lakers, setting the 76ers up with the potential to be one of the best teams in the league.They certainly didn't have a smooth start but played better as the game went on. The Sixers closed the third quarter with an 11-0 run, capped by Brown's second straight 3-pointer that came at the buzzer and gave Philadelphia an 83-76 lead.Maxey's three-point play early in the fourth made it 87-78. The Knicks cut it to 96-95 when Towns made a 3-pointer, but Joel Embiid answered with one and the Sixers stayed ahead.Embiid finished with 13 points, 11 rebounds and six assists.Brunson, wearing gold sneakers for the occasion, couldn't help the Knicks recover by hitting the type of big shots he did when they repeatedly came back to beat San Antonio in five games for their first championship since 1973.The festive pregame party gave way to a first half filled with long stretches of fouls and missed shots, not leaving much reason for the cheers to continue. The Knicks went ahead by 10 with one good flurry but it was down to 58-54 at halftime.Up next76ers: Host Cleveland on Thursday night.Knicks: Visit Boston on Friday night.

title: Who is behind the transgender mailers flooding Texas mailboxes?
description: The mailer, which presents itself as a resource guide for LGBTQ+​ students, began appearing as early voting got underway for the 2026 midterm election​.
content: A flyer addressed to Texas students is showing up in mailboxes across the state. It claims to come from an organization called the Texas Transgender Student Union. But who is behind it remains a mystery.The mailer, which presents itself as a resource guide for LGBTQ+ students, began appearing as early voting got underway for the Nov. 3, 2026, midterm election. The pamphlet includes information on topics ranging from gender identity to what students can do if their parents do not support them.Images of the flyer have spread widely on social media. Some users have expressed outrage over its contents, while others have questioned who created it and why it is being mailed to students.Much of the information in the mailer appears to come from the Transgender Education Network of Texas, known as TENT.However, TENT says it had nothing to do with the mailing.TENT denies any involvement in the mailingIn a statement posted on its website, the organization said the flyer was not authored, approved or distributed by the group.That raises a key question: If TENT didn't send the mailer, who did?The return address listed on the flyer, 1611 W. Airport Blvd., Suite 123, Meadows Place, Texas, 77477, does not appear to correspond to a valid address. However, a nearly identical address, 11611 W. Airport Blvd., leads to a mailbox at a UPS Store in the Houston area.A Wyoming LLC and a questionable Texas return addressThe organization listed on the return address, the Texas Transgender Student Union, appears to have no website and no public social media presence.But business records reviewed by the CBS News Texas I-Team show a company registered under that name in Wyoming.According to state business filings, the Texas Transgender Student Union LLC was formed Sept. 2, 2026.The company's listed address leads to an office building in Sheridan, Wyoming, that serves as the address for a registered-agent service used by hundreds of thousands of businesses. Reporting by The Sheridan Press found that the same address is associated with nearly 300,000 of Wyoming's approximately 830,000 limited liability companies.Those records, however, do not identify who created the company or who may be responsible for the mailers.The flyers are arriving as transgender issues continue to play a prominent role in political messaging surrounding Texas' U.S. Senate race.Campaigns deny links to the mailerCBS News Texas contacted the campaigns of Ken Paxton and James Talarico. Both said they had no involvement with the mailer.Southern Methodist University political science professor Cal Jillson said the timing and subject matter suggest the mailing could be intended to draw attention to an issue already at the center of political debate."I can only imagine that it was sent out by conservative groups to fire up their conservative base," Jillson said.He said messages like these are often less about changing minds and more about shaping the issues voters discuss as they head to the polls."It's not going to change many people's minds, but it changes the agenda in the sense of what we're talking about," Jillson said.CBS News Texas reached out to the United States Postal Service on Tuesday about the flyer and has not heard back.

title: ICE agents conduct "special enforcement" in Canton Township, police say
description: The Canton Police Department says U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents were conducting "special enforcement" in the area, prompting a nearby elementary school to enact a shelter-in-place Tuesday morning.
content: The Canton Police Department says U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents were conducting "special enforcement" in the area, prompting a nearby elementary school to enact a shelter-in-place Tuesday morning.Police say the Plymouth-Canton Community School District enacted the shelter-in-place at Hulsing Elementary School at about 10 a.m. It lasted a little more than an hour and ended when law enforcement deemed the situation safe, according to police. Canton police say that neither the department nor the Plymouth-Canton Community Schools had knowledge of or involvement in the ICE enforcement."Upon receiving notification of the event, our police officers worked with the school to ensure students and staff were secured safely in their building," said Joseph Bialy, director of Police Services, in a statement. Details on the ICE enforcement have not been released.Michigan Congresswoman Debbie Dingell says the incident "understandably caused fear and concern throughout the community.""I have been in contact with ICE, which acknowledged that there were issues with today's enforcement activities. I will continue working with ICE, the township supervisor, and other relevant parties to address these concerns," Dingell said.

title: Stars snap Bruins' 5-game winning streak with 3-2 overtime win
description: The Dallas Stars beat Boston 3-2 on Tuesday night to snap the Bruins' five-game winning streak.
content: Mikko Rantanen scored in overtime to complete a hat trick, and the Dallas Stars beat Boston 3-2 on Tuesday night to snap the Bruins' five-game winning streak. It was the 11th career three-goal game for Rantanen and his first in the regular season since joining the Stars in a trade during the 2024-25 season. He became the fourth Stars player with an overtime hat trick since the team moved to Dallas for the 1993-94 season. Rantanen got his first goal early in the second period to tie the game at 1-all, and he tied it again in the third. His winner came on the power play at 3:52 of overtime when he did some nifty stick work in close and fired a shot past the left shoulder of Jeremy Swayman, who earlier in the extra period stopped Wyatt Johnston on two breakaway attempts 10 seconds apart and finished with 22 saves. Jake Oettinger stopped 18 shots for Dallas (5-3-1) in its third straight win.Matthew Poitras and James Hagens scored for the Bruins (7-2-1), who concluded their Western Conference trip at 3-0-1. Boston went 0 for 4 on the power play against Dallas, which came in allowing an NHL-best 1.5 goals per game and had the fourth-best penalty kill in the league. The Stars have allowed one power-play goal on opponents' last 25 chances. Roope Hintz had a shot from in close deflect off the leg of Boston's Charlie McAvoy, and the loose puck ricocheted directly to Rantanen, who poked it past Swayman with 6:22 left in regulation to tie it at 2-all. Up next Bruins: Host Nashville on Thursday. Stars: Host Winnipeg on Thursday.

title: Gov. Wes Moore says second term is about getting the job done for Marylanders
description: The governor is coming in as the incumbent in the 2026 gubernatorial election, facing off against Republican challenger Dan Cox​.
content: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says that getting a second term is about taking care of unfinished business.The governor is coming in as the incumbent in the 2026 gubernatorial election, facing off against Republican challenger Dan Cox.Moore defeated Cox in the 2022 election to become Maryland's 63rd governor and first Black governor. He wants to bolster the work he put into his first term.In an interview with CBS News Baltimore, the governor talked about what a second term would look like.Moore also reaffirmed his commitment to the state, "I wouldn't be running for reelection if I wasn't exclusively focused on the people of Maryland."AffordabilityA big focus for Moore in his reelection campaign is making the state affordable for Marylanders.He especially wants to crack down on energy bills. His solution is to set Maryland up to produce more of its own energy.To do that, Moore wants to streamline the permitting processes for this infrastructure, whether it be for solar, wind or nuclear energy."Right now we still import more energy than we export as a state. We got to be able to reverse that trend because that will also help bring energy prices down."Controlling state spending and jumpstarting the economyThe governor wants to continue to bring more businesses and investments to Maryland to diversify the state's economy.He points to the recent announcement that Anduril Industries is investing $3.7 billion in a new high-tech shipyard in Baltimore County's Tradepoint Atlantic industrial center.It's expected to create 3,100 new jobs.Moore said his first term focused on bringing in industries of the future, and that work will continue should he win four more years."We were working for a year on this deal," he said. "That comes on the heels of things like AstraZeneca [expanding its manufacturing in the state], that comes on the heels of Samsung Biologics picking Maryland for its first U.S. manufacturing facility."Jumpstarting the economy, as the governor puts it, has been necessary given the structural issues with the state's budget, which has a projected gap of roughly $3 billion next fiscal year.Moore will continue to cut spending."I do not want to hand off to my successor what I was handed, which was a multi-billion dollar structural deficit," he said. "We've got to get this spending under control and we've got to grow the economy. That's how we're going to address this."Keeping Maryland in the spotlightMoore said he wants to continue to wean off of the state's reliance on Washington.Aside from finding different revenue streams, it also means continuing to be outspoken against President Trump.Trump is the primary reason Moore has been pushing for mid-cycle redistricting, which has resulted in Ballot Question 3 on the November ballot.For him, the question isn't just about protecting the country's democracy -- it's about keeping Maryland in the national conversation."There will be a post-Trump moment and we all have got to make sure we are preserving our democracy," Moore said. "I'm committed to making sure that Maryland does not sit out of that conversation."

title: Man says teens riding e-bikes assaulted him and other walkers on Methuen, Massachusetts rail trail
description: Police are looking to identify a group of e-bike riders after a man says he and other walkers were assaulted on a Methuen, Massachusetts, rail trail.
content: Police are looking to identify a group of teenagers riding e-bikes after a man says he and other walkers were assaulted on a Methuen, Massachusetts, rail trail last Friday.The incident happened on Oct. 16 at about 5:35 p.m. near the Nevins Farm MSPCA animal shelter. Surveillance images posted by police show seven boys, believed to be between 15 and 17 years old, on e-bikes.Greg Curtis spoke out at a Methuen City Council meeting Monday night. The self-described senior citizen said he was taking a "pleasant walk on the rail trail" when suddenly he felt a painful blow to the back."I was being assaulted, blindsided, punched," he said. "They all had their hoods up. One of them turned around and smiled, the one in the red hoodie, at what he had done."Curtis told WBZ the attack was completely unprovoked. "This teenager with a red hoodie punched me in the back and the power of his e-bike moving at 30 miles per hour is what really delivered a painful blow to my kidney," Curtis said. Curtis said he talked to three other women on the path who said they were also assaulted and that the teens were swearing at them. Another woman also said she was almost knocked over and was afraid she'd be hurt, Curtis said."They were just terrorizing people on the trail," Curtis said. Curtis said he's fine, but thinks something needs to be done about teenagers recklessly riding e-bikes. The Medford School Committee has considered banning e-bikes on school campuses because of a rise in accidents over the past several months.Instead of seeking punishment, Curtis told WBZ he wants the teens to turn themselves in so they can walk the trail together and talk it out. "If you come forward, I will not press charges, but there's a catch," Curtis said. "Thirty days, 30 days of walking the rail trail with me, and maybe I can hear you out, get to know you a little bit, and you can get to know me as a person not as a target."Methuen Police Chief Jamie Moore said the teens' behavior is unacceptable. "This should never have happened," Moore said. "This gentleman was out taking a walk minding his own business and something like this happens. We don't appreciate that and I think it was uncalled for."Police say it's believed the teenagers were coming from Lawrence and heading north toward Salem, New Hampshire. Anyone with information is asked to contact police.

title: Baltimore County Council votes to raise its members' salaries by 74%
description: The Baltimore County Council has voted to raise the salaries of its members by a 74% margin beginning next year.
content: The Baltimore County Council has voted to raise the salaries of its members by a 74% margin beginning next year. Council members' pay will increase from $69,000 to $119,000 per year starting with the next term, a spokeswoman for Baltimore County confirmed to CBS News Baltimore. The council chair's salary will increase from $77,000 to $129,750.The county executive's salary will be increased by about 20% to $240,000 a year. The spokesperson noted, however, that the salary change only applies to the next term and does not affect the pay of the county's current executive, Kathy Klausmeier. The pay raises were approved during a council meeting on Monday night. Only two councilmembers -- David Marks and Nino Mangione -- voted against the raises. "This is a job that requires a lot of hours and requires difficult decisions, but the taxpayers of Baltimore County, I just feel like they were let down, and we should be putting their needs ahead of a 74% pay raise for politicians, and that's why I voted no," Mangione said. The increases come after voters approved an expansion of the Baltimore County Council from seven members to nine. The salary change indicates that council members and the chair would be paid as full-time employees, our media partner, the Baltimore Banner, reported last month. The increases do not bar council members from taking outside work. But the idea presented to voters was that it would not be necessary for members to have outside jobs because the new salary rate is more in line with the cost of living.In March, the Baltimore County Council passed, but then rescinded, earlier legislation that tied the hikes in salaries to members' pensions, the Banner reported. That law would have allowed current council members to receive far larger pension increases than those available to county employees. The council rolled back the proposed legislation after a public outcry.Councilman Julian Jones, who is running to be the next county executive, said during Monday's meeting that he has only received one raise on council since 2014, and the pay has not kept pace with other employees in the county government."I received one raise of a couple of thousand dollars in 12 years and that raise has not kept pace with the employees that work here," Jones said. Patrick Dyer, who is running against Jones, says that money should be going to support the first responders and not county council."We need to take care of those who take care of us first," Dyer said. "We need to fix our roads first. It's all about priorities. Well, our priorities with this particular decision were out of line and I don't agree with it."Some Baltimore County residents told CBS News Baltimore they are disappointed that councilmembers voted on a large pay increase for themselves."For most people, a raise of that magnitude is not possible or even conceivable, so it's a little disappointing that they would vote themselves an increase that large," Baltimore County resident Neil Pohlhaus said.Councilmembers who voted in favor of the raise say it will allow them to focus more time and energy to an already demanding job.

title: Rancho Cordova soccer arena proposal advances as residents debate cost to taxpayers
description: Plans for a new 7,500-seat soccer and entertainment arena in Rancho Cordova are moving closer to a decision, but residents remain divided over the project's potential economic benefits and the financial assistance it would require from the city.
content: Plans for a new 7,500-seat soccer and entertainment arena in Rancho Cordova are moving closer to a decision, but residents remain divided over the project's potential economic benefits and the financial assistance it would require from the city.The city held its final public workshop Tuesday night, giving developers and officials an opportunity to answer questions and hear concerns ahead of upcoming City Council discussions.The proposed arena would be part of a larger development known as Downtown DOVA, which developers say would create a new destination for sports, entertainment and community events.But some residents questioned whether the project would ultimately cost taxpayers too much."I think taxpayers are going to be on the hook quite a bit," Rancho Cordova resident Marilyn Metzger said.Developer Joshua Wood said the project would not require a tax increase and would provide new amenities for the growing city."It doesn't put taxpayers at risk. There's no tax increase, and what do we get instead? We get a downtown city center for the entire city," Wood said.The proposed arena would accommodate a professional indoor soccer team and other events. The broader development would also include restaurants, housing, a hotel and a casino on currently vacant, city-owned land.Wood said the project could help address the lack of evening entertainment options in Rancho Cordova."There's not a lot of places at night or things to do and we want to be a community that's fun," he said.However, the proposal would require financial assistance from the city that could total up to $185 million. The proposed assistance includes waiving development and impact fees and sharing sales tax revenue generated by the project."The applicant actually has to stand up a successful project in order for these revenues to be generated," Rancho Cordova Communications Director Maria Chacon Kniestedt said.Some residents remain concerned about the potential loss of revenue and the use of public funds to support the development."We're going to be losing millions of dollars the moment they build it," resident James Garcia said.Garcia also questioned why the city should cover costs that developers would typically be expected to pay."The reality is we're going to be paying for it, it's coming out of our general fund to pay for impact fees that a developer would normally pay," Garcia said.Traffic was another concern raised during the workshop, with residents questioning how the city would handle crowds attending arena events."A very successful arena is going to have some traffic, but the point is to make sure the people who are coming to the arena are safe," she said.Other Rancho Cordova residents are looking forward to having a new place to hold civic events and see sporting matches in their own community."It will bring more entertainment, families will come out, I'm going to come enjoy it," Rancho Cordova resident Daphanee Williams said.Rancho Cordova will be holding a special city council meeting next Monday to discuss the project, and a final decision could be made at the Nov. 2 council meeting.

title: St. Charles North High School girls flag football team ends championship winning season undefeated
description: The St. Charles North High School team capped off an undefeated 26-0 season with a 32-13 victory over Prospect.
content: A celebration was held in St. Charles, Illinois, on Tuesday night to honor the inaugural girls' state flag football champions, the North Stars.The St. Charles North High School team capped off an undefeated 26-0 season with a 32-13 victory over the Prospect Knights.A ceremony was held in the main gym of the school, featuring the championship trophy presentation."It's amazing. It's a special moment for us. We have a special community here to support us all. It's just wonderful," said player Laila Bibbings."Fans have been great this season. We've had a lot of support, especially only in our second season as an IHSA team, but it was just crazy, like a crazy thing to be a part of and it was just amazing," said Kayleigh Assell.Throughout the North Stars' seven-game play-off run, they outscored their opponents by a whopping 251 to 76.

title: What do North Texans care about ahead of the November midterm elections?
description: With early voting for the November midterm elections underway, candidates are making their final push to reach voters.
content: With early voting for the November midterm elections underway, candidates are making their final push to reach voters. For months, CBS News Texas has been following polls and hearing directly from politicians about their platforms. But polls and stump speeches only tell part of the story. Those things don't quite give the sense of who Texans are or why they care about the things they care about. For that, Ken Molestina and a CBS News Texas crew hit the road to hear directly from voters across the metroplex. For the next couple of weeks, until Election Day, we'll be hearing their stories. What do North Texans care about?Over the past several weeks, we've spoken to Texans across the Dallas-Fort Worth area and beyond about what they're concerned about ahead of Election Day. Here's a sampling of what we heard: "Gas prices, for one. A war that we don't know anything about.""Unity.""Cash, money, wages, jobs, the price of groceries.""Family, God, country.""Water rights.""Health care is number one.""No more fighting. No more blame."

title: How often do medical misdiagnoses occur? Here's the data
description: Actress Christina Applegate says doctors misdiagnosed her years ago​. How often do errors like that happen, and how can they be prevented?
content: An outspoken advocate for patients with multiple sclerosis just revealed she didn't have the chronic condition after all.Actress Christina Applegate says doctors misdiagnosed her years ago. How often do errors like that happen, and how can they be prevented? There have been several studies into this problem with sobering findings.One of the more recent ones came from the medical journal BMJ Quality and Safety.It found 1 in every 14 hospital patients who are there for a general medicine reason receive a harmful diagnostic error.Some people, however, might go to urgent care or a specialist to diagnose their sickness or condition. BMJ did a study on these cases as well, and released its findings back in 2014.It found 12 million adults who seek outpatient care get a medical misdiagnosis each year. At the time, that was about 1 in 20 adultsIt's also estimated that nearly 800,000 Americans per year die or become permanently disabled as a result of a misdiagnosis.The physical impact is clear, but there's also an emotional toll. In her podcast, Applegate describes feeling lost after being told she doesn't have multiple sclerosis."This may come as great news but to me, it comes as very, like I'm back at square one," she said.There are several reasons why a medical misdiagnosis happens. It could be a doctor misinterpreting test results, or problems when ordering diagnostic tests.On the other side, patients might not provide an accurate medical history or description of their symptoms.So, how can this be prevented?For patients, doctors say to explain your medical history in a clear, chronological way, including family history. They encourage people to detail every symptom, even if they seem minor or unrelated.And follow up on your test results rather than assuming no news is good news.The conditions with the highest likelihood of a misdiagnosis include cancers and vascular events like a heart attack and infections.

title: American Airlines plane lands at Chicago O'Hare International Airport with blown tire
description: An American Airlines plane blew a tire when landing at Chicago O'Hare Airport on Tuesday afternoon.
content: An American Airlines plane blew a tire when landing at Chicago O'Hare Airport on Tuesday afternoon. The Federal Aviation Administration said the plane was American Airlines Flight 41 from Barcelona to Chicago.The FAA said around 2:30 p.m., the crew reported a brake issue and then, after landing, a blown tire. Pilots suspect the brakes locked up, causing two tires to blow.A passenger who was on board the flight told CBS News Chicago that he immediately knew something was wrong."We knew something was wrong because it was like nothing I've ever heard before on a landing. It was a nice big boom," said WoodJohn Abbate.He said the captain explained to the 245 passengers that they had blown some tires. He added that people weren't panicking, but were shocked about what happened."There was no screaming or panicking, but everybody, I mean, they were kind of in shock. You could see that everybody's looking at each other, not knowing how to react to this."Passengers were able to deplane via the stairs and were bused to the terminal, the FAA said. The Chicago Fire Department said one person was taken to a local hospital to be checked out, but was in good condition. Sources said that person was not injured as a result of the landing, but became ill during the flight, and asked to go to the hospital after getting off the plane."But in the end, it turned out well, nobody got hurt and, you know, just, glad to make it across the ocean, so, you know," Abbate said.American Airlines released a statement saying the flight "experienced a tire issue.""Per procedure, first responders met the aircraft out of an abundance of caution and customers were transported safely to the terminal by bus. The aircraft has been taken out of service to be inspected by our maintenance team. We thank our team members for their professionalism and we apologize to our customers for their experience," the statement continued. The FAA said it will investigate the incident, but had no further information. The incident comes after at least four planes sustained blown tires while taxiing or landing at O'Hare in a two-week span in August.

title: Man arrested in Chicago after alleged cross-country killings of coworker, parents
description: Michael Anthony O'Neal Flemming, 33, of Seattle, was taken into custody in Chicago following a week-long search.
content: A man accused of fatally shooting a coworker in Seattle and his parents in Wisconsin was arrested in Chicago this week, the Kenosha Police Department announced on Tuesday.Michael Anthony O'Neal Flemming, 33, of Seattle, was taken into custody following a week-long search.Authorities said that O'Neal Flemming allegedly shot and killed his former co-worker at the 76 gas station on Broad Street in Seattle around 5 a.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Security video captured him walking between the gas station and a nearby 7-Eleven store on Denny Way for half an hour before entering the gas station and shooting the victim.He then traveled to Wisconsin, where he shot and killed his mother, Rena O'Neal, 59, and her husband, Rodney Brushwood, 57. Both were found fatally shot during a welfare check on Monday at their residence in the 5500 block of Washington Road. O'Neal Flemming was identified as a person of interest in the killings.Authorities said text messages between family members indicated that he was in Chicago, leading to his arrest.O'Neal Flemming was charged with first-degree murder with a firearm on Tuesday in King County Superior Court in Seattle after prosecutors conducted an independent review.Court documents read that O'Neal Flemming was recently acting erratically and was believed to have been experiencing a mental health crisis. Documents also said that he had no known criminal convictions.His bail is set at $5 million, and his arraignment is scheduled for Nov. 2. Kenosha police said detectives will work with the Kenosha County District Attorney's Office to initiate extradition proceedings and pursue charges in Wisconsin.

title: Westonka schools develop AI policymaking group to prepare for evolving technology
description: Artificial intelligence in the classroom is a hot topic, and one Minnesota school district is aiming to get on top of the tech with a new policymaking group.
content: Artificial intelligence in the classroom is a hot topic, and one Minnesota school district is aiming to get on top of the tech with a new policymaking group.Right now, it's a process of elimination keeping kids from cheating, but Westonka Public Schools' new AI cabinet is made to vet new advancements in this rapidly evolving technology before they enter the classroom."We really had to think quickly how are we going to manage this thing called AI" said Mark Femrite.Femrite oversees more than 2,400 students as Westonka's assistant superintendent of teaching and learning. Westonka Public Schools ISD 277 sits on the northwest end of Lake Minnetonka."You know nothing surprises me" said Femrite, who's worked for the district since 1990. He calls artificial intelligence a "disrupter.""My definition of a disrupter is it can be positive or negative and we're gonna take the positive route with this" said Femrite. He says in June 2025, the district held a one-day training for staff on AI, discussing guidelines and a new manual on the topic. He thought that'd be enough, but now says, "every building in our district is working on AI. They each have a committee."Each committee reports to a cabinet with six strategically-picked staff members from across the district."We wrap around them to support them" he added. He says the cabinet thinks outside the box and guides the district's implementation as a whole."We vet AI tools before they ever reach the classroom," he said, which he's proud of.The current policy at Westonka Schools says students can't use AI at all. When it comes to teachers, they're allowed to, but can only use Gemini."I'm not sure what's going to happen in January, but we're ready" Femrite told WCCO. He says he realizes the technology is not going anywhere."We have to understand how AI impacts instruction, and we need to learn how to change our instruction" said Femrite. "We'll adapt as things change and we'll end up on top."Femrite says they're aware students could then use the tech on personal devices. Part of the guidance in place is to teach teachers on how to detect it and more.Westonka Public School includes:Westonka High SchoolWestonka Middle SchoolShirley Hills Primary SchoolHilltop Primary SchoolWestonka Early LearningThe Minnesota Department of Education has more information about artificial intelligence in education online.

title: Oswego man accused of possessing images of underage girls changing at Yorkville banquet hall
description: The images depicted underage females in a designated changing area during multiple events hosted by the business in 2023, police said.
content: A man is facing felony charges after police said they found images of underage girls changing on his cell phone, believed to have been copied from surveillance video at a banquet hall in Yorkville.Eleno Silva, 57, from Oswego, Illinois, was charged with six counts of child pornography and three counts of child sexual abuse material.Police said on Monday, June 15, 2026, the department's investigations division was contacted by the Montgomery Police Department, which had recovered images from Silva's cell phone during an unrelated investigation. The images found in the phone depicted underage girls in various stages of undress and appeared to have been captured while the individuals were at the Martini Banquet Hall at 171 block of Saravanos Dr. in Yorkville.Further investigation by Yorkville Police revealed evidence of multiple images on Silva's device that investigators believe were copied from surveillance video recorded inside the business. The images depicted underage girls in a designated changing area during multiple events hosted by the business in 2023, police said. Police said Silva turned himself in to the Kendall County Jail after investigators obtained an arrest warrant for him on Monday, Oct. 19.Yorkville police are seeking assistance from anyone who attended or hosted an event at Martini Banquet Hall during 2023. Individuals with relevant information are encouraged to contact the Yorkville Police Department at ypdtipline@yorkville.il.us or 630-553-8590.

title: Woman alleges rape at University of Chicago fraternity party in lawsuit naming Alpha Delta Phi
description: A woman has filed a lawsuit against Alpha Delta Phi at the University of Chicago, alleging she was raped at a fraternity party in February and that years of sexual assault reports have been covered up.
author_name: Sara  Tenenbaum, Jermont  Terry, Sabrina  Franza
content: A woman has filed a lawsuit against Alpha Delta Phi at the University of Chicago, alleging she was raped at a fraternity party in February and that the fraternity and the university were aware of years of sexual assault reports.The law firm Gould, Grieco & Hensley announced the lawsuit, which was filed in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Tuesday morning. The university is named as a respondent in the lawsuit. According to the complaint, the victim, identified only as Jane Doe, attended a party at the Alpha Delta Phi house in the 5700 block of South University Avenue on Feb. 7, 2026. According to the complaint, at the party Doe was given a shot of unidentified alcohol by one of the fraternity members, which the complaint identifies as student Kevin Shim, and encouraged to drink it. The lawsuit says "almost immediately" after she drank the alcohol, she began to feel "unsteady and lightheaded."At that point, according to the complaint, Shim coerced her upstairs to a bedroom, led her to a bed and sexually assaulted her. The complaint states Doe told him multiple times that she felt unsteady and lightheaded, but he ignored her. The complaint also says that while in the room, Doe "lost all physical and verbal ability to refuse" the frat member.The complaint states Doe was raped while unable to consent or to verbally or physically refuse Shim, but she did plead with him to wear a condom. According to the complaint, he refused.After the assault, Jane Doe alleges Shim left her in the room, and another frat brother blocked her friends from going upstairs to find her. The lawsuit alleges her friends were not allowed to go upstairs until her assailant told his frat brother that it was OK.Doe alleges she was still unconscious when her friends found her, and she struggled to speak and walk as they helped her out of the house. She reported the assault to Chicago police the next morning when she discovered bloodstains in her underwear, according to the lawsuit.Chicago police confirmed they received that report, and said Doe took herself to Illinois Masonic Hospital for treatment. They also confirmed the investigation is ongoing. We are waiting to hear more about their investigation. Attorneys for Doe told CBS News Chicago they hope the civil suit will help bring about criminal charges in the assault. The lawsuit also alleges that in the days after the rape, University of Chicago Police reached out to Doe about the incident and created an incident report, but that UCPD has refused to provide her with a copy of any report or records related to her case without a subpoena.According to the complaint, this chapter of Alpha Delta Phi has been investigated by police multiple times since 2009 for reports of sexual assaults, and alleges both the frat and the university were "aware of the danger of sexual assault by fraternity members on its on-campus fraternity housing."Two sexual assaults were reported five days apart in January 2009, and CPD and University of Chicago Police also investigated a reported assault connected to the frat's weekly "Bar Night" gathering, in which the victim had to be taken by ambulance to the emergency room, according to the lawsuit. The complaint does not specify what kind of medical treatment was needed.In September 2022, an anonymous post on the Instagram account @shareyourstoryuchicago described another sex assault at the Alpha Delta Phi house and asked for the frat to be put on probation, according to the complaint.In these cases, the complaint alleges high-ranking officials with the fraternity put out statements that they were cooperating with police on investigations into the incidents, but reports continued. The lawsuit says between 2009 and 2026, the fraternity received more reports of sexual misconduct involving their members and social events, including through their own internal reporting processes.Despite that, the lawsuit says the national Alpha Delta Phi organization did not impose any disciplinary actions against the University of Chicago chapters, did not restrict or place conditions on their social events, did not require the living quarters of the frat house be secured during social events, and did not require sober monitors be placed on the residential floors during parties.Alpha Delta Phi's Chicago chapter is not currently listed as being on probation or under disciplinary status. ADPhi said in a statement that they are aware of the allegations and "take them extremely seriously." They said they have suspended the member involved. "The conduct described is deeply troubling and inconsistent with our values," the statement says. "We are committed to the safety and wellbeing of our members and communities and will cooperate with law enforcement as appropriate."Because of the ongoing litigation, the fraternity said they could comment further on specifics. Tuesday afternoon, the university responded in a statement, writing, "These allegations are very disturbing to the University community. The University of Chicago is committed to addressing and preventing incidents of sexual assault.""The University will cooperate by providing information and is prepared to help the Chicago Police Department in its investigation. The University will take appropriate further steps as new information emerges," the statement continues.While there are more than 20 fraternities and sororities at the University of Chicago, the university does not officially recognize, affiliate with, or regulate any of them.Chicago police are currently investigating another report of a sexual assault at the Alpha Epsilon Pi frat house on the same block of University Avenue earlier in October. The two incidents are not connected. The investigation into the AEPi assault is ongoing, but a person of interest has been identified, according to Chicago police.

title: St. Paul loses English language learning students, eyes teacher cuts in wake of Operation Metro Surge
description: The St. Paul Federation of Educators says up to 18 English learner teachers could be cut midyear, affecting at least two dozen schools. The school board is set to discuss the proposal Tuesday.
content: St. Paul Public Schools is proposing to eliminate educators midyear, and the teachers' union says the cuts would fall on English learner teachers and were planned in secret.Union President Carrie Kyung said the plan includes cutting up to 18 English learner teachers and would affect at least two dozen schools. Kyung said the school board is trying to rush the plan through and should reject it and reconsider its options for balancing the budget.Superintendent Stacie Stanley outlined the proposal in a letter to families. She wrote that many students who are no longer enrolled in the district's schools are English learners, citing the effects of Operation Metro Surge, the federal immigration enforcement operation in the Twin Cities, and an overall decline in district families. Stanley said district funding is based largely on enrollment and she refuted the accusation that the cuts were planned behind closed doors."I wish the circumstances were different, and that we were not in this situation that none of us asked to be in," Stanley wrote.Her letter also says the district is committed to keeping the financial reserves required by board policy. The district would not comment beyond the letter.Kyung questioned the district's enrollment figures, asking where the more than 500 students the district says are missing have gone and what it is doing to reach families and help them enroll.Educators, union members and families rallied outside of district headquarters ahead of the meeting. "They need the support in language and they wouldn't be getting that," said Kristine Ranweiler, an English language teacher, told WCCO ahead of the meeting. "Support out students, support our families. When we don't support them they leave to go to other districts and other schools and we love our students and we want them to stay in St. Paul."Families and teachers disrupted the school board meeting Tuesday night, chanting "let them speak" when public comment ended after 45 minutes. Two people took a megaphone and spoke to the crowded room, opposing the cuts before the board eventually voted to allow more people to share their thoughts. "This plan will decimate our EL program and our ability to provide quality service to our students," one woman told the board. Based on numbers from last January, the district projected 8,787 English learning students would enroll in St. Paul schools, but as of Oct. 1 the actual enrollment is 8,245 — a drop of 542 students.The district blames the drop in English learning students on Operation Metro Surge. The superintendent acknowledged the complex situation, saying it brings "no easy answer.""I certainly could not have imagined having to sit here tonight in a situation that was not created by my board that was not created by my senior executive leadership team and was not created by me," Stanley said. "It was created by the effect of Operation Surge."The district said students who need EL services will still have access, but acknowledged many will experience a disruption. Many board members stressed the difficulty of weighing both the necessity of fiscal responsibility and meeting students needs."Unfortunately, we have to bridge a divide of our students. Their needs especially, our EL students, their needs which have been doubly affected and the fact that the future of the district long term needs to be taken care of," said Board Member Yusef Carillo."I think in this moment we have to make some very difficult decisions. When we don't make difficult decisions in the moment it impacts things in the future," said Board Member Chauntyll Allen.When it approved its budget for the 2025-26 school year, the district said it faced a $51.5 million deficit.

title: Rocklin woman stresses importance of breast cancer screenings as cases rises among younger women
description: While the disease remains more common among women over 50, diagnoses among younger women are increasing, prompting cancer specialists to encourage earlier conversations about individual risk.
content: One in eight women in the United States will develop breast cancer during her lifetime. While the disease remains more common among women over 50, diagnoses among younger women are increasing, prompting cancer specialists to encourage earlier conversations about individual risk.For Rocklin jewelry designer Jessica Pearce, that reality became personal at age 30, when she discovered a lump during a self-exam five years ago and was diagnosed with breast cancer.Feeling isolated at a young age, Pearce turned to social media to connect with others facing similar experiences."I started posting on TikTok when I was first diagnosed," Pearce said.She said she now knows "so many young women diagnosed in their 20s, 30s and 40s" and is "tired of losing my friends so young."Pearce has since found support through the Young Survival Coalition, an organization focused on young adults affected by breast cancer."I go to these conferences for women diagnosed under 40 and there are hundreds of us. It's surreal to look around and see everyone," she said.At UC Davis Health, cancer specialists are encouraging women to discuss their breast cancer risk with a doctor as early as age 25, even though routine mammograms generally begin at age 40 for women at average risk."Now we look at this data from the past few years and the incidence is rising faster for women who are under 50," Radiologist Dr. Shadi Aminololama-Shakeri said.Aminololama-Shakeri said an early risk assessment can help determine whether someone should begin screening before the standard recommended age."We are now recommending women at least at age 25 ask about risk assessment because that's knowledge that's going to help them going forward. They may be able to start screening before age 40," she said.According to the American Cancer Society, breast cancer incidence among women under 50 has been rising by about 1.4% annually, roughly twice the rate among women 50 and older.Asked about possible contributors such as stress, chemicals and alcohol, Aminololama-Shakeri said the causes are likely complex."A lot of people are working on this and are interested in that. It is probably some of the things you said (above) and is multi-factorial, with environmental and genetic factors," she said.She also pointed to lifestyle changes women can consider, including limiting alcohol consumption."Staying away from alcohol completely is one of those things," she said.Pearce has stopped drinking alcohol and has turned her experience into an effort to support other breast cancer survivors. She runs Sacramento Flatties, a website and Facebook group for survivors, and organizes events for younger women navigating treatment and recovery."I think it makes a huge difference having people younger relate with and I was diagnosed at 30, with surgery 31, it is a big life difference when young," Pearce said.Beyond the emotional toll, Pearce said treatment can be expensive, adding to the challenges younger patients face while navigating a diagnosis.She wants women facing breast cancer to know they are not alone and hopes more funding will be directed toward understanding why diagnoses among younger women are increasing."Far too many are being diagnosed. We're all aware, now what are we doing about it?" Pearce said.She encourages survivors to seek out support groups that connect them with others who understand what they are experiencing. Organizations such as Albie Aware and the National Breast Cancer Foundation also offer resources for people affected by breast cancer.While Pearce emphasizes the importance of early detection and access to treatment, she said she also wants to see more research into why younger women are developing the disease.She is particularly concerned about aggressive cancers and stage 4 diagnoses, which she said can affect younger patients, and hopes to see more funding dedicated to those cases.

title: Eric Dickerson's son sues LA County school over racial bullying, lawsuit says
description: LA Rams superstar Erick Dickerson's family sued Oaks Christian School over allegations that their son was subjected to "relentless" racial bullying, according to a lawsuit.
content: Los Angeles Rams superstar Erick Dickerson's family sued Oaks Christian School over allegations that their son was subjected to "relentless" racial bullying, according to a lawsuit. The family's attorneys stated in their lawsuit that the Westlake Village private school "allowed, and by its repeated inaction actively encouraged," the racial harassment to continue despite the family reporting the incidents and a video showing a student beating the sixth grader. In a statement, the school said it "disputes the allegations regarding its conduct and will respond through the legal process.""Oaks Christian School is committed to the dignity of every student, consistent with our Christian faith," the school wrote. "This matter involves minors, and out of respect for the privacy of all students involved, we will not comment on individual students or the specifics of the case."Attorneys claimed students repeatedly called the family's son racial epithets throughout his sixth-grade year. While they focused on a single student as the primary bully hurling slurs, the family's lawyers said several students joined in and called the sixth grader slurs throughout the school year. "This is a sixth grade black boy who goes to school, thinks he's going to be safe there," said Robert Glassman, an attorney at Panish, Shea, Ravipudi LLP which is representing the family. "Thinks this is a place that has his well-bring at top of mind and what they end up doing is they subject him to horrible, ugly racism."They added that the harassment extended outside of the classroom, highlighting an instance during a "school-sponsored field trip" to a zoo. The family's lawyers said the student continued to hurl racial slurs and compared Dickerson's son to a statue of an animal before his classmates joined in. "The behavior was constant and widespread, and it occurred in a setting for which Oaks Christian bore full supervisory responsibility," lawyers wrote. In the lawsuit, the family also claimed that an Oaks Christian School teacher accused their son of lying about the harassment after a student called him a racial epithet inside a classroom. They also detailed an instance where a female student assaulted Dickerson's son during a lunch break, "striking him in the head, taking his lunch, and deliberately pouring out his water.""Despite having video evidence, Oaks Christian's response was merely to bring the student in, speak with her, and advise her not to do it again.
