content: In less than 48 hours, five people were killed, and as many as 10 others were injured in multiple shootings across Baltimore, prompting Mayor Brandon Scott to call a meeting with police command staff to discuss efforts to stop retaliatory violence.Scott said he wanted to "refocus" the department on small groups of people responsible for violence in city neighborhoods."We cannot have another two weeks like the two weeks we've been having," Scott said.The effort to prevent retaliatory shootings involves not only police officers but also community partners who have experienced the impact of gun violence firsthand."Let's do something now before the knock comes on your door," Nicole Warren, a site coordinator for Safe Streets Sandtown, told WJZ reporter Tara Lynch.Turning pain into actionWarren remembers the knock on her own door in 2018, when her 17-year-old son was killed in a shooting. She has since turned her grief into action, walking the streets of her community and working to prevent other families from experiencing the pain of losing a loved one to gun violence."I felt like I was on an island by myself, and to the God that I serve, I kept praying, and I said, 'Just get me through,'" Warren said. "I had a lot of orange [Safe Streets volunteers] show up for me. That's why I bring a lot of orange to show up for others."Warren has worked for Safe Streets for nine years, helping communities affected by violence. On Tuesday, she walked near the 2800 block of Edmondson Avenue, stopping to talk with business owners and neighbors.On Sunday, two people were killed and three others injured after several suspects opened fire at a BP gas station in West Baltimore.Officers responded around 10:30 p.m. and found a woman and three men suffering from gunshot wounds. Another man arrived at a hospital with gunshot wounds.The woman and one of the men died. The three other men are expected to survive.Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said there appeared to be two or three shooters, and that high-powered rifles were used. No arrests have been announced.Earlier Sunday night, three people were injured in a shooting at a liquor store in Northwest Baltimore, according to police.Officers responded around 8:30 p.m. to Pepper Liquor Store in the 5400 block of Reisterstown Road, where they found two women, ages 26 and 22, suffering from gunshot wounds.Both women were taken to a hospital in stable condition.While at the scene, officers learned that a 27-year-old man had arrived at a hospital with non-life-threatening gunshot wounds.Multiple gunmen wanted in Northwest Baltimore shootingDisturbing video obtained exclusively by WJZ shows two men running with guns drawn near the intersection of Muth Avenue and North Forest Park Avenue in broad daylight. The men get into a silver car and flee.Officers responded around 4:30 p.m. to the area near Carroll Motor Fuels in the 5200 block of Muth Avenue, where three men were found shot.A 24-year-old man and a 30-year-old man died. A 21-year-old man was taken to a hospital in stable condition.A business owner told WJZ that he had chased people off his property before and had even considered closing his business because of the violence.Mayor meets with police command staffOn Tuesday, Scott called a meeting with police command staff that he described as a "talk." During the closed-door meeting, he said he urged department leaders to push their officers to intensify efforts to identify and track down small groups of people involved in retaliatory shootings."Making sure that everybody that wears the badge is bought into and understands we know the people, and we have to focus on them," Scott said.As of Tuesday morning, 253 people had been shot in Baltimore in 2026, compared with 247 at the same point last year, according to police. The city had recorded 101 homicides this year, down from 105 during the same period in 2025.Worley said officers were being deployed throughout the city to disrupt groups involved in violence. He also said the department needed to return to basic policing strategies, including conducting vehicle stops and approaching groups gathered on street corners."Right now, we've got to stop them from shooting each other, so that we can get a grip on it," Worley said. "We do that by more cops in the right places doing the right thing."Later Monday night, a 39-year-old man was killed near Belair Road. An officer conducting a business check in the 3200 block of Belair Road around 11 p.m. heard multiple gunshots and went outside to investigate, according to police.Two other victims, both 21-year-old men, were shot and injured.Since mid-September, at least seven shootings across Baltimore have left multiple people dead or injured.Several mass shootings have killed or injured children and adults during that time. At least four mass shootings have occurred over the past month, including a shooting earlier this month that killed a 12-year-old girl at a West Baltimore park.Another mass shooting in the Winchester neighborhood of West Baltimore left an 18-year-old and a 19-year-old dead and two other people wounded.Community safety workers are stretched thin in many neighborhoods as they try to prevent further violence and help residents move forward."Every day, is it a good day? No, it's not, but I'm going to make the best of it, and I'm going to keep moving, and I'm going to show you how I'm living, and getting through what I went through," Warren said. "What can we do different? ... I know we can be saved. I know we can."Anyone with information about these shootings is asked to call Baltimore police at 410-396-2466 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.

title: St. Anthony Village to become second municipality in Minnesota to operate city-owned cannabis dispensary
description: St. Anthony Village is set to open a city-owned cannabis dispensary Saturday, becoming the second municipality in Minnesota to operate one, alongside Anoka.
content: St. Anthony Village is set to open a city-owned cannabis dispensary Saturday, becoming the second municipality in Minnesota to operate one, alongside Anoka.The new business marks an expansion of the city's municipal liquor operation, which has been in business for 80 years."It's a natural progression from what we've been doing for the last 80 years with the liquor store," said Dave Anglum, a retail operations manager.Over the past 15 years, the city's municipal liquor store has generated nearly $3.5 million. City leaders hope cannabis sales will create another revenue stream to benefit the community."Those profits go back into the community for special projects, offsetting levy increases, things like that," Anglum said.The city says education and responsible sales will be central to the dispensary's operation. Staff members will be available to help customers understand the products and explore their options."We're not just here to push products on customers. We want to give them a great selection and a great opportunity to discover more about what the products are," Anglum said.According to the city, community feedback about the new business has been positive.City leaders hope the dispensary will generate revenue that benefits residents, regardless of whether they choose to purchase cannabis."Our goal is to generate enough income that we can positively impact the lives and residents here in the community," Anglum said.

title: Michigan audit finds thousands of foster children without oversight; Advocates disagree
description: The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services disagreed with the State Auditor's finding that more than half of foster children in their care aren't monitored.
content: An audit of Michigan's foster care system revealed that more than half of children in its care didn't receive monitoring by the state to make sure their needs were being met. However, those who work alongside the state say this audit doesn't tell the full story.Michigan's Auditor General found that the state wasn't monitoring more than half of the foster children in its care, but according to foster care advocates, that doesn't mean there is no oversight."When kids are in foster care, they have an assigned foster care worker who is required to see them at least monthly in their foster home," said Guiding Harbor CEO Jennifer Trotter. The Michigan Children's Institute (MCI) is the state agency that monitors the organization."MCI Doesn't provide any of the direct oversight; the foster care agencies are tasked with that role," Trotter said.The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services disagreed with the State Auditor's finding, arguing in the report that "...MCI's responsibilities are fulfilled through MDHHS's multilayered foster care oversight system."A foster care advocate explained why, out of the 5,000 children in foster care identified by the State Auditor, only 2,200 of them had a record of monitoring by MCI."While MCI might not have its paperwork in order, they do have social workers from other foster care agencies. It makes it look like these kids are being neglected where it's really mismanagement of their paperwork," said adoptive parent Connie Smith."That is concerning because these are kids that are up for adoption. If at the state level the paperwork is missing, that makes it harder for their adoptive workers and their foster care workers to get them to their forever home."As someone who went through the foster care system herself, Smith says that addressing the declining number of foster families in Michigan should be the state's top priority.

title: Clock repairer brings treasured chimes and family memories back to life
description: Ricky Weigand restores a couple's cherished 40-year-old grandfather clock, bringing its familiar chimes back into their home.
content: In an era defined by fast-paced digital screens and disposable technology, the intricate craft of repairing mechanical antique clocks is becoming a rare and delicate discipline. But for master horologist Ricky Weigand, it is a daily calling dedicated to keeping family histories alive, one tick at a time.A horologist is a highly trained specialist, skilled in the science of measuring time and servicing complex mechanical movements. Weigand spends much of his time on house calls, reviving cherished heirlooms that have long fallen silent.Recently, Weigand visited the home of Regina and Van to service a 40-year-old grandfather clock that had stopped chiming. Handcrafted by an artisan in South Carolina, the clock holds deep personal significance for the couple."The gentleman who built the clock, he built many, many clocks, but the first he built was for Van's parents, and the last one he built for us," Regina said.Van considers the timepiece the centerpiece of their home. "We've love it, and for Regina, this is one of her prized possessions," he noted. "It just really sets the tone when we have people come over here, friends and people in our church. Nobody walks in this house without coming in and saying, 'Oh my gosh, what a beautiful clock.'"When the clock's steady rhythm and chimes finally went quiet, Regina knew it was time to call for a specialist. "I couldn't wait to get them out here; I wanted Ricky out here as soon as possible."Restoring a grandfather clock requires methodical focus. Every adjustment directly impacts whether the delicate internal melody can properly strike again.To begin the overhaul, Weigand disassembled the clock on site, carefully detaching the heavy weights and unhooking the pendulum."The front and the back are where the oil is stored in the bushings," Weigand explained during the process. "Those are the pieces that need to be cleaned off and re-oiled."Over the course of the repair, Weigand systematically fine-tuned every component, including:Cleaning and re-lubricating aged brass bushingsInspecting and aligning each brass gear tooth and barrelBalancing the tension springsCalibrating the moon dial, which features markings numbered 1 through 29½ to track the lunar cycleFor Weigand, the technical labor often yields an emotional reward. "I've had clocks that it's been 5, 10 years since the last time they heard a chime," Weigand said. "And you know, when it starts chiming, I'll get tears, or I'll get stories of where they were, when they were..."About an hour into the repair, the work was complete. After reassembling the housing, the pendulum swung freely, and the familiar chimes echoed through the house once more."It just makes a home seem alive," said Regina.While horology businesses often maintain dedicated storefronts, mobile technicians remain vital to the preservation of these instruments. Grandfather clocks are exceptionally fragile; even moving an assembled clock across a room can bend delicate escapements, knock movements out of alignment, or cause pendulums to damage fragile internal components without professional disassembly first.

title: Crews battle blaze at home in Westmoreland City
description: Crews were called to a house fire in Westmoreland City, North Huntingdon Township, on Tuesday.
content: Crews were called to a house fire in Westmoreland City on Tuesday.The call for the blaze at Fourth and Broadway streets went out just before 2 p.m. When crews arrived, they found the backside of the house engulfed in flames. Neighbors said they were the first to spot this fire, and several people rushed to the house and alerted the person home at the time. Luckily, the fire department was also close by, as the fire house is next door. "Literally right next door," Westmoreland City Volunteer Fire Chief Michael Doshen said. "It didn't take us long to get here. We pulled in, got our lines off. We attacked it from the interior to the exterior."Doshen went on to say that while he doesn't feel the house is a total loss, he said it will need significant work to restore it.Everyone made it out, but one of the homeowners said that two of their four cats were unaccounted for. The dog that lived in the house, Lucy, was rescued from under the shed and reunited with her owners shortly after crews arrived. Tom Marcius said that this house was his father's, and his daughter and her family took it over when he died. He said he is just grateful that everyone is safe."Kinda shook," Marcius said. "On the borderline of being mad and starting to cry, you know? But what are you going to do?"Right now, it is not known what caused the blaze, but the fire marshal is investigating.

title: Donora man disputes police account after video shows officer punching, tasing him
description: A Donora man seen in a recent video being punched and tased by a police officer is now telling his side of the story.
content: A Donora man seen in a recent video being punched and tased by a police officer is now telling his side of the story.Shawn Bowman disputes the officer's account of his arrest and shared a photograph showing his bloodied face afterward, adding that he no longer feels safe in his own community.Bowman says he wasn't fighting the officer or resisting arrest, but the officer's criminal complaint tells a different story."I wasn't resisting. I was complying to all of what he was saying," Bowman said.Another picture Bowman provided shows him in the back of an ambulance after the encounter.Bowman says the force used against him was unnecessary."He used the handcuffs and punched me right here in my face, and I had blood in my inner left ear, and I couldn't see," Bowman said. "I had to get stitches above my left eye. I had to get three stitches."Police were originally called to the home for a reported domestic disturbance.As the officer attempted to handcuff Bowman, the video shows Bowman move his hand toward the officer's hands before the punches.There is no audio on the recording reviewed by KDKA-TV.In the criminal complaint, the officer alleges Bowman pulled his hands away and refused commands to put them behind his back.The officer also alleges Bowman continued resisting after the taser was used, before eventually complying.Bowman says the encounter has changed how he feels about the police department charged with protecting him."I don't feel safe at all. I feel like I'm going to get harassed every time he sees me," Bowman said. "I don't trust the Donora Police Department anymore. They're supposed to be there to serve and protect."KDKA-TV reached out to the Donora police chief on Tuesday to inquire about the status of the involved officer and whether an internal investigation is underway.Chief Mark Shemansky provided KDKA-TV with the following statement.Final personnel decisions rest solely with the Borough Council. My role as chief is to ensure a completely impartial rigorous investigation into the facts. We are compiling all evidence, body camera footage, and reports to present to council so they can make an informed, legally sound decision regarding the officer's status. In the interim we are taking all necessary administrative steps to ensure community safety and maintain the integrity of this department.Bowman faces charges of simple assault and resisting arrest.

title: More than 1 million Georgia voters cast ballots ahead of November election
description: More than 1 million Georgians have cast ballots in the November election, according to the secretary of state's Election Data Hub.
content: More than 1 million Georgians have already voted in person in the November election, according to the secretary of state's office.As of noon Tuesday, 1,007,015 people had voted early in person, compared with 894,412 at the same point in 2022. That's an increase of about 13%.Another 48,916 absentee ballots had been accepted, bringing overall turnout to 1,055,931. That represents about 14% of approximately 7.5 million active registered voters, roughly 1 in 7."We continue to break records each day of early voting," Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said. "This is evidence that Georgians trust our election process. The strong turnout reflects the work our 159 county election officials do to make our elections free, fair, and fast."The milestone follows a record-setting opening day for early in-person voting in a Georgia midterm election.The secretary of state's office reported that 188,667 people voted in person on Oct. 13. That was 53,705 more than the first day in 2022, an increase of about 40%. The first-day total in 2018 was 70,849.Tuesday's figures reflect overall participation, not votes for individual candidates. The totals are unofficial and will continue to be updated.Georgia voters share what's driving them to the pollsMany voters told CBS News Atlanta that their top concerns include the economy, inflation, healthcare, and international conflicts. Dean Owens said he voted because of concerns about "the economy" and believes "it was more important to come out and show support for decency and democracy and to support the Constitution." "In order to get the economy fixed, it is going to take some people using common sense and a little less corruption," Owen said.John Flick said rising costs motivated him to vote, pointing to "gas, food" and concerns about affordability for younger generations. "My children don't have houses because they can't afford them. It is crazy. It has just gone nuts," he said.College student Asia Quigley said healthcare and "body autonomy" were key issues for her. She also emphasized the importance of civic engagement among young voters, saying many people her age "don't know how powerful their vote can be."Other voters said they cast ballots simply out of civic responsibility. "It is my duty of being a citizen," C.V. Sudarshan said.Malik Webb said he felt compelled to vote because of the activism of his ancestors. "My ancestors protested for me to have the right to vote," Webb said. Jane McGuigan traveled with a group of friends and neighbors from a senior living facility. She said she voted because she believed everyone should vote and express their opinions, especially because of the significance of the United States in the world. "Our country is a special wonderful country," she said.The record numbers of early voters could be a reflection of the heightened interest in this year's race as Georgia remains a key battleground state. Early voting continues through Oct. 30. Voters can find their county's voting locations and hours on the state's My Voter Page. Updated turnout figures are available through the secretary of state's Election Data Hub.

title: Man arrested after shots fired in pickup line outside of an Aurora high school during road rage argument
description: A man was arrested in Aurora on Tuesday after police say he fired a weapon in the parking lot of a high school.
content: A man was arrested in Aurora on Tuesday after police say he fired a weapon in the parking lot of a high school.The Aurora Police Department says two men were at Rangeview High School to pick up students when an argument broke out between them over a road rage incident. The argument turned physical, and investigators say one of the men fired a weapon before fleeing from the scene.No one was injured in the shooting.The high school was placed on a secure perimeter for approximately 10 minutes, which delayed school dismissal.Rangeview's school resource officers gathered information on the suspect and the vehicle. Aurora police then used Flock cameras, city cameras and drones to find the suspect's vehicle and shared its location with officers. The suspect was arrested shortly after. Officers also recovered a firearm.The APD says the man's name will be released at a later time.

title: 7th District race in Illinois pits state Rep. La Shawn Ford against perennial candidate Chad Koppie
description: A veteran Illinois state lawmaker is hoping to take over Congressman Danny Davis' seat in November's election, and is facing off against a perennial Republican candidate who has described himself as "not electable."
content: As longtime Democratic U.S. Rep. Danny Davis prepares to retire at the end of his term, a veteran Illinois state lawmaker is hoping to take over the seat in November's election, and is facing off against a perennial Republican candidate who has described himself as "not electable."Davis has represented the district that includes the Loop, much of the West Side, and several western suburbs for nearly 30 years. In the March primaries, 15 people lined up to be his successor.Illinois state Rep. La Shawn Ford (D-Chicago) defeated 12 other candidates in the Democratic primary with Davis' endorsement. Kane County farmer Chad Koppie defeated radio host Patricia Easley in the Republican primary.Koppie has been a perennial GOP candidate in Illinois for decades, often running in races where Republicans are very long shots. He has had failed bids for the U.S. Senate in 1992, 1996, 2008, 2014, 2016, and 2020. He also unsuccessfully ran for governor in 1998 and for lieutenant governor in 2018."As a very conservative individual, I've run for office so many times already," Koppie said. "I am considered as not electable because of my position on abortion."With affordability the top issue for voters, CBS News Chicago asked Ford what he could do if he is elected. "We will repeal the president and the Republicans' tax breaks and cuts to the ultra rich, and pass that back to the American people," he said.For his part, Koppie said his priority would be lowering taxes, but he could not say where the federal government should cut spending to offset the lost revenue."I can't address that, because I'm not that up on that particular aspect of the issue, but … it wouldn't take me long to learn," Koppie said.Ford said, if he is elected, impeaching President Trump would not be a priority for him."The priority of mine is to make sure that seniors are able to receive more benefits for Social Security," he said.Asked on what issues he disagrees with President Trump, Koppie pointed to the war with Iran and tariffs that have hurt farmers.Pressed on if that means he places some of the blame for the country's current economic situation on the president, Koppie said, "True that."Ford said, while crime is down significantly in Chicago in recent years, there's still a lot of work to do."The way we do it is make sure that people have health care, so that they can receive physical and mental support," he said.Asked whether he feels the Trump administration's controversial immigration enforcement effort in Chicago last year was a success, Koppie said he believes federal immigration agents were "too tough" during Operation Midway Blitz."In other words, there are people getting hurt, there are people getting shot," he said. "I'm critical of it to a certain degree; not to a large, large degree, but to a certain degree."

title: Woman and husband killed in Wilmington, Delaware fire, relative says
description: A fire broke out Tuesday morning at 8th and Maryland avenues in Wilmington, Delaware.
author_name: Ross  DiMattei, Joe  Brandt, Josh  Sanders
content: Two adults died in a townhome fire early Tuesday in Wilmington, Delaware, as intense heat and collapsing floors forced firefighters to retreat twice while trying to enter the three-story home, officials said.Firefighters arrived shortly before 3 a.m. to find heavy flames throughout the home on 8th and Maryland avenues. Two firefighters suffered minor injuries and were treated and released from area hospitals."My older sister's gone, her and her husband," a woman told CBS News Philadelphia. "I'm on the phone with my pastor right now, she's trying to keep me calm." Neighbors said they woke to fire alarms and smoke as flames shot from windows and burning embers fell from the roof."It really could've been my house and my family," said Glenrick Squires, who lives two doors down from the home and said he had known the couple for years.Brennan Rivers, another neighbor, said he woke to alarms and smoke seeping into his home."It was scary, man. It was tough," Rivers said.As the fire spread, Rivers said, his primary concern was getting people out safely."Making sure that everyone that was in those houses were getting out and getting away as fast as we could," he said. "We can save the property later, but get the people out first."Firefighters attempted to enter the home twice but were forced back by extreme heat and collapsing floors. After battling the fire from outside, crews later discovered two adults dead inside.Authorities have not released the victims' identities.Sharon Osburn, the sister of one of the victims, described the loss as overwhelming."It was a bad fire that took the life from both of them," Osburn said. "Too much. Too much is going through my mind right now."Squires said he was struggling to accept the deaths of the couple, whom he described as longtime friends."It's real sad. He's a good guy, you know? He's a good inspiration to me," Squires said.Squires recalled spending time talking with his neighbor and said the loss of the man and his wife was difficult to comprehend.Investigators are working to determine what caused the fire.

title: Alabama governor commutes death sentence of Toforest Johnson after doubts raised over his murder conviction
description: Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey said she was commuting Toforest Johnson's death sentence to life in prison without parole.
content: Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey on Tuesday commuted the death sentence of a death-row inmate after a number of former public officials and the current district attorney raised doubts about his conviction. The Republican governor said she was commuting Toforest Johnson's death sentence to life in prison without parole. Johnson was convicted of the 1995 murder of Jefferson County Deputy Sheriff William Hardy. Johnson has long maintained he is innocent. "When presented with Mr. Johnson's case, I had concerns there was not enough direct evidence to carry out the most serious punishment, death," Ivey said in a statement. "My decision is not a determination of innocence, but a recognition that the circumstances of this case justify commuting his death sentence to life imprisonment, without possibility of parole."Ivey has overseen 27 executions during her time as governor. She has commuted the death sentences of three death-row inmates. Prior to the commutation, Ivey said she notified Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall and a designated member of Hardy's family, Beverly Hardy, of her decision. "Capital punishment is too important of a tool for Alabama to not approach it carefully and seriously," Ivey added in her statement. "Mr. Johnson will serve the remainder of his life behind bars for the senseless murder of Deputy Sheriff William Hardy. No doubt, he is paying the price."Hardy was shot twice in the head while working off-duty security at a hotel. Johnson has maintained he was on the other side of town at the time of the shooting.Ty Alper, one of Toforest Johnson's attorneys, said they are grateful to Ivey for "diligently reviewing Toforest's case and taking action to spare an innocent man from execution." Alper said the fight to overturn the conviction will continue."Toforest Johnson is innocent. Now it is up to the courts to overturn his conviction and grant him a new trial. We will keep fighting until he is home with his family," Alper said.There has been a long-running legal effort to win a new trial in the case that has garnered national attention and was the subject of a podcast. Jefferson County District Attorney Danny Carr, who was elected in 2018, has supported Johnson's bid for a new trial. Carr wrote in a 2024 court filing that the "evidence in this case has unraveled over 20 years."Carr said in 2024 that credible alibi witnesses place Johnson elsewhere at the time of the crime. He said there are multiple reasons to doubt the key prosecution witness, a woman who "claimed she overheard Johnson confess to the murder on a three-way phone call on which she was eavesdropping."The key prosecution witness at Johnson's 1998 trial testified that, while eavesdropping on a phone call, she heard a man she believed was Johnson admitting to the crime. She was paid $5,000 in 2001 for her testimony, and Johnson's lawyers argue that the state withheld evidence of monetary motivation for the testimony.A number of former judges and prosecutors have joined those seeking a new trial for Johnson amid questions about his conviction more than 20 years ago. Former Alabama Attorney General Bill Baxley, former Chief Justices Sonny Hornsby and Drayton Nabers, and several former judges and prosecutors have submitted briefs or written editorials supporting a new trial.

title: Seasonal hiring underway in Chicago, including Target, Macy's, Amazon
description: Companies are looking to fill thousands of positions ahead of the busy holiday shopping season.
content: The holiday's almost here and not only will shoppers be looking for the best deals, but job seekers will also be on the hunt for those seasonal gigs. One expert says you can expect to see a lot of job openings here in Chicago."For Chicago specifically, they said 52% of Chicago area companies were planning to increase contract talent over the course of the second half of 2026," said Derek Walsh, regional director of recruiting and employment agency Robert Half.Big retail stores like Amazon, Macy's and Target have announced seasonal hiring.Target says they're adding more than 4,300 seasonal team members across the Chicago area, with some roles being filled this month.Amazon says they're creating 9,000 jobs here in the Chicagoland area for seasonal, part-time and full-time roles.Walsh says unemployment numbers are near a historic low."For college-degreed workers, we're looking at a 2.5% unemployment rate. If you're looking at the national average, non-farmer, we're looking at a little over 4%."Walsh says he understands there are some people who are skeptical that artificial intelligence is a job eliminator, but he says it's going to create different ways of doing work."With the adoption of artificial intelligence over the last couple of years, which we'll continue, we're starting to see more jobs where human discretion and thought and critical thinking are becoming now more important than ever."For job seekers who feel like they're in a rut and struggling to find those gigs, Walsh says there are a few things that can be done, including highlighting transferable skills and the impact they can make."Your employers want to know that your history and your presence is what they would expect of anybody they would hire in that organization."Macy's says candidates can apply in person on Thursday, Oct. 22, for the nationwide hiring event. The next one will be held on Thursday, Nov. 19.Robert Half says, from an employment standpoint, there's more of an appetite to find people with specific skills that can make an impact with the company quickly.

title: Minneapolis police officer fired after alerting brother he was involved in shooting investigation
description: An officer with the Minneapolis Police Department was discharged earlier this year, with official reports stating she may have tipped off her brother about a possible police investigation into him.
content: A Minneapolis police officer exchanged messages with her brother for hours while on duty, then sent him a police bulletin seeking to identify a shooting suspect who was later confirmed to be him, according to a newly released disciplinary decision.Chanica Hall was discharged in April, and official reports say she may have tipped off her brother about a possible police investigation into him. Then-Police Chief Brian O'Hara said she "put the legitimacy and reputation of the department at risk."Phone records show Hall and her brother exchanged messages for hours while she was on duty. He texted, "You got me worried sis," and later pressed her repeatedly for information: "I need to know ASAP. You got me worried." Hall replied: "should be." "Wow. sis for real?" he wrote.At nearly 2 a.m., Hall began a FaceTime call with him that lasted more than an hour. During the call, minutes after her shift ended, she texted him the bulletin.The bulletin was an "attempt to identify" notice about a suspect in a September 2025 shooting. She used her personal phone to send him a photo of the bulletin.Hall stated during the investigation the person described as the shooter "resembled" her brother, but she didn't know if it was him. She would later admit to sending the bulletin to her brother, but maintained she didn't know it wasn't for the public to see, adding "my intent in my head was, honest to God, to tell him to turn himself in if he's doing something."O'Hara rejected that explanation, writing that her claims were "not credible on their face."Police say she did not contact department investigators, adding they believe her actions delayed identifying the suspect. It was later confirmed the suspect was in fact her brother. He was arrested about seven weeks after the bulletin went out.The department also alleges Hall didn't even list her brother in the "family information" section of a pre-employment background packet. She then signed the packet saying that everything in it was true and complete. Investigators noted he had previous criminal convictions.A review panel and O'Hara investigated five allegations against Hall, according to official documents on the department's Discipline Decision Dashboard. Those allegations include neglect of duty and violations of the department's code of conduct.Hall was also under investigation by the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension for possible criminal charges, but the Hennepin County Attorney's Office ultimately declined to charge her.Rachel Moran, a professor at the University of St. Thomas School of Law, said the evidence supports the department's decision. "What's clear is that she did commit policy violations, and several of them," Moran said.Whether Hall committed a crime is less clear cut, Moran said. She said the department noted that prosecutors didn't think there was enough evidence to move forward but concluded Hall had committed crimes anyway.O'Hara resigned weeks after Hall's discharge, after Mayor Jacob Frey said an investigation found he interfered with an earlier probe into allegations that he "engaged in sexual intimate relationships" with city employees. Investigators concluded those underlying allegations were not substantiated.

title: Ben Kindel suffers "medical episode" on Penguins plane, team says
description: Ben Kindel, a forward for the Pittsburgh Penguins, suffered a "medical episode" on the team plane shortly after taking off in Salt Lake City, the team said.
content: Ben Kindel suffered a "medical episode" on the Pittsburgh Penguins' team plane shortly after taking off from Salt Lake City International Airport on Tuesday, the team said.Kindel â who the Penguins said is conscious, alert and in stable condition â was taken to the University of Utah Hospital for further evaluation. Pittsburgh played the Utah Mammoth at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday night, and Kindel was on the ice for nearly 19 minutes.In a statement posted to social media at 4:30 p.m. on Tuesday, the Penguins said that shortly after takeoff, the team plane returned to Salt Lake City's airport because of a "medical episode" involving Kindel. The team's physician and medical staff were on board and immediately attended to Kindel, the Penguins said. The team didn't provide any other details on Kindel's situation, but said, "The health and safety of our players, as well as the privacy for their families, are our top priority." The Penguins added that more details will be shared "when appropriate." The 19-year-old forward, who was drafted 11th overall in the 2025 draft, has scored two goals and recorded two assists in nine games. In 77 games last season, Kindel had 17 goals and 18 assists. The right-hander is a native of Coquitlam, British Columbia.

title: Man charged after reported burglary leads to illegal drug bust in Aurora, Illinois
description: A 33-year-old Aurora man has been charged after police seized illegal drugs and cash following a reported burglary on Wednesday, Oct. 14.
content: A man has been charged after police said they have seized illegal drugs and cash while responding to a burglary in Aurora last week.Mickey Stewart Jr., 33, of Aurora, was charged with two felony counts of manufacturing or delivering a controlled substance, one count of possessing a controlled substance, two counts of manufacturing or delivering cannabis, three counts of possessing cannabis and one count of possessing a controlled substance.According to police, officers responded to the 400 block of South Lincoln Avenue on Wednesday, Oct. 14, for a reported burglary in progress. Police said that witnesses spotted two people entering a residence and leaving with multiple bags and then fled in a vehicle. The officers noticed forced entry and conducted a sweep of the residence — resulting in the discovery of a large bag containing suspected cannabis and numerous pills that was in plain view. Investigators with the department's Special Operations Group obtained a search warrant to further investigate the suspected illegal drug activity, police said.During the investigation, it was alleged that Stewart, who is a resident, returned to the property and was later taken into custody for obstructing a peace officer. The department said that officers also recovered suspected controlled substances from him.Investigators during the search recovered approximately 1,066.49 grams of suspected cannabis, 28.05 grams of suspected cocaine, 15.51 grams of suspected crack cocaine, 4.27 grams of suspected MDMA known as Ecstasy, 4,886 suspected amphetamine pills known as Adderall, 76.25 suspected alprazolam pills known as Xanax, 266.5 assorted pills and $2,624 in U.S. currency. Digital scales and packaging materials were also seized.Stewart remains in custody at the Kane County Adult Justice Center. He is due back in court on Thursday, Oct. 22.

title: Columbine High School head softball coach arrested on suspected DUI
description: Deputies arrested Columbine High School's head softball coach over the weekend after investigators say he was driving a golf cart while drunk.
content: Deputies arrested Columbine High School's head softball coach over the weekend after investigators say he was driving a golf cart while drunk.According to the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office, the South Metro Fire Department responded to Clement Park on Saturday when a man fell off a golf cart and was injured. That man, later identified as Columbine High School Assistant Coach James Scott, hit his head when he fell off the vehicle onto the bike path.JCSO deputies were called to the scene after first responders said one of the people there was intoxicated and argumentative. Deputies said Scott and James Santaniello, Columbine's head softball coach, told law enforcement that they were coming from Wingstop and decided to take a golf cart for a ride.JCSO documents say Santaniello was driving, and Scott tried to get out of the moving cart from the passenger seat. He fell and injured his head and was taken to a hospital for treatment.Authorities had blood drawn and sent for testing. They arrested Santaniello on suspicion of driving under the influence.

title: California law to expand insurance coverage for cancer cooling caps in 2027
description: Starting in January 2027, more California cancer patients will have access to scalp-cooling treatments designed to reduce hair loss during chemotherapy, with insurance coverage required under a new state law.
content: Hair loss can be one of the most difficult side effects of the cancer treatment journey. But starting in January 2027, more California patients will have access to scalp-cooling treatments designed to reduce hair loss during chemotherapy, with insurance coverage required under a new state law.For Elk Grove breast cancer survivor Rebecca Dierssen, using a DigniCap cooling system during chemotherapy helped her maintain some privacy during an otherwise challenging time."It was my choice to tell someone and not have everyone feeling sorry for me," Dierssen said.Dierssen underwent breast cancer treatment three years ago at Dignity Health Mercy Cancer Center in Sacramento. During each chemotherapy session, she used the cooling cap, which is fitted snugly over wet hair and connected to a machine that lowers the temperature of the scalp.Looking back at a photo on her phone, Dierssen recalled seeing progress about a month into treatment."I was very pleased with the progress at that point," she said.Dierssen said she did lose some hair but never lost all of it. She believes the treatment helped her maintain a sense of normalcy while going through chemotherapy.The treatment can be uncomfortable at first. Dierssen said she bundled up before each chemotherapy session because of the cold, with the first 10 to 15 minutes often being the most difficult.Scalp-cooling systems work by lowering the temperature of the scalp, which reduces blood flow to hair follicles and limits the amount of chemotherapy medication reaching them. That can help reduce hair loss for some patients.Dr. Shahzad Siddique of Dignity Health Mercy Medical Group said hair loss is a major concern for many breast cancer patients."It's a big priority, and one of the first things they ask about. Unfortunately, most breast cancer chemo treatments result in 90% hair loss, and a cool cap for two-thirds of patients can reduce loss to less than 50%," Siddique said.California's AB 1682 will require insurance coverage for certain machine-based scalp-cooling treatments beginning in January 2027. The law covers systems such as DigniCap and Paxman, potentially saving patients thousands of dollars in out-of-pocket costs.Medicare already covers some scalp-cooling treatments.Dierssen hopes the expanded coverage will make the option more accessible to patients who want to try it."Ask your oncologist and if they say no, ask why. Be your own advocate. I think this bill will help, since the cost will be reduced," she said.

title: Philadelphia honors fallen officer Shane Seiber at emotional funeral service
description: Fellow officers and Philadelphia leaders shared stories of officer Shane Seiber on Tuesday as the city honored the fallen military veteran and father of two.
content: Philadelphia paid its respects Tuesday to fallen officer Shane Seiber at funeral services at the Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul.Seiber was shot on Oct. 10 near 52nd and Arch streets in West Philadelphia. The shooter is in custody, and Seiber's partner, officer Hector Rodriguez, is still recovering from his injuries. Rodriguez and his wife were in attendance at the funeral service on Tuesday, days after sources told CBS News Philadelphia that the officer who was shot 12 times was "up and walking."A public viewing was held for Seiber on Monday, Oct. 19. Then at 6 a.m. Tuesday, a procession brought his casket to the funeral site. Mayor Cherelle Parker and Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel took part in the walking procession and attended the funeral.Seiber was posthumously promoted to sergeant at the service and received the Philadelphia Police Department's Medal of Honor and Purple Heart.Dignitaries remember officer Shane Seiber, who made the ultimate sacrificeSeiber, 40, had the nickname "Colgate" because he was always smiling, said Bethel, sharing a story about the fallen officer.He was rejected on his first application to the Philadelphia police academy and crumpled up his rejection letter. But his wife Lisa, a fourth grade teacher, wouldn't let him give up. She dug the letter out and saved it.Lisa applied, in secret, on her husband's behalf — and the second time around, Seiber was approved. They later took a photo together in which "Officer Shane" held both letters: the unfurled rejection letter and the new acceptance letter.The couple met after a Sgt. Murphy in PPD, who served with Seiber in Iraq, introduced them. Guests would later learn that Murphy was a key factor in the couple's courting on the social media platform MySpace.Bethel spoke with that sergeant and said he "shared something that had been weighing on me heavily.""It's difficult for me to understand how Shane could serve two tours in Iraq, come home safely and lose his life serving as a police officer here in Philadelphia," Bethel said.Murphy told Bethel that Seiber understood the risks could include giving their lives one day, and yet they chose to serve."That is not easy to understand, but it tells us something about the courage and commitment of people like Shane," Bethel said. "They don't serve because the work is safe; they serve because they believe the work matters."Murphy didn't simply describe Shane as a friend — he said, 'Shane is my brother,'" Bethel said.Parker shared a story she had heard about a duckling that Seiber once rescued, after finding it stranded in the middle of a road in Michigan."The duck ended up safely tucked into a box on the kitchen table," Parker said."That was his compassion," Parker said. "Sometimes people don't need to listen to what you say to know who you are. All we have to do is watch what they do, the actions affirm to us who he was."Seiber's uncle, Dan Farris, said it was Seiber's dream to serve as a police officer with the men he served with in Iraq."I hope the love in this room reminds you all that you're not walking through this alone," police officer Quishanna Lee said.Lee also addressed Seiber's son and daughter, Finn and Emily, directly:"As much as Shane cared about his work, his greatest love was at home — Lisa, Finn and Emily, you were not a footnote in his story," Lee said. "Your father's legacy is not only found in photographs, medals or stories of his bravery. It lives in the love he had for you and as your babies grow I hope you hear again and again about his smile, his generosity and the way he made people feel seen."Viewing and funeral for Philadelphia police officer Shane SeiberThe first of two public viewings for Seiber was held Monday at the Givnish Funeral Home in Northeast Philadelphia.There was a Commander's March from Archbishop Ryan High School, and then members of the PPD walked inside one by one to pay their respects.The funeral was held at the Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul at 18th Street and the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. Earlier Tuesday morning, Parker, Bethel, members of the 19th Police District and other police department leaders escorted Seiber's casket to the basilica.A second public viewing was held at the church from 8-10:30 a.m. before a service at 11:15 a.m.Ceremonial honors, including a flyover and an honor guard salute, were held at noon before Seiber was taken to a private interment.Seiber was a veteran, dad of two, gamerSeiber was born in Trenton, New Jersey, and lived in Bucks County and Northeast Philly, according to his obituary.He enlisted in the U.S. Air Force in 2006 and served at Dover Air Force Base. He completed two tours of duty in Iraq from 2007 to 2009, then joined PPD in 2016. Seiber practiced jiu-jitsu and was an avid gamer, especially enjoying World of Warcraft.

title: Abdul El-Sayed, Mike Rogers answer questions about AI, lowering housing costs from Detroit Economic Club
description: Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed are in the home stretch of the race to represent Michigan in the Senate. On Tuesday they laid out their different financial visions at the Detroit Economic Club.
content: Michigan U.S. Senate candidates Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed are in the home stretch of the 2026 midterm election. On Tuesday, they laid out their different financial visions at the Detroit Economic Club. The two candidates recently met for a debate on Oct. 8 and are gearing up for their second debate on Wednesday.El-Sayed and Rogers each spent about 20 minutes answering the same eight questions, focusing on different sectors of the economy. On lowering housing costs, Rogers said, "If we get this right, we can have houses being built, we have students from the high school participating in the apprenticeship of building these homes and giving them a skill set."On whether to regulate artificial intelligence, El-Sayed said, "We need AI under democracy and AI under control. AI should not be able to do certain things like fire weapons or fire you or deny your healthcare. We need an SCC or FDA-style regulatory agency that can oversee the development of these models to make sure we don't open Pandora's box only for us to hate it at the end."In an interview on CBS News' "Face The Nation" last month, El-Sayed called for public oversight of AI to prevent it from serving the "interests of a few against the well-being of a many."Attendees said that, for the most part, they've already made up their minds about who they're going to vote for, but said Tuesday's event is an opportunity to hear more about how each candidate will improve the economy. "I know who I'm voting for, I know who my guy is," said Michael Hale Jr., a member of the Club and an attendee on Tuesday. "But again, it's always good to see the other side and to learn, hey, what are the policies across the aisle that we need to hear?"

title: Authorities identify 5 people killed in quadruple murder-suicide in Mundelein
description: The five people who were shot and killed in a quadruple murder-suicide over the weekend in north suburban Mundelein have been identified.
content: The five people who were shot and killed in a murder-suicide over the weekend in north suburban Mundelein have been identified. At 11:45 p.m. Sunday, Mundelein police were called for a wellbeing check at a house in the 200 block of Wellington Avenue after a concerned family member reported they couldn't reach their relatives.Inside, officers found three men and two women dead. All five appeared to have been shot at close range with a handgun. A preliminary investigation determined the five people were killed in an apparent murder-suicide, police said.On Tuesday, the Lake County Coroner's office released the names of all five victims.James Schmidt, 80, who lived at the home where all five victims were found, died from multiple gunshot wounds.Rebecca Schmidt, 77, who also lived at the home, also died of multiple gunshot wounds.Their grandson, Maclaine Schmidt, 22, who lived in Lake Bluff, died from a gunshot wound to the head.Their son, Bryan Schmidt, 51, who lived in Antioch, died of an intraoral gunshot wound to the head. The coroner's office said it appeared his death was a suicide.Nicole Heiser, 37, who was in a long-term relationship with Bryan Schmidt, and also lived in Antioch, died from a gunshot wound to the head.Mundelein police said their investigation found Bryan shot the four others in close proximity of each other, then turned the gun on himself. They said detectives found multiple suicide notes he left at the scene and in his vehicle. Police said they believe the shootings happened between 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. Sunday. Police said they are analyzing evidence from the scene, including electronic devices, as they try to determine a motive. They said the department had no prior contact with Bryan or any other of the victims.Police offered their condolences to the victims' relatives and the wider community. "The Mundelein Police Department extends its condolences to the victims loved ones and recognizes the impact this tragedy has had on our community. We ask the public to respect the privacy of the families during this difficult time," they wrote Anyone with information on the incident is asked to call Mundelein police at 847-968-4600.

title: Arlington couple charged in fatal shooting of 17-year-old on St. Louis highway
description: A Texas couple is charged in the deadly shooting of a 17-year-old student-athlete on a St. Louis highway. Surveillance footage helped investigators track them down in Illinois.
content: A husband and wife from Arlington are charged in the shooting death of a teenager on a St. Louis highway last week, officials said. Willie Hernon, 42, is charged with murder and armed criminal action and is held on a $1 million bond. His wife, Taiya Herndon, 45, is charged with hindering prosecution and has a $500,000 bond.Authorities say the couple pulled over on the side of the highway and shot into 17-year-old Alyssa Wilson's car. The student-athlete was headed to a Halloween event at the zoo. She was shot once and killed."Alyssa was 17," her father, Robert Hickman, said. "Excited about her life, excited about her future. She had 60 days until she turned 18. And we were getting ready to take our first family vacation together, to go to Disney, for her to see her favorite person in the world, Princess Tiana. And unfortunately, she's not gonna get to do that anymore."What surveillance footage revealedInvestigators recovered video surveillance from the area of the shooting, which captured video and audio of the incident, and said road rage was not involved, and that it appears that the couple didn't know Wilson. According to the report, the suspect vehicle pulled over to the right shoulder of Interstate 170 and turned on its hazard lights. "Approximately 40 seconds after stopping, the passenger door of the suspect vehicle opened," the report states. One minute and 33 seconds later, video surveillance captured a person exiting the passenger side of the vehicle and moving around outside. Moments later, Wilson's vehicle approaches the area; seconds later, video surveillance captured the "distinct sound of a gunshot." Shortly after the shooting, Wilson's vehicle crashed. Within two to three seconds of the gunshot, the passenger door of the suspect vehicle closed. The suspect vehicle then pulled back onto Interstate 170, passing the victim, and fleeing the area. The next day, Oct. 15, investigators found a cartridge case consistent with a high-powered rifle located in the grass near where the suspect vehicle had parked. Using license plate recognition systems, investigators traced the car to the Herndons at a hotel in Illinois. Although the couple had swapped the vehicle's license plates, an Arkansas Razorbacks logo seen in surveillance footage was still affixed to the rear of the vehicle. Willie and Taiya Herndon were taken into custody in Caseyville, Illinois, and are awaiting extradition to St. Louis County.In their hotel room, officials found an ABC-15 rifle with a scope, which was loaded with MaxxTech 23 7.62x39 ammunition, located in plain view on the bed. They also found receipts from a gas station from an exit in the immediate area of the Interstate 170 crime scene, approximately one hour prior to the shooting.Documents indicative of travel, including parking tickets from Dallas-Fort Worth Airport and Delta Air Lines receipts reflecting travel from Utah to Texas. Couple has previous charges in multiple statesWillie Herndon has previous separate convictions in Los Angeles, California, for taking a vehicle without consent, possession of a stolen vehicle and stolen property and felony burglary.He was previously arrested by the Tarrant County Sheriff's Office for hindering proceedings by disorderly conduct in August 2026. There is also a theft charge from the North Richland Hills Police.Taiya Herndon has previously been charged with theft, tampering with evidence and possession of a controlled substance by the North Richland Hills Police Department.Authorities haven't yet released any details about a possible motive. The investigation is ongoing.

title: Trump presents $10,000 check to Nick Shirley, the YouTuber behind Minnesota day care fraud furor
description: Nick Shirley got the check in the Oval Office as the White House launched a $25 million fraud tip program. His video about Minnesota day care centers drew visits from state regulators and federal agents.
content: President Trump handed Nick Shirley, the conservative YouTuber behind viral fraud videos filmed in Minnesota, a $10,000 check from the Oval Office as the White House launched a program that pays people who report suspected government fraud.Mr. Trump and Vice President JD Vance announced the $25 million Whistleblower Incentive Program, known as WHIP. Anyone can submit a tip at Fraud.gov, and the Justice Department will lead the program. Tipsters whose reports help lead to a fraud conviction could receive up to $30,000, the White House said.Mr. Trump said he thinks the incentive will "keep a lot of people honest."Shirley's 42-minute video, posted in December 2025, alleged that nearly a dozen Minnesota day care centers were receiving public money without providing any service. State officials and Homeland Security agents visited some of the centers in the days after it spread online.A CBS News review of state records at the time found that all but two of the centers had active licenses and that regulators had visited the active ones in the previous six months. It found dozens of citations for safety and other violations but no recorded evidence of fraud, as of Dec. 30, 2025.One center in the video, Quality Learning Center in Minneapolis, closed in January, according to state records. The center received $1.9 million from Minnesota's Child Care Assistance Program in fiscal year 2025, the state said.A woman who appeared in one of Shirley's videos has pleaded guilty to wire fraud and conspiracy to defraud the United States.

title: Temperatures climb into 80s as rain chances remain slim across North Texas
description: Temperatures in the afternoon will climb above average and remain above average into this weekend and early next week.
content: Another beautiful fall day is underway across North Texas.After a refreshing start with temperatures in the upper 40s and 50s, we'll warm into the upper 70s and lower 80s Tuesday afternoon. High pressure and upper-level ridging remain firmly in control of our weather, keeping skies mostly sunny, winds light and humidity relatively low.Temperatures will continue climbing gradually through the week, with afternoon highs returning to the middle 80s by Thursday and Friday. Although that's above normal for late October, we're not expecting extreme heat or temperatures approaching record levels.Unfortunately, our dry weather pattern also continues. Storm systems moving across the country are being diverted around the ridge, keeping meaningful rainfall away from North Texas. A potential change in the upper-level pattern next week could eventually allow a cold front and some rain chances to return, but confidence remains low regarding timing and impacts.Tuesday, a pleasant evening is expected, with mainly clear skies and occasional passing high clouds. Winds will become light and variable overnight, allowing temperatures to cool efficiently after sunset. Most communities will fall into the lower and middle 50s, with a few outlying locations potentially dropping into the upper 40s. We can expect a low near 57° at DFW. A very weak upper-level disturbance will pass north of Texas overnight into Wednesday. It may bring some additional high clouds, but no rainfall is expected.Another beautiful day is expected on Wednesday as upper-level ridging continues across the Southern Plains. We'll start with temperatures generally in the 50s, followed by another pleasant afternoon with sunshine and passing high clouds. East-southeast winds will remain light, helping keep the warming trend gradual. Afternoon highs will range from the upper 70s to the lower and middle 80s across North Texas. Humidity should remain relatively comfortable, and no rain is expected.Warming trend continues in North Texas on ThursdayThe warming trend continues as the upper-level ridge remains the dominant weather feature. Morning temperatures will generally be in the middle 50s to lower 60s, followed by afternoon highs in the lower and middle 80s. The high will be around 84–85° in Dallas–Fort Worth, with some locations potentially reaching the upper 80s.Skies will remain mostly sunny with occasional high clouds. Despite the warmer temperatures, moisture levels will remain relatively limited, so conditions should not feel excessively humid. No rain is expected.Friday, another warm, mainly sunny and dry day is expected. Afternoon temperatures will once again reach the lower and middle 80s, with a high near 85° at DFW. An upper-level trough will continue developing over the western United States, sending several weak disturbances into the Plains. However, these disturbances will remain displaced north and west of North Texas, while the ridge continues protecting our region from significant rainfall. A few more clouds may begin appearing, but the overall forecast remains dry.Beautiful, sunny weekend in DFWThe weekend begins with another pleasant morning, followed by a warm afternoon. Temperatures will generally start in the upper 50s and lower 60s before climbing into the lower and middle 80s. Highs around 84–85° in the metroplex. Sunshine will continue, although some passing high clouds are possible as the upper-level pattern begins slowly evolving.Winds should remain light to moderate, and humidity is not expected to become excessively high. Sunday, the upper-level ridge will begin weakening and gradually shifting eastward, allowing additional cloud cover to spread into parts of North Texas. Morning temperatures will remain comfortable, generally in the upper 50s and lower 60s.Afternoon highs should reach the lower and middle 80s, although additional clouds could hold temperatures a degree or two lower than Saturday. A developing upper-level trough over the western United States may begin shifting east, with moisture increasing across West Texas. However, any meaningful rain chances are expected to remain outside North Texas through the weekend. The Metroplex forecast remains dry.Pattern change could be aheadThe pattern may begin changing as the upper-level ridge flattens and shifts toward the Gulf states. This could allow a more progressive weather pattern to develop across the Southern Plains. For now, Monday still looks mainly dry across Dallas–Fort Worth, with a few more clouds and afternoon temperatures generally in the lower to middle 80s.Some longer-range model guidance suggests that a frontal boundary and upper-level disturbance could approach North Texas sometime next week. If the ridge weakens sufficiently, this could eventually open the door to returning rain chances. However, the timing, coverage and potential rainfall amounts remain highly uncertain. There is currently no strong indication of a significant intrusion of cold air, so temperatures may remain above normal even if a front eventually arrives. We'll continue monitoring the pattern, especially given the ongoing need for rainfall across North Texas.

title: Superintendent suggests closing STEAM academy in Denver due to enrollment
description: Denver Public Schools recently announced it may close a STEAM school in the district due to declining enrollment.
content: Denver Public Schools recently announced it may close a STEAM school in the district due to declining enrollment.As Denver schools continue to struggle with enrollment, DPS Superintendent Alex Marrero recommended closing one of the district's newest schools. Robert F. Smith STEAM Academy opened just five years ago, but enrollment plummeted to 24 students this year.In 2025, the Denver school board passed a policy directing the superintendent to review and adjust enrollment boundaries and zones for the 2027-28 school year and continue to reevaluate them every five years after. CBS Colorado previously reported that district enrollment is down 1,800 students from last year. The district considered changing school zoning boundaries but paused the plan because families pushed back."The Board has begun working on a revised Executive Limitation, EL-18, which would consolidate EL-18 School Consolidations and Closures and EL-19 Enrollment Boundaries and Zones. There could be Board of Education action on this policy as soon as Oct. 26, 2026. If there are school closures in the future, then school boundary or enrollment zone changes would likely be required as part of a closure. However, those changes would take place after the 2027-28 school year. We anticipate sharing an update on this work later this fall if the Board of Education formally adopts the revised policy," DPS said in a public notice.The school board would have to approve any school closures.

title: Archdiocese of Detroit anticipates loss of 90 priests over the next decade
description: The Archdiocese of Detroit is now in round two of a massive restructuring process that could change where Catholics across the region attend Mass.
content: The Archdiocese of Detroit is now in round two of a massive restructuring process that could change where Catholics across the region attend Mass.After more than 40,000 people took part in listening sessions and more than 17,000 survey responses came in, church leaders say that feedback has already reshaped every original proposal."In one way or another, 100% of the models that were initially proposed have changed. Sometimes it's a minor change, sometimes it's a completely new model that has emerged," said Reverend Mario Amore, executive director of parish renewal for the Archdiocese of Detroit.Amore says the feedback included practical concerns, such as proximity between churches, parking, building capacity and parishes that already work together.But those preferences are being weighed against some much bigger numbers.The Archdiocese expects to have almost 90 fewer priests over the next decade and says it is also facing $94 million in unfunded building maintenance costs."What's really difficult to hear, but what is true, is that the church is not a museum. We're not in the business of keeping buildings open, just for the sake of keeping buildings open," said Amore.That means some of the most consequential decisions are still ahead, including which church sites will continue to hold Sunday Mass and exactly how parishes will be grouped going forward.The feedback process is also changing in this round.Instead of conducting another general public survey, priests and key parish leaders will gather input locally, with one response from each parish sent back to the archdiocese."We'll review that feedback and then begin making any changes that need to be made to the current models that we have. Ultimately, one model will emerge," said Amore.The final plan is expected to be revealed in April 2027, with implementation beginning July 1.

title: Brinks armored truck driver robbed at gunpoint outside bank in Lansing, Illinois
description: A Brinks armored truck driver was robbed at gunpoint on Tuesday morning outside a bank in south suburban Lansing.
content: A Brinks armored truck driver was robbed at gunpoint on Tuesday morning outside a bank in south suburban Lansing.Police said, shortly before 9 a.m., officers responded to an armed robbery at the Chase Bank branch at 3115 Ridge Road.Three armed robbers had approached a Brinks employee while they were servicing the bank's ATM, and stole a substantial amount of cash at gunpoint before fleeing the scene, according to police.No injuries were reported. Lansing police and the FBI were investigating.Anyone with information on the robbery is asked to contact the FBI's Chicago office at 312-421-6700 or submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov.

title: Long Beach Alamitos Bay dredging project begins, includes sand replenishment
description: The Alamitos Bay Entrance Dredging Project, planned since 2023, will deepen the entrance to the bay and bring about 415,000 cubic yards of sand to Peninsula Beach.
content: As the ocean has been taking chunks out of the Long Beach Peninsula, the city is working to rehabilitate the storm-torn area, as its Alamitos Bay dredging project and beach sand replenishment project are underway. Three recent storms battered the shoreline, washing away sand, ripping apart sections of the historic boardwalk, and damaging the seawall and homes.Now, city crews are mobilizing near 72nd Place to begin an $11.4 million project to provide the Peninsula with much-needed protection. The Alamitos Bay Entrance Dredging Project, planned since 2023, will deepen the entrance to the bay and bring about 415,000 cubic yards of sand to Peninsula Beach. The goal is vessel safety, as navigable depths in the channel will be restored by removing deposited sediments, which build up over time.The dredged material will be reused to widen the shoreline by about 200 feet in the targeted area, creating a greater buffer between the ocean and homes. "This environmentally preferred practice for dredging aligns with regional sediment management practices, and helps combat erosion, preserve recreational space and coastal access," the city wrote in a news release.It has been more than 20 years since the entrance channel was last dredged, according to the city."They're trying to mitigate the possibility of disaster by building it up and building it properly, so we'll see what happens," resident Steve Shinn said.Not everyone is convinced the extra sand will be enough. Robert Smith says he welcomes the effort, but he's not forgetting what happened. "If the currents have taken away the existing beach, there seems to be a certain logic in the beach not lasting as long as they want," Smith said. With king tides and the threat of more El NiÃ±o storms ahead, residents know the newly built beach could soon face another test."Good luck. You try to outguess Mother Nature, and you're going to come out on the short end every time," Shinn said.The dredging project stretches from 61st Street to 72nd Place and is scheduled to conclude in February 2027.

title: Michigan man faces murder charge after mother shot to death in home
description: A Michigan man accused of killing his mother last week is now facing a murder charge, according to the Kent County Sheriff's Office.
content: A Michigan man accused of killing his mother last week is now facing a murder charge, according to the Kent County Sheriff's Office.Court records show that Ryan Hansen, 30, was arraigned on Monday for one count of open murder and one count of felony firearm. Hansen was not given a bond. The sheriff's office says that on Oct. 15, deputies responded to a residence in the 1200 block of Indian Lakes Road in Algoma Township for a shooting and found 56-year-old Diane Kilmar-Luman with multiple gunshot wounds. Family members who were inside the home told the deputies that Hansen fled the home in a vehicle.The sheriff's office and Michigan State Police began searching for Hansen, who was later spotted near Ritchie Avenue and 14 Mile Road. Authorities say Hansen's car broke down and he was getting into another car when he was taken into custody. An investigation revealed that the other car was a rideshare ordered by Hansen.A search of the home and Hansen's car uncovered multiple spent bullet casings.Hansen is due back in court on Oct. 28, according to court records.An investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to call the Kent County Sheriff's Office at 616-632-6125 or submit a tip to the Silent Observer online or by calling 616-774-2345.

title: Canadian authorities seize nearly 280 pounds of cocaine at Ambassador Bridge
description: Two men were arrested by Canadian authorities after nearly 280 pounds of cocaine was found on a commercial truck making the border crossing at the Ambassador Bridge.
content: Two men were arrested by Canadian authorities after nearly 280 pounds of cocaine was found on a commercial truck making the border crossing at the Ambassador Bridge between Detroit and Windsor, Ontario. The seizure happened on Sept. 11, the Canada Border Services Agency said in a news release issued Monday on the circumstances. Border officials used the assistance of a detection dog for a secondary inspection on the commercial truck arriving from the United States and found 127 kilograms of suspected cocaine. That works out to just under 280 pounds. The Canada Border Services Agency then took two Ontario men, ages 61 and 41, into custody. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police has since charged them with importation of cocaine and possession of cocaine for the purpose of trafficking under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act. The matter is currently before the Ontario Court of Justice in Windsor. The charges are subject to validation by the court, the border agency said. "The seizure of this significant quantity of cocaine at the Ambassador Bridge demonstrates our government's action to protect Canadians from the threat of cross-border organized crime and illicit drugs. I commend the Canada Border Services Agency and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police for their work to protect Canadians and strengthen public safety," Gary Anandasangaree, Minister of Public Safety, said. So far this year, CBSA's Southern Ontario Region, whose jurisdiction includes the Ambassador Bridge, has seized 1.67 metric tonnes of cocaine, which works out to about 3,680 pounds.

title: More than 1.1 million Floridians have cast ballots as early voting opens in over half the state
description: Democrats have cast about 400,000 mail ballots to Republicans' 340,000, and in-person early votes are nearly even so far.
content: More than 1.1 million votes have been cast for the November election, with the in-person early voting option now available in more than half the state.The state Division of Elections posted Tuesday morning that just over 171,000 people cast ballots at in-person early voting locations that became available in more than half of Florida's 67 counties on Monday. Early in-person voting is mandatory statewide starting Saturday through Oct. 31.Another 933,000 ballots have been cast through the mail from among the 13.7 million Floridians registered to vote in the Nov. 3 contest.Ulysses Roberson, a Tallahassee voter at the Lake Jackson Community Center on Monday, said he preferred early voting as "you don't have to fight the crowd.""We fought for this vote and our civil rights. I've come out here and done it because of that," Roberson said. "My ancestors always did this. When I was coming up, they always told us in my family to do this."Before the early voting locations opened in Leon County on Monday, Supervisor of Elections Mark Earley encouraged voters to consider the option "as a way of avoiding lines on Election Day."Statewide, Democrats accounted for nearly 400,000 vote-by-mail ballots and just over 68,500 early votes, compared to about 340,000 vote-by-mail ballots and 69,000 early votes by registered Republicans.Floridians without a party affiliation accounted for nearly 30,000 early votes and 175,000 votes through the mail at the same time.Those registered with a third party accounted for just over 4,000 early votes and nearly 23,000 have cast mail ballots.In the past few election cycles, Democrats have been more willing to use the vote-by-mail option than Republicans, as President Donald Trump has slammed that method of voting, despite frequently casting mail ballots himself. Conversely, Republicans have exceeded Democratic vote-by-mail gains by flooding early voting locations.But some former Democratic political strategists speculated that recent changes in Florida's election procedures, focused on vote-by-mail, are shifting more Democrats toward early voting, where counties set up polling locations in select public places such as libraries and community centers."It's really early but one real issue with reading Florida VBM data is the state completely deleted the VBM request list a few years back, meaning everyone has to reapply every cycle. Undoubtedly plenty of people will choose another way of voting," Steve Schale, a Tallahassee Democratic consultant, stated in a post on X on Monday. In the 2018 general election, Republicans accounted for 1.08 million vote-by-mail ballots to 1.03 million Democrats. In early voting that year, Democrats accounted for 1.14 million early votes to 1.05 million Republicans.Those numbers started to shift in 2020 as Trump pointed to mail ballots while falsely raising issues of "rigged" and fraudulent elections.Even though Trump won Florida, Democrat Joe Biden defeated him in the Electoral College, winning the 2020 election. Nevertheless, the GOP-led state Legislature passed a law in 2021 requiring that requests for vote-by-mail ballots be submitted after each general election.Democrats accounted for 1.19 million of the 2.77 million vote-by-mail ballots cast in the 2022 general election, compared to just over 1 million mail votes from Republicans. Meanwhile, 1.17 million Republicans went to early voting locations compared to just over 675,000 Democrats.Two years later, Democrats were up in vote-by-mail voting, 1.26 million to 1.05 million, while 2.5 million Republicans used early voting compared to 1.5 million by Democrats.Of the 7.8 million votes cast in Florida's 2022 general election, 2.7 million were by mail, and 2.29 million went to early voting locations.

title: Ocean City's Boardwalk Rock music festival announces lineup
description: The lineup has been announced for the Boardwalk Rock music festival to be held in Ocean City in May.
content: The lineup has been announced for the Boardwalk Rock music festival to be held in Ocean City in May.Among the headlining groups that will play at the May 14-16 event will be Korn, Bad Omens and Iron Maiden. Others include Breaking Benjamin, Good Charlotte, Alice in Chains, Judas Priest, Marilyn Manson and The Prodigy. In addition, Cypress Hill, Slash Featuring Myles Kennedy and the Conspirators and Sleeping with Sirens will perform.
