A flyer promoting the lineup invites fans to sign up to receive a presale passcode to get advance access to tickets. The Facebook post reads: "Sign up now for a presale passcode at boardwalkrockfest.com to access guaranteed lowest-price GA Tickets for 1 HOUR ONLY!"

title: Suspect in murder of Illinois National Guardsman Chrys Carvajal added to FBI's "Most Wanted List"
description: A fugitive charged in the 2021 murder of Illinois Army National Guardsman Chrys Carvajal has been added to the FBI's "Ten Most Wanted List," and the reward for his arrest and conviction has been increased to $1 million.
author_name: Tara  Molina, Darius  Johnson, Todd  Feurer
content: A fugitive charged in the 2021 murder of Illinois Army National Guardsman Chrys Carvajal has been added to the FBI's "Ten Most Wanted List," and the reward for his arrest and conviction has been increased to $1 million.Carvajal, 19, was shot and killed after returning home from military training. Since then, his family has been fighting for justice.Carvajal had just returned home from basic training with the Army National Guard basic training. Police said he was walking to his car after leaving a party in the Belmont Cragin neighborhood over the Fourth of July weekend when he was shot and killed.In July 2024, Joseph Matos and Gary Roberson were indicted on racketeering charges in connection with his death. Federal prosecutors accuse the two of killing Carvajal to improve their standing in the Milwaukee Kings street gang."Chrys had no criminal history and no ties to any gang activity. He was gunned down simply for being in the wrong place at the wrong time. That night, the life of a young man destined to serve and protect our country was extinguished. He was a son, a brother, and a friend. His loss has left a hole in our community ever since," said Ryan Whalen, the FBI Special Agent in Charge of the agency's Chicago office.Roberson is in custody and awaiting trial, but Matos remains a fugitive.The FBI originally was offering a $50,000 reward for information leading to Matos' arrest and conviction, but on Wednesday announced the reward had increased to $1 million as he was added to the FBI's national "Ten Most Wanted List."Carvajal's family joined the FBI on Tuesday to announce the increased reward for Matos' capture and conviction, and said they will never stop fighting for justice for him."Chrys was so much more than a name or a case. He was a loving son, a brother, a loyal friend, and a brave young man with a beautiful heart and a purpose in this world," said his sister, Jennifer Ramirez. "His legacy will never be forgotten. Our family will never stop fighting for the justice Chrys deserves."Matos, 44, is described as a 6-foot-2, 220-pound Hispanic man with brown hair and brown eyes. He has multiple tattoos, incluidng "M-Town Kings" on the right side of his neck, "1300" on the left side of his neck, "Move in Silence" on his right hand," Trust no one" on his left hand, "MOST WANTED" on his stomach, and "Heavensent, Hellbound" on his arms. The FBI said he is considered to be armed and dangerous.Whalen said Matos has ties to Dallas and California, but is believed to be hiding out in the Chicago area. Anyone helping to hide Matos could face criminal charges. The FBI asked anyone with information on Matos' whereabouts to contact their toll-free tipline at 1-800-CALLFBI (1-800-225-5324) or submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov. All information can be submitted anonymously. "To Joseph Matos, you cannot hide from the FBI. Whether you are close to home or in the furthest corner of the world, the FBI's reach has no limits. Justice will find you," Whalen said. "There's someone out there that knows where Matos is, and there's someone out there that's probably helping them. Take this opportunity. Help us take someone off the street that shouldn't still be out there, and bring some closure to this family."

title: Denver audiences treated to special cultural collaboration
description: Cleo Parker Robinson and the Colorado Symphony perform "The Firebird" for Denver audiences.
content: "The Firebird" is a ballet and orchestral concert work by the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky. It's based on a Russian fairy tale called the Firebird, which is about a young prince who rescues a coterie of princesses from an evil sorcerer. "I chose the Hawaiian culture to bring that into fruition because, I think, my working on the volcano for 10 years on Big Island. I was just mesmerized by it and the power of the volcano and the Goddess Pele and so I said, 'I'd love to try it.' So we created a whole other idea through a Hawaiian lens," said Cleo Parker Robinson, founder and Artistic Director of Cleo Parker Robinson Dance. In Parker Robinson's interpretation of "The Firebird", the Firebird is an incarnation of Pele, the Hawaiian Goddess of the Volcano. There is also a literal volcano feature built directly on stage as a central piece of the performance. Denver Mayor Mike Johnston dropped in on rehearsal for the performance as the City promotes Denver Arts Week. The orchestra paints a colorful musical portrait for the choreography. "It's Stravinsky's ballet. He's one of the most influential composers of the 20th century. There are moments of subline beaty. There are moments of just growing excitement and moments of shock. It translates so well to Cleo's creation," said Anthony Pierce, Chief Artistic Officer of the Colorado Symphony.In addition to "The Firebird", Principal Horn Michael Thornton will perform John Williams' Horn Concerto with accompaniment from the entire orchestra. It's a technically demanding piece, which Williams described as a symphonic poem that explores a variety of colors and moods. "Our beloved principal horn Michael Thornton is performing John Williams' French Horn Concerto. So it is John Williams...the guy who wrote Star Wars and Jurassic Park," Pierce added. LINK: "The Firebird" with Cleo Parker Robinson Dance & John Williams Horn Concerto "The Firebird" with Cleo Parker Robinson Dance & John Williams Horn Concerto is October 23 - 25, 2026 at Boettcher Concert Hall.

title: Judge declines to immediately halt Hope Florida ads; appeals court weighs unsealing filings
description: A Highlands County judge rejected the Republican Party of Florida's request for an immediate halt, and the 1st District Court of Appeal ordered those named in the grand jury report to show why court filings shouldn't be made public.
content: The legal position of the Hope Florida grand jury report, already widely reported but also expunged by an appellate court, grew murkier Tuesday amid a multi-pronged effort to prohibit any publication of the document.A group of people named in the grand jury report, first leaked in August, petitioned the 1st District Court of Appeal on Friday to "prohibit illegal publication" of the report, but the request was denied. The substance of the petition and the court order aren't publicly available, but the case docket shows the petition was denied.In a separate case filed by the Republican Party of Florida, a Highlands County judge on Tuesday rejected its request to immediately stop television stations from airing political ads from the Florida Democratic Party highlighting the report. RPOF had filed the lawsuit late Friday evening, as first reported by the Florida Trident. Judge Peter Estrada denied the request to immediately halt the ads but ordered a hearing on the matter.The 1st DCA has already ordered Leon County State Attorney Jack Campbell, who oversaw the grand jury proceedings, to justify his actions in handling the report. Now, it's ordering those named in the report to show why the entire court proceedings shouldn't be made public.In two separate cases before the 1st DCA, the court on Monday and Tuesday ordered those named in the report to, within five days, "show cause why the briefs, record on appeal, notices, motions, and other filings of the parties should not be given unrestricted status on the docket and made available for public viewing."The report was finalized in January. It found that, in 2024, the diversion of $10 million from a $67 million Medicaid settlement ended up in a political committee headed by James Uthmeier, then-Gov. Ron DeSantis' chief of staff, meant the money was "misappropriated"; no one could be indicted in the case.Uthmeier was later appointed by DeSantis as attorney general in January 2025, and is in the middle of an election campaign against Democrat Jose Javier Rodriguez, a former state senator who was named as a defendant in RPOF's lawsuit.The money was first given to the Hope Florida Foundation as part of the settlement with Centene to resolve overpayments. That group then gave the money to two nonprofits, which in turn gave it to Uthmeier's political committee, which opposed two measures on the 2024 ballot. The proposals would have legalized recreational marijuana and installed a right to an abortion in the state constitution, but failed to pass.What the leak and expungement mean for the grand jury report The lack of an indictment means that, under state law, the report can be sealed and blocked from public view. Those named in the report petitioned a trial court to prevent its publication, and the court partially agreed, allowing some redactions to be made public.Those named in the report appealed to the 1st DCA, which originally ruled on Aug. 25 that the grand jury presentment should be expunged, but that ruling was also kept hidden from public view. Within 24 hours, CBS News Miami published the unredacted report.In its expungement order, the 1st DCA found that the grand jury was incorrect as a matter of law and that the $10 million was never "state money" because it was part of a settlement completed before any legal action was initiated; therefore, the money wasn't "misappropriated."The leak prompted an inquest by the 1st DCA. Initially, Campbell pointed to the 1st DCA's administration, but the court stated it had not received the unredacted grand jury report until Sept. 9.On Oct. 9, the court gave Campbell five days to show why a special master shouldn't be appointed to investigate the leak of the report, why he shouldn't be sanctioned for implying the clerks of the trial court or the 1st DCA had inadvertently leaked the report, and why he shouldn't be referred to the Florida Bar for disciplinary action. Campbell responded on Oct. 13 with a more than 200-page filing, but that has been sealed by the court.On Friday, the court ordered Campbell to detail which parts of his response should be redacted. And on Monday and Tuesday, the two orders were issued to all parties involved, requiring them to justify why the court filings shouldn't be made public.

title: LA Rams sign Brandon McManus, their third kicker in 2 weeks
description: The Los Angeles Rams signed veteran Brandon McManus to be their third kicker of the season.
content: The Los Angeles Rams signed veteran Brandon McManus on Tuesday to be their third kicker of the season.McManus will begin his 13th NFL season with the Rams (2-4), who cut struggling kicker Harrison Mevis last week. Los Angeles then lost replacement Blake Grupe for the season when he tore a knee ligament while making a tackle on kickoff coverage in his debut during last Sunday's 18-16 loss to Arizona.McManus spent the past two seasons with Green Bay, and he began his career with nine seasons in Denver. He won a Super Bowl ring as the Broncos' kicker in the 2015 season.The Packers dropped McManus in the offseason after he missed two field-goal attempts and an extra point attempt in their 31-27 playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. He lasted just one season with Green Bay after agreeing to a three-year, $15.3 million contract in March 2025.McManus has made 297 of his 362 field-goal attempts during his career while missing only 10 of his 384 extra point attempts.McManus will be the Rams' sixth kicker in less than 3 1/2 seasons since they allowed Matt Gay, the kicker on their Super Bowl-winning team in the 2021 season, to leave as a free agent in early 2023.Mevis' four missed field-goal attempts this season are only part of the Rams' comprehensive struggles on special teams during their dismal start to a season that began with Super Bowl aspirations. Los Angeles has struggled badly on kick coverage, and Grupe got hurt only because he was forced to stop a long return on the ensuing kickoff after he made his first field goal for his new team.McManus resumed his NFL career in Green Bay in October 2024 after two women sued him and the Jacksonville Jaguars in May 2024, alleging he sexually assaulted them when they were working as flight attendants on the Jaguars' trip to London during the 2023 season.The Washington Commanders released McManus after the lawsuit was filed, but the NFL said its investigation did not find sufficient evidence that McManus had violated the league's personal conduct policy. The women's lawsuit was also settled before he signed with the Packers.

title: Hegseth meets with Netanyahu in Israel ahead of elections and possible restart to Iran war
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel just over a week before Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stands for elections, and as President Trump floats restarting the Iran war.
content: Washington — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth quietly visited Israel on Monday and met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, according to a senior U.S. military official who spoke to CBS News under condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. A second source involved in the matter in Israel confirmed Tuesday morning that Netanyahu met Hegseth.The unannounced visit came just over a week before Netanyahu's party faces elections. It also comes after President Trump floated resuming military operations against Iran following next month's U.S. midterm elections.Hegseth confirmed the visit in comments to reporters Tuesday, saying he "was there visiting our troops" and "had a chance to talk to the prime minister.""Of course, the nature of our conversations is not something I would talk about but they've been good partners and I appreciate that," Hegseth said.The Pentagon declined to comment on the visit. CBS News has reached out to the Israeli government for comment.Axios was first to report Hegseth's visit.Israeli and U.S. forces jointly launched strikes against Iran in late February, and the two allies worked closely with each other early in the war. The U.S. also struck three Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025 during a broader conflict between Israel and Iran.Iran and the U.S. have largely refrained from striking each other in recent weeks, but Mr. Trump has said openly that he is still weighing whether to cut a deal with Iran's leadership or "annihilate" the country — a decision he says could come after the November midterm elections.Netanyahu, the longest-serving prime minister in Israeli history, faces his own political uncertainty a week from Tuesday. The coalition led by his right-wing Likud party is seeking to remain in power, but it faces several more centrist challengers, including one party run by former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot.Netanyahu told Israeli media last week he is not planning to launch renewed strikes against Iran before the Oct. 27 elections, saying, "it is not convenient for us."Mr. Trump endorsed Netanyahu on Sunday, calling him "a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran."The U.S. president has maintained a close relationship with Netanyahu, though he has put pressure on Israel at times. Over the spring and summer, the Trump administration urged Israel to ease up on striking Lebanon, home to Iran-backed militant group Hezbollah.The administration has also encouraged Israel to crack down on settler violence in the West Bank and cut a longer-term deal with Hamas in the Gaza Strip.Last month, Trump envoy Jared Kushner suggested the upcoming Israeli elections may have delayed progress in Gaza, saying at a conference in Kyiv: "They just have a crazy election, and that makes them a little irrational in certain regards."

title: Student who died after Atlanta Technical College shooting identified as 60-year-old
description: The student who died after a shooting at Atlanta Technical College​ on Monday has been identified as 60-year-old Donald Silva, according to the Fulton County Medical Examiner's Office.
content: The student who died after a shooting at Atlanta Technical College on Monday has been identified as 60-year-old Donald Silva, according to the Fulton County Medical Examiner's Office.Atlanta police said Silva was carrying a gun in a classroom when it accidentally fired, striking another student in the leg. He then left the classroom and died from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.Officers responded to the campus at 1560 Metropolitan Parkway SW around 8:45 a.m. The injured student was alert, conscious and breathing when taken to a hospital by ambulance. The college said that student is expected to recover.Atlanta Technical College said the campus was secured after the incident and that classes and operations resumed. Police described the incident as isolated and said there was no active threat to the community."Our thoughts are with the students, their families and the entire Atlanta Technical College community during this time," the school said in a social media statement.The investigation remains ongoing.

title: Hunter accused of shooting and killing fellow hunter in West Virginia
description: A hunter is facing charges after he accidentally fatally shot another hunter in Braxton County, West Virginia, authorities said.
content: A hunter is facing charges after he accidentally fatally shot another hunter in Braxton County, West Virginia, authorities said.West Virginia State Police said 64-year-old Arthur Allen Neff of Strange Creek is facing numerous charges in connection with the accidental shooting earlier this week. In an update on Oct. 20, Neff was charged with involuntary manslaughter because the victim died from his injuries. According to the original news release on Oct. 14, troopers were called to a shooting off Keeners Ridge on Oct. 13 around 5 p.m. The investigation found that Neff accidentally shot 42-year-old Bobby Allen Stilwell while hunting. Stilwell was initially transported by emergency medical services but had to be flown to Ruby Memorial Hospital for further treatment. The extent of his injuries was not immediately released. The 64-year-old Neff was arrested and charged within voluntary manslaughter, prohibited person in possession of a firearm, wanton endangerment and negligent shooting while hunting. He was taken to Central Regional Jail. He is awaiting his next court appearance. This investigation into the accidental shooting continues, state police said.

title: Pepper spray incident ends dance at Maryland's Crofton High School, officials say student responsible
description: Students participating in a homecoming dance at Crofton High School on Saturday were forced to leave the event early after someone released pepper spray on the dance floor that affected several people.
content: Students participating in a homecoming dance at Crofton High School on Saturday were forced to leave the event early after someone released pepper spray that affected several people on the dance floor. The dance was about halfway through at 8:30 p.m. when the pepper spray was discharged in the cafeteria, said a letter sent to families by principal Greg Ryan and shared with CBS News Baltimore. Staff members quickly responded to the situation and students were evacuated to the school's main lobby and outside. "Out of an abundance of caution, and in consultation with the police officers on duty, our administrative team made the decision to end the dance early," the letter said. "Students were instructed to contact their families to arrange transportation home."In another letter sent to families on Monday, Principal Ryan provided more details about the incident. "Working with county police, we have been able to identify the person we believe was responsible for discharging the pepper spray inside the school at the dance. That person is a Crofton High School student."The Anne Arundel County school said that in addition to any charges that might come from police, officials were taking "appropriate action in accordance with our Code of Student Conduct" with respect to the student and any other student found to be involved. Families were encouraged to provide any information they have on the incident to school staff. i"I know this incident has caused consternation among students and families because it interrupted the final piece of what was a great Homecoming Week," Ryan wrote. "However, I am going to work with our Student Government Association and Principal's Advisory Council to discuss potential opportunities for another event in the winter or spring. I will provide any information on such an event if and when it is planned."

title: Pole falls off Pittsburgh's new Commercial Street Bridge, nearly hitting car below
description: A pole fell off the new Commercial Street Bridge this weekend and almost hit a car below.
content: The Commercial Street Bridge on Pittsburgh's Parkway East is only a few months old, but it's making headlines again after a pole fell off the bridge over the weekend and almost hit a car below. According to Swisshelm Forward secretary Vicki Yann, a husband and wife were about to drive under the bridge on Commercial Street when the wife saw the pole start to fall. After yelling at her husband, they were able to stop about 20 feet from the pole. "I'm just glad that nobody got hurt," Yann said.The neighborhood group says it's concerned, as this is the second mishap with the bridge and its construction. Just after the demolition of the old bridge in July, unexploded dynamite detonated. No one was hurt. "Who's paying attention to what and what is going to happen next? I really don't want three to be a charm and there be a fatality," Yann said. PennDOT says a subcontractor accidentally backed into the pole as crews were preparing for a consultant bridge inspection. It said this is not a cause for concern about the bridge structure."I think that PennDOT really needs to kind of do some communication with the neighborhood to say what they're doing to make sure that accidents like this don't happen again," Yann said. Yann said she learned the cause of the accident from KDKA. PennDOT had not given a response to her neighborhood group by the time KDKA's story aired. For drivers, seeing something like this happen is not giving them confidence to drive underneath it. "I'll probably go faster underneath the bridge, which isn't the most ideal way of approaching this," Yann said. PennDOT is talking with the subcontractor and consultant and guarantees any new necessary protocols will be added to make sure this doesn't happen again. The couple that witnessed everything is currently out of town and wasn't available to talk to KDKA.

title: U.S. ramps up warnings to Americans in Middle East after deadly Houthi strikes
description: U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of warnings to Americans amid attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia.
content: U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of security warnings to Americans amid escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed an American citizen.The alerts, issued Sunday by U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries, warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting. The advisories urged Americans to exercise vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions."We are actively warning U.S. citizens about the very real threat the Houthis pose and urging them to heed official guidance," Edgar Vasquez, the State Department's deputy assistant secretary for press, told CBS News."These alerts are part of a proactive effort by the Trump administration to ensure Americans are aware of potential risks," Vasquez said, adding that the safety and security of American citizens remain the department's "top priority."The State Department has maintained restrictions on diplomatic operations across parts of the region since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran in February. State Department officials have said the restrictions are intended to be temporary and allow embassies to adjust staffing as security conditions evolve.Under a longstanding "no double standard" policy, embassies are required to share security threat information with private American citizens when the same risks apply to U.S. diplomatic personnel.The latest alerts follow a surge in Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including repeated strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and oil facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco. The Oct. 10 airport attack killed at least 13 people and injured more than 300, according to Saudi authorities.The attacks continued Tuesday, with the Saudi-led coalition reporting it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh as well as a drone near the capital.The escalating attacks have raised questions about the effectiveness of the Trump administration's approach to the conflict. While the administration has provided intelligence and targeting support to Saudi Arabia, President Trump has thus far declined repeated requests from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for direct U.S. military intervention. He has left open the possibility of joining in airstrikes but has not announced a decision."We may," Mr. Trump said on Oct. 10, after the deadly attack on Riyadh's airport. "We're going to look at it." The Houthis have continued to make territorial gains in Yemen, where a Houthi attack killed two teenage girls in Taiz on Tuesday. That came a day after a strike on a government military camp killed 73 recruits and wounded more than 200.In an interview Tuesday with CBS News, Ambassador Marwan Ali Noman, political adviser to the minister of foreign affairs of the government of Yemen, warned that the Houthis would continue expanding their attacks unless confronted. He argued that Yemen's military campaign was intended to protect the wider region as well as its own population."We are fighting on behalf of everyone, because the threat and risk of the Houthis will expand," Noman said.He added that Yemen's government was seeking expanded U.S. and international assistance, including greater intelligence sharing, air defenses and support for its coast guard, but was not asking Washington to deploy ground troops.The requests come as the Trump administration faces competing demands for air defense weapons. Speaking to reporters in India on Tuesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged that countries including Saudi Arabia and Israel are seeking additional American-made missile interceptors, even as Ukraine presses for more supplies."Every country in the world would like interceptors," Rubio said. "It's probably the most in-demand product right now in the defense field."

title: Vacaville, Sacramento residents among 28 charged in California voter fraud crackdown
description: Two Sacramento men and one Vacaville woman are among 28 people living in California charged in a federal investigation into allegations of illegal voting and fraudulent voter registration, according to federal officials.
content: Two Sacramento men and one Vacaville woman are among 28 people living in California charged in a federal investigation into allegations of illegal voting and fraudulent voter registration, according to federal officials.The Vacaville resident — Giezell Viduya Adawag, 41 — made her first appearance in federal court Monday after being charged with allegedly registering to vote and casting a ballot in the November 2024 general election while falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. She was released on her own recognizance.Regarding the two Sacramento men, Juan Antonio Rivas García, 46, is accused of falsely claiming U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in 2018 and 2020 and casting ballots in the 2022 and 2024 elections, federal officials say. Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah, 67, faces a similar accusation and allegedly casted a ballot on Election Day in November 2024. The arrests are part of a federal initiative called "Operation Protect the Vote," which prosecutors say is aimed at investigating alleged violations of federal election laws.All 28 defendants are lawful permanent residents, also known as green card holders, according to the Justice Department. While they have legal immigration status, they are not U.S. citizens and are not eligible to vote in federal elections.Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said the department would pursue cases involving alleged illegal voting."This Department of Justice will not look the other way while non-citizens vote in federal elections," McCotter said.Adawag's defense attorney questions federal crackdownAdawag's attorney, Megan McLoughlin, said the case was unusual in her experience."This is the first time I've ever seen this type of charge," McLoughlin said. "It's really traumatizing and scary to be arrested when the marshals come to your door for any reason."If convicted, federal officials said Adawag faces a maximum sentence of one year in federal prison.Advocacy group alleges voter intimidationGiselle García, program director of NorCal Resist, said the organization photographed federal agents at the Sutter County elections office on Monday. The group alleges their presence was an attempt to intimidate voters."The fact that these federal agents were present at a polling location with full uniforms with their bulletproof vests and masked up, that is absolutely intimidation," García said.Sutter County Registrar of Voters Donna Johnston did not identify the officers' agency but said she did not believe they were there to intimidate anyone."We didn't think anything of it whatsoever," Johnston said.DOJ says California declined to cooperateFederal prosecutors said the investigation involved coordination among California's four U.S. attorneys' offices.According to the Justice Department, the federal government provided California with a list of individuals on Oct. 13 and asked state officials to set aside their vote-by-mail ballots until their citizenship status could be confirmed.The department said California declined to assist, prompting the federal government to file a lawsuit seeking a court order to prevent the counting of ballots it alleges were unlawfully cast."We asked California to work collaboratively on this and we never heard anything back," McCotter said.The Justice Department said it made 112 arrests nationwide in recent weeks involving voting- and registration-related offenses.California Gov. Gavin Newsom responded to the federal announcement, saying the statistics undermine claims of widespread voter fraud.Editor's Note: An earlier version of this story incorrectly referred to Giselle Garcia as the executive director of NorCal Resist. She is the program director of the organization.

title: Firefighters in south Denver metro area extinguish fire at Ranch View Middle School
description: Firefighters in Highlands Ranch quickly extinguished a fire at Ranch View Middle School on Tuesday.
content: Firefighters in the south Denver metro area quickly extinguished a fire at Ranch View Middle School on Tuesday.Around 1:05 p.m., South Metro Fire Rescue said it was responding to a fire at 1731 W. Wildcat Reserve Pkwy. A little over 20 minutes later, the fire department announced the flames were under control.Everyone in the building was evacuated safely. SMFR said no injuries were reported.There were some issues with ventilating the area, and the fire department said it is working on a plan to remove the smoke from the building.The SMFR Fire Marshal's Office says an electrical malfunction in a light fixture in an unoccupied classroom caused the fire.The Douglas County School District says all students were moved to ThunderRidge High School.A spokesperson for the district said that parents may pick up their children at any time, and members of the middle school's administrative team are located in the ThunderRidge High School's west side parking lot. They advised families to be patient because both schools will be dismissing in the same area today, meaning there will be a larger amount of traffic.Students can pick up their belongings once they are dismissed.The buses are scheduled to run as normal, and after school activities will continue as planned, the district added.They said middle school classes will resume on Wednesday.

title: Amazon says it will hire 300,000 workers for seasonal jobs this year
description: The online retailer plans to sharply boost its hiring for the holiday season this year. Here's what kind of positions they're looking to fill and how much they pay.
content: Amazon said on Tuesday that it plans to hire 300,000 seasonal, part-time and full-time workers across the U.S. this holiday season, up 20% from the same period last year.Holiday retail sales this year are expected to top $1 trillion for the first time, according to a forecast from the National Retail Federation. In September, Amazon announced that it was boosting the minimum starting wage for full-time workers to $20 an hour, while average pay for full-time staffers is roughly $24 per hour, according to the retailer. Seasonal workers earn an average of $20 per hour, according to Amazon. Starting in 2027, seasonal employees who work at least 30 hours per week will also be eligible for the same healthcare benefits provided to full-time workers, the company said. Job listings will be posted weekly from October through December, according to Amazon. Here's a snapshot of the jobs the company is looking to fill, along with the salary:Locker+ Retail Associate in Jackson, WyomingPay: $21.50-$22 per hour plus up to $3,000 signing bonusDelivery Station Warehouse Associate in Danbury, ConnecticutPay: $21-$23.50 per hour Warehouse equipment operator in Easton, PennsylvaniaPay: $21.25-$23.75 per hourXL Warehouse Equipment Operator, Huntley, IllinoisPay: $22-$24.50 per hourRobotics Warehouse Associate, Omaha, NebraskaPay: $20.25-$22.75 per hour

title: Former Georgia police sergeant charged with misusing Flock license plate reader system
description: A former Vidalia police sergeant has been arrested after investigators say he repeatedly accessed the department's Flock Safety license plate reader system for reasons unrelated to police work.
content: A former Vidalia police sergeant has been arrested after investigators say he repeatedly accessed the department's Flock Safety license plate reader system for reasons unrelated to police work.Santonio Wilcher, 37, of Lyons, faces two counts of misuse of a license plate reader system and a charge of violation of oath of office, according to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation.Vidalia police requested the GBI investigation on Oct. 14 after an internal audit raised concerns about Wilcher's use of the system.Preliminary findings indicate Wilcher accessed it on multiple occasions for non-law enforcement purposes, the GBI said. The agency did not provide details about the searches or whom they involved.Wilcher no longer works for the Vidalia Police Department. He was booked into the Toombs County Jail.

title: Colorado voters with disabilities entitled to accommodations and assistance on Election Day
description: Colorado voters with disabilities are entitled to accommodations and assistance on Election Day, according to the group Disability Justice.
content: Colorado voters with disabilities are entitled to accommodations and assistance on Election Day, according to the group Disability Justice. The group wants to remind voters and poll workers of this before ballots are returned. The group maintains that voting booths and ballot boxes should be accessible. Individuals with disabilities can ask for help filling out their ballot. Employers or union representatives are not allowed to help, but poll workers can assist. Those voters also have additional time to cast their ballot. "People are often hesitant to ask for help, and then people are often hesitant to give that help. But sometimes a person does need that support to be able to cast their vote, so it's just a matter of following that voter's intent, making sure that their voice is heard too," said Disability Justice attorney Sara Ridenour.People with disabilities are entitled to vote alone without family or caregivers present if that is what they prefer.

title: Michigan voters have returned nearly 790,000 ballots with two weeks until Election Day
description: About 10.7% of the state's 7.4 million registered voters have returned ballots, nearly all of them absentee, according to the Michigan Secretary of State's dashboard. Early in-person voting is just getting started.
content: Michigan voter turnout in the midterm election has reached 10% with two weeks to go before Election Day on Nov. 3.The Michigan Voting Dashboard, run by the Michigan Secretary of State, shows that 7.4 million people are registered to vote in the state as of Tuesday morning. Of that count, more than 2.1 million people have requested ballots, the Secretary of State office says. That's 17% ahead of this time before the 2022 election. And of those voters, 789,572, or 10.7%, have returned their ballots."With Election Day only two weeks away, now is the time to return your mail ballot if you have not already done so," said Deputy Secretary of State Aghogho Edevbie. "Voters should avoid putting their ballot in the mail and instead hand-deliver it to your assigned drop box, clerk's office, or put it into the machine yourself at an early voting site or at a polling location on Election Day."The vast majority of the ballots returned so far are absentee ballots, an option that has become as popular as Election Day voting in recent years. Michigan allows "no-reason" absentee ballots; voters just need to request one or ask to be placed on the permanent absentee ballot list.Turnout in Michigan's August primary was just under 22% of registered voters, and far more people voted absentee or early in person than on Election Day.The early in-person voting season is just starting, with 96 such votes cast as of Tuesday morning.The City of East Lansing opened one of its two early in-person voting locations on Monday at WKAR Public Media Studio A on the Michigan State University campus; the other East Lansing site will open on Saturday. Only voters whose address is registered in East Lansing can vote at the MSU site. The Grand Rapids early voting center opened on Tuesday. Again, the Grand Rapids site is available only to Grand Rapids residents.In most communities, early in-person voting begins on Saturday. That's the schedule Detroit's election office will follow, for example. Early voting locations and dates for your registered address can be found at the Michigan Secretary of State website.Historically, the busiest days for early in-person voting in Michigan are Saturday, Sunday and Monday before Election Day, the Secretary of State says.Michigan voter turnout set a record during the November 2024 election, with 74.6% of eligible voters casting ballots, the Michigan Secretary of State said. More than 60% of those ballots were submitted through absentee voting or early in-person voting.

title: With early race for 2028 fast approaching, 3 more Democrats slated to join summit to plot out future
description: Sens. Cory Booker and Chris Van Hollen and Rep. Ro Khanna are among the latest additions to a post-midterm gathering in Denver, where Democrats will strategize about the future of the party.
content: Nine days after next month's midterm elections, three prominent Democrats who are widely believed to have presidential ambitions will join other potential 2028 party contenders in Denver to discuss the future of the party.Sens. Cory Booker of New Jersey and Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, as well as Rep. Ro Khanna of California, are among the latest additions who plan to join the "What's Next" summit, according to an updated list of attendees first shared with CBS News. All three lawmakers identify as progressives, and all three have drawn national attention over their political ambitions in recent years. Booker ran for president in 2020 but dropped out before the first primary contests. Khanna has described himself as a "long-shot presidential candidate," and Van Hollen has acknowledged that he is "kicking the tires" on a possible 2028 run. The three have also introduced tax plans that could be precursors to 2028 platforms.The meeting will take place from Nov. 12 to 14, and is being hosted by Majority Democrats, a group formed last year by largely moderate elected officials and other high-profile Democrats who say they are "committed to reshaping and growing the Democratic Party." Chaired by Rep. Jake Auchincloss of Massachusetts, the organization says it aims to take lessons from the 2026 races into the upcoming presidential election, in part by bringing together leading voices from across different factions within the party."Democrats have talked a big game about building a 'big tent' that can hold onto a majority. The sad reality is, we were all hat, no cattle when it came time to live up to those ideals," said Matt Corridoni, a spokesperson for Majority Democrats. "What's Next is an opportunity for Democrats from every wing of the party to have the open and often difficult conversations we need to win in 2028."The three latest entrants join an initial lineup of other possible presidential candidates including former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Sens. Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Ruben Gallego of Arizona and Chris Murphy of Connecticut.Govs. Abigail Spanberger of Virginia and Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey plan to attend, as well as other members of Congress and political strategists.Democrats hope to win control of the House in November's midterm elections and carry the momentum into the 2028 presidential race. Many feel the party has not settled on a political identity after losing the White House in 2024, and moderate and progressive Democrats disagree on the party's direction.That split has not helped the party win over voters: In a February CBS News poll, most voters described the Democratic Party as "weak." Presidential contenders could begin launching their campaigns in the coming months, and some possible 2028 candidates have sought to raise their profile on the midterm trail, appearing alongside Democrats in key states. New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio Cortez and former Vice President Kamala Harris have both visited Michigan this fall to campaign with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. California Gov. Gavin Newsom campaigned in New Hampshire last weekend with Rep. Chris Pappas, who is in a tight race for Senate. Organizers chose to hold the inaugural What's Next summit in Denver as it is one of the cities under consideration to host the 2028 Democratic National Convention. Over 2,000 people are expected to attend, according to a person familiar with the planning."Winning in 2028 will require us coming together to take the best ideas from every corner of the Democratic Party and forging them into an agenda that can build a durable majority and deliver for the American people," said executive director of Majority Democrats Rohan Patel.

title: LaGuardia Airport named best airport in the U.S. for 3rd year in a row by Forbes Travel Guide
description: LaGuardia Airport has once again been named the best airport in the U.S.​ by Forbes Travel Guide​, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey announced Tuesday.
content: LaGuardia Airport has once again been named the best airport in the U.S. by Forbes Travel Guide, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey announced Tuesday. It's the third year in a row LaGuardia has taken the top spot. Some 9,000 travel advisers and hospitality experts participated in the survey that awarded LaGuardia the accolade. Forbes Travel Guide praised LaGuardia for its modern design, art, and food. LaGuardia - once considered the worst airport in the country - has won numerous accolades since undergoing its $8 billion transformation from 2016-2022. "Thank you again to Forbes Travel Guide. Our third Verified Air Travel Award once again proves that LaGuardia airport has gone from worst to best in the nation," Port Authority Executive Director Kathryn Garcia said. "This award also shows that not only did we build a world class airport with our partners, LaGuardia Gateway Partners and Delta Air Lines, but that our standards for maintaining and operating LaGuardia are just as world-class.""LaGuardia Airport's third consecutive win reflects how dramatically it has transformed and how much passengers have embraced the experience of being there," Forbes Travel Guide CEO Hermann Elger said. "We commend LaGuardia on establishing such a high standard for what an airport can be through its elevated design and amenities.""Being named the nation's best airport by Forbes Travel Guide for the third consecutive year is a tremendous recognition of how far LaGuardia has come and the world-class experience we've built for our customers," Ryan Marzullo of Delta Air Lines said. "We're proud of our continued partnership with the Port Authority to deliver a state-of-the-art terminal and premium travel experience for New Yorkers and visitors alike."

title: 49th Denver Film Festival brings all the buzz of Hollywood to the Mile High City
description: Denver Film Festival will screen 143 films over 11-days.
content: Denver Film Festival runs from October 22 - November 1, 2026. The Festival is 11-days of some of the industry's best movies. From beginning to end 143 films will screen many of them are generating some Oscar buzz. "Our slate is full of awards contenders. One that we're particularly excited about is 'Ink.' This will be screening at the Ellie Caulkins Opera House on Saturday, October 24th. This is Danny Boyles new film starring Guy Pierce, Claire Foy, Jack O'Connell about the advent of tabloid journalism in London in the 60's," said Matthew Campbell, Artistic Director for the Denver Film Festival. From special guests and world premieres to hidden gems and local spotlights, Denver Film Festival has it all. Opening Night will feature "I Play Rocky" which is about Sylvester Stallone's journey to write and make the movie "Rocky." Two Centerpiece presentations will feature "Behemoth" and "Ink." Closing night will feature "Paper Tiger" which is about what happens when two brothers get tangled up with the Russian mafia. The Festival will also be presenting several awards for exceptional work in the industry. "Carrie Coon will receive the Excellence in Acting Award with the film 'The Liberation.' That performance is just outstanding. We definitely think she'll get nominated as well. We have John Cho receiving our Outlaw Award which this is to celebrate an antagonistic performance," Campbell explained. While the Festival has something for everyone. Denver Film is working hard to make sure everyone has the chance to participate. There will be "pay what you can" screenings for all the the Ellie Caulkins Red Carpet presentations. "We've partnered with Amazon so we're providing free screenings for high school students. We'll have four of those at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science. We're really excited to get about 1,600 kids in there for free to have hopefully their first film festival experience," said Kevin Smith, CEO of Denver Film. LINK: For Tickets & Information for 49th Denver Film FestivalThe 49th Denver Film Festival runs October 22 - November 1 at various theaters across Denver including the Sie FilmCenter, MCA Denver at the Holiday Theater, Tattered Cover (Colfax), and the Dormer Harping Hospitality Lounge.

title: Gun used in Oregon elementary school shooting was birthday gift from shooter's mom, sources say
description: The Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun was purchased legally in August 2026 by Shauntai Nickerson, the mother of the shooter, and given to him for recreational use, sources told CBS News.
content: The gun used by a 16-year-old who shot and killed three children and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, last week was a birthday gift from the shooter's mom, sources told CBS News.The Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun was purchased legally in August 2026 by Shauntai Nickerson, the mother of Griffin J. John II, and given to him for recreational use, the sources said.In 2020, Nickerson told a local television station that her son, who was 10 years old at the time, had special needs and was struggling with remote learning during the pandemic. She told KTVZ, "It'll be great for my son to get back in there and get the help that he needs with the skilled teachers that he needs to get it from." The shooter initially fired at a passing pickup truck, whose driver made the initial 911 call, before forcing his way into the school by shooting through the glass panes of a set of double doors, police said last week. He then went into the first classroom to the left of those doors, where he killed all four victims and wounded two others.The children killed in the shooting were ages 5, 8 and 11, police said. The teacher who was killed was identified as 25-year-old Megan Lambert. The 5-year-old victim was identified by police and his family as Rhoam Summer. The families of the two other children have not made their names public, Bend police said. Two wounded victims are a 7-year-old girl and a 54-year-old teacher.Police said Monday there were a total of nine people — four adults and five children — in the classroom at the time. The shooter was shot and killed by a bystander, 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco, who saw the first shooting with the pickup truck and followed the shooter into the school. Giamanco is a Bend resident with two daughters who attend Silver Rail Elementary School.The suspect was a former student of Silver Rail Elementary, police said. No motive for the attack has been provided. The Bend Police Department said Monday it expected to finish collecting evidence at the school by the end of the day, and would then turn the building back over to the school district. Law enforcement sources previously told CBS News that investigators are combing through the computer, phone, social media, search history and other online activity of the attacker.

title: Mom, boyfriend charged after newborn found dead inside dumpster at Fort Worth motel, police say
description: Police said Avia Cantrell has been charged with capital murder, and Camron Baker has been charged with abuse of a corpse.
content: A 23-year-old woman and her 26-year-old boyfriend have been charged in the death of her newborn baby who was found in a dumpster at a Fort Worth motel over the weekend, an arrest affidavit revealed Monday. Police said Avia Cantrell has been charged with capital murder of a person under 10 years old, and Camron Baker has been charged with abuse of a corpse. How the baby was foundThe Fort Worth Police Department said at about 8:40 p.m. on Sunday, Oct. 18, officers responded to the Drummers Inn in the 7300 block of Camp Bowie Boulevard after an infant was found and was possibly dead. When they arrived, a homeless woman admitted that she was dumpster diving when she found a bag, opened it at the business next door and found the child, the arrest affidavit said. The woman told her friend, who also checked the bag to make sure, and they alerted someone at the Drummers Inn and borrowed a phone to call 911. Police said the baby was transported to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead. Evidence leads to the mother, her boyfriendFWPD told CBS News Texas that investigators returned to the motel on Monday to review surveillance video. The affidavit reveals that at about that same time, Cantrell's sister-in-law called police for a welfare check at the motel because Cantrell was pregnant and due soon. Her sister-in-law said that Cantrell had a history of having a baby that nobody knew about. An officer then made contact with Cantrell, who was living at the motel, and said that she "seemed nervous when speaking with him." The officer also said that Cantrell denied being pregnant. However, as surveillance footage was being reviewed, video from June 2026 showed Cantrell with a larger stomach, police said. There was also footage of a woman walking to the dumpster and carrying a box of items, including a car seat, where the baby was found on Oct. 18.Police said that the motel manager identified Cantrell as the woman in the video and confirmed that she lived at the motel. Officers then responded to the room where Cantrell was staying with her three children, who are now with a relative.As she was being interviewed, Cantrell admitted that she had been living in the motel with her boyfriend and children for the last two years, according to the affidavit. Cantrell told police that she had four children and two miscarriages, including two of those children who were both at home and not in the hospital. Cantrell kept denying being pregnant until she finally confessed to what happened, police said. While crying, Cantrell told police that the baby was born at 7 a.m. on Oct. 14, in the bathtub of her motel room. When describing the birth, Cantrell admitted that the tub was filled with water and after the child came out and was moving, she left the baby "face down in the water approximately 30 minutes before moving the child," the affidavit said. Cantrell confessed that the baby's feet were white, and she assumed the baby was no longer alive, so she covered the child up and placed the child inside a bag, which matched the bag the baby was later discovered in, according to the affidavit. Cantrell said that's when she called her boyfriend, Baker, and told him what happened. Cantrell also told police that this had happened before, saying that Baker had thrown away a miscarriage that she had previously had. However, police stated in the affidavit that this was not a miscarriage and the baby was born at full term. Police said Cantrell and Baker then kept the dead baby's body in the bag near the toilet for about four days before Baker placed it in an overnight bag and put it in the dumpster along with another black trash bag. According to the affidavit, Baker admitted to these actions and told police he didn't call them because "they didn't want to catch a case." He said that Cantrell told him to throw the baby's body in the dumpster because "she couldn't do it." Both Cantrell and Baker are still in custody, and no bond amounts have been released at this time. The investigation remains ongoing.

title: Cranberry Township police seek help identifying person in property damage cases
description: Cranberry Township police in Butler County are asking for help identifying a person or people who are responsible for damaging property.
content: Cranberry Township police in Butler County are asking for the public's help after they say a person or people are responsible for damaging property.Bristol Creek's Homeowners Association President Ryan Wollerton is one of many who saw a Cranberry Township police social media post asking for help identifying a person and possibly others suspected of damaging property between midnight and 3 a.m. over the last few weekends."It's extraordinarily quiet," Wollerton said. "Everybody here knows each other," adding that he was "surprised when I was told it was on the police blotter. I was shocked."Police said the crimes include property damage and criminal mischief at Bristol Creek and Washington Farms developments.A picture taken from surveillance footage shows a person on Oct. 17, time-stamped 12:42 a.m."[It] shouldn't be occurring that late at night," said Wollerton. He heard from neighbors that the damage included "marks on doors, things knocked over."Minor damage or not, Wollerton said repercussions could be serious. "Unfortunately, if they're old enough to know better, there's a good chance they're old enough where they could potentially have a permanent record," said Wollerton.It's why he hoped the neighborhood could've addressed it first. "It should've been addressed within the community. There's a good chance you might know the family. It should've been handled that way, in my opinion," Wollerton said.If you recognize this person or have information about the alleged crimes, you are asked to contact Cranberry Township police at 724-776-5180 or tips@cranberrytownship.org.

title: Trump pledges $8 billion in relief for farmers struggling with soaring diesel prices
description: The USDA said farmers don't need crop insurance to qualify and can prepare to apply by creating a Login.gov account.
content: President Trump said his administration will provide $8 billion in aid to farmers hurt by record diesel prices. "Tonight I'm also pleased to announce that the Department of Agriculture will be launching a new Harvest Fuel Relief program, providing our farmers with $8 billion in support to offset diesel costs during this harvest season," Mr. Trump said at a rally in Kansas Monday night."When Republicans win, we will pass even more funding for our farmers. We love our farmers," he added.Earlier this month, Mr. Trump also signed an executive order to ease limits on the tax-free use of red-dyed diesel, a move aimed at lowering costs for farmers and truckers. That came after a $12 billion aid package for farmers announced by the Trump administration in December.Farmers have faced financial pressures from soaring diesel prices, which are used to run agricultural machinery. Diesel reached a record of $6.53 a gallon on Sept. 22, although it's eased slightly since then, with average U.S. prices now at $6.32 a gallon, up from $3.62 a year ago, according to AAA data. "This $8 billion investment will help bring certainty to our farmers during this harvest so they can continue to feed our nation," U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said in a statement. Farmers would benefit more from a resolution in the U.S. war with Iran, which would likely result in lower energy prices, Gbenga Ajilore, chief economist at the nonpartisan Center on Budget and Policy Priorities and formerly a senior adviser in the Office of the Undersecretary for Rural Development at the Department of Agriculture, said in an email. Ending the Trump administration's tariffs would also help ease prices for farmers, he added."The president's economic aid to farmers ahead of the midterm elections follows a pattern dating back to his first term: He imposes policies that harm farmers, then spends taxpayer money to offset the damage his policies create," Ajilore said.The USDA said the plan, called the Harvest Fuel Relief program, will pay farmers to cover part of their estimated losses for the 2026 crop year, using a standard formula. The calculation will use planted acreage reported to the Farm Service Agency, estimated production costs and crop yields and prices from the USDA's World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report.The agency said it will announce payment rates for major commodity crops in November, with details for other eligible products to follow. Farmers won't need crop insurance to qualify and can prepare to apply by creating a Login.gov account linked to USDA. The USDA estimates that net farm income will drop 2.6% this year as production costs rise 4.5%. Fuel and oil expenses alone are expected to jump nearly 30%, according to a September forecast by the agency.

title: South Florida sees some showers Tuesday, but rain chances rise by end of week
description: The strong onshore winds are also leading to a dangerous high risk of rip currents along our Atlantic beaches.
content: Spotty showers were blowing in on the breeze on Tuesday morning in parts of South Florida, with most of the rain rolling in across Miami-Dade.We are also enjoying a taste of fall with slightly cooler and more comfortable temperatures in the low to mid-70s to start the day.On Tuesday afternoon, temperatures are expected to climb into the mid-80s.The breeze will build and gusts could reach 25 to 30 mph. It's also expected to be blustery at times.The strong onshore winds are also leading to a dangerous high risk of rip currents along our Atlantic beaches. That high risk of rip currents will likely continue through Friday.A small craft advisory is also in effect for the Atlantic waters and Keys waters due to the hazardous marine conditions.Wednesday morning is expected to be even cooler with low temperatures falling into the upper 60s inland and the low 70s closest to the coast.We will stay breezy but not as blustery on Wednesday with a few showers possible.Wind gusts could still reach 15 mph to 20 mph. High temperatures will climb into the low 80s.We will continue to enjoy a pleasant morning with temperatures in the low 70s and upper 60s for the rest of the week.High temperatures will remain in the low 80s through the weekend.Passing showers will be possible on Thursday, but rain chances will be higher late week and especially into the weekend with more scattered showers and thunderstorms around.

title: Video shows intense fire that broke out at mobile home in West Little River
description: The fire broke out in the 1200 block of Northwest 79th Street just before 3:30 a.m., according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue.
content: An investigation is underway in Northwest Miami-Dade after a massive fire tore through a mobile home in West Little River early Tuesday morning, according to investigators.According to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, about 10 units responded to a report of a fire in the 1200 block of Northwest 79th Street just before 3:30 a.m.When units arrived at the scene, they said they found a fully engulfed converted trailer and box truck. Crews were able to quickly deploy their hose lines and initiate a fire attack, and they were able to prevent the flames from spreading to nearby vehicles and materials.Once they were able to contain the fire, they were able to use a specialized firefighting foam to reduce the risk of remaining fuels from possibly reigniting.Vladmirmi Agguirre said he watched as his mobile home went up in flames not knowing if his two dogs and two bunnies were okay.He told CBS News Miami that it was hard to explain just how difficult it was not knowing where his pets were.However, hours after the blaze was extinguished, he got some good news – his dogs and bunnies were safe.MDFR said that it is possible that the fire broke out as a result of a blown transformer nearby, but the cause remains under investigation.

title: Atlanta Hawks announce Prime Video streaming deal while keeping free local TV broadcasts
description: The Hawks announced Tuesday that Prime Video will be their exclusive streaming home for the 2026-27 season.
content: Atlanta Hawks fans will be able to stream games on Prime Video this season without paying for an additional subscription. The Hawks announced Tuesday that Prime Video will be their exclusive streaming home for the 2026-27 season. Games that are not exclusive national broadcasts will be included with a Prime membership for fans within the team's television territory, which spans parts of Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina and Mississippi.The agreement makes Atlanta the first NBA team to stream its local games exclusively on Prime Video, according to the Hawks.Fans will also have a free television option. Under a partnership announced in July, local games will air over the air on WANF and Peachtree Sports Network, with coverage through Gray Media stations across Georgia.The Hawks said 74 regular-season games are scheduled for those television broadcasts and Prime Video streaming."We are committed to putting our fans first and maximizing accessibility throughout the state of Georgia and the Southeast," said Andrew Saltzman, president of business enterprise and chief commercial officer of the Hawks and State Farm Arena.Prime members in the team's market can watch through a web browser or the Prime Video app on compatible televisions, phones, tablets, game consoles and other devices. Raycom Sports will produce the local broadcasts.The Hawks open the regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against the Orlando Magic. Tipoff is scheduled for 7 p.m.

title: Lakeville man convicted of murdering sister, her unborn child in 2024
description: A man from Lakeville, Minnesota, was found guilty Tuesday of murdering his sister and her unborn child over two years ago, according to the Dakota County Attorney's Office.
content: A man from Lakeville, Minnesota, was found guilty Tuesday of murdering his sister and her unborn child over two years ago, according to the Dakota County Attorney's Office.Jack Joseph Ball, 25, was charged with two counts of second-degree murder in connection with the attack on May 23, 2024, inside his Lakeville home that killed 30-year-old Bethany Ann Israel. The criminal complaint states Israel, of Bloomington, was between 17 and 18 weeks pregnant at the time.A Dakota County grand jury later indicted ball on two counts of premeditated first-degree murder and two counts of intentional second-degree murder.Court documents state Israel went to her brother's residence on Encina Path for dinner, but family members called 911 after she didn't return. One of their relatives then drove by Ball's home and saw him leaving.The relative walked into the home, where they saw a "significant amount of blood" and called police, according to the criminal complaint. An officer arrived at the scene and found "bloody knives and several dismembered body parts" inside.Ball's vehicle was later spotted by police in Rosemount, and soon after a city resident reported seeing a man on his doorbell camera place what looked like a body part on his lawn.Ball was found by police in a neighboring backyard, suffering from an apparent self-inflicted wound to his neck, court documents state.The county attorney's office says Ball first pleaded guilty to one count of premeditated first-degree murder and one count of premeditated first-degree murder of an unborn child. In January, he unsuccessfully asserted "a defense of mental illness."Ball is scheduled to be sentenced Thursday afternoon inside a Hastings courtroom. A first-degree murder conviction in Minnesota carries a mandatory sentence of life in prison.If you or someone you know is in emotional distress, get help from the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988. Trained crisis counselors are available 24 hours a day to talk about anything.In addition, help is available from the National Alliance on Mental Illness, or NAMI. Call the NAMI Helpline at 800-950-6264 or text "HelpLine" to 62640. There are more than 600 local NAMI organizations and affiliates across the country, many of which offer free support and education programs.

title: Macomb County asks residents to report spongy moth egg masses by Nov. 15
description: Macomb County officials ask the public to report spongy moth egg masses to help them track the invasive species.
content: Macomb County residents are being asked to check their property this fall for spongy moth egg masses and to submit the location, along with photos, to local officials if they find any. The goal is to detect and head off an infestation of the invasive insect next year, county officials said.Residents should report sightings by Nov. 15, either online or by calling the Macomb County MSU Extension office at 586-469-6432.The egg masses are light brown, teardrop-shaped and about 1 to 2 inches long, county officials said. They are usually found on tree trunks and branches but can also form on outdoor furniture, fences or homes. Michigan State University's website has pictures of a typical egg mass.Spongy moths, formerly known as gypsy moths, are an invasive insect that can damage trees and create nuisances for residents, county officials said. The insects have few natural predators in the U.S. In the caterpillar stage, they can strip healthy trees of their leaves, and repeated infestations will weaken or kill a tree.Removing egg masses before they hatch into caterpillars is "one of the most effective steps homeowners can take" to reduce local populations, county officials said.

title: Widespread rain headed to Southern California along with high surf
description: About 1 inch of rain is expected in parts of inland Los Angeles County on Wednesday and Thursday.
content: The first typical, non-tropical rain event of the season is headed toward Southern California starting Wednesday, forecasts say.According to the National Weather Service, the region can expect "lots of action" Wednesday night and into Thursday morning as a low-pressure system rolls in.CBS LA has issued a Next Weather Alert for Wednesday and Thursday due to chances for rain and isolated thunderstorms across Southern California.While the start of the region's rain season is Oct. 1, the event is expected to provide around double the rain in a two-day span that Los Angeles typically experiences in all of the month."Average rain in LA in October is only 0.58 [inches]," said CBS LA Chief Meteorologist Paul Deanno. "Some areas may get twice that amount over the two-day period."The bulk of that rainfall is anticipated late Wednesday and into Thursday morning, forecasts show. The rain could continue throughout the day on Thursday and into Friday morning's early hours.That rainfall is expected to be widespread, with similar totals of around 1 inch hitting inland LA, Orange, San Bernardino and Riverside counties, according to the NWS.Thunderstorm chances on Thursday could bring those totals higher.Along the coast, hazardous beach conditions are possible through Thursday night. The NWS issued a Beach Hazards Statement for Ventura, LA, Orange and San Diego counties. "There is an increased risk of ocean drowning," the NWS said. "Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore."Newport Beach is expecting high tides to potentially cause more urban flooding in places like the Balboa Peninsula, similar to events that took place earlier this month.Forecasters believe flooding concerns are not widespread."Thankfully, widespread flooding is not expected, although roads and highways will be much slower than normal because of the rain," Deanno said.

title: 2 men rearrested on suspicion of spying for Iran over suspected plot at U.S.-run air base in England
description: Police said a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual U.K.-Iranian national were arrested under the National Security Act.
content: British police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service over the suspected plot at a U.S.-run air base in England last month. Counter Terrorism Policing said the men, a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual U.K.-Iranian national, were arrested under the National Security Act. The men were earlier arrested but had been bailed pending more investigation. Police are investigating a suspected terror plot on Sept. 27 against the U.S.-run base at RAF Fairford in western England, which has been used to bomb Iran during this year's war. Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant - gasoline - in three vans at the site, but no explosives. British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Five other men who were also arrested earlier remain on bail. No one has yet been charged. Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K., said detectives are looking at "many lines of enquiry involved in this hugely complex investigation." "This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement," he said in a statement. "Our investigators are continuing to examine what that level of involvement was and the ambition behind it," he added.Iranian officials have said several times since the beginning of the war that any bases used to attack the country would be considered legitimate targets. But the Iranian Embassy in London said in a previous statement that the regime "categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran" to the incident.Earlier this month, the U.S. Air Force removed all of its bombers from the air base following the security incident.

title: Colorado Department of Transportation unveils trucks to protect emergency responders from crashes
description: The Colorado Department of Transportation is unveiling its new crash prevention trucks that will help protect emergency crews responding to scenes.
content: The Colorado Department of Transportation is unveiling its new crash prevention trucks that will help protect emergency crews responding to scenes. This is part of the agency's traffic incident management training to keep everyone safe.CDOT says each of these trucks will be used to protect emergency responders. If a driver is too close and they are not paying attention, the attenuators will take the impact of the crash. As drivers are going through an area of a crash, sometimes the secondary crash is a lot worse than the first. CDOT says each of these trucks costs about $250,000 and will be mostly used around the Denver area. Right now, they have about two of them that would be used for crash protection. Each time one of these attenuators takes the blow, it protects the firefighters, police officers, tow truck operators, and EMS on scene. CDOT says these are way easier to replace at $30,000 than it would be to replace a fire truck that was hit at $2 million. Now, even though they have these vehicles to help protect from a secondary crash, emergency responders say all crashes are preventable, so it should never happen in the first place."Secondary accidents are too common, and it's unacceptable," FHWA Administrator Sean McMaster said. "Zero is the only number of accidents we will accept.""Emergency responders are also reminding everyone of the Move Over law. If you see them responding, you need to either move over a lane or slow down past them.

title: Man sentenced for killing cousin during fight in Bloomington driveway
description: A 19-year-old Richfield, Minnesota, man learned his prison sentence for fatally shooting his cousin during an argument last year.
content: A 19-year-old Richfield, Minnesota, man learned his prison sentence for fatally shooting his cousin during an argument last year. According to court records, Exon Alfonzo Sanchez Garzon was sentenced to over 21 years in prison, with credit for a year and several months already served. He was scheduled to be sentenced on Monday. According to the criminal complaint, the shooting happened on June 22, 2025, at a house on the 200 block of West 92nd Street in Bloomington. Responding officers found a man who had been shot multiple times lying near the driveway of the house, charges say. He died at the scene. An investigation revealed that an argument led to the shooting. At one point during the fight, Garzon is seen on surveillance video grabbing a pistol from his cross-body bag and shooting it around three times at the victim.Charges say he then took a step back, pointed the gun at the victim and shot around five more times. Garzon then fled the scene. He was found and arrested later that same day.Garzon's girlfriend was with him when he was taken into custody. She told police that she picked up Garzon in Minneapolis and that "he was crying and said he killed his cousin," according to charges.

title: LA County small businesses can apply for LA28 licensing on locally made products
description: The Los Angeles-based business, Homeboy Industries, is the first to participate in the Made for Two-Eight licensing program.
content: Small businesses in Los Angeles County have a chance to participate in a new program to become official LA28 Olympic Games licensees and use the LA28 emblem on products they create locally. In a Tuesday announcement, LA28 CEO Reynold Hoover said, "We want to make sure that millions of visitors buy a souvenir. That when they do that, and they buy that souvenir, that they're really taking home a piece of real LA culture." The Los Angeles-based business, Homeboy Industries, is the first to participate in the Made for Two-Eight licensing program. The company revealed its Homeboy LA28 T-shirt, featuring a prominent blazing Olympic torch that reflects "the hopefulness of the Olympic torch to our community." Homeboy Industries co-CEO Steve Delgado said the company has been one of the preeminent silkscreen businesses in Los Angeles since 1994."Homeboy loves Los Angeles, and we've been anchored here for nearly 40 years," Homeboy Industries founder Father Greg Boyle said. "We serve the city; 10,000 folks a year walk through our doors, wanting to reimagine their lives."Boyle said the Games mimic the business model of inclusion; they are for everyone.Last month, applications for another LA28 program opened: the LA Authentic Program. Hoover said it will be the largest integration of restaurants, caterers, food trucks, carts, and mobile vendors in Olympic history."So, between our local food concessions and our new Made for Two-Eight licensing program, we are opening a different door to ensure that neighborhood entrepreneurs thrive," Hoover said.Priority will be given to Made for Two- Eight applications for businesses in the host city of Los Angeles. The opportunity to apply begins on Oct. 30. Small businesses must meet qualifications under the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) size standards.

title: Boosie gets speeding ticket and help with suspended license during South Fulton traffic stop
description: Rapper Boosie received a speeding ticket in South Fulton on Friday, but the traffic stop also brought help with a suspended driver's license, according to police.
content: Rapper Boosie received a speeding ticket in South Fulton on Friday, but the traffic stop also brought help with a suspended driver's license, according to police.Officers conducting speed enforcement on South Fulton Parkway stopped the rapper on Oct. 16 and discovered his license was suspended, the South Fulton Police Department said in a statement.Boosie told officers that another police department had informed him of the suspension during a separate traffic stop earlier that day.A South Fulton officer helped him navigate the Georgia Department of Driver Services' online reinstatement process, including paying the required fee.
