title: At least 3 Colorado lawmakers receive suspicious letters containing white powder
description: Multiple Colorado lawmakers confirmed on Monday that they had received suspicious letters in the mail containing a white powder.
content: Multiple Colorado lawmakers confirmed on Monday that they had received suspicious letters in the mail containing a white powder.A statement from U.S. Rep. Neguse's office said, "Today a suspicious letter containing white powder was delivered to Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse's district office in Boulder County. The matter is now being investigated by Federal authorities, including the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, FBI, and U.S. Capitol Police. "Public officials across the country have reported receiving similar letters containing an unknown white powder. These include many election officials and congressional offices.Deputy Chief Inspector at the USPIS Brendan Donahue told CBS, "We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable," Donahue said. "Our partners, including the FBI and we at the Postal Inspection Service, will bring all of our resources to bear on these investigations."Neguse said that, so far, none of those letters have been determined to contain hazardous substances.Letters were also sent to the offices of U.S. Rep. Jason Crow and U.S. Rep. Brittany Pettersen. Pettersen's office told CBS Colorado that the FBI responded immediately and retrieved the envelope for testing. The U.S. Postal Service intercepted another suspicious letter addressed to U.S. Sen. John Hickenlooper's office.A statement released by Crow said:"Earlier today, my congressional office in Aurora received a letter with a suspicious substance. This appears to be one of many unfortunate instances across the country where congressional offices have received mail containing unknown, suspicious substances.My staff is safe, and our district office remains open for those who need assistance. Attempts to intimidate me or my team will not stop our work on behalf of Coloradans.I want to thank the FBI, U.S. Capitol Police, Aurora Police Department, and other law enforcement for swiftly working to investigate this matter and keeping everyone safe."Neguse also thanked law enforcement for responding quickly to the threat and said it will not deter him from serving his constituents:"I take seriously the safety of my staff and the community I represent, and I'd like to extend my gratitude to the local and Federal law enforcement officials who acted swiftly to respond to reports of a threatening letter with suspicious substances being sent to our district office in Boulder County. Because of them, there is no continued threat to public safety in the area.The nature of this mailing, and others like it being received by elected officials across the country, whether to cause physical harm or provoke unease among public servants, will not prevent me and my team from working day in and day out to serve the people of Colorado's 2nd District. It's clear that there has been a real, palpable sense of fear percolating in communities across the country lately. And while we know that fear can be contagious, I firmly believe that so is hope. I'll continue to do everything in my power to choose hope — and to stand up for the people of Colorado."

title: Somerville hopes "Neighborways" will stop Boston drivers using side streets as traffic shortcuts: "A game of chicken"
description: Somerville, Massachusetts is using "Neighborways" to discourage drivers who cut through side streets to get around Boston traffic.
content: Somerville, Massachusetts is trying to discourage drivers who use GPS maps to cut through neighborhood side streets to get around Boston traffic.The city has installed so-called Neighborways to slow traffic, improve safety and reduce stress on neighborhood roads that weren't meant to become thruways."I think a Neighborway to me is just a side street that's an unofficial pedestrian bikeway," Somerville City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin told WBZ-TV.One of them just opened on Tufts Street. A key feature is bump outs in the curbs and pavement.McLaughlin said drivers in other spots ignore their attempts to halt cut-through driving."This is kind of the best way of dealing with it, is to change the actual structure of the road. So yeah, you can still drive through here if you want, but you're going to drive slow and you might want to pick a better road to ride on," he said.Bill Trudell pedaled through here from Arlington just to test it out."Cars just take these side roads and giant trucks and they zip down them and it's an accident waiting to happen," Trudell told WBZ.Now it's a challenge. Drivers have to stop at the pinch points to let one car through at a time."It's two raised curbs, so you're playing a game of chicken with the person in front of you," said resident John Chandler. He drives and bikes the street but said there's a learning curve and it's working."I don't hear nearly as much car noise, so I think that it is kind of deterring people from using it," Chandler said.Now bikers have a new way to commute where they are the right of way."If this road wasn't built like this, the cars riding by us would be driving 10 miles an hour faster," McLaughlin said.

title: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over waiving Russia sanctions
description: President Trump is defending his decision to waive sanctions, which will refill Russia's pocketbooks as it attacks Ukraine.
author_name: Kathryn  Watson, Caitlin  Yilek, Kaia  Hubbard
content: Washington — President Trump is getting bipartisan blowback over his surprise decision to waive new sanctions on Russia two days before they were to go into effect.Congress approved the bipartisan legislation — championed by the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, who died before it was passed — and it was signed into law by Mr. Trump on Sept. 18. It also comes as a blow to Graham's legacy, given that the senator, a close friend of Mr. Trump, pushed the legislation as one of his final acts. But Mr. Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Ukraine, and on Monday criticized Ukraine, even as Russia continues to strike civilian sites in Ukraine. "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine, they haven't been doing much," the president told reporters on the White House South Lawn Monday. He added, "We've given a lot to Ukraine, they've given us nothing." In its most recent strikes, Russia recently hit Ukraine energy and infrastructure, as well as a medical clinic, school, metro station and residential buildings, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday. The economic restrictions were intended to penalize top Russian figures and the biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas as the U.S. seeks to end Russian President Vladimir Putin's four-year war in Ukraine. But the legislation gives Mr. Trump the authority to waive parts of the law if he certifies to Congress that halting the sanctions is "in the national interests of the United States." The Trump administration is facing intense pressure to act to bring down fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections."I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act," Mr. Trump said in an executive order issued Friday. "I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States."The order did not explain Mr. Trump's decision, which came a week after the president eased sanctions on Russia's energy sector and announced a deal with Putin to import diesel to the U.S. market."Beyond irresponsible," GOP Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina said of the president's latest move, calling it "unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine and butchers innocent civilians every single day.""If the president wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin," Tillis added. The 300,000 tons of diesel the U.S. is buying from Russia is about 2.2 million barrels — and that's just over half the 4.1 million barrels of diesel the U.S. uses in a single day. And since Ukraine has damaged much of Russia's refining capacity, it's unclear when Russia would be able to deliver the fuel. Experts say the deal with Russia will not offset the disruptions to oil supplies resulting from the Iran war.GOP Sen. John Cornyn of Texas agrees and said of the sanction waiver, "Lindsey would be appalled.""Helping Putin in Ukraine is reckless," Cornyn said. "He would not stop with Ukraine and our NATO allies would be next. Putin is fanatically committed to restoring Russia's glory days, calling the collapse of the Soviet Union "the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the century" and claiming Russia was "robbed" in the breakup."Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that he shared his colleagues' position, arguing that "capitulating to a bully generally means they're going to make more demands going forward.""That's the problem with taking sort of a business negotiation approach to negotiating with a thug, which is what Vladimir Putin is," he said.Several House Republicans also railed against the president's move."The president is prolonging the war, not ending it," GOP Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska wrote Friday. On Saturday, Bacon added that Mr. Trump's "agenda is dead." "The President has an agenda: supplemental, reconciliation, Ballroom, etc.," Bacon wrote. "Many of us won't fund these things knowing he is propping up a dictator's invasion and throwing an ally under the bus." GOP Rep. Michael McCaul, former chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, urged Mr. Trump to reconsider. "Time and again, we have seen how Putin responds to American concessions: with contempt for the United States and increased violence against innocent Ukrainians," he said Saturday. Rep. Gregory Meeks of New York, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said the waiver should come as no surprise. Meeks had argued against the bill's passage, saying it would expand the presidential tariff authorities. "He has had the power to sanction Russia for years. What he lacks is the will," Meeks said in a statement Saturday. "By giving the Russian economy life support, Trump's deal with the devil keeps getting dirtier," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, who represents New York, said in a separate statement. The president's decision to waive Russia sanctions was also met with immediate criticism and concern from Zelenskyy. Earlier this month, Mr. Trump said Ukraine should "get a new leader." Zelenskyy told reporters last week he thinks the president's actions that contradict the intent of the Lindsey Graham Act would continue, "unfortunately." "It's unfortunate because we all had great respect for Lindsey," Zelenskyy said. "He devoted his life to America. We had an excellent relationship with him. And shortly before the tragedy, Lindsey was in Ukraine. He always supported us very strongly and pushed for as much assistance to Ukraine as possible. It's difficult without him, I'll be honest. I want to thank both Democrats and Republicans who supported his bill. That was a major victory: this truly bipartisan support. And now, the decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me. And it definitely helps only the Russians."On Sunday, Mr. Trump sought to explain the sanctions waiver by saying he didn't want to drive Russia away from the negotiating table. "My decision on Russia is a very simple one," he wrote on Truth Social in the face of rising public criticism. "I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table."But Mr. Trump has long touted a friendlier relationship with Putin, a departure from all of his predecessors. New photos of Mr. Trump with both Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping adorn the White House's Palm Room, where reporters exit and enter the White House to see the president's take off and land from Marine One. Mr. Trump has blasted Ukraine for striking diesel refineries in Russia. He has called on both Ukraine and Russia to end the war, although Russia started it, and could end the war by withdrawing all occupying troops and stopping its attacks. Mr. Trump is facing political pressure to lower gas prices, two weeks out from midterm elections in which Republicans are expected to struggle. The cost of living and gas prices remain top issues for voters, with the Iran war driving up gas and diesel prices and pushing overall inflation higher, too. Mr. Trump has claimed the war will end once the midterm elections are over, although it's unclear how, and that gas prices will drop precipitously then. At the same time, Ukrainian officials have recently been reporting difficulties with Starlink, the commercial satellite network owned by SpaceX's Elon Musk, and Starshield, the military version built on the same network. Zelenskyy said over the weekend that the throttling of Starshield network speeds has meant that Ukraine has been unable to use its interceptors to shoot down Russian Shahed drones, has prompted questions about who was behind the slowdown. Mr. Trump on Friday denied he had limited Ukraine's access to Starlink, and added he didn't believe Musk was responsible either. Musk said last Wednesday he isn't responsible for deciding how Starshield is used, writing on X: "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."Secretary of State Marco Rubio also told reporters Saturday that the administration had "nothing to do with that." On Monday, Mr. Trump said he didn't know who ordered the interruption, "but I'd like to find out." The explanations haven't satisfied a number of lawmakers, including some Republicans. Last week, a bipartisan group of nine senators, including Republican Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Susan Collins of Maine, John Cornyn of Texas and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, asked the Defense Department inspector general to investigate. They asked the IG to look into "whether actions or decisions by the Department of Defense or its contractors contributed to these dangerous circumstances.""Any restrictions on these capabilities, particularly without advance notification, raise serious questions about the Department of Defense's contractual oversight and its responsibility to ensure continuity of essential services," the senators wrote in the letter.Cramer and GOP Rep. Mike Turner of Ohio also joined growing calls for a congressional investigation into the move on "Face the Nation" Sunday. "There needs to be an investigation; we need to find out who these people are because lives are at risk and lives are lost over these things," Turner said.Tillis and Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut hosted a video call with Zelenskyy Monday, and said he confirmed that "critical Starlink services remain degraded," impeding Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones. The senators said Zelenskyy also reported disruptions to U.S. intelligence sharing regarding early warning of Russian ballistic missile launches. The pair said Zelenskyy also raised "serious concerns" about critical air defense interceptor delays and Mr. Trump's decision to waive sanctions against Russia."Trying to appease a murderous thug like Vladimir Putin will only prolong this war and bring greater casualties," Tillis and Blumenthal said.

title: Frisco city leaders to discuss economic development agreement for Toyota Stadium
description: A new hotel and convention center are part of the suggested plan.
content: Frisco city leaders will take a closer look at a proposed economic development agreement on Tuesday that would bring more businesses near the home of FC Dallas.The proposed agreement aims to add a 250-bed hotel near the stadium, along with a 15,000 square-foot convention center, 30,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, and parking garage improvements on the Toyota Stadium and Soccer Center campus. It would build upon mixed-use development agreements approved in September 2024. The city and the developer, identified as DP6 Hotel & CC, would apply for state incentives through the qualified hotel project program.If approved, the proposal says that the eligible state hotel and sales taxes generated by the project would then be passed from the state through the city to the developer. City funds would not be used for state incentive payments, and the proposal says the developer would pay application-related consultant and legal costs. The city would also provide 50% of the city hotel occupancy tax collected from the new hotel for 10 years, capped at $5 million, and it would waive 50% of the city development fees for improvements covered by the agreement. The proposal says the hotel and convention center are expected to bring in more visitors, meetings, and events to the Toyota Stadium campus. It also notes that grant payments are dependent upon meeting the agreement's performance requirements and receiving applicable tax revenues.

title: Crash-and-grab burglars target jewelry store in Chicago's Rogers Park neighborhood
description: Crash-and-grab burglars target jewelry store in Rogers Park
content: Thieves raided a jewelry store in a crash-and-grab burglary in Chicago's Rogers Park neighborhood early Tuesday morning.At 5:02 a.m., a Honda sedan of an unspecified model struck the front of Fanny's Jewelry at 6981 N. Clark St., police said.Inside, the thieves took property from inside, and fled the scene in another vehicle nearby.Video showed an entire wall missing from the jewelry store.No one was injured, police said. Belmont Area detectives were investigating.

title: Perot Museum of Nature and Science announces expansion, adding hands-on attractions and outdoor space
description: Officials told CBS News Texas that the project's groundbreaking is expected to begin in early 2027, with completion in late 2028.
content: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas has announced plans to expand. Leaders are expected to unveil the design on Tuesday, which will nearly double the campus's size with new experiences for visitors.Officials told CBS News Texas that the project's groundbreaking is expected to begin in early 2027, with completion in late 2028. The museum will expand by at least four acres, doubling exhibit space with 60,000 sq. ft. of outdoor science experiences. The new area will feature hands-on attractions, including a mist maze, geysers, a lightning and thunder pavilion, a giant water vortex and a fire tornado, officials said. The project will also add new green space, upgraded amenities, and improved access for school groups. So far, officials said the museum has reached $135 million of its $185 million fundraising campaign. Once finished, the expansion is expected to attract an additional 400,000 visitors each year.

title: Angel Reese leads Dream to first WNBA Finals win with 30 points and 16 rebounds
description: Angel Reese wanted to leave her mark on Game 2. She delivered a performance that gave the Atlanta Dream their first WNBA Finals victory.
content: Angel Reese wanted to leave her mark on Game 2. She delivered a performance that gave the Atlanta Dream their first WNBA Finals victory.Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds as Atlanta beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 on Monday, tying the series at one game apiece."I let my team down last game, not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said. "I wanted to make sure that I came out tonight and left my mark and do what I could to win, and I think I did that tonight."Allisha Gray added 18 points, and Jordin Canada finished with 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds. Rhyne Howard set a WNBA Finals single-game record with six steals. Atlanta led 39-37 at halftime before taking control with a 21-9 third quarter. The Dream carried a 60-46 advantage into the fourth and led by as many as 21 points.Reese shot 10-of-16 from the field and made 9 of 11 free throws. She became the youngest player in WNBA history to record a double-double with at least 20 points in the Finals and the first Dream player with consecutive Finals double-doubles."We feed off her energy," Canada said. "She was talking to us the whole game, keeping us confident."Atlanta's defense helped make up for another difficult shooting night. The Dream shot 33.9% but collected 14 steals and forced 19 turnovers, turning those mistakes into 24 points. Atlanta also outscored Golden State 19-0 on fast breaks.Coach Karl Smesko said the Dream focused on correcting defensive breakdowns, rebounding and improving their offense after reviewing film."Even though we didn't shoot it great again, our shot quality was better, our pace was better," Smesko said. "I thought the players did a great job taking from film, taking what we emphasized and then making it a reality on the floor. All the credit to them."Atlanta made 30 of 35 free throws and held a 17-7 advantage in second-chance points.Tiffany Hayes and Gabby Williams scored 14 points apiece for Golden State. Veronica Burton added 11, while Kiah Stokes had 11 rebounds and four blocks.The series now shifts to Atlanta for Game 3.

title: Colorado town votes to construct entrance gate amid traffic dispute with Denver, Littleton
description: Bow Mar, a small town in Colorado, sits between Denver and Littleton, and community leaders have been pushing back against drivers who use local streets as shortcuts.
content: Bow Mar, a small town in Colorado, sits between Denver and Littleton, and community leaders have been pushing back against drivers who use local streets as shortcuts. Now, the town is moving forward with plans to construct a gate at one of its entrances.The town's population is about 950, but a traffic study found that about 1,200 vehicles travel through the community every day. The study says a majority of those drivers do not live in Bow Mar.The town says the traffic puts children, retirees and seniors in the community at risk. It has introduced speed bumps, installed "kids at play" signs, and lowered the speed limit to 20 mph in order to calm traffic, but residents tell CBS Colorado that they still have safety concerns.Bow Mar leaders proposed building controlled-access gates at two of the town's three main entrances and closing a smaller entrance near Tufts Avenue.Denver and Littleton leaders opposed the idea. Both cities asked Bow Mar to pause the proposal and work with them on a different solution. They argued that "Bow Mar undoubtedly expects its residents to have reasonable access to Denver and Littleton roads and rights-of-way. Denver and Littleton expect the same in turn."Denver City Councilman Kevin Flynn told CBS Colorado that the plan to close off public streets would disrupt traffic and create safety concerns by cutting off access to the traffic signal at Quincy Avenue and Sheridan Boulevard.But a car found in Bowles Lake on Wednesday renewed community calls for action.On Monday, the town's board of trustees announced unanimous approval to move forward with an engineering firm in Bow Mar. They said the first gate could be installed as early as Thanksgiving, but won't be operational until mid-January, and added that the town will release more information about construction at the Sheridan entrance in the coming weeks.Bow Mar did not clarify how the gate would operate or whether it would be closed during rush hours or 24/7. Town leaders said this is something that will be discussed, and they hope to have a decision soon.They also shared that the town will measure the impact of the current project before moving forward with any additional gates, but it does not currently have accident report data. Last week, CBS Colorado submitted multiple requests for accident data to Columbine Valley Police (who cover Bow Mar) and has not yet heard back.

title: Newport Beach prepares for potential king tides next week by declaring local emergency
description: The new declaration comes just weeks after the city experienced severe flooding on the Balboa Peninsula.
content: In preparation for potential coastal flooding that can pour into low-lying neighborhoods, Newport Beach declared a local emergency and activated other protocols on Monday night, nearly a week before the anticipated event."Exceptionally high tides" are anticipated between Monday and Wednesday of next week, the city said, the first in a series of king tide events expected to continue into the new year. During Monday's city council meeting, Newport Beach also activated its Emergency Operations Center in an effort to coordinate plans more effectively as conditions change rapidly.Also approved on Monday was a contract for the West Newport Beach Sand Replenishment Project, allowing about 100,000 cubic yards of sand from the Santa Ana River to be placed along eroded beach areas between 36th and 62nd Streets. That sand will replenish beaches affected by recent storms. The project is expected to begin next week.The city said upcoming king tides have the potential to cause flooding along the Balboa Peninsula, islands in Newport Harbor and other areas. Less than two weeks ago, urban flooding on the Balboa Peninsula disrupted daily life for residents and forced an additional local emergency declaration."It was honestly life-threatening," resident Gary Winthrop said about the coastal flooding on Oct. 10. "We were pretty scared it was going to come into the house. But thankfully we got sandbags pretty quick, all the neighbors were super supportive."Newport Beach told the public it's taking "proactive measures" to reduce upcoming flooding impacts, including the reinforcement of beach berms and positioning of sandbags in flood-prone locations.The city urged residents to take the following actions to protect their homes and property:Placing sandbags or temporary flood barriers along all vulnerable areas, including seawalls, garages, doorways and other low-lying openings.Inspect waterfront walls and private flood protection measures for potential vulnerabilities.Clear debris from private drains, gutters and drainage areas.Relocate vehicles, particularly low-clearance vehicles, away from flood-prone streets and parking areas.Avoid walking or driving through flooded streets and follow posted warnings and temporary road closures.Free prefilled sandbags are being provided at the following locations:Corporation Yard, 592 Superior Ave.Marina Park, 1600 W. Balboa Blvd.Temporary Fire Station No. 1, East Ocean Front Parking Lot near Balboa PierFor ongoing updates, residents are encouraged to:Sign up for Newport Notified emergency alerts at NBPD.org to receive important public safety notifications.Follow @CityofNewportBeach on Instagram and Facebook and the City's official Nextdoor account for updates on coastal conditions, road closures, and other important information.

title: Meet the childhood pals behind Minnesota's Plucky Pickle Dip
description: What started as a food experiment between two childhood friends has grown into a snack brand sold in thousands of stores across the country.
content: What started as a food experiment between two childhood friends has grown into a snack brand sold in thousands of stores across the country.Sara Doherty and Britt Jungerberg, co-owners of Plucky Pickle Dip, have been friends since ninth grade, when they bonded over food in their school cafeteria.Years later, the two started experimenting with recipes while hosting get-togethers with family and friends. One recipe quickly became a favorite: pickle dip."We were making a pickle dip that everybody loved," Doherty said.Plucky Pickle Dip was born. The friends started selling their dip at Minneapolis farmers markets in 2017.The dip's base combines cream cheese and white beans, blended smooth with either kosher dill or bread-and-butter pickles, depending on the flavor.Today, Plucky Pickle Dip comes in five varieties: Original Dill, Cheddar Mustard, Spicy Pickle, Sweet Pickle and Sweet and Spicy."It [pickles] is like a perfect ingredient. It's acidic. It's salty. You can get savory. It's a perfect ingredient for us to use," Jungerberg said.The dip can be served simply with vegetables or crackers, but the pair said its versatility is part of what makes it popular. The duo share simple, few-ingredient recipes on their website. The dip can also be mixed with tuna or chicken, used as a burger topping or stirred into egg yolks for a quick egg salad."We've got a lot of different options and usage occasions for each of them," Jungerberg said. The business has grown far beyond those early farmers market days. The snack brand is now sold in about 2,600 stores nationwide, including Target, Lunds & Byerlys and Kowalski's.For Doherty and Jungerberg, building the company together has been just as important as the product itself.The friends have gone through major life milestones together, from graduation and jobs to maternity leave and raising families. They've also navigated the challenges of launching a food company while working full-time jobs and raising young children.For several years, the pair made their product themselves in a rental kitchen, wearing hairnets and working through the production process after their day jobs.Eventually, they were able to move from the commissary kitchen to a professional manufacturer — a milestone Jungerberg said was one of the best moments of the company's journey.And through it all, they've had each other."We get to bounce things off of each other and always have each other to make the decisions with," Doherty said. "I just couldn't imagine being the only one making the decisions or going through the journey by yourself.""There's so many Minnesota brands that are killing it right now," she said. "So that's fun, too, to be a part of it."From a school cafeteria to Minneapolis farmers markets and now supermarket shelves across the country."It's her and I playing with it in the kitchen and seeing what makes sense," Doherty said.The pair said they're excited to keep growing — and they're always interested in hearing how customers are using their dip in new ways.WCCO is always looking for local businesses to highlight in its Homegrown MN series.If you know of a Minnesota business that should be featured, email Beret Leone at Beret.Leone@cbs.com.

title: Video shows Long Beach man, a U.S. citizen, injured during apparent ICE operation
description: The video, which has now gone viral, shows masked federal agents dressed in uniforms bearing the words "Police ICE" restraining the man.
content: Video shows the moment a Long Beach man was allegedly injured during an arrest following an apparent Immigration and Customs Enforcement operation over the weekend. The man has been identified by his family and Rep. Robert Garcia, who represents California's 42nd congressional district, as Ricardo Gonzalez, a U.S. citizen. The video, which has now gone viral, shows masked federal agents dressed in uniforms bearing the words "Police ICE" restraining Gonzalez. While on the ground, he can be heard yelling that his arm was broken. It is unclear what led up to the arrest. In a statement to CBS LA, a spokesperson for ICE said agents were conducting a targeted enforcement operation to "arrest an at-large criminal illegal alien." The spokesperson added that during the operation, anti-ICE agitators attempted to impede, damaging government vehicles "despite officers giving lawful commands.""Officers followed their training and used the minimum amount of force," the statement said. "ICE did NOT hit an individual on a bike. An individual was arrested after he smashed the mirror of a government vehicle."ICE officials said the person was transferred to the custody of local police. The department is investigating potential charges for the damage to a government vehicle. In an online post, Gonzalez's daughter said her father was struck by an ICE vehicle and "tased twice, pinned to the ground, and taken to the hospital for serious injuries."Garcia posted on X alleging ICE agents "brutally attacked and broke the arm of a North Long Beach resident and U.S. citizen.""The videos are horrific and should concern not just our community but the country," Garcia wrote. "Long Beach stands with our community and our immigrant families. ICE is not welcome in Long Beach."During a news conference on Monday, Garcia called the incident "incredibly disturbing" and added that there should be an investigation into what took place."The immigration actions, the terror that happened in North Long Beach over the weekend, is not welcome in our city or our community," Garcia said.When asked by reporters about the incident on Monday, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said he didn't believe it was a criminal operation and added that DHS was conducting its immigration enforcement. "There may be charges coming out of that," Essayli said. "I'm not sure; it has not been presented to my office yet."In a statement, the Long Beach Police Department said it responded to an incident on Saturday after ICE "requested emergency assistance" due to "vehicle vandalism taking place and a subject in need of medical aid.""Upon arrival, officers observed a large group disturbance involving the ICE agents," the department said. "One officer located a handcuffed male adult, being detained by ICE, who was bleeding."The department added that officers were "not involved in any immigration enforcement and LBPD personnel did not make any arrests."

title: Colorado residents can apply to college for free this week as part of statewide program
description: This week, Coloradans looking to pursue higher education can save money while doing so. The ninth annual Colorado Free Application Days are Tuesday, Oct. 20 through Thursday, Oct. 22.
content: This week, Coloradans looking to pursue higher education can save money while doing so. The ninth annual Colorado Free Application Days are Tuesday, Oct. 20 through Thursday, Oct. 22.All 32 public colleges and universities in Colorado and several private institutions allow students to apply for free in the month of October, as part of the Free Application Days.Colorado leads the nation in the percentage of residents who have some type of college-level education, with 62.9% having a certificate, certification, or degree, data shows. The statewide program encourages residents to continue that trend, like West High School Senior Mahi Hardiman. "I want to be a photographer, study photography, fashion design, and look into engineering," he said.Denver Scholarship Foundation College Advisor Yosedit Romero is alongside him for the journey, helping make it happen. "My main role is to support students and their families through the college-going process. So, we support by asking questions, providing resources, and getting them involved from 9th through 12th grade for whatever they want to do.""They start almost like a caterpillar, right?" she said with a hand gesture and smile. "They're developing and doing all the things, and they blossom into a butterfly by the time they get to graduation and take these big adult steps."She highly recommends taking advantage of Free Application Days. "Really setting the stepping stones to apply to a couple of colleges, see what's out there, what are the options. If you don't apply, you're closing your own doors on yourself. It really does add up when you think one college is $50 and another college is $75, and an out-of-state one is $100.""That will help me a lot, knowing I didn't come from money. I'll use it to my advantage to apply to schools that I want to go to," Hardiman said. So, his future at his top schools is looking brighter than ever. "My number one choice is CSU - Fort Collins. Then probably CU Boulder, and the University of Northern Colorado."Students can apply online by following the Colorado Free Application Day instructions.

title: ATM taken during crash-and-grab burglary at BP gas station on Chicago's Uptown neighborhood
description: An ATM was taken during a crash-and-grab burglary at a BP gas station in Chicago's Uptown neighborhood early Tuesday morning.
content: An ATM was taken during a crash-and-grab burglary at a BP gas station in Chicago's Uptown neighborhood early Tuesday morning. Chicago police said a blue Jeep crashed into the gas station in the 5100 block of North Broadway around 3:30 a.m.Police said a witness reported seeing three people get out of another sport-utility vehicle at the scene and enter the gas station. The witness said the group took an ATM and drove off in a black SUV with the driver of the Jeep. It is not clear how much money was taken. No injuries were reported. Belmont Area detectives are investigating

title: Arlington city leaders to consider clarifying AT&T Stadium agreement with Cowboys
description: The Cowboys are still expected to fund and complete improvements by 2043.
content: The Arlington City Council is looking at an amended lease agreement with the Dallas Cowboys that clarifies what the city will pay to maintain AT&T Stadium and what the team will pay for.A resolution the council is set to consider offers more details. The proposal clarifies that the city's contribution covers the actual costs of maintaining, operating, and managing the stadium. The Cowboys, meanwhile, must fund and complete improvements specified in the Master Agreement by 2043.Those improvements include hardening perimeters, building pedestrian bridges, adding security screening shacks, getting more security cameras, adding more venue parking, digital signage, kitchen and concession build-outs, and improvements to the stadium plaza, among others. Improvements to the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems are also included in what the Cowboys are expected to pay for.The proposed changes follow the city's approval of a $273 million stadium deal earlier this year, despite concerns from residents who have called for a referendum to let voters decide. The Cowboys have offered to pay for all the upgrades up front, with the city paying them back $50 million in 2028 and $20 million every year after through 2048.

title: Air quality alert in place for parts of the Pittsburgh area today
description: The Mon Valley in southern Allegheny County is usually the area most impacted by poor air quality.
content: An air quality alert is in place today for parts of the Pittsburgh area.Any alert days ahead? Nope. There are frost advisories in place for a couple of places this morning. Air quality alert in place for Allegheny County.Aware: Patchy fog in place today. Conditions look to be more conducive to fog on Wednesday & Thursday mornings Steelers in Paris: Dry for game day with game-time temperatures in the upper 50s. Rain chance for Saturday.High pressure that responsible for our current seasonal weather pattern, anchored over the Great Lakes region will cause conditions favorable for low air quality. Air quality will likely be the worst for the hours starting at sunrise and continuing for the next two to three hours. Very fine particles, those of PM2.5 or smaller, are the biggest concern. This means surgical masks won't be much help for those who have respiratory issues. N95 respirators will filter out these fine particles that come from factory emissions. While these emissions are always present, wind speeds and mixing in the atmosphere often help to filter these particles down to levels that aren't too harmful for us. High pressure causes sinking air, trapping these particles close to the surface. This, along with light wind speeds, means little mixing in the atmosphere to 'water down' the impact. The Mon Valley in southern Allegheny County is usually the area most impacted by poor air quality. Atmospheric conditions will continue to be conducive to poor air quality, especially during morning hours, through at least Thursday morning and probably through the weekend.High pressure also means the stretch of pleasant weather will continue. Yesterday, high temperatures reached the mid to upper 60s across our area after a chilly start to the day. We should see highs back into the upper 60s today. I have Pittsburgh seeing a high of 67 degrees with sunny skies and light winds coming from the north. There will be some patchy fog around, especially north of I-80. Sunset is at 6:33 p.m.Model data shows that fog chances both Wednesday and Thursday morning will be even more conducive to fog than this morning. We could see a fog advisory issued for those mornings. Morning lows, similar to this morning, should dip into the 30s most places. I have highs also remaining in the upper 60s. Dew points will tick up slightly, and this is the reason for the higher fog chance.The weekend is looking pleasant with highs on Friday in the low 60s. Saturday highs should be in the mid-60s, with highs near 70 on Sunday and Monday.

title: Tuesday begins on cool side as Philadelphia region's sunny week continues. Here's the weather forecast.
description: After a beautifully sunny Monday, Tuesday will keep the trend running.
content: Another beautiful fall day ahead! We're starting off chilly, but plenty of sunshine will send temperatures into the lower 70s this afternoon. We'll start the day with temps in the low-mid 40s in most spots, with temperatures in Philadelphia closer to 50 degrees. Sunshine will get to work early, and warm temperatures will reach the mid-60s by lunchtime before peaking in the low 70s Tuesday afternoon.Most of the week looks dry and seasonable around Philadelphia, with highs dropping back into the 60s on Wednesday. NEXT big weather changesThe big story is the nor'easter offshore, bringing several rounds of coastal flooding, strong northeast winds and beach erosion to the Jersey Shore. Low pressure strengthening off the Carolina coast will start to turn north, while high pressure remains anchored to our north. The tightening pressure gradient between these systems will produce a prolonged period of northeast winds, pushing water toward the beaches and into the back bays.Minor flooding is expected around this evening's high tide, with Wednesday evening still looking like the highest-risk cycle. Some moderate flooding is possible in vulnerable back-bay communities before conditions gradually improve Thursday. Coastal flood advisories are in effect Tuesday afternoon and evening, with minor tidal flooding expected around high tide. Additional moderate flooding is possible Wednesday, with the Wednesday evening high tide currently looking like the greatest concern. Minor to locally moderate flooding could affect low-lying roads and back bay communities, especially where water doesn't fully drain between tide cycles. Northeast wind gusts of 30–35 mph and seas of 7–12 feet could also lead to dangerous marine conditions and additional beach erosion.For Philadelphia and our inland suburbs, the forecast is much quieter. A northeast breeze will pick up Tuesday, but become more noticeable Wednesday, with highs dropping into the mid-60s.The coastal storm should begin to pull away Thursday, allowing winds and water levels to gradually subside. The rest of the week looks relatively quiet, with a mix of sunshine and clouds and temperatures generally in the 60s.Another push of some cooler air will arrive Friday and keep high temperatures Friday afternoon in the low 60s. By Friday night, temperatures will likely return to the mid-upper 30s.The weekend currently looks mainly dry and seasonable, with temperatures warming back to near 70 degrees by Sunday and Monday.Here's your 7-day forecast:Tuesday: Sunny. High 72, Low 49Wednesday: Sunny. High 65, Low 48Thursday: Sunny. High 69, Low 46Friday: Sunny. High 62, Low 46Saturday: Sunny. High 64, Low 39Sunday: Sunny. High 68, Low 40Monday: Sunny. title: Man, 42, fatally struck by combine in southern Minnesota
description: A 42-year-old man is dead after he was hit by a combine in Sand Creek Township, Minnesota, on Sunday afternoon, the Scott County Sheriff's Office said.
content: A 42-year-old man is dead after he was hit by a combine in Sand Creek Township, Minnesota, on Sunday afternoon, the Scott County Sheriff's Office said.The incident near the 17000 block of Baseline Avenue was reported to emergency personnel around 3:33 p.m. Responding deputies and officers found the man, who had sustained serious injuries, the sheriff's office said.According to officials, the man died at the scene despite lifesaving efforts by deputies, the Jordan Fire Department and Allina Health Emergency Medical Services.Investigators are working to learn the circumstances surrounding the collision. The sheriff's office says the Hennepin County Medical Examiner's Office will positively identify the man.Sand Creek Township is around 35 miles southwest of Minneapolis.

title: FAA flags 2 near midair collisions at airport in Colorado, restricts parallel takeoffs at Centennial
description: The Federal Aviation Administration is restricting takeoffs at Centennial Airport after identifying dozens of safety-related incidents, including two verified near-midair collisions.
content: The Federal Aviation Administration is restricting takeoffs at Centennial Airport after identifying dozens of safety-related incidents, including two verified near-midair collisions. Local flight schools say the changes are disrupting training, with one instructor saying they are losing business as pilots look for other airports.CBS Colorado obtained a new FAA safety assessment outlining the agency's concerns. The report reviewed flights from May 2025 through April 2026 and classified Centennial Airport's parallel departures as high risk for safety incidents involving deviation or "drift resulting in unmitigated convergence."The FAA directed air traffic management at Centennial Airport to pause simultaneous departures from parallel runways on Oct. 1. The FAA's assessment is dated Sept. 29, and a memo to an air traffic official is dated Sept. 30. The airport says they did not receive that memo until Oct. 1.In a statement in part, Centennial Airport posted, "Neither the FAA Control Tower nor the Airport Authority received advance notice of the directive, or the standard opportunity for stakeholder engagement before the restrictions took effect..." The airport also called the move "highly unusual."The restrictions are also affecting flight schools that rely on Centennial's runways to teach student pilots.Earlier this month, pilots received a message from the airport's air traffic control tower stating: "All runways unavailable for touch and goes, pattern work."A touch-and-go is a training maneuver in which a plane lands and immediately takes off again.J.T. Murphy, an independent flight instructor at Centennial and owner of Breakthrough Aviation, said while safety is paramount, the lack of warning has impacted his business."Myself and several other instructors were kind of scrambling to find other locations to train," Murphy said, "As we have to fly to other airports, that's less time that we're able to practice the skills that are vital to becoming a private pilot."Multiple flight schools at the airport said the changes were impacting their programs as well, including pushing pilots to use more fuel to fly to farther airports to train repeated takeoffs and landings."I've had a number of students that have canceled flights and are looking at other opportunities. So that's lost business or about a 50% loss in business as they move to other airports that aren't going to cost as much to train at," Murphy said.Flight schools and airport officials share concerns beyond Centennial, as shifting training flights to other airports could put additional pressure on facilities that are already busy.The FAA's safety assessment identified concerns involving aircraft operating on Centennial's parallel runways, including planes drifting toward one another. The report included 54 recent safety-related incidents, among them two verified near-midair collisions.When Murphy was asked if the communications from the FAA came as a surprise, he said, "Absolutely. The way it came out through just a memo was very abrupt and was unusual for how the FAA normally conducts business."The FAA has not yet clarified its process for these changes, but said in a statement in part, "The FAA directed Centennial Airport (APA) air traffic management to pause simultaneous departures from parallel runways on October 1, 2026. Updated safety measures are expected to be implemented following a safety risk management panel, scheduled for later this month."The FAA has scheduled the panel for next Tuesday and Wednesday. Airport officials have also asked that local stakeholders be included in the process as the agency considers future safety measures.Centennial Airport's statement in its entirety has been posted online.

title: Roads near Westward Beach in Malibu closed after erosion exposes Los Angeles County water main
description: Westward Beach Road between the Birdview cul-de-sac and the west corner of The Sunset Restaurant will be closed until further notice.
content: Several roads near Westward Beach in Malibu are closed after additional erosion undermined the roadway and exposed a Los Angeles County water main. Malibu officials announced that Westward Beach Road between the Birdview cul-de-sac and the west corner of The Sunset Restaurant would be closed. Officials are asking the public to avoid the closed area and follow all traffic control instructions. A contractor for LA County will be using equipment and materials already on site from ongoing emergency revetment work to help prevent further erosion and damage. As an additional precaution, Water District 29 will temporarily shut off water service, affecting the Sunset Restaurant. The city officials will continue assessing conditions throughout the night to determine when the road can safely reopen.

title: Brock Purdy, 49ers hold on to defeat Commanders, stay undefeated
description: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 for their sixth straight win to open the season.
content: Brock Purdy and the offense staked San Francisco to a big lead. The defense made sure the 49ers remained undefeated. Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the 49ers made two late stops to hold off the Washington Commanders 23-17 on Monday night for their sixth straight win to open the season."You're not always happy exactly with how some of the stuff was frustrating, but real proud of the guys for just the competitive stamina to keep it going all game," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I was really proud of the defense for finding a way to overcome."The Niners followed up an emotional win last week at division-rival Seattle by building a 20-point lead and then escaping at the end when the defense stepped up.Jayden Daniels threw two touchdown passes in the second half to cut a 20-point deficit to 23-17, but Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass to Treylon Burks near the goal line with 1:54 to play to preserve the lead."I'm just reading the stem of the receiver, and then he broke out, and I was just trying to race to the pylon," Mustapha said. "Once we got to the catch point, I just wanted to be physical at the point of attack and get that ball out."Washington got the ball back at its 46 with 52 seconds remaining and moved down to the 28 before Daniels was called for intentional grounding, giving the Commanders one last play from the 40. Daniels was then sacked by Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo before he could throw up a desperation pass.The Niners extended their best start of a season since winning their first eight games in 2019 on the way to a Super Bowl appearance."We dug ourselves in a hole, and it bit us at the end of it," Daniels said. "We have to be a four-quarter team, not just a half team."Purdy started the game fast with a 24-yard strike to Mike Evans on the third play of the game and an 11-yard touchdown to George Kittle to finish that drive. Purdy went 21 of 29 for 264 yards and officially became the highest-rated passer in NFL history as he passed the 1,500-attempt threshold to qualify. His 105.6 rating is ahead of Lamar Jackson's 102.7.The Commanders were unable to bounce back from last week's tie against the New York Giants, when they mismanaged the clock in overtime to cost them a chance at a game-winning field goal.The game was one-sided early, with the 49ers scoring touchdowns on the first two drives on Purdy's pass to Kittle and a 1-yard run by McCaffrey.San Francisco expanded the lead to 20-3 late in the half on McCaffrey's second touchdown run as the Niners gained as many first downs (17) in the first half as the Commanders ran plays.The 49ers outgained Washington 303 yards to 90 in the half but were held to three first downs and 72 yards after halftime."I'm obviously a little upset with how I finish the game," Purdy said. "But I know that moving forward, every single game matters when it comes down to playoffs and getting in and all the things. So we'll take this W as a team."Washington's best chance at scoring a touchdown in the first half ended when Daniels threw the ball away on fourth-and-2 from the 13. "San Francisco's already a tough team and we spent way too much time in the first half battling ourselves," coach Dan Quinn said. "I'm sick about the ending, but we showed a lot of fight."Shanahan and Quinn renew their historyThe game featured a matchup of coaches with a history together, after Shanahan working for two years in Atlanta as offensive coordinator for Quinn. That run included a trip to the Super Bowl in the 2016 season when the Falcons blew a 28-3 lead against New England. This is the second time they've squared off as head coaches since then, with Quinn winning with Atlanta in 2019 while Shanahan won three matchups when Quinn was the defensive coordinator in Dallas.Shanahan has credited Quinn with teaching him the importance of people skills as a head coach.InjuriesCommanders: WR Terry McLaurin exited in the first quarter with a left knee injury that required an air cast before he was taken off the field on a cart. Quinn said the team fears the injury is significant. ... DT Javon Kinlaw (knee) also left in the first half. 49ers: Evans left late in the first half with Achilles tendinitis. He missed practice this week because of soreness in the tendon and broken ribs. Shanahan said Evans won't need additional testing and the injury isn't believed to be long term. ... LB Luke Gifford (groin) and DB Upton Stout (shoulder) also left the game.Up nextCommanders: After a bye, host Philadelphia on Nov. 1.49ers: Visit Atlanta on Sunday.

title: Pennsylvania nurse detained by ICE during Disneyland vacation fights to remain in U.S.
description: Monica Ryadi, a Delaware County, Pennsylvania nurse, spent two weeks in immigration detention after being arrested in California.
content: What was supposed to be a family vacation to Disneyland turned into two weeks in immigration detention for a Delaware County, Pennsylvania, nurse who was separated from her husband and 3-year-old son.Now back home in the Philadelphia area, 30-year-old Monica Ryadi is fighting to remain in the country she has lived in since childhood.Ryadi was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents at Los Angeles International Airport on Sept. 15, 2026, as her family was beginning a trip to Disneyland."I didn't think about myself. I just thought about my son, you know, the fact that he had to witness the whole thing," Ryadi said. "And when's the next time I'm going to see him?"Ryadi said her young son watched as federal agents took her into custody."He experienced the whole thing. Me being cuffed and had to walk away with these groups of men God knows where," she said.Ryadi spent two weeks in immigration detention in California before being released Sept. 29 and reunited with her family.Dispute over immigration statusRyadi came to the United States from Indonesia when she was 9 years old after her family fled religious persecution.According to the Department of Homeland Security, Ryadi legally entered the U.S. in December 2005, but her authorization to remain expired on June 29, 2006.DHS says an immigration judge issued a final order of removal in 2010.However, Ryadi's attorney, Eric Rosenfeld, disputes the government's characterization of her immigration status.Rosenfeld says Ryadi was granted withholding of removal in 2010, a form of legal protection that prevents the government from deporting someone to a country where they are likely to face persecution."Monica has been lawfully present since 2010, and she has not overstayed an order of withholding because you can't," Rosenfeld said.A withholding of removal order does not provide permanent residency or automatically eliminate a final removal order, but it generally prohibits deportation to the country covered by that protection.Nurse hopes to have ankle monitor removedRyadi was released from immigration detention last month under an order of supervision requiring GPS monitoring.On Thursday, CBS News Philadelphia accompanied Ryadi to an immigration check-in in Center City Philadelphia.Her attorney is pushing to have her ankle monitor removed, arguing that it creates an additional burden for Ryadi, who works as a nurse and spends long hours on her feet caring for patients.For Ryadi, the uncertainty extends far beyond the monitoring device.She has built a home and career in the Philadelphia area, where she lives with her husband and young son.Despite being reunited with her family, she fears another separation and the possibility of being forced to leave the country she has called home for most of her life."This is my home. I built a life here," Ryadi said. "I wouldn't know what to do if they sent me to another country."

title: Justice Department sues California, claiming it's mailing ballots to more than 20,000 noncitizens
description: The Justice Department sued California, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.
content: Washington — The Justice Department sued California on Thursday, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, came after Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter sent letters to counties earlier this week, including Los Angeles, ordering them to review a list of names of suspected noncitizens who he alleged received mail-in ballots for the upcoming midterm elections. "State-facilitated voter fraud is unacceptable in the United States of America," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement announcing the lawsuit."If found responsible in a court of law, the State of California will have seriously undermined confidence in our electoral system and violated laws that protect our nation's representative system of government."In the letter that McCotter sent to the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, he enclosed a password-protected thumb drive that he said contained names compiled by the Department of Homeland Security, and imposed a 48-hour deadline for the clerk's office to review the list.Dean Logan, the registrar-recorder and clerk, said in a statement responding to McCotter's demands that the county would not be reviewing the materials on the thumb drive because doing so would conflict with "established data privacy and information security protocols." He said the device was not considered a "secure medium."Secretary of State Shirley Weber, meanwhile, said the Justice Department had not provided the list of names and blasted the Trump administration for what it said were "unsubstantiated claims" that California had 190,000 noncitizens on its voter rolls.In Thursday's lawsuit, the Justice Department accused the state of failing to work with the federal government to correct the alleged problems with its voter rolls."The Federal Government asked California to work collaboratively to identify any noncitizens registered to vote in the State. California made no serious effort to do so," the lawsuit said. "The United States thus seeks commonplace election relief when a ballot is called into question. This Court should enjoin California from presently tabulating vote-by-mail ballots from likely noncitizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter's citizenship status can be determined," it added.In a statement provided to CBS News, the California Secretary of State's office said, "Due to the pending litigation, we have no further information we can share regarding the matter." It directed CBS News to its news release on the situation and Weber's letter to McCotter. CBS News has also reached out to the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk for comment.The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division has filed 31 lawsuits in an effort to force states to hand over unredacted copies of their voter rolls. The division has said it wants to ensure states are keeping clean voter lists, but it has since acknowledged that it also intends to share the data with the Department of Homeland Security so that the lists can be screened for noncitizens.Harmeet Dhillon, the assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division, sent letters to all 50 states in July threatening to take criminal action if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls.So far, the Justice Department has lost 26 of those cases, and has not achieved one legal victory to date. It has resorted to using publicly available voter lists and other investigative means to try to identify noncitizens who may be registered in those states.

title: 18-year-old pleads guilty to fatally stabbing teen at Long Island house party in 2025
description: An 18-year-old pleaded guilty Thursday to stabbing a teenager to death at a house party on Long Island last year.
content: An 18-year-old pleaded guilty Thursday to stabbing a teenager to death on Long Island last year.It happened on Nov. 3, 2025, at a home on Carlton Road in West Babylon, where police say 90-100 teenagers were gathered for a house party.According to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, Aiden Zachary, of Syosset, tried to get into the party, but he was asked to leave because he didn't have an invitation.Officials say Zachary, who was 17 at the time, then got into a fight with 15-year-old Liam Delemo, pulled out a knife, and stabbed Delemo in the abdomen and the arm before fleeing.Delemo's parents told CBS News New York they rushed to the scene after getting a call saying their son had been stabbed. The victim's mother said he was still conscious and alert when they arrived, and he told them, "I love you. I'm sorry."Delemo was transported to a local hospital, where he died.Zachary was arrested a week later. He pleaded guilty to first-degree manslaughter Thursday and is due back in court for sentencing on Nov. 4."This young defendant chose to escalate a dispute with a deadly weapon, resulting in the tragic death of a 15-year-old boy," District Attorney Raymond Tierney said in a statement. "Two families are now forever changed by this senseless act of violence. My office will continue to hold individuals accountable when they take a life, and I commend my Homicide Bureau for their dedication in securing justice for this young victim."Delemo's parents said their son was an only child and an 11th grade honor roll student at West Babylon High School.The homeowner, who police say let her grandchild host the party at her home, was charged with violating the county's social host law and endangering the welfare of a child.

title: Maryland AG releases body camera footage of deadly Howard County police pursuit
description: The Maryland Attorney General's Office released police body-worn camera footage from a deadly crash following a police pursuit that ended near the Howard and Anne Arundel county line on Sept. 6.
content: The Maryland Attorney General's Office released police body-worn camera footage from a deadly crash following a police pursuit that ended near the Howard and Anne Arundel county line on Sept. 6.Police said the pursuit began around 2:15 a.m. at a Royal Farms in the 7100 block of Montevideo Road in Jessup, when the driver of a 2018 Infiniti Q60 backed into a parked Howard County police cruiser that was occupied by an officer.The officer then pursued the Infiniti, which crashed into a retaining wall about a mile away.One man was pronounced dead at the scene, and two other people were taken to a hospital in stable condition, police said.Police dispatch audio indicated that all three occupants were ejected from the vehicle and that the driver was conscious after the crash.A Jessup resident told CBS News Baltimore that the Infiniti narrowly missed two utility poles. The vehicle also appeared to have struck a traffic sign and two mailboxes."They drive really crazy out here. I've been living in Howard County for the past 15 years, and there are no safe drivers," Howard County resident Jasmine Ortiz said. "Even out in Annapolis, I even work out there. They don't even put on their signal. They're zigzagging, it's ridiculous."

title: Soaring heating oil prices put struggling Maine families in a bind as winter nears: "How are we going to stay warm?"
description: The price of heating oil in Maine has soared from $3.34 per gallon one year ago to $5.97 today, a jump of roughly 79%.
content: In Freeport, Maine, Chris and Cheryl Oliver are making tough choices as they try to make ends meet on roughly $60,000 a year."Am I going to get food this week, or am I going to get gas this week?" Cheryl Oliver told CBS News. Then came another blow. Just as diesel and gas prices have risen considerably since the start of the Iran war, the price of heating oil in Maine has soared from $3.34 per gallon one year ago to $5.97 today, a jump of roughly 79%. The Olivers qualified for 100 gallons of free heating oil through a local community center, help worth about $700. Unfortunately, it still won't get them through the winter."I was panicking, like, how are we going to fill our tank and how are we going to stay warm?" Cheryl Oliver asked. Nationwide, more than 4 million households use heating oil as their primary fuel source, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, and of those, 82% are concentrated in the Northeast. Tony DiMarco, co-founder of the Freeport Wood Bank, a food pantry of sorts for firewood, said the demand right now is "extremely high." Donations keep it running. "I don't think people fully recognize how big of an impact it's going to have when heating oil costs twice as much as it did last year, and people are already spending as much as they did last year," DiMarco said. "I just don't think people fully grasp the severity of the problem."The Freeport Wood Bank is one of about 17 similar wood banks across the state. Freeport can supply about 50 families with firewood, but DiMarco says it will run out of its supply by the middle of winter. This week, DiMarco delivered two free cords of firewood to help the Olivers stretch their heating oil. It's a lifeline for a family already struggling. Chris Oliver lost one of his legs to diabetes and later suffered a heart attack. "Tony and that place, they're unbelievable," an emotional Chris Oliver said. "I don't know without them if we'd have heat."

title: Researcher visits Miami Beach addresses tied to fake businesses using stolen identities, he says
description: Georgia State professor David Maimon says criminals buy stolen identities for around $100 on dark net marketplaces to register fake businesses and open bank accounts.
content: A Georgia State University professor who studies online fraud is visiting Miami Beach addresses where he says criminals have set up fake businesses using stolen identities.David Maimon leads a cybersecurity research group at the university and also works for an identity verification firm. CBS News Miami went with him as he knocked on doors at locations around Miami Beach that he says criminals used with the stolen identities of people who no longer live in the United States."What I do for a living is trying to understand the online fraud ecosystem and how they work to prevent what they are doing," Maimon said.Maimon said dark net marketplaces frequently sell stolen identities for around $100. He said thieves use the records to register fraudulent businesses, open bank accounts, and obtain lines of credit, thereby defrauding financial institutions.He said he targeted specific addresses linked to large numbers of stolen identities used during customer onboarding at financial institutions. He has done similar research in Southern California with CBS News Miami's sister station in Los Angeles.To protect against identity theft, Maimon recommends checking your credit report often and signing up for identity theft protection services.

title: Video shows officer punching and tasing man sitting in chair on Donora porch
description: Video of an arrest in Donora that shows an officer punching a man sitting in a chair and using a Taser on him is prompting calls for an investigation.
content: Video of an arrest in Donora that shows an officer punching a man sitting in a chair and using a Taser on him is prompting calls for an investigation. The video shows Shawn Bowman sitting in a chair as an officer tries to handcuff him after being called to his home for a domestic disturbance.In the video, you see Bowman move his hand toward the officer's hands. Then the officer punches him in the face twice and uses a Taser. Bowman falls to the ground.Longtime Donora resident Dennis Hawkins Jr. said the video raises questions. "I just started shaking," Hawkins said. "I can't believe that someone in our town is going through this from a person who is supposed to protect and serve the people of this community."There's no audio on the video we reviewed, so we can't hear their exchange.In the criminal complaint, the officer writes that after he used the Taser, he repeatedly ordered Bowman to get on the ground and put his hands behind his back before Bowman eventually complied."If they're not resisting arrest or causing any threat to you, that force shouldn't be taken," Hawkins said. "It looks like a rogue officer exercising his right to do whatever he wants to do because he has a badge on," he added. Hawkins often uses his Facebook page to bring attention to community concerns. After he shared this video, questions about the officer's use of force poured in.He says the reaction goes beyond anger. "People are scared," he said. "It seems like no one is safe cause that guy was probably 60 years old." KDKA-TV took those concerns to Donora police to ask whether they were aware of the video. The chief wasn't in, and we didn't hear back by airtime.

title: Appeals court removes injunction blocking Georgia's social media age verification law
description: A federal appeals court will allow a Georgia law requiring age verification for social media accounts to go forward after a legal battle that has lasted more than a year.
content: A federal appeals court will allow a Georgia law requiring age verification for social media accounts to go forward after a legal battle that has lasted more than a year.In 2024, Georgia lawmakers passed SB 351. The law would require social media services to make "commercially reasonable efforts" to verify someone's age, without anyone who can't be verified being treated a minor.Parents of children younger than 16 would have to consent to their children joining a service, and social media companies would be limited in how they could customize ads for children younger than 16 and how much information they could collect on those children.NetChoice, a technology industry trade group, sued in federal court in Atlanta to overturn the law before it was set to take effect on July 1, 2025. U.S. District Judge Amy Totenberg then sided with the group, blocking the law until there was a full ruling on the issue."The state seeks to erect barriers to speech that cannot withstand the rigorous scrutiny that the Constitution requires," Totenberg wrote in her 2025 ruling, finding the law restricts the rights of minors, chills the right to anonymous speech online and restricts the ability of people to receive speech from social media platforms.While the law has remained in legal limbo since Totenberg's ruling, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit found in favor of the state on Thursday, vacating Totenberg's injunction. According to the court, while NetChoice could challenge the validity of the Georgia law, the group had not sufficiently argued that enforcement of the law would be unconstitutional. "It's not necessarily true that social-media websites engage exclusively in "fully protected" speech. The state contends (and no one seems to dispute) that some platforms, like X and Reddit, do host at least some pornography—which is protected for adults but, importantly, not for minors," the court's ruling reads in part.The judges found that NetChoice did not adequately address the "full range" of the law's applications, noting that the group "hasn't provided even a full list of its own members to which SB 351 applies."With the injunction vacated, the law now goes back to district court for additional proceedings.Attorney General Chris Carr called the ruling a "major win for Georgia families and a huge blow to those who would stand in the way of commonsense solutions to protect our kids.""We have said before — it shouldn't take lawsuits, investigations or legislation to do the right thing," Carr said. "This is about keeping our children safe from online predators and mental health harms. Nothing is more important."

title: Pennsylvania man who killed 8 people, including pregnant daughter, was a "controlling" patriarch, police say
description: The Pennsylvania man accused of killing eight people "exercised significant control" over his family at their Erie home, police said.
content: The Pennsylvania man accused of killing eight people, including his pregnant daughter, "exercised significant control" over his family at their Erie home, which was described as "extremely filthy" by authorities during a press conference detailing the investigation into last week's mass shooting. "There are still questions that we cannot answer, particularly about why this happened, but what we have been able to establish is a much clearer picture of the events on Friday, Oct. 9," Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said on Thursday. Matthew Stone Sr., 45, is accused of killing his wife, Michelle Stone, 44; his pregnant daughter, Angelina Stone, 24; his sons Jonathan Stone, 19, and Matthew Stone, 21; and two children, ages 1 and 5. Two people who came to the home on Perry Street, Lora Roberts, 37, and Twila Tanner, 51, were also killed. Patriarch was "controlling" Lorah said relatives told investigators that the family's patriarch, Matthew Stone Sr., had "significant control" for years over his wife and their children and grandchildren. He controlled finances and restricted when family members could leave the house, Lorah said. When detectives went inside the home after the shooting, they described the home as "extremely filthy.""The shower, toilet and kitchen sink did not appear to be working," Lorah said. "Numerous 2-liter bottles were filled with urine throughout the house." In 2019, authorities said Matthew Stone Sr. was charged with a domestic violence incident involving his wife. A firearm, the same .40 caliber handgun that was used in the mass shooting on Friday, was involved, Lorah said. The charges, however, were withdrawn after Michelle Stone changed her statement at a preliminary hearing, the police chief said.Lorah said family members raised concerns about Matthew Stone Sr.'s mental health, possible physical health problems and suspected substance abuse, including methamphetamine. Investigators couldn't find any medical records confirming a mental health diagnosis, but drug paraphernalia was found inside the home, though Lorah said it's unknown what role drugs played in the shooting. Pregnant daughter planned to leave Angelina Stone had expressed concerns about her father's well-being, Lorah said, and last year, she tried to change her last name because she wanted to pursue a career in medicine. "More recently, Angelina had been sending messages indicating she planned to leave the family home after giving birth," Lorah said. "In those messages, she said her father was kicking her and her brothers out of the residence. She also reported that he had been physically abusive to her brothers."When detectives searched the home after the shooting, the police chief said they found belongings packed in bags and boxes in her bedroom.Timeline of shootingThe afternoon of the shooting, shortly after 4:39 p.m., the police chief said Angelina Stone called her aunt, Lora Roberts, on Facebook Messenger and talked to her for about two minutes. When that call ended, the chief said Roberts, who was Michelle Stone's sister, said she was on the way.Within 10 minutes, police said Roberts and Tanner arrived outside.Just three minutes later, the city's ShotSpotter system detected gunfire. Between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m., authorities said the SWAT and hostage negotiation teams were notified, and a little after 7 p.m., officers breached the front door, which had been partially barricaded. Police said officers found the bodies of two young children on the first floor, followed by Angelina Stone on the stairwell, and then Michelle Stone and the couple's two sons, Jonathan Stone and Matthew Stone. Matthew Stone Sr. was found on the second floor with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, investigators said. Lorah said with everything that investigators know, there are still questions that can't be answered. "What we cannot say with certainty is what happened inside the home between those communications and the shooting or exactly what caused Matthew Stone Sr. to take these actions," Lorah said. "Those are important limits to what this investigation can tell us. We recognize that the community has been looking for answers. We have worked to establish the facts as carefully and thoroughly as possible and we wanted to share those findings so that the people have a clear understanding of what happened."City of Erie looking to heal At the press conference, Erie Mayor Daria Devlin questioned if there was anything the city could have done to prevent the shooting. "Were there opportunities to recognize that this family was struggling?" Devlin asked. "Were there places where our systems could have responded differently? And how do we make sure other families in our community who are suffering or struggling don't fall through the cracks?" Devlin said she has begun conversations with healthcare leaders and community organizations about supporting families experiencing domestic violence and isolation. Now the city's focus will turn to helping the Perry Street neighborhood heal. "We cannot change what happened on Friday.
