In 1994, he became a state senator and, in 2000, ran for a U.S. Congressional seat, where he served on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and as chair of the House Intelligence Committee.Rogers says that he will "stand with President Trump to deliver on the mandate given to him by the American people."He says his plans include bringing manufacturing jobs back; lowering the cost of gas, groceries and prescription drugs; protecting seniors' Social Security and Medicare; and prioritizing education over indoctrination.Lydia ChristensenLydia Christensen is running for Michigan's U.S. Senate as the Libertarian Party nominee. Christensen's background is in computer science and computer programming.According to her campaign, Christensen "speaks for all Michiganders free from left-right party constraints."Christensen says her plan focuses on Great Lakes protection, housing, tribal sovereignty, civil liberties and economic opportunity.Timothy LongTimothy Long is running for Michigan's U.S. Senate as the U.S. Taxpayers Party candidate.Long says on his Facebook page that he supports the right to life, is against giving money to other countries when the U.S. is in debt and thinks the two-party system is broken.Douglas P. MarshThe Green Party's candidate for Michigan's U.S. Senate is Douglas P. Marsh. Marsh is a community journalist who says, "What if regular, working-class people made the law?" Marsh says his priorities include affordability, universal healthcare, housing market reforms, ceasefire and clean water.Walter P. KristyWalter P. Kristy is the candidate for the Natural Law Party for Michigan's U.S. Senate. However, he says on his campaign website, "The Natural Law Party allows me to run an independent campaign. There isn't any party control over my political positions."Kristy's background is in economics, and he says he stands for women's rights to choose an abortion, the right to bear arms, protecting civil liberties, protecting the environment and upgrading the power grid.

title: No charges will be filed in connection with crash that killed four Yough High School students
description: Sources said that a photo shows the teens at a home on the night of the crash where alcohol can be seen at a table they were sitting at.
content: Pennsylvania State Police troopers have completed their investigation into the crash that took the lives of four Yough High School students earlier this year. No charges will be filed in the case, officials told KDKA's Erika Stanish.A memorial continues to grow at the crash site where 15-year-old Brady Hunker, 18-year-old Rocco Zugai, 15-year-old Felicity Martini and 16-year-old Kylee Korber were all killed near Creek Road in Sewickley Township in March.By the time first responders arrived at the crash site, the vehicle had burned completely. The fire was so intense that there was almost nothing left of the victims, requiring dental records for identification, State Police said.Sources said that a photo shows the teens at a home on the night of the crash where alcohol could be seen on a table they were sitting at.Police said the driver of the vehicle had acquired the alcohol on his own and that it doesn't appear anyone supplied it.In the days following the crash, police confirmed that speed was a factor, but the events leading up to the incident remained unclear.

title: Off-duty Jeffco deputy pulls unconscious driver from burning vehicle after crash
description: An off-duty Jefferson County Sheriff's deputy is being hailed as a hero after he rushed to help pull an unconscious driver from a burning vehicle.
content: An off-duty Jefferson County Sheriff's deputy is being hailed as a hero after he rushed to help pull an unconscious driver from a burning vehicle. According to investigators, Deputy Dobson was off duty and driving south of Pierce when he saw a crash near Columbine High School. A Jeep Grand Cherokee slammed into a light pole and the driver was unconscious.Dobson rushed toward the burning SUV and pulled the man from the vehicle as smoke and fire billowed out. Another deputy arrived to help and determined there weren't any more people inside the SUV. As he searched, the SUV became engulfed in flames. Investigators said Dobson stayed with the driver until an off-duty nurse arrived and took over. Paramedics then rushed the driver to a nearby hospital. South Metro Fire Rescue crews extinguished the fire to keep it from spreading to nearby vegetation and homes. The Jefferson County Sheriff's Office provided this statement, "We are incredibly proud of Deputy Dobson for his dedication to our mission to protect and serve. He was off duty, but his commitment to our community was not. A big thanks also to the off-duty nurse, the community members who stepped up to help, and our fire and EMS partners. We are grateful to everyone who answered the call in those frightening moments."

title: Suspect found dead after barricaded situation on Detroit's west side, police say
description: A barricaded situation on Detroit's west side has ended with officers finding the fugitive dead inside the home, Michigan State Police said.
content: A barricaded situation on Detroit's west side ended with officers finding the fugitive dead inside the home, Michigan State Police said.The scene on Wednesday in the 19900 block of Westbrook Street involved a suspect who was wanted on a 28-count drug warrant and had not appeared in court. Lt. Ty Howard said the fugitive team went to execute a search at the Westbrook home and heard a gunshot from the back of the house. Howard says the team then called for backup.Howard confirmed that MSP and U.S. Marshals were able to get into the home. At first, they did not find anyone inside.Shortly after 6 a.m. on Thursday, state police said the suspect was found inside "with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound."The Michigan State Police teams on scene included its Emergency Support Team, the bomb squad, hostage negotiators, aviation unit and motor unit. State police said troopers did not fire their weapons during the incident."It's a bad situation, and we need to keep our cities and our streets safe," said Chandra Scott, whose mother lives in the neighborhood.

title: Northern California PG&E shutoffs increase; tens of thousands without power
description: Nearly 90,000 customers across 29 counties were without power, with more shutoffs expected Thursday and Friday.
content: PG&E has shut off power to nearly 90,000 customers across California as strong winds and dry conditions raise wildfire risk.The Public Safety Power Shutoff began around 5:30 p.m. Wednesday. As of 10 a.m. Thursday, an estimated 87,475 customers had lost power across 29 counties, nearly 30,000 more than Wednesday's numbers, and the utility said more shutoffs were possible on Friday morning.Some of the largest outages in Northern California include 10,790 customers in Calaveras County, 8,757 in El Dorado County, 8,771 in San Luis Obispo County, 7,273 in Madera County, and 7,248 in Tuolumne County.Nearly 4,600 customers were without power in Amador County and about 5,300 in Placer County. More than 3,000 customers have also been shut off in Butte County.In the Bay Area, about 4,700 in Alameda County customers have lost power, along with roughly 3,000 customers in Napa County and about 2,000 in Sonoma County. More than 1,600 were without power in Contra Costa County.The shutoffs come after the potential scope grew rapidly earlier this week, from about 30,000 customers Monday to 70,000 Tuesday and roughly 88,000 Wednesday.PG&E said the latest event could continue through Saturday afternoon. Customers can check their address and estimated restoration time on the utility's PSPS website.More than 40 Community Resource Centers are also opening across 25 counties with device charging, Wi-Fi, water and other supplies.

title: Chicago man's life insurance payout stalled for months after cyberattack
description: A Chicago man's daughter has been left waiting for months for a life insurance payout after her father's death, after a cyberattack disrupted services at TruStage earlier this year.
content: A Chicago man's daughter has been left waiting for months for a life insurance payout after her father's death, after a cyberattack disrupted services at TruStage earlier this year.When Stephanie McWoods lost her 64-year-old father in July, she said she expected to grieve, but not to have to fight. "I imagined this experience being a lot smoother," she said.McWoods anticipated the life insurance policy her father left behind would help her family through a difficult time and help pay to put him to rest. But when she called TruStage to start a claim on July 25, she only got an automated response."It basically informed you that they were going through a cyberattack, and that they don't have access to any records, and there's no one that you can talk to," she said.She said she repeatedly submitted information and called for updates, but still couldn't get any answers about when her claim would be paid.To make things worse, she said TruStage kept withdrawing premium payments after her dad died. "This does not feel right. It doesn't seem legal," she said.McWoods said she didn't get a claim number from TruStage until Oct. 1, and more than 80 days after first reaching out, she still hasn't gotten the funds from her dad's policy. "It's possible these extenuating circumstances are allowed by the state regulator," said Mark Friedlander, spokesman for the Insurance Information Institute.Friedlander said a cyberattack is not a typical reason for a life insurance death benefit to go unpaid.He said, normally under Illinois regulations, an insurer has 15 business days to acknowledge the claim. In straightforward cases, insurers must pay claims within 30 to 60 days of receiving all necessary documents. "It seems to be a broader problem, certainly," he said.Friedlander said that's why the Illinois Department of Insurance needs to step in to investigate. TruStage acknowledged that claims processing has been impacted by the cyberattack, and apologized for the frustration it has caused."A recent cyberattack significantly disrupted our digital systems, impacting our normal ability to process claims and communicate with customers," a TruStage spokesperson said. "In some cases, this incident has caused delays and gaps in the updates that customers expect, and we understand the frustration it has caused. We continue to expand servicing and claims capabilities as our recovery progresses, including expanding our customer service support team and creating new processes to help meet customer needs as fast as possible." But within less than 48 hours of the CBS News Chicago Investigators reaching out, McWoods said she finally got the call she's been waiting for from TruStage, telling her a check would be mailed in the next two business days. While she doesn't have it yet, she hopes her experience will help others "to hopefully get answers and to get their payout." The Illinois Department of Insurance did not immediately respond to requests for comment, but TruStage said they have been in touch with state regulators.The company also said it will reimburse McWoods for any premium payments that were withdrawn after her father's death.CBS News Chicago Investigators asked the Illinois Department of Insurance several questions related to this story. After it aired, we received their answers. Our questions and their answers are below.Q: Has the Department received complaints from Illinois policyholders or beneficiaries regarding TruStage's delays in acknowledging claims, communicating with beneficiaries, or paying life insurance death benefits? If so, how many complaints have been received, and what concerns have they raised?A: Since July 11, 2026, the Department has received total of 14 consumer complaints regarding claims issues for TruStage Financial Group. There were 17 other complaints received during that time period regarding unrelated issues.Q: Is the Department aware of TruStage's reported claims-processing disruptions following the cyberattack, and has it communicated with the company about the impact on Illinois consumers?A: Pursuant to 215 ILCS 215/20, the company has communicated regular updates to Illinois on their ongoing efforts to restore their systems following the recent cybersecurity event. In addition, the Iowa Insurance Division in the company's domicile state has provided updates to all states on these efforts as well. Q: Based on the delays reported by beneficiaries, could TruStage be in violation of Illinois insurance regulations? A viewer we spoke with did not get acknowledgment of her claim for more than 11 weeks and she is now well beyond the 60-day pay out deadline. Has the Department opened an inquiry or investigation into the company's handling of these claims?A: The Department is aware of the cybersecurity event, and we stand ready to assist any consumer experiencing concerns related to this event. We recommend that insurance consumers visit the company's website for information here: TruStage recovery status and online resources. Consumers can also file a complaint with the Department, if they believe the company is not honoring the terms of their policy. Consumers looking for more information about the complaint process are encouraged to visit our "Understanding the Consumer Complaint Process" resource page. Q: Does a cyberattack or loss of access to policy records excuse an insurer from otherwise applicable claims-handling requirements? Has the Department granted TruStage any extensions or other regulatory relief related to this incident?A: There have been no extensions to statutory or regulatory requirements due to the cybersecurity event.Q: What should beneficiaries do if they have been unable to obtain updates on their claims or receive payment within the applicable timeframe?A: The Department recommends that insurance consumers visit the company's website for information here: TruStage recovery status and online resources. Consumers can also file a complaint with the Department, if they believe the company is not honoring the terms of their policy. Consumers looking for more information about the complaint process are encouraged to visit our "Understanding the Consumer Complaint Process" resource page.

title: Chicago Public Schools IG closes probe into school board president candidate Hilario Dominguez
description: The Chicago Public Schools Inspector General has once again closed an investigation into school board president candidate Hilario Dominguez.
content: The Chicago Public Schools Inspector General has once again closed an investigation into school board president candidate Hilario Dominguez.The investigation stemmed from allegations of sexual harassment with a student back in 2017.On Wednesday, Dominguez's campaign shared a letter from the CPS Office of Inspector General, which read: "Following an investigation of the allegations, the OIG has determined that there is no actionable finding of sexual misconduct and makes no additional findings with respect to possible Chicago Public Schools (CPS) policy or guidelines violations relating to this incident. This investigation has concluded and the matter is closed. No further action will be taken."The district revived an investigation into Dominguez's conduct after closing a probe earlier this summer.Dominguez has repeatedly denied the allegations.A former student claimed Dominguez, a former political coordinator of the Chicago Teachers Union and the CTU's endorsed candidate, asked her about her dating life and picked her up while they were alone in 2017.The woman, now 26, took issue with the handling of the investigation into her allegations and accused the Chicago Public Schools Office of Inspector General of failing to take action for five years, the Chicago Tribune reported.In a letter to the OIG quoted by the Chicago Tribune, the woman wrote that she was enrolled in the Chicago youth summer jobs program when she herself was 17, as an organizer with the Pilsen neighborhood-based nonprofit The Resurrection Project, the Tribune reported. Dominguez was 24 and working as a coordinator at the nonprofit at the time.The woman said Dominguez was driving her to a work event when he asked her what kind of men she was interested in, the Tribune reported.The woman also said Dominguez put his arms around her and picked her up to twirl her when no one else was around, the newspaper reported. She said her feet were off the ground and her breasts and legs were "pressed against [Dominguez's] body," the newspaper reported.Dominguez said his relationship to the then-teenage girl was one of a mentor and mentee. Dominguez also denied any inappropriate behavior during a forum recently.Dominguez has also faced allegations of inappropriate behavior when he was working as a CPS special education teacher.Back in 2021, Dominguez was the subject of a complaint by a fellow teacher who alleged that Dominguez made a Nazi salute and called the teacher "Hitler" in front of students, multiple published reports note. Dominguez emphasized that the teacher withdrew the complaint, and that what really happened was that he stood up for his students in the face of racism.However, he did not deny the incident ever happened.Dominguez is a former political coordinator of the Chicago Teachers Union and the CTU's endorsed candidate. Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson has maintained support for Dominguez despite the allegations.

title: Detroit man accused of assaulting sister and stabbing her dog
description: A Detroit man was charged in connection with the assault of his 25-year-old sister and the non-fatal stabbing of her dog, Wayne County Prosecutor says.
content: A Detroit man was charged in connection with the assault of his 25-year-old sister and the non-fatal stabbing of her dog, Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy's office says.Joshua Shakur Leroy Cawthon, 18, was charged with one count of first-degree animal killing or torturing, one count of felonious assault, and one count of domestic violence.Cawthon and the victim were residing together at the 16500 block of Lesure Street in Detroit at the time of the incident, when they were allegedly involved in a verbal altercation on Oct. 3 at around 9:54 p.m., prosecutors say.It is alleged that the altercation escalated, and Cawthon produced a pocketknife, threatened the victim and stabbed the victim's dog, according to prosecutors.Prosecutors say that Cawthon turned himself in to the Detroit Detention Center on Oct. 13.Cawthon was arraigned Wednesday afternoon in the 36th District Court before Magistrate William Burton and received a $10,000 personal bond.The probable cause conference is scheduled for Oct. 21 at 8:30 a.m., and the preliminary examination is scheduled for Oct. 28 at 8:30 a.m. before Judge Shawn Jacque.Domestic Violence Resources: For anonymous, confidential help, people can call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 or 1-800-787-3224.If you or someone you know is in emotional distress, get help from the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988. Trained crisis counselors are available 24 hours a day to talk about anything.In addition, help is available from the National Alliance on Mental Illness, or NAMI. Call the NAMI Helpline at 800-950-6264 or text "HelpLine" to 62640. There are more than 600 local NAMI organizations and affiliates across the country, many of which offer free support and education programs.

title: Hilary Swank announces she is pregnant with her third child at 52
description: The Oscar winner and "Million Dollar Baby" star, who had twins at 48, said she is due in December.
content: Hilary Swank has surprised fans with a big announcement: She is pregnant with her third child at the age of 52, after having twins at 48. The "Million Dollar Baby" star and her family shared the news on social media with a video showing them dancing with glowsticks taped to their bodies, which then revealed the mom's baby bump. The caption reads, "A lot of people have been asking what project I'm doing next, this one releases in December." Three years ago, the Oscar winner gave birth to twins, daughter Aya and son Ohm, with her husband Philip Schneider, who is also 52. Dr. Kameelah Phillips, OB-GYN, said it's "extremely rare" to be pregnant at 52, and that it comes with serious medical considerations. "Most women in this age group are entering menopause," she said. "But ... even if your ovaries have started to become quiet ... your uterus can actually be convinced to carry a pregnancy through the process of IVF." "She's definitely probably being seen by a high-risk team," said Phillips. "For moms, they have the increased risk of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, diabetes, increased risk of C-section." Swank spoke to "CBS Sunday Morning" two years ago, after the birth of her twins. "I think for me being a parent who is on the older side, the beauty in it for me has been that I had the opportunity to dive deep into this dream of being an actor and now I can dive deep into this dream of being a mom because I'm not pulled in any other direction," she said.

title: Hollister police civilian workers laid off amid budget woes; officers push back
description: Citing financial woes, the City of Hollister laid off civilian employees of the police department on Wednesday. Meanwhile, officers are pushing back, saying the cuts will hurt public safety.
content: Citing financial woes, the City of Hollister laid off civilian employees of the police department on Wednesday. Meanwhile, officers are pushing back, saying the cuts will hurt public safety.Officers held an emotional sendoff for the employees, women who worked in the records department in non-sworn positions. The workers, who processed reports and helped gather evidence to submit to court, said they were all laid off and given little to no notice."These are our people. This is our family. This is our home away from home. We spend more time here than we do at home with our own families sometimes," said Jenelle Hoefling, who was among those laid off.Combined, Hoefling and Jennifer Corona have worked for Hollister PD for the past 15 years. They argue civilian staff at the department is indispensable, and the layoffs could create a public safety issue."We have 72 hours to get that report to the District Attorney, so that they can file with the court, that's just not going to happen. Which potentially means someone who should not be out on the streets is going to get released from jail," Corona said.Hoefling added, "We're going to stand together. And our POA isâ¦we're going to fight it the best we can. The POA is in full support of us."Outside of City Hall on Wednesday, employees stood in solidarity. The city said the cuts are due to Hollister facing a severe budget deficit of roughly $2 million. Bo Leland, president of the Hollister Police Association, said cutting civilian positions is not the answer."Right now, what the City Manager is proposing is that we maintain funding for seven vacant police officer positions, which accounts for about $1.99 million worth of funding," Leland told CBS News Bay Area.The union proposed other solutions to the issue."Our point in this entire protest is that if you had come to us first, we could have told you to get rid of five of those positions, keep our civilian staff so we can maintain our level of service that we provide to the community. And we still would have the ability to hire two police officers," Leland added.CBS News Bay Area reached out to City Manager Ana Cortez for comment. As Cortez arrived at City Hall on Wednesday, she was heckled by protesters who made comments about her salary. In response, Cortez seemed to motion to the crowd as if she was dishing out money, which brought out boos from people in attendance.Reporter Veronica Macias, who was on scene, asked Cortez if she was mocking the crowd. Cortez did not respond.The support was appreciated by those who were impacted by the layoffs."When you see them rallying around us. It's very heartwarming and solidifies even more how much I love what I do. I love my job," Hoefling said.

title: Clark Atlanta student killed in crash during homecoming week; driver charged with vehicular homicide
description: Clark Atlanta University is mourning student Morgan Gamble after a driver struck her vehicle in a fatal crash Tuesday night in Atlanta.
content: Clark Atlanta University is mourning student Morgan Gamble after a driver struck her vehicle in a fatal crash Tuesday night in Atlanta.The driver, Nikolai Dunford, was arrested at the scene and charged with speeding, reckless driving and first-degree vehicular homicide, according to Atlanta police.Officers responded around 11:30 p.m. to Hank Aaron Drive and Glen Street, where they found Gamble with critical injuries. She was taken to a hospital and later died.Investigators believe Dunford was driving north at a high speed when he struck Gamble, who was traveling west. The investigation remains ongoing."The loss of a member of our University community is deeply felt, and we extend our heartfelt condolences to Morgan's family, friends, classmates and all who knew and loved Morgan," Clark Atlanta said in a statement.The university asked its community to respect her family's privacy and encouraged students to seek support.Support is available Thursday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. in the Office of the Honors Program on the first floor of Trevor Arnett Hall and from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. in the first-floor Yugo study rooms.Ongoing spiritual and emotional care will remain available through the Office of Spiritual Life and the Counseling Services Office.Dunford is due in court Thursday.

title: San Rafael fatal stabbing stemmed from dispute between co-workers, police say
description: A fatal stabbing in San Rafael on Monday stemmed from an ongoing dispute between two co-workers that escalated into a physical confrontation, police said on Tuesday.
content: A fatal stabbing in San Rafael on Monday stemmed from an ongoing dispute between two co-workers that escalated into a physical confrontation, police said on Tuesday.Just after 1 p.m. on Monday, police dispatchers received an emergency call about a person who had fallen and was being given first aid outside the Northgate Medical Dental Center at 750 Las Gallinas Avenue and Northgate Drive in San Rafael's Terra Linda district. The San Rafael Police Department said officers arrived to find the victim had been stabbed, and he was taken to a hospital where he died of his injuries.Police said Monday that a person had been detained, and investigators were still sorting out what happened. On Tuesday, the department issued an update, saying that based on the victim's clothing, investigators determined that he was an employee of a business in the adjacent Northgate One Shopping Center, and that the stabbing followed a fight between the victim and a co-worker. The man arrested was identified as 20-year-old Richmond resident Justin Amilcar Gutierrez-Navarette. Police said that shortly after the investigation began, Gutierrez-Navarette contacted the department to arrange his surrender, and he cooperated with detectives during the interview process, police said. Gutierrez-Navarette and the victim had been involved in an ongoing dispute that turned into a fight on Monday, during which Gutierrez-Navarette stabbed the victim, according to investigators. After being stabbed, the victim fled out of the rear entrance of the business before collapsing outside the medical office building on Las Gallinas Avenue.On Thursday, the coroner's office identified the victim as Mathew Ryan Lambdin, a 27-year-old San Rafael resident.Gutierrez-Navarette was booked into the Marin County Jail on a charge of murder, and police said there were no other outstanding suspects. Anyone with information about this crime was asked to call the San Rafael Police Department at 415-485-3000 or visit http://www.srpd.org/tips.

title: James Talarico announces record-breaking $64 million fundraising haul in Texas Senate race
description: The Talarico campaign said that brings his total fundraising to $134 million since he announced his candidacy last year.
content: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico raised a record-breaking $64 million in three months — more than any Senate candidate ever in the third quarter — his campaign announced Thursday.The campaign said that brings Talarico's total fundraising to $134 million since he announced his candidacy last year.His Republican opponent, Attorney General Ken Paxton, said earlier this month that he had raised $18 million in the same period. Talarico broke Jamie Harrison's record of $57 million, raised during the third quarter in his unsuccessful 2020 Senate campaign in South Carolina.Although a Democrat hasn't won a Senate election in Texas since 1988, Democrats there have been powerhouse fundraisers. In 2018, candidate Beto O'Rourke raised a then-record $38 million in the same three-month period. Recent polls have shown Talarico with a slight lead over Paxton. Incumbent GOP Sen. John Cornyn, a prolific fundraiser, lost the primary earlier this year to Paxton, who has long struggled as a fundraiser. Republicans have dumped hundreds of millions into the race to support Paxton, even as there have been leaks of audio clips of Paxton appearing to disparage national involvement in the race.President Trump, who backed Paxton in the primary against Cornyn and is a longtime ally, has traveled to Texas three times in a month to campaign for Paxton. CNN hosted a town hall with Talarico on Wednesday night, and said Paxton had been invited but declined to respond. CNN and CBS are both owned by Skydance. At the town hall, Talarico drove home the economic theme of his campaign, telling voters, "We have an affordability crisis because we have a corruption crisis." He also addressed issues ranging from abortion to his recent absence from the campaign trail, confirming that he had the flu and slamming online conspiracy theories about it. "That decision to stay home for a week sent my opponent and his conspiracy theorists spiraling. I opened up social media and learned that I had apparently dropped out of the race, flown to a mental health facility in Ohio, that I had died," Talarico said. "This is crazy. I mean, these false claims got millions of views online."Paxton announced Wednesday that his campaign is kicking off a two-week bus tour this weekend near Fort Worth that will wrap up the night before Election Day at the Alamo.Early voting starts Monday in Texas.

title: 3 megadonors account for $24 million of GOP candidate's $26 million haul in Wisconsin governor's race
description: Republican Tom Tiffany raised more than $26 million in the latest two-month reporting period, with more than $24 million from three people. David Crowley is attacking Tiffany's ties to Trump and his billionaire backers.
content: Democrats got the matchup they wanted for governor in Wisconsin.Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley defeated a democratic socialist in the primary and faces one of President Trump's closest allies in Washington. It's a dream matchup for Democrats in a midterm election where Trump's approval ratings are at record lows.But the race remains close based on the latest public polling. Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, who survived a small plane crash while campaigning, distanced himself from some of Trump's most unpopular policies while tapping three billionaire megadonors to hammer Crowley as weak on crime and illegal immigration.The attacks and Tiffany's financial advantage, along with Wisconsin's long history as a state narrowly divided between Republicans and Democrats, are helping to keep the campaign close in a midterm election in which Democrats are hoping to notch big wins nationwide."We think we're in a great spot," Tiffany said after a law enforcement roundtable in Rock Springs earlier this month. "We basically see a dead heat race at this point."Democratic strategist Joe Zepecki said Crowley is doing better than people think — noting that in 2018, the last midterm when Trump was in office, Democrats defeated a two-term Republican incumbent governor and reelected U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin by double digits. The wave is shaping up to be even bigger for Democrats this year, he said."The political environment is doing a lot of work for David Crowley," Zepecki said. "The handwringing is what Democrats do, and I'm fine with nervous energy motivating people to run through the tape on Nov. 3."Tiffany has been a longtime ally of Trump but in recent months has taken steps to distance himself from the unpopular Republican president.Tiffany voted five times against resolutions in the U.S. House that would've prohibited Trump from continuing military activities in Iran without congressional approval, but in May he said it was time to "wrap up" the war.In an interview with WMTV on Tuesday, Tiffany sidestepped a question about whether he approved of Trump's performance."The president is doing what he believes is best for the United States of America," Tiffany said. "What I'm focused on is being the best governor possible in Wisconsin."Tiffany has also been critical of artificial intelligence data centers, breaking with Trump, who has said communities that don't embrace them will be "backwards and poor." Instead, Tiffany has tried to paint Crowley as an advocate for building data centers, referring to him as "Data Center David Crowley."Crowley has said his comments on AI data centers were taken out of context. He has said local communities must have veto authority, while also calling data centers a part of the modern economy that could bring significant economic benefits to the state.Tiffany and his supporters have tried to paint Crowley as weak on crime, hitting him for a Milwaukee County program that provides computer tablets to inmates that some used to contact and harass victims and witnesses. Crowley last week suspended messaging features on the tablets after criticism from Tiffany.Crowley and his backers have tried to hammer Tiffany on his loyalty to Trump, his past support for the war in Iran, high tariffs and soaring gas prices.Crowley this month launched an ad accusing Tiffany of pledging his loyalty to Trump and his billionaire backers. Tiffany raised more than $26 million during the most recent two-month reporting period, with $24 million-plus coming from just three people."These billionaires know that if they buy Congressman Tom Tiffany this election, he will sell Wisconsin out to them," Crowley told supporters last week.Tiffany said he thinks Crowley's attacks linking him and Trump aren't landing."People of Wisconsin are really savvy voters," Tiffany said. "They're like, 'We're not voting for president in this election. We're voting for the governor.'"Liberal activist Scot Ross said Crowley and his supporters have to do more to remind voters about Tiffany's ties to Trump given voter anger over high gas prices, the Iran war and inflation."The number one thing in politics is anger wanes," Ross said. "In campaigns, you need to be reminded why you're angry. And you're angry because of what Tom Tiffany, Trump and Republicans have done."A Marquette University Law School poll of 692 likely voters conducted Sept. 16-23 showed the governor's race to be about even.Tiffany and his backers have outspent Crowley and his supporters $53 million to roughly $35 million, according to AdImpact, which tracks political advertising."We think that we have momentum on our side at this point," Tiffany said. "I think David Crowley is struggling to get his message out."Republican strategist Ben Voelkel said given the "challenging national environment," he thinks Tiffany is running a strong campaign aided by the financial advantage."He's offering voters a choice and something different from the status quo, which is what I think David Crowley represents," Voelkel said.Crowley emerged from a chaotic Democratic primary that saw two top candidates drop out within a month of the election. Crowley had also dropped out, but he got back in at the urging of two-term incumbent Gov. Tony Evers as part of an effort by more mainstream Democrats to defeat democratic socialist Francesca Hong.Crowley eked out a primary win by less than half a percentage point in August, and Tiffany is banking on low turnout among Democrats."People are not excited about David Crowley, and you can see it out there," Tiffany said. "He's counting on the generic ballot getting them across the finish line."But Democratic leaders are rallying around Crowley. Besides Evers' ongoing support, Hong is also campaigning on Crowley's behalf."Let's win this together," she said in an Oct. 1 social media post.In another attempt to unify Democrats and boost turnout, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore campaigned with Crowley across Wisconsin last week, noting that Crowley is vying to become Wisconsin's first Black governor. Moore is the first Black governor of Maryland and just the third Black person elected governor in U.S. history.Former Vice President Kamala Harris, the first Black person to hold that position, is scheduled to campaign with Crowley on Oct. 26.Five of the past seven presidential elections were decided by less than a percentage point in Wisconsin. In 2018, the last Trump midterm election, Evers defeated Republican then-Gov. Scott Walker by 1.1 percentage points. In 2022, Evers won reelection by 3.4 percentage points, a landslide by Wisconsin standards.The governor's race is open for the first time in 16 years after Evers decided against seeking a third term. Democrats hope to hang onto the office and flip control of the Legislature, which has been majority Republican since 2011.Crowley and Tiffany are running statewide for the first time. Crowley served three years in the state Assembly and has been the top elected official in Milwaukee County since 2020.Tiffany, also a former state lawmaker, has served in Congress representing a mostly rural northern Wisconsin district since 2020."Three months ago people didn't really know either of these candidates," said Gordon Hintz, a former Democratic state lawmaker who served as Crowley's mentor when he was first elected to the Assembly. "It's kind of a race to the finish of who best defines themselves to the voters."

title: GoldenSky reveals headliners for 2027 Sacramento return with drone show over Tower Bridge
description: Sacramento's GoldenSky country music festival held a drone show over the Tower Bridge on Wednesday night to announce the headliners for its return in 2027 after a two-year hiatus.
content: Sacramento's GoldenSky country music festival has revealed its full lineup for its return in 2027 after a two-year hiatus.The announcement comes a day after organizers used a drone show over the Tower Bridge to reveal several of the biggest names on the bill, including Zach Bryan, Megan Moroney, Ty Myers and Treaty Oak Revival.The full lineup released Thursday also includes Whiskey Myers, Hudson Westbrook, Max McNown, Wyatt Flores, Vincent Mason, Avery Anna, Braxton Keith, Kaitlin Butts, Alexandra Kay and The Band Perry, among others. GoldenSky will return to Discovery Park on Oct. 9-10, 2027. Ticket sales begin Friday. The festival's return was first announced in June during Sacramento's annual State of Tourism address.GoldenSky hasn't been held in Sacramento since 2024, when the festival expanded to three days. Organizers later cited competition in the festival market and challenges booking country artists as factors in skipping 2025 and 2026. Danny Wimmer Presents produces both GoldenSky and Aftershock, Sacramento's much larger rock and metal festival. Both are held at Discovery Park, and organizers previously said the festivals are expected to return on back-to-back weekends in 2027.

title: Elderly couple found dead inside Attleboro home with "evidence of significant fire"
description: Investigators say there was evidence of a significant fire inside an Attleboro, Massachusetts, home where a couple were found dead Wednesday.
content: An elderly couple was found dead inside their house on Andover Avenue in Attleboro, Massachusetts, on Wednesday afternoon. A home health aide called for a welfare check in the morning, when she could not get in contact with her clients. Police said they had to make a forced entry and that's when they found 78-year-old Carol Courtemanche and 76-year-old husband Paul dead inside along with a cat. Officers said there was "evidence of a significant fire."Local and state police along with fire crews spent hours going in and out of the house, but they don't suspect foul play. "Currently it's being investigated as an unattended death. The Bristol County DA's office and the fire services have been called in to assist," Attleboro Deputy Police Chief Timothy Cook said. It's not clear when the fire broke out or when the couple died, but a neighbor across the street said he saw Carol Courtemanche last week. He said he never saw any indication of smoke or a fire coming from their house. "They're the type of people that check on you all the time, and you know, caring," neighbor Keith Wyman said. Wyman said the couple was a staple in the neighborhood, living in that house for decades and often traveling around in their campers. But he said they always made time for others. "She always brought things over for the kids and that's just who she was," Wyman recalled. "They're extremely caring and helpful people. We loved them and it's a shocker. It's a shock and it's a total loss. They're going to be dearly missed."

title: Metra MD-W trains resume service in Elgin after police activity
description: Metra MD-W trains resumed service in Elgin, Illinois, early Thursday night after a police investigation.
content: Metra MD-W trains resumed service in Elgin, Illinois, early Thursday night after a police investigation. Metra officials said inbound and outbound train service will run with normal service, making all scheduled stops to and from Big Timber Road. Some trains may run with delays. CBS News Chicago has reached out to Elgin police for more information on the investigation. Commuters can check service alerts and updates on the Metra website.

title: Wisconsin elections officials approve guidance for clerks if federal agents show up at polls
description: Clerks should alert county and state officials if ICE, FBI or other officers arrive, under guidance approved Thursday. One Republican commissioner voted no, saying it could scare people away from the polls.
content: Elections officials in battleground Wisconsin on Thursday approved guidance for local clerks to help them know what to do if federal law enforcement officials show up at the polls on Election Day, as some activists fear might happen.A Republican on the bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission cast the lone vote against sending the guidance, saying it "is only going to scare away some people from the polls." A hotly contested race for governor tops the ballot in Wisconsin."I personally think this guidance is unnecessary because we have not seemed to need it the past 201 years," Republican Commissioner Bob Spindell said.Clerks have been deluged with questions from voters about what they would do if agents showed up at the polls, Wisconsin elections administrator Meagan Wolfe said. The guidance is intended to explain how to handle it, she said."I see this as just like any other contingency planning we do to assist our clerks," she said.The memo tells Wisconsin's roughly 1,800 clerks who administer elections what to do if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, Department of Homeland Security officials, FBI agents or local law enforcement shows up at the polls.If officers arrive, the guidance says the head of the polling site should inform the municipal clerk, who should then tell the county clerk and the state elections commission. If the agents are there to observe, they must check in like any other observer and be subject to rules governing them, the guidance says.Democratic Commissioner Ann Jacobs said she was concerned about uniformed officers intimidating voters. The commission agreed to her recommendation that the guidance tell clerks to encourage law enforcement agents planning to come to the polls to be in plain clothes and not uniforms."I don't think we want full flak jacket, whatever, law enforcement three feet from our voters," Jacobs said. "I think that is much different from an ordinary, quiet observation by somebody in plain clothes."Department of Homeland Security officials have said they don't plan to send immigration enforcement officers en masse to patrol the polls and have dismissed concerns that they plan to do so as "fearmongering."Election legal experts say federal law clearly prevents the government from deploying any armed troops, agents or officers to election sites except to "repel armed enemies of the United States" — a high bar to clear.But organizations that represent Latino, Black and Asian American voters say the rhetoric and ICE's own activity make them worried at a time the number of immigration arrests is soaring as President Trump carries out his mass deportation agenda.Wisconsin elections officials have been traveling the state in recent days holding news conferences to discuss the process for casting and counting ballots. They have been saying they don't anticipate anything unusual at the polls this year."I expect this election will go like all other elections," Republican Don Millis, chair of the elections commission, said Thursday.

title: Group chats from Nolan Wells' phone show what his friends said before and after he vanished
description: Messages pulled from Nolan Wells​' phone show what his friends said before and after the 18-year-old disappeared in early July following a boat outing with friends.
content: Group chats pulled from Nolan Wells' cellphone show what his friends said before and after the Mississippi teen vanished in early July following a boat outing with friends. Wells disappeared after he and a group of friends celebrated the Fourth of July holiday off the Gulf Coast. They say he left his phone on their boat but didn't return with them. A nearly 300-page report analyzing the late teen's phone and recently uploaded on the Justice for Nolan Wells website reveals his friends' reactions to his disappearance and speculation about his death in dozens of group chats. On July 5, one group chat discusses when Wells was last seen, saying, "He got off our boat with this other guy and they started walking back to their boat." Minutes later, one friend calls it suspicious, saying, "There is def some sus s*** going on." At one point, they talked about trying to find Wells, asking everyone to check their camera rolls. Another user added, "See if he was talking to anyone we don't know." Another message read: "That's not like Nolan bro just to get left." Someone else writes, "Hes gotta be shlumped somewhere rn hopefully." Another answers: "It's already noon though," followed by, "He might've got drugged or something." Wells' body was recovered in the waters off Horn Island two days later. Once news broke of his death, one friend messaged: "Nolan was the most nice and caring guy we knew." The day after his disappearance, the group appeared frustrated with the national headlines, writing: "All i keep seeing is white folk made it home and the one black kid didn't." Another answered: "It ain't ever been like that with us bro." Last month, Jackson County's district attorney announced a Mississippi grand jury found no criminal wrongdoing in Wells' death. Legal analyst Jessica Levinson told CBS News there is nothing in the recently released report that would change the DA's conclusion that there is no evidence of a crime. Wells' parents spoke to CBS News in July, with his father Elmore Wonsley saying he didn't believe his son decided to stay on the island by himself. "It just doesn't — that's not his character," he said.

title: Pittsburgh Regional Transit announces plans to permanently close the Wabash Tunnel
description: PRT said that keeping the tunnel open for long-term use would require an estimated $43 million in rehabilitation costs.
content: Pittsburgh Regional Transit has announced plans to permanently close the Wabash Tunnel.If plans are approved by the agency's board, which is scheduled to meet next week, PRT said the tunnel will close for good on Dec. 1.PRT said that keeping the tunnel open for long-term use would require an estimated $43 million in rehabilitation costs."The Wabash Tunnel has a long history in Pittsburgh, but today it primarily serves private vehicle traffic rather than public transit," said PRT CEO Katharine Kelleman. "With an estimated $43 million needed to rehabilitate the tunnel, we have a responsibility to focus our limited resources on the infrastructure that is most critical to delivering safe, reliable transit service." PRT said that while the tunnel structure overall remains in fair condition, several components of the infrastructure like lighting, ventilation and electrical systems are considered to be in "poor to critical" condition. The tunnel, which was originally constructed in 1903 as part of the Wabash-Pittsburg Terminal Railroad, connects Woodruff Street near Saw Mill Run Boulevard to West Carson Street near Station Square, and is not currently a part of PRT's regular transit network.PRT currently does not provide scheduled transit service through the tunnel, only using it as a detour route when bus service has been disrupted by roadwork and special events.The closure of the tunnel is not expected to affect the Wabash Park and Ride.

title: Newly renovated Illinois Holocaust Museum in Skokie to reopen in November
description: The newly renovated Illinois Holocaust Museum will reopen in Skokie, Illinois, next month.
content: The newly renovated Illinois Holocaust Museum in Skokie, Illinois, will reopen next month. After being closed since July of last year, the museum will reopen on November 11. It's located on Woods Drive off Golf Road near the Edens Expressway. The renovation included a redesigned auditorium and gallery as well as a welcome center with a bigger lobby. The museum now features a new reflection gallery where guests can gather after their experience. "We're building this museum for a new generation of witnesses, a new generation of upstanders, people who are seeing what is troubling them around the world and ready to take on the mantle of leading change," Bernard Cherkasov, with the Illinois Holocaust Museum, said. "We cannot ask Holocaust survivors to carry their memories and the lessons of the Holocaust forever." Visitors can still learn from witnesses through the virtual reality theater and the holographic theater. Last month, CBS News Chicago shared Holocaust survivor Aaron Elster's story through his own hologram at the museum. He is still telling his story eight years after his death. The museum's temporary location, known as Experience360 , will remain open at State and Kinzie streets through the end of the year.

title: Michigan firewood ban starts Jan. 1, with warnings and fines to follow in 2028
description: State agriculture officials will focus on education during the first year. Starting Jan. 1, 2028, violators get a warning letter, and repeat violations can bring fines of $1,000 to $10,000.
content: Starting Jan. 1, 2027, firewood that hasn't been heat-treated and certified can't be brought into Michigan.The firewood quarantine, issued by the Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, applies to everyone entering the state, including campers and travelers. Firewood must be certified by the department, another state's agriculture department or the U.S. Department of Agriculture, and it must carry a label showing it received an approved treatment.The department says more than 140 plant pests and diseases can move in firewood, including Asian longhorned beetle and spotted lanternfly. They can hide beneath bark or inside the wood, making them hard to inspect.Certified firewood has been heated in a kiln to a core temperature of at least 140 degrees Fahrenheit for at least 60 minutes. Kiln-dried firewood isn't automatically exempt, because drying wood doesn't show it reached that temperature. Kiln-dried lumber, wood pellets and wood chips no larger than one inch in two dimensions are exempt.The department recommends buying firewood within 10 miles of where you plan to burn it and leaving leftovers behind.The department will focus on education during 2027. Beginning Jan. 1, 2028, violators will receive a warning letter. Repeat violations may bring fines of $1,000 to $10,000, or no more than $500 if the person voluntarily reports the violation.

title: 81-year-old man killed outside Georgia Walmart was likely a bystander, investigators say
description: An 81-year-old Lula man was shot and killed in a Georgia Walmart parking lot Wednesday, and now police are searching for the shooter.
content: An 81-year-old Lula man was shot and killed in a Georgia Walmart parking lot Wednesday, and now police are searching for the shooter. According to the Gainesville Police Department, James Edward McDaniel was struck just after 7 p.m. when gunfire erupted outside the store. Investigators believe he was an innocent bystander, according to the preliminary findings.The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to call 911.

title: FTC issues subpoenas to Anthropic and OpenAI over safety incidents
description: The demands come amid mounting public concerns about the potential risks posed by frontier AI models.
content: The Federal Trade Commission has subpoenaed Anthropic and OpenAI to gather information about potential consumer protection violations, a spokesperson for the agency confirmed.The development, first reported by Axios, comes just two weeks after the FTC said it was investigating the artificial intelligence companies as part of a probe it launched this summer. The agency declined further comment about the probe. The FTC is seeking documents on safety incidents, privacy policies and safeguards at Anthropic and OpenAI, Axios reported. The companies have come under public scrutiny in recent months after several incidents in which their AI models went rogue and hacked into websites.The agency, which sent civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI on Wednesday, will also issue subpoenas to third-party organizations at a later date, according to Axios, which cited a person familiar with the matter.The FTC could compel Anthropic and OpenAI to testify before Congress about their products, a move that would allow the government to press the companies about the safety of their technology as the public grows increasingly wary about its potential harms. A recent poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research found that 64% of U.S. adults think AI is developing "too fast." Eight in 10 said it's "extremely" or "very" important for the U.S. government to ensure that AI stays under human control.President Trump has resisted calls to slow the development of AI, saying that the technology is vital to U.S. national interests. He recently announced the creation of a "Super Intelligence Force" to coordinate with the federal government on AI matters and engage with consumers, public interest groups and other stakeholders.

title: San Francisco Police Commission meets over drone-related privacy issues
description: It was a heated San Francisco Police Commission meeting Wednesday night, as people debated the issue of drones.
content: It was a heated San Francisco Police Commission meeting Wednesday night, as people debated the issue of drones.In 2024, San Franciscans passed Proposition E to allow the police department to use drones. Now, the commission is trying to draft a policy on when and how they are used.The hot topic Wednesday night was Department General Order 10:12. It addresses privacy issues related to drones, such as when and how they are used. San Franciscans chimed in with hours of public comment. Some speakers asked for the process to be slowed down, to get more community feedback on the DGO.Before the police commission meeting, there was a protest outside City Hall, with speakers opposing the use of drones. Their main concern is privacy."There have been instances of this drone use monitoring civilians in the street," Yehya Abuzaid with the Council on American-Islamic Relations said. "Monitoring people just as they go about their daily business, capturing the whole person. Which is leading to, in my opinion, some egregious violations of our rights."There is already a policy that states drones are only deployed for public safety response, to help in an active criminal investigation or during training. Abuzaid feels the policy needs to be clearer and have strict privacy protections."It's not necessarily about one technology or another; it's about anytime there's a policy that's threatening to violate any of our rights, we stand against it," he said.Alex Bastian was at the meeting. He formerly worked in the District Attorney's Office and is currently the CEO of the Hotel Council of San Francisco. He says San Francisco Police have made great strides in bringing down crime in the last few years, and feels technology has played a big role."What's so important is to, of course, be passionate and also use common sense in this," Bastian said. "Everyone's opinion matters, but I think we can do both. And I think that's the San Francisco way. I'm so encouraged by what we're doing in this city."In the end, the police commission voted to approve DGO 10:12, with only one dissenting vote. This issue will now go to the Board of Supervisors, where there will be more public input on this issue."Yes, we also care about privacy. I personally care about privacy a lot, and we need to continue to have this dialogue," Bastian said. "But at the same time we need to employ common sense solutions to advance public safety."

title: Maryland Rep. Andy Harris questions student reporter's right to record him after contentious debate
description: Rep. Andy Harris clashed with audience members during a debate with Democratic challenger Dan Schwartz and later tried to have a student journalist removed.
content: It was a contentious night on Maryland's Eastern Shore for Rep. Andy Harris, the state's only Republican in Congress.Harris, who represents Maryland's 1st Congressional District, clashed with audience members during a debate Tuesday in Cambridge with his Democratic challenger, Dan Schwartz. Afterward, he challenged a student journalist's right to record him and sought to have the reporter removed from a press gaggle.Following the debate, reporters gathered to interview Harris. During the exchange, he challenged a reporter from The Baltimore Banner before singling out Cat Murphy, a student journalist from the University of Maryland, and arguing that she did not have permission to record him.The exchange was caught on camera.Harris cited Maryland's two-party consent law, which generally requires all parties to consent to the recording of a private conversation. But attorney Jeremy Eldridge told CBS News Baltimore that the law did not apply to the interaction because it took place in a public setting.Contentious debateThe debate itself featured tense moments, with audience members interrupting both candidates and Harris engaging in a heated exchange with a woman in the crowd."You all say you believe there's a First Amendment but only if you agree with you," Harris said. "You should let me finish the sentence, ma'am. You are rude."Schwartz also challenged Harris over his record in Congress."This guy put forward his own legislation in 2013 that would have limited members to six terms. Now he's running for his ninth," Schwartz said.Rafael Lorente, dean of the University of Maryland's Philip Merrill College of Journalism, addressed the incident involving the student journalist in a statement posted on social media."Merrill College students know their rights as journalists," Lorente said."Cat Murphy is a master's student at the University of Maryland, credentialed as a reporter for our Capital News Service and doing the job we teach our students to do," Lorente continued. "Cat recorded openly in a public space alongside other news outlets, and that is her legal right."Murphy spoke with CNN about the exchange."I was focused on doing my job, and asking my questions that I wanted answers to, and I think I did that," she said.CBS News Baltimore reached out to Harris for comment but has not heard back.Attorney explains Maryland's two-party consent lawEldridge told CBS News Baltimore that Harris did not have a reasonable expectation of privacy during the exchange because he was speaking with reporters in a public venue."If the congressman is having a conversation with journalists whom he invited into a public venue, then the congressman would not have an expectation of privacy, meaning what we would refer to as a two-party consent rule would not be applicable," Eldridge said.In 2019, a college student at Salisbury University was charged with illegally streaming a meeting with a congressional staffer for Harris.Eldridge said that earlier case may help explain why Harris was particularly sensitive to the issue, but he said the circumstances of Tuesday's exchange were different."This congressman in particular has been the victim of illegal wiretapping previously and that matter was prosecuted in the Maryland court system," Eldridge said. "So the congressman is probably sensitive to this issue, but in this situation, the congressman was wrong on the law."

title: Temple University investigates alleged rape at off-campus apartment building in North Philadelphia
description: Temple University officials are investigating an alleged rape that happened at an apartment building near the campus.
content: Temple University is investigating an alleged rape that happened at an off-campus apartment building for students near the school. According to the Temple University crime log, the rape happened around 2:30 a.m. Saturday at University Village on the 1700 block of North 10th Street. The rape was reported Tuesday morning and was referred to the student code of conduct. In a statement, a spokesperson for Temple said in part, "Because this incident occurred at a private, off-campus residence, it is being addressed through Temple's Student Conduct Code. This process allows the university to investigate allegations and hold students accountable under university policy."Students who report a sexual assault can choose whether they want to participate in a criminal investigation. Officials do not believe there is a threat to the community and are investigating the incident, the statement said.Temple previously said it has gathered a group of students, faculty and staff to review its current practices and make recommendations to administration in light of recent sexual assault allegations at Cornell University.

title: Little Five Points ghost tours bring Atlanta's spooky stories and queer history to life
description: Little Five Points is known for going big during spooky season. Throughout October, ghost tours are giving visitors a look at the neighborhood's history and haunting local lore.
content: Little Five Points is known for going big during spooky season. Throughout October, ghost tours are giving visitors a look at the neighborhood's history and haunting local lore.The neighborhood offers three types of tours: Queens of the Crypt, an LGBTQ+ tour led by drag performers, regular ghost tours, and boozy ghost tours, according to tour manager Karla Beasley."There's already so much queer history here that it just makes sense to talk about it more," said Hera Kane, one of the drag queens who leads Queens of the Crypt.All ticket sales go back into the neighborhood, helping pay for community events and security, Beasley said.She said the tours introduce visitors to local businesses and attract guests from outside Georgia."It's really neat to see just how far our reach is," Beasley said.Locals enjoy the tours, too. Kane said longtime visitors can learn something new about buildings they have passed countless times.For a small neighborhood, there are plenty of spooky stories."Right here in the center, there used to be a church, it burnt down, and they still say apartments around here, if you're falling asleep, you can still hear the choir singing," Kane said.Katrina Prowess, another Queens of the Crypt guide, shared a story about an alleged ghost at the Clothing Warehouse."They say that there is a ghost girl that lives in the clothing warehouse. She'll come up to you while you're working, tug on your clothes and say, excuse me. Hello, can you help me?" Prowess said.The guides are making sure the neighborhood's stories — and its queer history — are shared."I think something that makes Little Five so special is the queer community that inhabits Little Five," Prowess said.Tours take place on weekend nights throughout October. Tickets are available on the Little Five Points website.

title: RTD provides affordable options to get to Denver Broncos game against Seattle Seahawks
description: The Regional Transportation District believes that traffic is going to be heavy for the Denver Broncos game against the Seattle Seahawks Thursday night.
content: The Regional Transportation District believes that traffic is going to be heavy for the Denver Broncos game against the Seattle Seahawks Thursday night. The game starts at 6:15 p.m. at Empower Field at Mile High.The Broncos say the stadium lots are already sold out, so drivers will have to find spaces away from the stadium. RTD says drivers should avoid getting stuck in traffic and attempting to park by taking their transit services.RTD says the C, E, and W lines will take you directly to Empower Field at Mile High. RTD says they will have additional rail cars to fit a lot more people. Travelers can also take the A, B, G, and N lines if you are traveling from Union Station. All of these options will get you around traffic and parking-related issues."You can take transit and get right there," said Pauline Haberman, Program Manager for Special Projects, RTD. "Skip the parking. Skip paying for parking. Skip the trouble. Skip the walk. Just take transit and get straight over to Empower Field. It's easy." RTD says a three-hour pass is $2.75, and a full day pass is $5.50. Anyone under the age of 19 can ride for free. RTD says extra security will be around Union Station and Empower Field's platforms. To plan your trip, use the RTD Next Ride app. Just type in Broncos and let the app plan the trip for you.

title: Two detainees at Florida's Deportation Depot mistakenly released, later apprehended
description: When Deportation Depot first opened in September, an ICE spokesperson said the facility could house up to 2,000 people.
content: Two detainees held at Florida's Deportation Depot west of Jacksonville were released by mistake over the weekend and later apprehended and returned to the detention facility, officials have confirmed.In a statement to the News Service of Florida, the Florida Division of Emergency Management said an administrative error resulted in two detainees being bonded out. "Both individuals were quickly located and returned to custody," said FDEM spokeswoman Stephanie Hartman. "There is no ongoing threat to the public."It is unknown whether the detainees had criminal records. "The matter is being reviewed to ensure accountability and prevent similar incidents," Hartman said.FDEM, housed under Gov. Ron DeSantis' executive office, is the agency in charge of running the state's immigration detention facilities. Alligator Alcatraz, a tented immigration facility in the Everglades, closed down in June. But Deportation Depot, which is located in the former Baker Correctional Institute in Sanderson, continues to operate and house detained undocumented immigrants before they are transferred into the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.According to state documents, Florida has a maximum $101 million contract with GEO|CDR BAKER for "administrative staffing, correctional officers, intake staffing, health and medical personnel," at Deportation Depot.As of Sept. 22, the state has paid GEO|CDR BAKER approximately $32 million as part of the contract, according to the Florida Accountability Contract Tracking System.The company was created in late August 2025, according to state business records, and is headed by executive leaders from The GEO Group, the largest private detention contractor in the country, and CDR Health Care.Deportation Depot currently holds about 1,000 detainees, ICE saysDeportation Depot, about 40 miles west of Jacksonville, is not the same facility as Baker County Detention Center, which is run by ICE. When Deportation Depot first opened in September, an ICE spokesperson said the facility could house up to 2,000 people. The facility currently holds about 1,000 detainees.FDEM is also the agency in charge of hurricane response. On Friday, Hurricane Isaias whipped through the Florida Panhandle, making landfall in Okaloosa County as a Category 2 hurricane with sustained winds of 120 mph.Isaias knocked the power out of nearly 450,000 homes and businesses in Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa and Bay counties. As of Wednesday afternoon, power had been restored to all but 11,376 customers.In September, the agency issued a report showing they could have a $1.5 billion deficit at the end of the fiscal year.According to the report, with a full reimbursement from the federal government for illegal immigration enforcement and an influx of $500 million from the Legislature, the agency still projected a "worst-case scenario" of a $1.5 billion deficit in the Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund at the end of the 2026-2027 fiscal year if the state experiences two natural disasters.The report also stated FDEM had only received $84.6 million out of the promised $608 million in federal grant money.As of Oct. 14, the state has assisted in the arrests of 27,898 undocumented immigrants in Florida.

title: Marilyn Mosby, former Baltimore State's Attorney, has mortgage fraud conviction formally dismissed
description: Former Baltimore State's Attorney Marilyn Mosby's mortgage fraud conviction has been dismissed after prosecutors decided not to pursue a retrial.
content: Former Baltimore State's Attorney Marilyn Mosby's mortgage fraud conviction has been dismissed after prosecutors decided not to pursue a retrial.Mosby said in a statement that her conviction was "rightfully reversed and vacated."Mosby was convicted of mortgage fraud in February 2024 after a jury determined that she submitted a false mortgage application in 2021 while purchasing a home in Florida. She was serving as Baltimore's State's Attorney at the time.A federal appeals court overturned the conviction in July 2025. The U.S. Attorney's Office in Maryland later decided not to retry her on the mortgage fraud charge, and the conviction has now been formally dismissed following a consent motion.The decision means Mosby can keep the Florida vacation home that was at the center of the case."I thank GOD that this painful chapter of my life is finally over," Mosby said in a statement. "Despite the attempts to discredit me and dismantle my career, I am still standing. I am deeply grateful to my attorneys for their unwavering advocacy, dedication, and commitment to fighting for justice on my behalf."Earlier this month, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to consider an appeal related to Mosby's convictions.Mosby has maintained her innocence throughout the legal proceedings.The mortgage fraud case centered on $5,000 Mosby received from her then-husband. Mosby argued that the money was a gift and that she used it to purchase property, according to court documents. Prosecutors alleged that she misrepresented the source of the money on her mortgage application in order to obtain a lower interest rate.The Department of Justice argued that the money was not a gift, but rather funds Mosby had sent to her husband before he transferred them back to her.In May 2024, Mosby was sentenced to three years of probation and one year of home detention following her mortgage fraud and perjury convictions.The mortgage fraud conviction was appealed shortly after her home detention ended. When the appeals court overturned the conviction, it also vacated an order requiring Mosby to forfeit the Florida property.Her perjury convictions remain in place.Mosby said she is celebrating the dismissal of the mortgage fraud conviction but continues to fight to retain her law license."I will continue that fight with faith, resilience, and the unwavering belief that truth and justice will prevail," Mosby said.

title: Michigan DNR says firefighting crews making "steady progress" against U.P. wildfires
description: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources says crews are making "steady progress" against three wildfires that are burning in the Upper Peninsula.
content: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources says crews are making "steady progress" against three wildfires that are burning amid rugged, remote terrain in the Upper Peninsula. Agencies working to contain the fires and keep residents informed include DNR teams, the U.S. Forest Service, Michigan State Police, local Sheriff's Offices, emergency management teams, and local fire departments. Here's a quick look at the conditions: Ridge Fire The Ridge Fire is estimated at 434 acres in size and was 30% contained as of Wednesday evening. This fire is about 10 miles northwest of Marquette, north of the Dead River Basin. It was spotted by a DNR pilot on Oct. 9. The cause remains under investigation. The Ready, Set, Go! status for residents along North Basin Drive remains at "Ready." Residents are encouraged to stay prepared for further instructions. A Temporary Flight Restriction for 5 nautical miles remains in effect below 3,500 feet over the Ridge Fire. Drones are strictly prohibited as they halt all air operations. Craig Lake Fire The Craig Lake Fire is estimated at 605 acres and was 50% contained as of Wednesday evening. This fire is north of Craig Lake State Park. The cause was confirmed to be a lightning strike that occurred between Oct. 5 and 8, when a DNR pilot noticed the fire. Some of the trails in Craig Lake State Park are temporarily closed to visitors due to firefighting efforts. A Temporary Flight Restriction for 5 nautical miles remains in effect below 3,500 feet over the Craig Lake fire. Drones are strictly prohibited as they halt all air operations. Black River Fire The Black River Fire is estimated at 382 acres and was 50% contained as of Wednesday evening. This fire is about four miles south of Wakefield in a densely forested, hard-to-access area. The DNR says it took over management of the fire from the U.S. Forest Service on Tuesday. The above video originally aired on Oct. 13, 2026.

title: Massachusetts computer repair shop sees business grow as cost of buying new becomes "ridiculously expensive"
description: While gas and energy prices are driving the latest uptick in inflation, they are followed close behind by computers, software and accessories.
content: While gas and energy prices are driving the latest uptick in inflation, they are followed close behind by computers, software and accessories.According to the September 2026 Consumer Price Index, prices for computers, software and accessories have risen more than 28% over the past year, making the category one of the leading drivers of inflation, behind gasoline and energy.Martin Wang, a software developer who began repairing broken computers more than a decade ago, says his popular Brookline, Massachusetts, repair shop has seen an uptick in business as customers look for alternatives to buying new devices.Wang says the rising costs are particularly noticeable when it comes to computer components, including memory and hard drives."The RAMs, and the hard drive, ridiculously expensive. The price jumped like not double, triple, triple or four times higher than the original price in the last year," Wang said, showing a 1 TB solid-state hard drive purchased for $400, the same one he said would have cost him a little more than $100 last year.Price increases are affecting both his business and customers, particularly students who may be shopping for new computers."It increases the cost for us to buy all the parts. And for the clients, most of them students, they might have to choose lower configuration, or they have to postpone their purchase plan," Wang said.Wang believes growing consumer demand, lack of supply, the expansion of artificial intelligence, tariffs and shipping are all contributing to higher prices.He says graphics cards, which are commonly used in gaming computers and AI applications, have become particularly expensive."Those are video cards. Because AI uses a lot of the good video cards, those cards for gamers became ridiculous expensive," Wang added.The higher costs have also changed how he operates his business. Instead of keeping a large inventory of computer parts on hand, Wang says he is stocking fewer components and purchasing them on an as-needed basis.Despite advances in technology that have historically helped make computers and their components more affordable, Wang says he sees little indication that prices will come down anytime soon from the recent upswing."There's Moore's Law in computers and all the parts are supposed to be cheaper and cheaper, but recently the parts became ridiculously expensive, and we even cannot see when it might come down. That is really bad news," Wang said.

title: Girl Scout report examines depression, isolation and safety concerns among Georgia girls
description: Georgia girls are excelling in the classroom, but many are struggling with their mental health and feeling isolated, according to a new report from two Girl Scout councils.
content: Georgia girls are excelling in the classroom, but many are struggling with their mental health and feeling isolated, according to a new report from two Girl Scout councils.The State of the Georgia Girl report, developed by Girl Scouts of Greater Atlanta and Girl Scouts of Historic Georgia, examines challenges involving mental health, social connection, and safety.Among its findings:90% of girls graduated from high school last year, outperforming boys by 5 percentage points.58% of middle and high school girls reported symptoms of depression.Two-thirds of high school girls lacked a caring adult to talk with about their feelings.Nearly 1 in 5 middle and high school girls reported seriously considering harming themselves in a 2023-24 survey.Jai Ferrell, CEO of Girl Scouts of Greater Atlanta, said the councils wanted to understand what is behind those struggles."What we needed to do was to get down into the academia and the real reason that our girls are in trouble. Some of it is a self-esteem, some of it is access to resources," Ferrell said.The councils are using the findings to shape their programs."Our girls are smart, but our girls are lonely," Ferrell said. "We have opportunities for girls to connect. We have places for girls to just be themselves."Following the report, the councils committed to providing 100 free annual Girl Scout memberships across Georgia.The two councils serve more than 40,000 girls.

title: 1 injured in crash involving semi truck on I-80 in Joliet, Illinois
