description: One person was injured in a crash on I-80 in Joliet, Illinois, early Thursday morning.
content: One person was injured in a crash on I-80 in Joliet, Illinois, early Thursday morning.Illinois State Police said a car and a semi truck crashed in the westbound lanes at I-55, near milepost 126. ISP said one person was taken to a local hospital with injuries. Their condition is unknown at this time. Traffic is down to one lane.

title: Fall finally arrives in Colorado with snow, rain and flight disruptions
description: Denver Water recommends disconnecting garden hoses and shutting off outdoor faucets before temperatures dip below freezing. Insulated faucet covers can also provide some extra protection.
content: Wednesday's rain made for a frustrating day for hundreds of travelers at Denver International Airport, including some football fans arriving for Thursday night's Broncos game.According to FlightAware, more than 700 flights were delayed, and five were canceled Wednesday. The FAA also put a ground delay program in place because of low clouds, wind, and a closed runway, with some flights facing delays of more than an hour.Among those arriving in Denver were Seattle Seahawks fans making the trip to watch their team take on the Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High.A few fans told CBS Colorado that the rain didn't bother them much. After all, they're used to it back home in Seattle.But rain isn't the only weather change headed our way.It was almost summer-like in Denver just a few days ago. Now, temps are expected to drop below freezing in some areas Thursday night into Friday morning.Fans heading to Mile High for Thursday Night Football will want to bundle up. The Broncos and Seahawks kick off at 6:15 p.m., just hours before temperatures could fall below freezing.While football fans are getting ready for the game, homeowners have some preparations of their own to make.Denver Water recommends disconnecting garden hoses and shutting off outdoor faucets before temperatures dip below freezing. Insulated faucet covers can also provide some extra protection.If you've been putting off that sprinkler blowout, now's the time to get it done. Homeowners who can't get a professional out before the freeze should at least shut off the water supply and drain their sprinkler systems. That won't always remove all the water trapped in the lines, but it can help reduce the risk of damage.When water freezes, it expands. That can crack pipes and leave homeowners dealing with expensive repairs.Denver Water also recommends insulating exposed pipes in unheated areas and knowing where your home's main water shutoff valve is just in case a pipe bursts.If you have sensitive plants, bring them inside or cover them to protect them from the cold. Temps could dip into the upper 20s early Friday morning. The cold won't stick around long!Denver could be back in the mid-70s by Saturday, with another mild day Sunday.

title: 10 freight train cars derail on Chicago's Southwest Side
description: A freight train partially derailed early Thursday morning on Chicago's Southwest Side, leaving 10 cars off the tracks but ultimately causing few problems.
content: A freight train partially derailed early Thursday morning on Chicago's Southwest Side, leaving 10 cars off the tracks but ultimately causing few problems.At 2:55 a.m., the 10 cars derailed from a CSX train near 75th Street and Central Park Avenue, where the freight train tracks divide the Chicago Lawn and Ashburn communities.CSX said five cars were turned on their side, four were leaning, and one set of trucks on a tenth car also derailed.All 10 cars were empty, CSX said.CSX said no crossings were affected and automotive traffic was not disrupted. There were no injuries, and there were no hazardous materials leaks or spills, CSX said.The cause of the derailment was under investigation Thursday morning.The track was expected to be cleared by Thursday afternoon, CSX said.

title: Sally Rooney's books withdrawn in U.K. over author's support for designated terror group Palestine Action
description: Irish author Sally Rooney's books are no longer being supplied to U.K. retailers over her support for the banned group Palestine Action.
content: London — World-renowned Irish author Sally Rooney's books will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the United Kingdom due to her public support for Palestine Action, a group banned as a terrorist organization in Britain.Rooney, the bestselling novelist behind "Normal People" and "Conversations with Friends," both of which have been adapted into television shows, and her publisher Faber have agreed to halt the supply of her books to British retailers, according to a statement from Faber."Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work. To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher," Faber said. Rooney previously said she intended to use proceeds from her work to financially support Palestine Action, potentially exposing her and her publisher to prosecution under British anti-terrorism laws.In an article published in The Irish Times in August 2025, Rooney wrote: "I want to be clear that I intend to use these proceeds of my work, as well as my public platform generally, to go on supporting Palestine Action and direct action against genocide in whatever way I can."What is Palestine Action?Founded in 2020, Palestine Action is a British direct-action group that has targeted arms manufacturers and other companies it accuses of supplying weapons to Israel with protests and sabotage.The group describes itself as a "movement committed to ending global complicity with Israel's genocidal apartheid regime."The British government designated Palestine Action as a terrorist organization in July 2025, citing the group's history of criminal damage and escalating attacks on defense infrastructure, including a factory belonging to U.S. defense company Teledyne Technologies in 2022.The 2025 decision came after the group claimed responsibility for breaking into a major air base, RAF Brize Norton, northwest of London, and damaging aircraft. The Associated Press and other outlets cited British police as putting the cost of the damage at around $9.4 million, though authorities have not publicly confirmed that figure.Under U.K. law it is a crime to be a member of a designated terrorist group, or to publicly support one.The ban on Palestine Action has prompted widespread protests and thousands of arrests across the U.K. According to the latest figures from Britain's Home Office, which oversees all domestic law enforcement, the average age of those arrested on suspicion of supporting Palestine Action is 59, compared to 28 for other terrorism-related arrests. The legality of the ban remains the subject of a Supreme Court challenge."Sally Rooney is finding out that she can't have her cake and eat it," a spokesperson for the U.K. activist group Campaign Against Antisemitism told CBS News, adding that it had reported the author to counterterrorism police over her vow to financially support Palestine Action.

title: MBTA to start issuing $125 fines for bus lane violations. Here's how they decide who gets a ticket.
description: In January, the MBTA will start issuing fines for drivers who are caught on camera blocking bus lanes​ and bus stops​ in the Boston area.
content: In January, the MBTA will start issuing fines for drivers who are caught on camera blocking bus lanes and bus stops in the Boston area. So, how does the T decide if you deserve a ticket, and how can you stay out of trouble?In city traffic, 60-foot buses are not a great fit. But slap a little red paint on the ground that says "Bus Only" then the wheels on the bus go round and round faster.In Greater Boston, the MBTA now has 40 miles of bus lanes between 7,000 bus stops. At Tufts Medical Center, WBZ-TV's David Wade jumped on the SL4 to South Station to see the use, and abuse, of bus lanes from the perspective of an MBTA passenger. That's where he met Macmarian Anibra. She said the bus lanes speed things up until drivers mess things up."I was late for an appointment on Saturday. I'm not making this up, just last Saturday. Someone was blocking the lane. The buses were all the way back," said Anibra.While getting off the bus, Wade saw a box truck parked in a bus lane for 15 minutes. He stuck around to ask the driver if he knew the MBTA will start handing out $125 tickets in January. He didn't respond. This month, the T started sending out warnings.Ryan Coholan, the MBTA's COO, said, "I think once citations start to go out and people realize that we're committed to this program, I think human behavior might change a little bit."The MBTA shared video of what bus drivers see every day. Cameras mounted on the buses show cars pulled over, dropping off people, or picking up food."Someone orders a beverage on their phone and they want to pull up to the curb to go get that beverage, I get it you want that coffee to be hot," said Coholan, who adds that forces buses to have to merge back in with cars, slowing traffic and sometimes means dropping off passengers in the middle of the road.The T has had enough."At some point, for lack of a better term, you have to rip the band-aid off. You know, the bus lanes have been in place for several years now. Without rules there's chaos. I think there is hope that people will respect that," said Coholan.About a third of all MBTA buses will now have special cameras. They're not supposed to record everything. Instead, every bus stop is "geofenced." Basically, that's an invisible boundary set by GPS. The cameras start recording only when they approach those spots.Alex Hallowell of the MBTA said all video clips marked as a violation will be reviewed by a staff member. "They can look at the incident, look at the context and say, 'Oh, that's clearly a police officer responding to an emergency, reject,'" Hallowell explained. "Or, 'Oh, that's clearly someone who just pulled over to grab a Dunkin' Donuts,' and they say approved, right."The MBTA will then send out a ticket in the mail which drivers can appeal. The agency said all video and personal information from license plates never leaves the MBTA database. It's the same system they use in some Commuter Rail lots to enforce parking fees.So how do you stay out of trouble?Here are a few tips: You cannot drive directly down the bus lane unless you're an emergency vehicle or getting out of the way of an emergency vehicle. You may cross over the bus lane to parallel park, but you can't stop in the bus lane. You can also get into the lane for turns, but you can't get over too early. You must wait until dashed lines on the road appear or signs allow it.But, in a city where space and patience are limited, not everyone is a fan of taking away an extra lane for cars. "You really want my opinion? My opinion is get rid of them," said a man named David who was stopped at a red light in Brighton. "They're a pain in the rear end!"The MBTA said it does not share or sell personal information, and photos and videos are deleted after 120 days. If you have a question you'd like us to look into, please email questioneverything@cbsboston.com.

title: New Logan Airport remote terminal being built in Braintree, Massachusetts
description: Construction is just getting underway in Braintree, Massachusetts on a new remote terminal for Logan Airport​ travelers.
content: Construction is just getting underway in Braintree, Massachusetts on a new remote terminal for Logan Airport travelers.Groundbreaking took place Tuesday on two new parking garages at the Braintree Logan Express site. One of the garages will host a new remote terminal facility.A pilot program in Framingham that lets flyers avoid security lines at the airport in Boston has proved to be a popular option since launching in June. More than 22,000 passengers have taken advantage of the remote terminal option so far."We saw the success of this approach in Framingham, and now we're bringing it to the South Shore," Gov. Maura Healey said in a statement. "This new terminal will give more travelers a convenient, affordable way to get to Logan Airport, while creating thousands of good-paying construction jobs and strengthening our economy."In Braintree, travelers will go through TSA security with their luggage and board a secure bus that takes them beyond the security checkpoint at Logan. Tickets will be $9 each way.The remote pilot program in Framingham is scheduled to run through at least March 2027, and it's expected to take a few years before the Braintree remote terminal is up and running. Logan Express and the remote terminal are two different facilities in Framingham, but they'll be combined into one in Braintree.The two eight-level parking garages will have more than 5,500 parking spaces once they're finished. Massport CEO Rich Davey said in July that Logan Express sites in Woburn and Danvers could be future homes to remote terminal locations. There's also been talk about adding a remote terminal in the Back Bay or the Seaport. Right now, the remote terminal service is only available to JetBlue and Delta passengers, but Massport said there are plans to add more airlines.

title: Construction set to begin on a major Pittsburgh bridge on Thursday night. Here's how you can avoid the traffic.
description: The Homestead Grays Bridge will be down to one lane in each direction on Thursday night through the weekend.
content: When major work is needed on one of Pittsburgh's many bridges, crews usually hold off until the weekend in order to minimize the traffic impact. That is not the case with the weekend work coming to the Homestead Grays Bridge, which will begin on Thursday and will impact the Friday rush hour. Simply put, be prepared for a mess in Homestead and Squirrel Hill. Which lanes will close on the Homestead Grays Bridge? The Homestead Grays Bridge is a critical link to the Parkway East from Homestead, Munhall, West Mifflin, and all points south. It also has about 40,000 drivers a day, and now, they're heading for another squeeze. Beginning on Thursday night at 9, the four lanes of the bridge will be down to just two lanes - one in each direction. The restrictions are being put into place for deck repairs, which are needed in multiple spots. What will make things more challenging is that the two lanes will change as needed to accomplish the repairs. On Thursday night, the first closures will be the middle two lanes of the bridge on the Homestead end of the bridge, and that means drivers will have to use the outside lanes - again, one in each direction. Similar work on recent weekends has resulted in extensive delays, and that work was not during the weekday rush, like it will be on Friday. Detours to take during work on Homestead Grays BridgeOn Friday morning, once the bridge is officially down to one lane, there are some options for detours. First, you can use the Rankin Bridge. That will take you across into Braddock, through Rankin, Swissvale, and then to the Parkway East. There is also the option of sticking with 837, which will take you through West Homestead to the Glenwood Bridge. That route, however, does have some construction, with some on the north end of the Glenwood Bridge. That detour takes you through Hazelwood. Finally, you can stick with 837 E. Carson Street and take that to the South Side, which avoids the construction.

title: Temperatures begin to tumble in the Pittsburgh area along with rain, wind, and potential storms
description: There will be a brief tick up on Friday before temperatures fall into the 50s this weekend.
content: Are you ready for a temperature tumble? It sounds way cooler than it actually is, in my opinion. The tumble begins around noon on Friday, with temperatures falling for the remainder of the day on Friday. The tumble will continue through the day on Saturday before we finally bottom out with lows near freezing on Sunday. Friday highs, near 70°, will be hit around noon. Saturday's high, and Friday's low (technically hit a fraction of a second earlier), will be hit at midnight on Saturday. Saturday's low will be hit just before midnight on Sunday. But wait, there's more! Anytime you have temperatures tumbling for a good 36 hours with little to no warming from hour to hour, you better believe you are going to have some wild weather that'll set it off. Most of the wild weather starts tonight, with wind speeds picking up and temperatures ticking up during the overnight hours behind a warm front and warm air advection. The area will be a real-world 'wind tunnel' with winds gusting up to 45 - 50 mph in some spots in the Laurel Highlands. Wind speeds will be strongest from 4 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Friday. The cold front that will start the temperature tumble moves through between 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Friday. We could potentially see storms strong enough and moving fast enough to set off severe thunderstorm warnings. The area is now under a level 1 (out of five) severe risk. The Storm Prediction Center calls it a 'marginal' risk. Scattered to isolated rain will begin as soon as this morning as warm air begins to move in ahead of the cold front today. Morning temperatures are in the 50s, with temperatures slowly climbing all the way up until the cold front arrives tomorrow. Think about us on the initial roller coaster hill at this point, with anticipation building for the Friday 'fall'. I have rain coverage for today at 40 percent, with the best chance for rain happening south and east of Pittsburgh. I have noon temperatures in the low 60s, with temperatures in the mid-60s as kids are getting out of school. Looking at the weekend, I wouldn't be surprised if we get a report or two about snow flurries on Saturday in the Laurel Highlands. It won't have any impact on anyone. Freeze warnings may be issues for a number of communities also on Sunday, with most places north of I-70 having a chance to see freezing temperatures in spots Sunday morning. Skies on Sunday morning should be clear and winds not too strong at sunrise. Next week is looking dry and seasonal, with highs in the 60s all week long.

title: Georgia midterms bring debates, record early voting and visits from Trump and Vance
description: With early voting underway, candidates are stepping up efforts to connect with voters across Georgia.
content: With early voting underway, candidates are stepping up efforts to connect with voters across Georgia.Candidates in some of the state's biggest races took the Atlanta Press Club's debate stage this week. Democratic U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff debated his Republican challenger, U.S. Rep. Mike Collins, on Tuesday. Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms appeared alone Monday after her Republican opponent in the governor's race, Rick Jackson, declined the club's invitation.National Republican leaders are also visiting Georgia. Vice President JD Vance met with supporters Wednesday at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. President Donald Trump is scheduled to hold a campaign rally Friday in Dalton.Omar Ali, an independent political strategist who has worked with Gov. Brian Kemp and former Vice President Kamala Harris, said Georgia's crossover voters make it a critical state for both parties."And so in Georgia, you have a lot of crossover votes," Ali said. "And so if the right message is sent, it can go either way."Georgia also set a first-day early voting record for a midterm election this week. The secretary of state's office reported 188,667 in-person ballots Tuesday, an increase of about 40% over the first day in 2022.Ali said concerns about federal policies and rising costs could be driving voters to the polls."So we're feeling that across the entire nation. And so Republicans and Democrats are feeling that," Ali said.He also offered his assessment of why Republicans are bringing Trump to communities such as Dalton to build support and encourage turnout."Most Republicans think that there's no chance whatsoever that Mayor Bottoms will win. And because of that, they're not as motivated," Ali said. "And so they are using President Trump in areas that is heavy MAGA base to motivate the rural areas to get out to vote."Trump's rally is scheduled for 1:30 p.m. Friday at Dalton Municipal Airport. Jackson and Collins are expected to attend.

title: Storms, wind and cold will impact Maryland this week
description: Friday and Saturday are First Alert Weather Days.
content: A record high of 88Â° was reached at BWI Marshall Airport on Wednesday afternoon. Baltimore's previous record was set at 86Â° back in 1975. It will remain warm and a bit humid through the afternoon.This week's weather whiplash will continue with drastic temperature changes, wind and storms in the forecast. Friday and Saturday are First Alert Weather Days, due to expected gusty winds, big temperatures swings and Friday evening storms.Temperatures cool off into tonight. We'll wake to temperatures ranging from the mid-50s to mid-60s across the state on Thursday morning. Plan on temperatures around 60 in Baltimore early Thursday. Scattered showers move through our area on Thursday. Temperatures remain in the mid-60s in many areas -- about 20Â° cooler than on Wednesday.Drastic weather changes will impact MarylandA burst of rain and strong gusty wind are most likely during the early hours of Friday evening. Afternoon temperatures will tumble from the lower 80s back into the 40s and 50s overnight with breezy winds, as the rain slowly exits during the overnight hours.Temperatures will be in the 40s and 50s on Saturday morning, with winds gusting 25 to 35 MPH. The breeze will make it feel chillier. It'll be a very brisk start to the Baltimore Running Festival. Wind-chills Saturday morning will be in the upper 30s and lower 40s for the first several hours of the morning. Few snowflakes possible in western Maryland mountainsIt's not out of the question that the first snowflakes of the season will fall across the mountains of western Maryland early Saturday morning. There won't be any accumulation. Saturday afternoon will be breezy and chilly, with afternoon temperatures in the mid to upper 50s. Wind gusts will remain in the 25 to 40 mph range through the afternoon. The winds relax by Saturday night. Keep gusty winds in mind if you're planning outdoor activities. The first widespread frost of the season is possible on Sunday morning. Despite a cold start to the day, sunshine will send temperatures back into the mid and upper 50s on Sunday afternoon, with much less wind.

title: Fake heiress who stole $30 million from California banks added to FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list
description: A 75-year-old woman has been added to the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters List for allegedly scamming California banks out of tens of millions of dollars nearly a decade ago while posing as the heiress to the McDonnell Aircraft Family.
content: A 75-year-old woman has been added to the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters List for allegedly scamming California banks out of tens of millions of dollars nearly a decade ago. Mary Carole McDonnell, of Missouri, has been on the run since she allegedly bilked banks in Los Angeles and Orange counties out of nearly $30 million in 2017 and 2018 while pretending to be the heiress of the McDonnell aircraft family. A reward of up to $150,000 has been offered for information leading to her arrest and conviction, the FBI said. "McDonnell is alleged to have knowingly, and with the intent to defraud, devised and participated in a scheme to obtain money, funds, assets, and property owned by Banc of California," said McDonnell's listing on the newly formed Most Wanted Fraudsters List. "McDonnell falsely claims to be an heir to the McDonnell Aircraft Family, with an $80 million secret trust to which she will have access."McDonnell is believed to be in Dubai and has ties to Southern California and Montgomery, Alabama. Federal agents say that McDonnell used the scheme to fraudulently take $14.7 million from Banc of California, "which she knew she was not entitled and has not paid back." They also believe that she defrauded other financial institutions in a similar fashion, resulting in an estimated loss of $15 million. In December 2018, federal prosecutors charged McDonnell with bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. An arrest warrant was issued at the same time. McDonnell is described as standing 5-foot-7 and weighing approximately 145 pounds. She has blonde hair and blue eyes, and detectives say she has a notable scar on her right knee. The FBI said she may have changed her appearance over the years and has gone by several aliases, including Mary C. Caroll and Mary Carole Carroll, Mary Carol McDonnell, Mary Caroll McDonell and Mary Caroll McDonald. "t's just a matter of time before McDonnell is caught as we work with our international partners to locate her. A generous reward is being offered in exchange for information leading to her apprehension and conviction, and a tip from the public might break the case," said a statement from FBI Los Angeles Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy.Federal investigators listed McDonnell's last known occupation as the chief executive officer of Bellum Entertainment, LLC, a Burbank-based television production and distribution company that made true crime shows. The company dissolved in 2017 due to undisclosed financial issues, which a CBS LA investigative story highlighted. During the investigation, employees said McDonnell did not pay them what they were owed.Anyone who knows more about McDonnell's whereabouts was asked to contact their local FBI office or the nearest American Embassy or Consulate. Online tips can also be submitted at tips.fbi.gov.

title: Caltrans plans multiple Highway 37 closures to prepare for El Niño
description: With a record El Niño likely to bring strong winter storms, Highway 37 in Sonoma, Napa and Solano counties will undergo multiple closures for emergency storm preparation, Caltrans announced.
content: With a record El NiÃ±o likely to bring strong winter storms, Highway 37 in Sonoma, Napa and Solano counties will undergo multiple closures for emergency storm preparation, Caltrans announced.The closures, which will take place over several weeks, will involve a stretch of the highway between Sears Point in Sonoma County and Mare Island in Vallejo. Crews are expediting work, which will require full shutdowns of the route, officials said."The water pretty much stayed out there in Vallejo the entire summer," said Caltrans spokesperson Bart Ney. "So, there's some damage to the roadway there. We have erosion that has taken some of the material that's underneath the roadway. And the pavement, of course, is cracked." Shutdowns will begin on Wednesday, Oct. 21 and Thursday, Oct. 22, as Caltrans closes the westbound direction of the highway from 7 p.m. to 4 a.m. the following day.The following weekend, both directions of the highway are scheduled to be closed for 55 hours, from 10 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 23 through 5 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 26.During the closures, crews will demolish the median and install K-rail to shift both eastbound and westbound traffic to what are currently the westbound lanes. Once the shift is complete, crews will focus on the eastbound lanes to raise portions of the roadway by 3 feet to address flooding concerns.Officials are also planning supplemental closures starting Friday, Nov. 13 at 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 15.Caltrans said motorists should expect delays and increased travel times. "The detours that are going to be in place for this 40-mile detour, over an hour, that's just the reality of the North Bay," he said. "There isn't the redundancy of routes that you see in other places in the Bay Area, or California for that matter. So, whenever we lose 37, we see how important that route actually is." The agency is recommending multiple detours around the closure. For westbound 37, drivers should exit Highway 29 (Sonoma Boulevard) in Vallejo and head north towards Napa. Drivers should continue to westbound Highway 12 (Carneros Highway) and then to southbound Highway 121, rejoining Highway 37 at Sears Point.Meanwhile, drivers using eastbound 37 will need to detour by taking northbound Highway 121, making a right on the Carneros Highway (Highways 12 and 121), followed by a right on Highway 12 and 29, rejoining Highway 37 in Vallejo.Officials said the roadwork is dependent on weather conditions.

title: Pakistan school roof collapses in Peshawar, killing almost 30 young students and a teacher
description: Almost 30 students and a teacher were killed when the roof of a small private school collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan, local officials say.
content: Islamabad — Almost 30 students and a teacher were killed Thursday when the roof of a private school collapsed in the Pakistani city of Peshawar, local officials said.The bodies of 17 children were brought to Lady Reading Hospital in the city following the incident, in addition to the body of a female teacher, Mohammad Asim, a spokesperson for the hospital told CBS News, adding that some survivors were also admitted in critical condition. At least 29 people were killed in total after the collapse at the Al-Khair Education Center in Peshawar's southwest Dir district, according to Asim and other local officials. The cause of the disaster remained unconfirmed, but a witness told CBS News the building appeared "not suitable" for use as a school, and a local police official said there was ongoing construction on the roof that could have overweighted the structure. "We have taken out at least 45 children," district emergency officer Iftikhar Khan said, according to the Reuters news agency. Mahwish Zaman, a teacher who was injured in the collapse, told the Associated Press after regaining consciousness in her hospital bed that the school had about 1,200 students enrolled, and she was in her class when the roof collapsed. She described it as feeling as if the sky had fallen. Zahir Hussain, who lives a couple of blocks from the school, told CBS News he was walking to work when he saw people running out onto the street. "I rushed to the spot and the school with others to see what had happened," he said. "Apparently first-period classes had just started … The building was overcrowded. The lesson had barely begun" when the collapse occurred.He said the school was in a relatively small residential building on a narrow street, and that it catered mainly to children from low-income families. Signage on the outside of the building indicated that there were classes for both boys and girls."The parents and families were in unbearable pain. The street was extremely narrow, which made it difficult for rescue teams to reach the site quickly," he told CBS News."The building was not suitable for use as a school at all. It is a very tragic incident, seeing dead innocent children's bodies left me silent, and it was extremely painful," Hussain said, calling it a "heavy tragedy for parents and the entire Dir colony." "It was a weak building structure," Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed said, according to Reuters. "Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse."

title: No plans on moving upcoming Steelers-Saints international game amid unrest in Paris, NFL says
description: The Steelers and Saints are poised to play the NFL's first-ever regular-season game in Paris next weekend.
content: The National Football League says it is continuing forward with plans for the upcoming Pittsburgh Steelers vs. New Orleans Saints game in Paris, amid ongoing unrest in the French capital. The Steelers and Saints are poised to play the first-ever NFL regular-season game next weekend in Paris, at the Stade de France.Ongoing protests over school conditions in recent weeks have led to violent clashes with police. The movement, which began in the Paris region and rapidly spread nationwide, has seen teenage students in their final years of high school block access to buildings and clash with law enforcement.The students say their school hours are excessively long, conditions inadequate including overheated classrooms and dilapidated buildings, and that there are too many staff absences.With the violence and unrest happening in the region, the NFL said that preparations are continuing as scheduled for the game between the Steelers and Saints on Oct. 25, as well as the events surrounding the contest."As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters," said NFL chief spokesperson Brian McCarthy in a statement. "We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."This marks the second straight year that Pittsburgh will be involved in an international game as the NFL expands its footprint throughout the world. Last fall, the Steelers were the home team when Pittsburgh hosted the Minnesota Vikings at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland, winning the game 24-21.

title: Brooklyn's Prospect Heights Alternate Side Parking pilot ends after compliance drops
description: A pilot program that reduced Alternate Side Parking requirements in Prospect Heights will not continue after sanitation officials said compliance fell and ticketing increased.
content: A pilot program that allowed some Prospect Heights residents to move their cars for street cleaning just once a week instead of twice has come to an end after city officials said the neighborhood failed to meet compliance goals.The New York City Department of Sanitation launched the test in August in partnership with City Council Member Crystal Hudson. The program reduced Alternate Side Parking requirements on selected streets, giving drivers fewer days to move their vehicles for street cleaning.Officials said they hoped the reduced schedule would encourage greater compliance. Instead, sanitation data showed the opposite.According to the Department of Sanitation, Alternate Side Parking compliance dropped by 11% during the pilot. The agency also reported that the number of parking tickets issued increased slightly, rising from 455 to 457 per month despite enforcement days being cut in half."I was expecting to see an increase in compliance given fewer days that folks would be required to move their cars, but that just wasn't the case," Hudson said.Department of Sanitation Press Secretary Vincent Gragnani said the pilot was designed to determine whether residents would comply with parking regulations if they only had to move their vehicles once per week."The concept was, in essence, to say, 'OK, you only have to move once per week per side, but you really have to do it,'" Gragnani said. "Unfortunately, as the council member said, people did not do that, and compliance got worse."Some residents said they were disappointed by the results. Rebecca Spivak said neighbors had hoped the program would become permanent and believed residents understood they were participating in a test.Others who complied with the rules said they would like to see the program return despite the outcome.Residents interviewed by CBS News New York speculated that some drivers may have chosen to pay an occasional $65 ticket rather than move their cars, undermining the pilot's goals.As a result of the findings, Alternate Side Parking regulations in Prospect Heights will remain unchanged.

title: Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduces bill to prohibit federal funding for Flock technology
description: Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib on Wednesday introduced a bill to ban the purchase of automated mass surveillance systems, such as license plate readers like Flock.
content: Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib on Wednesday introduced a bill to ban the purchase and operation of automated mass surveillance systems, such as license plate readers like Flock.The "Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act" would prohibit federal funding from being used to support the technology and require state and local governments to divest from the systems. The bill would also ban the federal government from using the systems and require that all data from them be permanently deleted."This is about the fact that we need to stop allowing our neighborhoods to be surveillance and that mass surveillance does not make us safer," Tlaib said at a press conference. "When they pull up at our residence and having them come and tell them that somehow this is going to make us safer is a lie."Several communities in Southeast Michigan have canceled their contracts with Flock, including Eastpointe, Milford, Madison Heights and Bedford Township. Additionally, some local law enforcement agencies identified instances of technology misuse by employees. Tlaib says she was "proud" of the cities that voted to end contracts with Flock.Despite city and county law enforcement officials arguing that the technology has helped solve crimes, many citizens have expressed concerns about privacy."Federal funds should be used to invest in our communities and real safety solutions. We need good jobs, affordable homes, clean water and reliable electricity. That's what's going to make us safer. Instead, our government is sacrificing our rights to big tech companies that care more about their profits, selling our data, than about our safety," Tlaib said. " Our residents don't want Flock cameras, and we're making our voices loud and clear."Tlaib called for cities like Inkster and Detroit to reconsider the use of Flock. On Tuesday, Inkster officials announced that they were expanding Flock in the city through a 10-year contract. Flock told CBS News Detroit that the contract includes 20 license plate readers, five video security cameras, 48 gunshot detection devices and one drone.The city initially started with six readers in 2023.Mayor Byron Nolen, who ran against Tlaib in the August primary, said on Tuesday that the technology was "another step forward for our city.""It's being proactive, preventing crime before it happens, responding faster when emergencies occur, and building a community that's united around safety and progress," Nolen said.Flock is also the topic of another bill introduced at the federal level by Missouri Sen. Josh Hawley last month. The Stop Flock Abuse Act would regulate automated license plate readers by imposing stricter limits on data, security and search functions. At the state level, two bills have been introduced in the House and Senate. House Bill 5492 would regulate the use of ALPRs by private and governmental entities and regulate the use of plate data. Under the bill, governmental entities could obtain or use privately captured plate data only pursuant to a warrant or request, provided the system retained the data for up to 14 days.A similar bill, Senate Bill 1131, was introduced in the state Senate by GOP Sen. Jim Runestad.

title: Tai Baribo scores on PK, adds assist to lead DC United to 2-1 victory over Red Bulls
description: Tai Baribo scored on a penalty kick then added an assist to lead D.C. United to a 2-1 victory over the New York Red Bulls.
content: Tai Baribo scored on a penalty kick then added an assist to lead D.C. United to a 2-1 victory over the New York Red Bulls on Wednesday night.DC United (7-9-12) took a 1-0 lead in the 5th minute on Baribo's PK. His 15th goal of the season came after he was fouled by Red Bulls midfielder Adri Mehmeti.Baribo used his head to snag an assist on first-year defender Silvan Hefti's header in the fifth minute of stoppage time and DC United led 2-0 at halftime. Keisuke Kurokawa helped set up Hefti's second goal off a corner kick.Defender Lucas Bartlett picked up his second yellow card, leaving DC United a man down from the 68th minute on and New York (10-13-6) cut it to 2-1 three minutes later on Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting's fifth goal. Emil Forsberg and Ronald Donkor had assists. Choupo-Moting and Forsberg both entered in the 57th minute.Sean Johnson turned away six shots for DC United to keep the Red Bulls at bay.Ethan Horvath had one save for New York, which began the day in eighth place in the Eastern Conference before losing to 12th-place DC.United played New York to a 4-4 draw on the road in April. The club has gone 2-2-2 since the start of September, while the Red Bulls are 3-3-1 over the same span.DC United improves to 5-5-5 at home and the Red Bulls fall to 5-7-3 on the road.Up nextNew York: Hosts Toronto FC on Saturday.DC: At Orlando City on Saturday.

title: L'Anse Creuse middle schoolers banned from attending high school football games
description: A notice sent to parents says that because of some ongoing behavior concerns at football games, students at Middle School Central and Middle School South wouldn't be allowed to attend high school games, even if they were with a parent.
content: Fighting among some L'Anse Creuse middle school students appears to have prompted officials to ban them from attending high school football games.CBS News Detroit spoke to parents, coaches and even a teacher, off camera, who said it was two Fridays ago when multiple fights broke out under the bleachers at a L'Anse Creuse High School football game. A notice sent to parents on behalf of the high school said that because of some ongoing behavior concerns at football games, students at Middle School Central and Middle School South wouldn't be allowed to attend high school games, even if they were with a parent. The notice came as families celebrated Senior Night for the varsity football team."The board did not hear about it. The board did not receive that communication; it was our community that reached out to us, so I'm very thankful to the parents who were not going to let this go who really pushed the issue," said L'Anse Creuse School Board Trustee Sandra Hernden. "What do I do with their siblings? They're middle schoolers, and you're telling me there's a blanket ban so you're separating our family."Hernden, a parent of three children in the district, says she heard from a group of upset parents who didn't understand why their middle schoolers couldn't attend the high school football games, even if their kids weren't the ones causing the distractions. "And the students that were causing those problems and those issues, those should've been the students that were addressed, not an entire blanket ban," said Hernden.Parents at a L'Anse Creuse seventh-grade football game say that the message was a shock, even though they had heard about middle schoolers fighting at games under the bleachers. "The whole point of the football game is to bring the school community together, and that's what makes Friday night football the best, and the fact that they decided all on their own completely on their own," said Board Trustee Shane Sellers. Sellers says he was frustrated with the message. After much backlash, the school eventually sent out another message just hours before Friday's game, stating that middle schoolers could attend under certain conditions."I think the whole thing was blown out of proportion on the principal's end," said Sellers.In a phone interview, L'Anse Creuse Superintendent Keith Howell said that principals have to make decisions all the time about how to manage situations, and that last Friday night turned out well because of the revision to the first notice.

title: Washington Township residents question proposed municipal authority takeover
description: A proposal that would see Washington Township, Fayette County, take over the township's municipal authority is on pause amid community outcry.
content: A proposal that would see Washington Township, Fayette County, take over the township's municipal authority is on pause amid community outcry.More than 100 people packed a meeting Wednesday evening, with many questioning why the township was considering the move in the first place for the authority that manages the township's water and sewage system. They pushed for answers, suggested solutions and shared their concerns."We're worried that they're going to sell [the municipal authority] to another private company or another water authority," said resident Eric Kostelac. "We're going to lose basically control of the water, and our prices are going to go up. We're going to have to pay more for little to no gain."The board of supervisors, their engineer and lawyers were able to answer some but not all of their community's questions. As board chair Derrick Powell acknowledged, they don't have the answers themselves, which is one thing holding them back from a vote. The topic had previously been on the agenda, but was removed.Jan Amoroso, the general manager of the Municipal Authority of Washington Township, said they had no advance warning that the township was looking to take over the authority."I had no idea. It was such a shock," she said. "There was no notice. Up until this point, they haven't spoken to us."The township hired a special council, Douglas Sepic, to assist them. When KDKA-TV asked him why supervisors want to take over the authority, he said, "There is a stormwater issue that has to be addressed by the township."But, as Amoroso pointed out, the township already manages the stormwater system, while the authority handles sewage. The township's solicitor, David Tamasy, explained further, saying they don't have the money to fix the stormwater system, which has to be replaced, and they already have multiple infrastructure projects they don't have money to pay for. The idea with the municipal authority then would be that they could own it and use it as an asset to leverage when applying for a loan.Neighbors said there were other ways the township could have gone about this, both from the perspective of tackling the issue and how little they were kept in the loop."Let's try and be more transparent, that's all I can ask for," Kostelac said during the meeting.When the idea of a town hall was brought up, board chair Powell acknowledged it is something they could have done. He said he personally plans to meet with Amoroso and hopes to resolve the issue by next week.The authority serves around 10,000 people both in and out of the township.

title: Downtown Miami neighbors, officials raise concerns over proposed LED billboards at Adrienne Arsht Center
description: County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava says the proposal would give the arts venue another source of revenue, while residents of nearby towers warn of light and quality-of-life impacts.
content: A battle is brewing in downtown Miami over a proposal to place massive LED billboards on the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts.The Miami Downtown Neighbors Alliance sent a letter to Miami-Dade County officials requesting an opportunity to participate in discussions before any final decisions are made."We're kindly asking that they should kind of involve us in the conversation piece," said Downtown Neighbors Alliance President James Torres.Torres warned that the billboards' light would harm the quality of life for residents in nearby high-rises."You're gonna have an impact on quality of life because if you look at where the structure is today or it could be across the street, there's a living, breathing community as well," Torres said. "There's about four towers across the street."Miami-Dade County owns the Arsht Center building, and the county commission will ultimately decide whether to install the signs. Details of the proposal are still being finalized.In a statement, Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava defended the project as a financial opportunity for the performing arts venue."The Arsht Center is a cultural anchor in our community, and we want to support its continued success," Levine Cava said. "This proposal gives the Arsht another source of revenue to support its programming and operations and helps diversify its funding."However, local elected officials have voiced strong opposition. Miami City Commissioner Damian Pardo said the advertising agency behind the proposal previously tried to push the project through the city of Miami, where it was shut down."We have been warning residents and warning people that this is going to continue to proliferate throughout our state," Pardo said. "You have noise, constant construction, traffic. People are just looking to escape that and preserve their quality of life. So adding LED signs that are enormous â that just does not work for the neighborhood."City of Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins also expressed opposition to the billboards in statements to the Miami Herald, but has not responded to CBS News Miami's request for comment.It remains unclear when the county commission will officially discuss the proposal. Torres noted that residents would be open to compromises, such as shutting off the displays at 10 p.m. or 11 p.m. to minimize disruption.CBS News Miami reached out to representatives for the Arsht Center and the advertising firm for comment, but responses were not immediately received.

title: Lawyers for man shot by ICE say agents didn't identify themselves in Marble Hill shooting
description: Lawyers for the man shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill last week are seeking his release, arguing in a newly filed court petition that federal agents never identified themselves before opening fire.
content: Lawyers for the man shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill last week are seeking his release, arguing in a newly filed court petition that federal agents never identified themselves before opening fire.The Legal Aid Society, which represents 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, filed the petition Wednesday.According to the filing, attorneys claim agents failed to show documentation or communicate with Belgal before firing into the vehicle. Belgal's 5-year-old son was in the back seat at the time of the shooting.The Department of Homeland Security did not comment on the new allegations Wednesday. However, DHS has previously said ICE agents fired their weapons because they believed their lives were in danger. The agency has also alleged that Belgal has ties to the Trinitarios gang.Belgal's attorneys said he remains in urgent need of medical care."ICE officers shot him in the neck in front of his 5-year-old son, failed to provide him with immediate medical assistance, and now continue to hold him in a facility notorious for medical neglect," attorneys Perry McAninch and Elyssa Williams of The Legal Aid Society said in a statement. "With a bullet still lodged in his neck and his serious medical needs unmet, every additional day in custody puts him at further risk. The Court must intervene and order his immediate release."Last Friday, a judge temporarily barred Belgal from being deported or transferred to any facility outside the Southern or Eastern Districts of New York or the District of New Jersey without prior court approval.Belgal remains detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.

title: South Placer Fire District seeks funding boost as voters weigh Measure B
description: Measure B will appear on the Nov. 3 ballot for voters in Granite Bay and Loomis. If approved, it would establish a $375 uniform parcel tax across the district to help fund fire and emergency services.
content: The South Placer Fire District is asking voters to approve a new parcel tax to address staffing shortages, rising operating costs and the potential closure of additional fire stations.Measure B will appear on the Nov. 3 ballot for voters in Granite Bay and Loomis. If approved, it would establish a $375 uniform parcel tax across the district to help fund fire and emergency services.Two of the district's six fire stations have already closed because of staffing shortages and funding challenges. Station 19 is among them, with a sign outside warning that no fire engine is staffed there.Fire Chief Darin Snedeker said a third station is operating below national staffing standards, affecting the district's ability to respond quickly to emergencies."When seconds matter in this industry, that's pretty significant for us," Snedeker said.The chief said the district has struggled to retain firefighters and paramedics, with wages and working conditions contributing to staffing challenges."We've lost 112% of our workforce over the last six years â 68% of that is from the firefighter-paramedic rank," Snedeker said.The district currently has seven vacancies among its firefighter-paramedic ranks, Snedeker noted."When you have vacancies like that, the firefighters are working on average 72, if not more, hours a week. And when you do that, over time, that wears on the employees' health, mental health and physical health as well," he said.Measure B would help the district address staffing needs, operating expenses and rising equipment costs. According to the district's website, the cost of purchasing a new fire engine has nearly doubled since 2021.Snedeker said if the measure fails, the district could face the closure of three of its six stations."Obviously, having to close firehouses just increases response time, and it increases in terms of the medical aid increases time, the effective time we can get the patient to the hospital for definitive care. And in the case of fire, unchecked fire doubles in size every minute," Snedeker said.The district has held community meetings and reached out to voters to build support for the measure, with campaign signs visible in neighborhoods throughout Granite Bay.But not everyone supports the proposed tax.Jeff Moss, a Granite Bay resident who served as a South Placer Fire District board member and volunteered with the district for nearly 20 years, is urging voters to reject Measure B."We have to be concerned about the dollars and how they're being spent," Moss said.Moss said the current situation stems from voters rejecting a previous ballot measure intended to fund the district. However, he disputes the district's warning that more stations could close without additional revenue."It's a scare tactic, if you want to put it that way, that we're in grave danger of losing stations if this tax doesn't pass. I believe the money is there to keep these stations open," Moss said.The measure would need support from at least two-thirds of voters to pass and replace the district's current annual tax.

title: Miami police investigate after dog found dead underwater, tied to cinder blocks off Coconut Grove
description: A boat resident discovered the dog Tuesday morning, and police say they questioned a possible owner who was arrested on unrelated charges.
content: Miami police are investigating an animal cruelty case after a dog was found dead underwater, tied to two cinder blocks in waters off Coconut Grove.Ryan Young, who lives aboard a sailboat in the area, said he discovered the dog Tuesday morning."It was the worst thing I had seen in my life," Young told CBS News Miami.Young said the dog's own leash and zip ties had been used to secure the animal to the blocks."The worst part about it was they tied the dog with its own leash," he said.Police said investigators have questioned someone believed to be the dog's possible owner, but ownership has not been established."The individual was questioned and arrested on unrelated charges," according to a statement attributed to Miami Police Chief Edwin Lopez. "The animal cruelty investigation remains ongoing."Miami Commissioner Damian Pardo, whose district includes the area where the dog was found, called for accountability Wednesday evening."This is a horrific incident," Pardo said.Pardo, who described himself as an animal lover, said he is committed to helping find whoever was responsible. He also expressed concern that someone capable of harming an animal could pose a danger to people."This is something that nobody would tolerate," he said. "It's cruel."The discovery also disturbed residents in Coconut Grove, especially local dog owners."The dogs are your family," Vicky Rosen told CBS News Miami. "Can you imagine finding your dog tied underwater or thrown over there? I can't believe it.""In my head, it's difficult to process that somebody can do that to an animal," Maria Maldonado, a local dog owner, said. "Somebody that does that to a dog is almostâ¦they need to kill somebody as well. Very very bad," another dog owner, Hernando Delaroche, said. "It's really unfortunate; there are so many people here that would love a dog like that," a third dog owner who did not want to be identified said. "That person should not be near more animals, kids, women, and people in general," Maldonado said. Young said he reached out to about 40 people who live aboard boats in the area via a WhatsApp group, hoping someone could identify the dog. He said none recognized the animal.Detectives continue to pursue leads as the animal cruelty investigation remains open.

title: Harford County boy at center of kitten rescue speaks out in support of school bus driver
description: A 10-year-old boy and his mother are joining thousands of others who have signed a petition calling for the school bus driver to be reinstated.
content: For 10-year-old Alex Thomas, the bond with a kitten named Brookie began the moment he spotted her in the middle of the road while on his way to North Harford Elementary School.The kitten got her name from her coloring, which reminded Alex of cookies and brownies."The kitten was like the size of a bag of Utz party mix. Like this big. She could fit in your hands," Thomas said.Alex said his bus driver, 67-year-old Cynthia Morgan, pulled over and let him off the bus to rescue the tiny kitten."She turned on the back lights things, opened up the door and she had the stop sign out and everything. And so what she did was she let me walk out and grab the kitten and then walk back on the bus," Thomas said. "The kitten pooped on the bus. A big stinky one on the floor."Rescue came at a costMorgan was removed from her Harford County Public Schools bus route after the incident for violating protocol."I was absolutely gutted by how she was treated. That nobody contacted me, nobody talked to Alex, nobody talked to any of the other parents before the decision was made to let her go," said Alex's mother, Taffy Thomas.Plea for school bus driver's reinstatementNow, Alex and his mother are joining thousands of others who have signed a petition calling for Morgan to be reinstated."She's been his driver since kindergarten. And she goes out of her way for these kids to get to know them," Taffy Thomas said. "I never thought my child was in danger. I was never concerned. It never even crossed my mind that she would put him in danger."Alex turns 11 next month, and he has a few birthday wishes.The first is a plea to the public."I don't think we should focus on the what-ifs and focus on what really happened," he said.The second is a plea to the school district."To bring back Ms. Cynthia because she did nothing wrong," Alex said.And the third?"If my dad is watching this, we need to get the kitten!" he said.Harford County schools respondHarford County Public Schools declined to comment on a personnel matter but said in a statement last week that "certification and decertification of a bus driver is not always based on a single incident."When asked whether the district planned to reconsider its decision to remove Morgan from the route, officials referred CBS News Baltimore back to that statement.Harford County School Board President Lauren Paige defended the district's decision in a statement, saying, in part, "We must evaluate situations involving student transportation not only by the intentions behind an action, but also by the potential risks involved. Allowing a student to exit a school bus and enter a roadway to retrieve an unfamiliar animal raises legitimate safety concerns…It is important to remember that good intentions and sound safety decisions are not always the same."

title: Police issue alert after woman fights off attacker on West Chester, Pennsylvania, walking trail
description: Police are looking for a man they say assaulted a woman on a trail near West Chester University.
content: The West Chester Police Department is looking for a man who they say assaulted a woman on a walking trail in the 500 block of Dean Street Tuesday evening. The woman was walking just before 7 p.m. when an unknown man approached and assaulted her, according to a news release from police. She was able to push the man away and run. Police released images from surveillance video captured nearby.The suspect was around 6 feet tall and was wearing a gray or silver hooded jacket, according to police. He was last seen running toward nearby Everhart Park. The trail is less than a mile from West Chester University.In a statement, police say the department "recognizes the concern this incident may cause within our community. We are committed to investigating this incident and appreciate any help from the community."Police are gathering evidence and increasing patrols in and around surrounding parks and neighborhoods. "I commend the victim for their courage in reporting this incident, and I encourage everyone to exercise safe practices out in the community, which include: walking with others when possible, staying in well-lit areas when possible, carrying a cell phone, and being observant of their surroundings," Chief Joshua Lee said in a statement. Jamie Paxson lives near where the attack occurred and came out to help search his wooded property moments after he heard about what happened. "I was just on my land here searching, seeing if anyone was hiding," Paxson said. "There are places to hide back there, but I didn't want to disturb the police, so I came up this way and police were right here."Paxson says he also let police know about the security cameras on a nearby home, including one his neighbor added just this past weekend, which recorded the incident."He had surveillance signs because I told police he's got a surveillance camera, but the one that caught that was one that was strapped to a blue bird box that he just put up Saturday, so what's the odds of that happening."Anyone with information is asked to contact West Chester police at 610-696-2700 and reference incident number WC-26-29110.

title: Baltimore City Council considers new department to send alternative responders to 911 calls
description: Baltimore City Council members held a hearing on a proposal to create a new Department of Neighborhood Safety, which would send trained responders to certain 911 calls instead of police.
content: Baltimore City Council members held a hearing on a proposal to create a new Department of Neighborhood Safety, which would send trained responders to certain 911 calls instead of police.The proposed department would establish an alternative response system for nonviolent emergencies, including calls involving people experiencing mental health crises.City leaders estimate that about 22,000 calls to 911 each year could be better handled by alternative responders rather than police.The proposal also calls for replacing the city's 911 dispatch system.Over the past year, the City Council held two hearings examining Baltimore's efforts to divert certain 911 calls to alternative responders. City leaders determined that existing options did not consistently provide the right response at the right time for residents experiencing mental health crises.City Council President Zeke Cohen and staff from Mayor Brandon Scott's office examined an alternative response program in Durham, North Carolina, called the Holistic Empathetic Assistance Response Team (HEART).During their visit, Baltimore officials saw HEART teams de-escalate mental health and other quality-of-life calls. The program dispatches trained teams to nonviolent emergencies that do not require a medical response.Cohen and Scott introduced the proposal to create the Department of Neighborhood Safety on Sept. 14."As the first city in America to legislate trauma-informed care, we should be meeting our residents with the right response when someone is experiencing a mental health crisis," Cohen said. "That person could be someone's parent, child, sibling, or partner â and we have a responsibility to make sure the city can respond appropriately and urgently in their darkest moments."The proposed department would house mental health clinicians and peer responders prepared to respond to nonviolent emergencies. It would also formally incorporate the work of the Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement (MONSE)."This new department will house mental health clinicians and peers ready to respond urgently to non-violent emergencies. It will also house and codify the important work of the Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement (MONSE)," Cohen said. "I am grateful for Mayor Scott's partnership and look forward to passing this legislation to create the new Department of Neighborhood Safety through the City Council."

title: 40-year-old woman dies after stabbing in West Baltimore, police say
description: A 40-year-old woman died after being stabbed Wednesday evening in West Baltimore, police said.
content: A 40-year-old woman died after being stabbed Wednesday evening in West Baltimore, police said.Officers responded around 5:25 p.m. to the 2400 block of Druid Hill Avenue, where they found the woman suffering from a stab wound.She was taken to a hospital, where she was pronounced dead.Police said a person of interest was taken into custody. No further details about the circumstances of the stabbing were immediately available.Anyone with information is asked to call Baltimore police at 410-396-2100 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.Baltimore has recorded 91 homicides so far this year, compared with 103 at this time in 2025, according to police data.

title: Man killed, 19-year-old seriously injured in separate Baltimore shootings
description: A 32-year-old man was shot and killed Wednesday evening in West Baltimore, police said.
content: A 32-year-old man was shot and killed Wednesday evening in West Baltimore, police said.Officers responded around 8:39 p.m. to the 2300 block of Avalon Avenue, where they found the man suffering from gunshot wounds, according to police.He was taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.Police have responded to 91 homicides in Baltimore this year.Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to call police at 410-396-2100 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.19-year-old seriously injured in South Baltimore shootingA 19-year-old was seriously injured in a shooting Wednesday evening in South Baltimore, police said.Officers responded around 7:10 p.m. to the 4200 block of Mariban Court, where they found the victim suffering from gunshot wounds.The 19-year-old was taken to a hospital in serious condition.Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to call police at 410-396-2499 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 1-866-7LOCKUP.

title: 3.0-magnitude earthquake shakes Riverside County
description: The earthquake happened at around 8:30 p.m., approximately two miles north of San Jacinto, according to the USGS.
content: A 3.0-magnitude earthquake caused a jolt in Riverside County on Wednesday night.It happened at around 8:30 p.m., approximately two miles north of San Jacinto, according to the United States Geological Survey. The temblor occurred at a geological depth of just over 13 miles and caused brief shaking throughout the surrounding area, with some people reporting to the USGS' "Did You Feel It?" tracker from communities like Wildomar, Menifee, Temecula and Fallbrook. There were no reports of damage or injury as a result of the tremor.

title: Sacramento looks to culture, history and food scene to attract more tourists
description: Sacramento tourism officials are looking beyond major events to attract more visitors, highlighting the capital city's cultural attractions, diverse communities, local restaurants and history.
content: Sacramento tourism officials are looking beyond major events to attract more visitors, highlighting the capital city's cultural attractions, diverse communities, local restaurants and history.The effort was a focus of a cultural tourism summit that brought together local artists, historians and tourism officials to discuss how to share Sacramento's story with a broader audience.Sacramento draws more than 15 million visitors a year, including people who come for major events such as Aftershock and the California International Marathon. But tourism leaders say the city has attractions that can draw visitors throughout the year."What we have appeals to people," said Sonya Bradley of Visit Sacramento.Bradley said the goal is to encourage visitors to explore more of the city and return for future trips."We always say, once we get them here they want to stay and they want to come back," Bradley said.Sacramento's museums and historic sites are central to that effort. Attractions such as the California State Railroad Museum, Sutter's Fort and the Crocker Art Museum offer visitors a look at the region's history and culture beyond its Gold Rush roots.Agustin Arteaga, CEO of the Crocker Art Museum, said visitors are often surprised by what they find."Their minds are blown because they probably don't expect what they're going to see," Arteaga said."This is one of the big magnets for visitors to come to Sacramento," he said.Tourism officials are also highlighting Sacramento's food scene, with an emphasis on locally owned restaurants that may be less familiar to out-of-town visitors."You know those places where the locals go, that's honestly the experience people want, they want the local experience," Bradley said.City officials say Sacramento's Indigenous and immigrant communities also offer opportunities to showcase the city's cultural identity through art, history and creative experiences."One of our amazing strengths is the diversity of our communities reaching back into the history of our communities," said Jason Jong, Sacramento's cultural and creative economy manager.Jong said promoting those experiences can also support local businesses and artists by bringing more tourism dollars into the community."We're really a nexus for a lot of cultural activity that does bring back dollars into the economy," Jong said.Bradley said the broader goal is to offer experiences that distinguish Sacramento from other California destinations."We want people to come, have a good time, and then go back and tell their friends and family to come visit Sacramento," she said.One opportunity for visitors to explore the region's history comes Saturday, when Sacramento hosts its annual Archives Crawl. The event gives people an inside look at historical documents and artifacts preserved by local archives, reflecting the city's history dating back to its founding in 1848.

title: Children abducted by father from Inkster found safe in Ohio, police say; suspect dead
description: Two children, who police say were abducted by the father in Inkster on Wednesday, have been found in Norwalk, Ohio. Police say the father died from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.
content: Two children, who police say were abducted by the father in Inkster on Wednesday, have been found in Norwalk, Ohio. Police say the father died from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. According to the Inkster Police Department, officers were contacted at about 10:04 a.m. about a domestic violence incident in the 4500 block of Springhill. A woman told police that the father of her children, ages 4 and 6, went into a bedroom and attempted to tie her up. The woman fought back, but the man allegedly struck her with a firearm and restrained her again before leaving the house with the children, according to police.The woman told police that she called the man, who said they were going to Rouge Park in Detroit and threatened to kill himself and their children. Police entered the vehicle's license plate into the Flock system, indicating that the vehicle had left the city of Inkster.Authorities say Detroit police received a call from the man's grandmother, who reported that the man had made similar suicidal threats. Police went to Rouge Park but were unable to locate the vehicle.Inkster police say the investigation led to an intersection in Norwalk, Ohio, where officers there were notified that the man might be in the area. Inkster police say officers were able to connect with the children, during which one of them told police that they were in a cornfield and that their father had shot himself.Police in Norwalk confirmed that the man has died and that their local investigation was turned over to the Huron County Sheriff's Office.Inkster police say officers are en route to Ohio to help coordinate the children's safe return to their mother. They say their investigation is ongoing.

title: Community holds vigil for Reading, Massachusetts woman as son faces murder charge
description: Flowers and candles were held in remembrance of a Reading, Massachusetts, mother who was allegedly murdered by her own son.
content: Flowers and candles were held Wednesday night in remembrance of a Reading, Massachusetts, mother who was allegedly murdered by her own son.On the same night that friends and neighbors held a memorial for Andria Hanafin, prosecutors announced her son Ryan Hanafin will stand before a judge Thursday afternoon, facing a murder charge and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon in connection with the death of his mother.From schoolteachers to town leaders and neighbors, hundreds came together at Memorial Park remembering Andria Hanafin by how she lived, as a beloved mom, veterinary technician, and florist with a heart for rescuing cats. "There are moments when words simply aren't enough when the sadness, the shock and the heartbreak are so profound that we struggle to make sense of what has happened," said Town Manager Jayne Wellman."She was just a helper and a giver with all the cats she loved and had such a big heart," said friend Holly Gillette through tears. "I want to be there for her because I just love her so much."The 49-year-old was found shot to death inside her Center Avenue home last Thursday.Prosecutors say her 22-year-old son Ryan Hanafin is now charged in connection with her murder. He fled to Vermont and was arrested and held without bail as a fugitive of justice but will be brought back to Massachusetts.Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan was at the vigil for Andria. "You never lose sight of the person at the heart of this, the loss to a family and to a community. These are the kinds of things that frighten people. They're hard for kids to process," Ryan said.Court documents reveal tension in the home. Investigators say Andria's husband told police his wife and son "had been getting in several arguments recently about the cats in the house, which the victim was rescuing."The MSPCA is now caring for 84 cats recovered from the home. Court documents also show the mom relayed yet another argument over the phone with her husband and said she wanted their son out of the family home.Investigators also say Ryan Hanafin had 19 guns in the house, 15 of them unsecured, and he faces charges for that too."No amount of training or experience prepares you for when the truly unthinkable happens in our town," said Reading Police Chief David Clark. "We stand with you as you grieve this profound tragedy."The DA's office says Ryan Hanafin will be arraigned in Woburn District Court Thursday afternoon.

title: Turgeman scores 2 goals, Revolution beat Cincinnati 3-2, clinch playoff berth
description: Dor Turgeman scored two goals and the New England Revolution beat FC Cincinnati 3-2 on Wednesday night to clinch a berth in the 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs.
content: Dor Turgeman scored two goals, Joshua Wynder added a goal and an assist, and the New England Revolution beat FC Cincinnati 3-2 on Wednesday night to clinch a berth in the 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Matt Turner had eight saves for the Revolution (15-10-4). Carles Gil had an assist and became the first player in MLS history with at least 10 assists in six consecutive seasons. Wynder, a 21-year-old center back acquired Sept. 3 on loan from Portuguese club SL Benfico, put away a header that gave the Revolution the lead for good in the 43rd minute. Turgeman put away passes from Peyton Miller in the 21st and 51st minutes, the 22-year-old's first multi-goal game in MLS. Tom Barlow opened the scoring in the 13th minute and Kevin Denkey added a goal in the 67th for Cincinnati (9-10-9) Barlow has scored a goal in each of his last three games and Denkey has six of his career-high 17 goals this season in the past four games. Cincinnati had 59% possession and outshot the Revolution 23-10, 10-5 on target. Up next Revolution: Hosts Chicago on Saturday. Cincinnati: Hosts Columbus on Sunday.

title: Linda residents raise concerns over rat infestation in neighborhood
description: Residents in the Edgewater neighborhood of Linda, near Marysville, say a growing rat problem is damaging vehicles, spreading through yards and raising concerns about potential health risks.
content: Residents in the Edgewater neighborhood of Linda, near Marysville, say a growing rat problem is damaging vehicles, spreading through yards and raising concerns about potential health risks.Homeowners say they have seen rats running between properties and getting into cars, and they're asking Yuba County for help addressing the problem.Tennasity Tidwell, who has lived in the neighborhood for years, said she recently received a text from a neighbor warning that a rat had climbed onto a vehicle and was heading toward the engine."The neighbor texted and said, 'Is your car out here? Because one of the rats is running up the tire, going into the engine.' Thankfully it was the other neighbor's car," Tidwell said.Tidwell said she had never experienced a rat problem in the neighborhood before."It's infested with rats. They're running into people's cars, running in and out of the yards, going into cars eating wires," she said.Tidwell said she has contacted county services but has not seen anyone come out to address the issue."Basically they just want everybody to get pest control but it's like, look at all the houses," she said.Tidwell said she already pays for pest control and that workers have treated her property. However, she believes the problem extends beyond individual homes, with rat nests scattered throughout the neighborhood.Another resident, who asked to remain anonymous, said the activity has become concerning enough that they take extra precautions before driving to work in the morning."I'm setting alarms off before I get in my car in the morning because it's dark. And the kids filmed one under my car. They start eating the wires, we've watched them go into other homes," the resident said.Yuba County said it has no complaints on file for the address. A county spokesperson also said rat activity can increase during harvest season, when rodents are displaced from agricultural fields.But Tidwell said the problem is new to her neighborhood."I've been here 5 years, I've never seen rats. Not once," she said. "I'm just worried about them damaging the cars, and I don't know if they're going to get people sick," she said.

title: Appeals court lets Florida enforce social media ban for kids under 14, overturning injunction
description: Florida has won a key court decision in a case involving a ban on social media accounts for kids under 14.
