Their disappearance has become one of the world's greatest mysteries. "We're the only people who have put together a plan to do something like that," Pettigrew said. "So it's entirely new."

title: New loan program offers funds for wildfire safety for California homeowners
description: A new California low-interest loan program aims to help those seeking to improve fire safety on their properties.
content: As California enters peak wildfire season, wildfire safety is top of mind for many homeowners. A new state low-interest loan program aims to help those seeking to improve fire safety on their properties without breaking the bank. SB 894, authored by Senator Ben Allen (D-Pacific Palisades) and signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom, creates the California Wildfire Resilience Loan Program. The program is designed to provide homeowners financial assistance to help keep their homes safe.Ted Moore lives in Auburn. He says his home is his haven, but the threat of a wildfire haunts him."Oh yeah, it's overhanging us all the time," Moore said. "We're kind of gambling here." Moore pays to have his defensible space cleared regularly. Getting home hardening done, like a new roof, windows, and vent, is out of his budget. "It's a lot of money," Moore said. "A lot of effort every year ... It's kind of an unattainable thing for me," Moore said. Karl Susman is an insurance industry expert. He says the public needs to put pressure on lawmakers to fund the new program with plenty of money. "Well, the commitment is that there will be funds put in," Susman said. "The amount of money that's put in is, we don't know yet. And again, I think it's going to have a lot to do with the public getting involved."State Senator Josh Becker (D-Menlo Park) served as chair of the Senate Natural Resources Committee and is concerned federal funding for wildfire prevention has slowed in California under the Trump administration."Wildfires don't discriminate against Democrats and Republicans," Becker said. "We're doing our part â we need the federal government to do its part as well."State lawmakers have committed to creating the low-interest loan fund starting Jan. 1, 2027. It remains unclear how much funding will be available, as well as what the application process will look like for homeowners.

title: Amber Alert issued for baby last seen in LA's Westlake District
description: The California Highway Patrol issued an Amber Alert for a baby last seen in LA's Westlake District.
content: The California Highway Patrol issued an Amber Alert for a baby last seen in Los Angeles' Westlake District. Officers said 9-month-old Nylah Austin was last seen on Oct. 12 with 29-year-old suspect Kennisha Austin walking around the area of W. 3rd Street and S. Bonnie Brae Street.While the pair were last seen in the Westlake District, CHP officers issued the Amber Alert on behalf of the Torrance Police Department, which handled the case. Torrance PD said they received the abduction report and handled it as a mutual-aid agreement with other agencies to get information out quicker.

title: Proposition 133 would make Colorado 7th state to require life without parole for child sex trafficking
description: Colorado would become the seventh state in the country to mandate sentences of life without parole for child sex trafficking if Proposition 133 passes this November.
content: State legislative analysts released a study in August on child sex trafficking statutes in all fifty states. They found sentences of up to life in prison in 23 states, but only 6 of those states mandate life without parole. Colorado would become the seventh if Proposition 133 passes.In Colorado, human trafficking of a minor for sexual servitude is defined as selling, recruiting and transporting a minor for commercial sexual activity. It's a Class 2 felony that carries a sentence of 8-48 years in prison with the possibility of parole. Judges can give longer sentences if they classify it as a crime of violence, or if the defendant caused serious bodily injury or used a deadly weapon.Proposition 133 would expand the definition of human trafficking of a minor for sexual servitude to include buying sexual activity with a minor. It would be a Class 1 felony with a mandatory sentence of life in prison without parole, which is the same as first-degree murder.State fiscal analysts estimate the measure would increase spending on prisons by more than $180,000 a year starting in 2041.Proponents say life sentences will help deter child sex trafficking.A study by Common Sense Institute found Colorado had the 15th-highest rate of human trafficking in 2024 and, on average, 64% of victims were children.Opponents of Proposition 133, including the Colorado Coalition Against Sexual Assault (CCASA), worry victims could face the same sentence as their traffickers. CCASA says many victims are forced to recruit other kids and, while state law allows them to use that in their defense, CCASA says those who can't prove they were coerced would now face life in prison because judges would no longer have discretion.Democrats killed a bill identical to Proposition 133 in the state legislature this year.It is statutory, so it needs a simple majority to pass, and the state legislature can change or repeal it.

title: Former Republican Colorado Congressman Ken Buck endorses Democrat Phil Weiser for governor
description: Former Republican Colorado Congressman Ken Buck says he's endorsing Democrat Phil Weiser for governor, according to CBS Colorado Political Reporter Shaun Boyd.
content: Former Republican Colorado Congressman Ken Buck says he's endorsing Democrat Phil Weiser for governor, according to CBS Colorado Political Reporter Shaun Boyd. Buck is a long-time Colorado Republican politician and former prosecutor whose career took him from congressional investigative staff work to federal law enforcement, local elected office and the U.S. House of Representatives. He represented Colorado's 4th Congressional District from January 2015 until his resignation on March 22, 2024. Weiser is term-limited out of the attorney general's office and is running for governor for the first time. Weiser was elected to Colorado Attorney General in 2019.Weiser and Republican nominee Victor Marx will face off in a November general election to replace term-limited Democratic Gov. Jared Polis. Marx beat out long-time Republican lawmaker Barb Kirkmeyer in the primary to appear on the ballot. Marx has been ordered to pay nearly $58,000 for accepting illegal campaign contributions. The hearing officer who issued the fine, Macon Cowles, says Marx took in 210 illegal donations between May and July totaling more than $83,000. Weiser's campaign late Wednesday emailed a list to CBS Colorado of all the Republicans who he says have endorsed him.Former Westminster Mayor Herb Acheson Former Senate Republican Leader; Former House Republican Leader Norma AndersonFormer Moffat County Commissioner Ray BeckFormer Department of Local Affairs Executive Director Mike BeasleyFormer Congressman Ken BuckFormer Prowers County Commissioner Wendy Buxton-AndradeFormer Great Outdoors Colorado CEO Chris CastilianFormer Attorney General Cynthia CoffmanFormer State Senator; Former State Representative Don CoramFormer Moffat County Commissioner Audrey DannerFormer Speaker of the Colorado House of Representatives Russ GeorgeLas Animas County Commissioner Tony HassFormer State Representative Tom MasseyTeller County Commissioner Dan WilliamsFormer State Representative Cole WistFormer State Representative Rob WitwerA Democrat has been in the governor's office in Colorado for the past 20 years.Election Day is Nov. 3.Colorado Voter's Guide

title: Pope Leo's lung cancer prognosis could depend on these factors, doctors say
description: Pope Leo XIV was diagnosed with lung cancer after a surgery that removed a nodular lesion from his right lung, the Vatican said.
content: Pope Leo XIV was recovering Wednesday, a day after having a lobe of his right lung removed and confirming a diagnosis of lung cancer. Leo had blood tests and a chest X-ray that showed a "normal post-operative course," the Holy See Press Office said. "The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed."The surgery removed what the pope and Vatican described as a localized nodular lesion."Those types of lesions can actually be removed and even cured just by surgery alone," CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook said. But the Vatican has not shared the stage of cancer, or whether it has spread, which would help determine if Leo needs further treatment. Here's what multiple doctors, who are not involved in the pope's treatment, told CBS News about his possible prognosis. What type of cancer does Leo have?Leo was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a common type of non-small cell lung cancer, doctors say. "It's very common and also generally a very good prognosis when found early on," Dr. Kalvin Lung, a thoracic surgeon at the Northwestern Medicine Canning Thoracic Institute, told CBS News 24/7 on Tuesday. The surgery Leo underwent "is also something we commonly do, and it's a very successful surgery and people can recover very quickly from it," Lung said. What stage is the cancer?The Vatican has not said what stage the cancer is. "They may not know yet," LaPook said Wednesday morning. But the information that has been provided suggests the cancer may have been caught early. "The fact that he can have a successful surgery so quickly is all a very good prognosticators of probably an early-stage lung cancer," Lung said. If there had been evidence that the cancer had spread elsewhere in the body, Leo may have had treatment before the surgery like chemotherapy or immunological therapy, LaPook said. "But the fact they went right in and tried to take it all out might say to you, well, they think maybe that's it," he said. If that is the case, Leo likely would not need further treatment, Lung and LaPook said. Is there lymph node involvement?If the cancer spread to the lymph nodes, which filter fluid in the body, that would change the prognosis and possible treatment plan, doctors said."Sometimes it looks like on all the tests beforehand that it's just localized, and it turns out the lymph nodes are involved," LaPook said. Further testing would determine the treatment, he said. "There are all these special tests you do. Look at the genetic makeup of it. Are there any special markers? Are there any special things on it that are driving it to multiply?" LaPook said.What is the recovery?Doctors have said the recovery from the surgery is typically a few weeks. Leo is expected to stay at the hospital for a week, according to the Vatican.The pope's recovery was "proceeding as expected," the Holy See Press Office said Wednesday."The Holy Father has carried out respiratory physiotherapy and has begun walking around his room," they said. "He has resumed a regular diet, having both breakfast and lunch."Leo may have some pain from the surgery "for the first couple of days up to the first one to two weeks," Lung said."I think he'll be back to doing what he wants to do around three to four weeks," said Dr. David Jones, chief of thoracic surgery at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. "Maybe a little slower, but he'll be fine."

title: Moisture moving into Colorado is a welcome shift for Aurora's water supply, manager says
description: An incoming weather system is bringing snow to Colorado's High Country, where much of Aurora's water supply begins.
content: Wednesday's light rain might not look significant, but Aurora Water managers say it's arriving at an important time after months of hot and dry conditions across Colorado.The moisture is helping replenish soils that have been unusually dry for much of the year. And, just as important, the same weather system is bringing snow to Colorado's High Country, where much of Aurora's water supply begins."We are absolutely thrilled that we're starting to get some of the moisture that is again moving back into the state," said Shonnie Cline, deputy director of Aurora Water's internal and external affairs. "We've had really low soil moisture. We've actually had some of the lowest soil moisture levels in the country this year."This week's rain offers relief for thirsty lawns, trees and landscapes; Aurora Water says the bigger benefit may come months down the road."It's saturating the soil, so that, way over the winter when it starts to cool down, we'll get more of that snowpack, and we'll be able to hopefully capitalize on that when it turns into runoff in the spring," Cline said.That runoff is critical because Aurora doesn't rely on rainwater that falls directly within city limits for its supply. Instead, much of the city's water originates in mountain watersheds, where winter storms build the snowpack that eventually melts into streams, rivers and reservoirs. Cline said that's why water managers are paying close attention to conditions in Colorado's High Country as the winter season approaches."The water that is coming down in any meaningful way in Aurora belongs to somebody else downstream," she said. "All of our water rights that matter are up in the mountains, and so I'm happy to say, right now, we're seeing snow that is coming into those mountains right this minute."As temperatures cool, Aurora Water is also reminding residents that the outdoor watering season is coming to an end. Oct. 15 is the deadline to shut off spray irrigation systems for the season. Cline said the recent moisture should help landscapes heading into winter, but added homeowners should continue monitoring trees and shrubs during dry stretches and hand water when needed.

title: Ventura County partial human remains found in 1990 identified as 57-year-old woman
description: The woman referred to as Jane Doe for decades has been identified as Patricia Diana Hunt Fielding, born on October 15, 1933, in Kern County, California.
content: The Ventura County Sheriff's Office announced it has learned the identity of partial human remains that were found 36 years ago along the highway in an unincorporated area of Ojai. The woman referred to as Jane Doe for decades has been identified as Patricia Diana Hunt Fielding, born on October 15, 1933, in Kern County, California.Her remains were found in 1990 by accident, as fire department crews were responding to a traffic collision down an embankment near Highway 33 and Creek Road.The Medical Examiner's Office recovered the remains for further investigation. It was estimated that the remains belonged to a female between 30 and 60 years old, with an estimated height between 5 feet 3 inches and 5 feet 6 inches.The cause of death could not be determined, and the person's identity had remained a mystery until now. The sheriff's office said advanced DNA testing was used, leading detectives to identify a family who had not heard from a relative in several decades. A Family Reference Sample was obtained and compared to the unidentified human remains. The comparison resulted in a positive identification.Fielding was a mother of four, but little is still known about her life or the circumstances surrounding her death, the sheriff's office said. Investigators hope that releasing her name will help provide additional information. Anyone with information regarding Patricia Diana Hunt Fielding is asked to contact the Ventura County Sheriff's Office Cold Case Unit at (805) 383-8739 or coldcase@venturacounty.gov.

title: Motorcyclist spotted going 120 mph leads deputies on multi-county chase, runs out of gas, authorities say
description: An Arlington man was arrested after refusing to stop for a Johnson County sheriff's deputy. The pursuit ended in Erath County.
content: A motorcycle rider spotted traveling about 120 mph led authorities on a multi-county pursuit that ended abruptly when he ran out of gas, according to the Johnson County Sheriff's Office.Joshua Saliema of Arlington was taken into custody and booked into jail following Tuesday's chase. Authorities did not specify what charges he faces.Mansfield police initially observed the motorcycle traveling at the high rate of speed, the sheriff's office said.Later that evening, a Johnson County deputy attempted to pull Saliema over in the northeastern part of the county. He refused to stop, prompting a pursuit that continued into Erath County, where he eventually ran out of fuel."The Johnson County Sheriff's Office appreciates the cooperation of our law enforcement partners in helping bring this incident to a safe conclusion," the sheriff's office said in a social media post.CBS News Texas will provide updates as more information becomes available.

title: Series of deaths connected to Red Lake Nation child welfare program leads to federal takeover
description: The Bureau of Indian Affairs took over the Ombimindwaa Gidinawemaaganinaadog, the tribe's child welfare program, last month.
content: There are new details after the federal government took over the Red Lake Nation's child welfare program last month. A letter dated Sept. 9 from the U.S. Department of the Interior to the Red Lake tribal chair says, "Child abuse and neglect conditions continue to rise within the Red Lake Nation." The Bureau of Indian Affairs took over the Ombimindwaa Gidinawemaaganinaadog, the tribe's child welfare program, last month.The letter lists concerns over the deaths of eight children in the last five years, including two deaths this July. It says the children died from malnutrition, abuse, neglect and drug overdoses.The FBI began to track the program after a child died in December 2021 when its mother passed out and fell asleep. Investigators say the woman was a "known addict" and believed the child had been "born addicted."Most recently, the FBI is investigating a case where a child was life-flighted twice from Red Lake with "serious medical issues." In the first incident, the child had a skull fracture and "suspicious bruising." Ombimindwaa was involved but did not notify law enforcement and placed the child back in the home. The same child was airlifted again with facial injuries. Authorities claim that when the FBI requested the child be placed outside the home until further investigation, Ombimindwaa refused.The letter says tribal officials have "consistently refused to engage with federal authorities responsible for protecting the welfare of the Red Lake Nation's children." A spokesperson for the Red Lake Nation says they are in talks with the Bureau of Indian Affairs and they're "committed to ensuring every child and family receives the care and protection they deserve."To report concerns about child abuse, neglect or sexual abuse, the Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families recommends contacting the county or Tribal Nation where the child lives. You can find a list of Minnesota's county and tribal child protection agencies by clicking here. If there is an immediate concern of harm to the child, the agency recommends calling 911.

title: Dispute over cigarette led to alleged baseball bat attack at Pittsburgh gas station, police say
description: A Vandergrift man is charged and accused of allegedly attacking another man with a baseball bat after an argument over a cigarette.
content: A Vandergrift man is charged and accused of allegedly attacking another man with a baseball bat after an argument over a cigarette.It happened outside the Sunoco gas station on Cedar Avenue on Pittsburgh's North Side.According to police paperwork, the victim, Josh Mascara, said he was hit with a baseball bat about 20 times and has a broken fibula.Police say things got heated when the suspect, 41-year-old David Rose, refused to give Mascara a cigarette and told him to "get a job.""You really went and got a bat to chase after a person about a cigarette? People are just angry nowadays for no reason. I don't understand it," said Toni Eubanks.Pittsburgh police responded to the Sunoco gas station around 4 a.m. Tuesday. An employee told police that Mascara asked Rose for a cigarette.Police documents say Rose refused and told Mascara, "No, get a job." They say that's when an argument started. Investigators say Mascara yelled at Rose and threw rocks in his direction, hitting Rose's Jeep. The employee told police Rose "chased Mascara through the parking lot and hit him with a baseball bat."Police found Mascara "lying in the middle of the road." The victim said he had been hit "about 20 times with a baseball bat all over his body. He feels that his right leg is broken, and his back and head got hit.""That is so sad because he didn't have to chase him. All he had to say was no," Eubanks said. "I'm sure those rocks didn't hurt [Rose]. A rock and a bat, they don't compare."The victim went to the hospital. A doctor told police Mascara's injuries are consistent with getting hit with a blunt object.Rose allegedly admitted to chasing Mascara through the parking lot, but said the victim fell in the middle of the road.Police say there is video of Rose with a baseball bat, but no video of the alleged attack."The guy just wanted a cigarette, and somebody is reacting to it and instead of just being like, 'Here, buddy,' or 'No, I can't help you; I am going to chase you around with a baseball bat,'" said Samantha Carlisi. "That's crazy. That scares me to go anywhere.""If someone asks you for a cigarette and you know in your heart and mind you do not want to assist this person, just simply say no. You don't have to be snarky," Tyrone Powell said. "For a person to do that, clearly he has some kind of mental issues." Rose is charged with aggravated assault, simple assault and disorderly conduct. At last check, he had not been arraigned.

title: Amazon Prime Air drones now making deliveries in south suburbs, causing mixed reactions from residents
description: Each drone is 5.5 feet tall and 5 feet wide and can carry packages up to 5 pounds.
content: Amazon drones are now delivering packages in Chicago's south suburbs.People who've seen them are expressing mixed reactions.Amazon Prime Air drones are officially delivering packages across the south suburbs to neighborhoods within their reach from the Amazon fulfillment center in Markham. Each one is said to be able to deliver up to 7.5 miles away.The magic number for each drone is five. They're 5.5 feet tall and 5 feet wide and can carry packages up to 5 pounds.According to Amazon spokesperson Caitlin Tully, the response to the delivery service has been positive."Prime Air's ultra-fast drone delivery is safe, reliable, and the customer response has been overwhelmingly positive. Available in locations around the country, Prime Air delivers a wide selection of essential products at everyday low prices, including diapers, baby formula, over-the-counter medications, medical supplies, pet food, and more. Our drones are fully electric and produce zero exhaust emissions. Each new site also creates skilled local jobs with great health and other benefits from day one," she said.According to Amazon, there are 21 drones at the Markham center and they aren't impacting jobs, but instead handle small deliveries while drivers continue delivering all other packages. Concerns still remain, as pointed out by those who shared cell phone video with CBS News Chicago from a Homewood neighborhood delivery — they're loud. "It was decently noisy!"It's the first thing that stood out to Julian Gomez when he saw one for the first time on Tuesday. "I was wondering who was piloting the drones?" he said.These aren't the first delivery drones to fly.Since this time last year, there have been reports of drones crashing, dropping packages in pools, along with general noise and nuisance complaints. "Sounds like a beehive coming right outside our house," said Texas resident Scott Bratcher. On Wednesday, Massachusetts lawmakers sent a letter to the Federal Aviation Administration expressing concerns about Amazon's proposed plans there, saying in part, "Local elected officials have sent letters calling for a pause on Amazon's drone operations pending further review of concerns including noise and safety."People in the south suburbs have expressed both noise and privacy concerns. Amazon responded to both. Amazon says no one is viewing anything from the drones live, with onboard cameras and sensors used only for navigation and obstacle detection, operating independently.As far as sound complaints go? Not really addressed. The sound of their drone was compared by them to the noise created by a passing car, but they said they're always working to improve the experience."As long as they can then figure out how to make the drones a little quieter so it's not so pervasive? That would be really good," Gomez said. According to Amazon, the drone delivery program created jobs, with 30 new positions at the Markham site.Note: Amazon issued a correction of jobs created from 55 to 30 after the airing of this story.

title: U.S. may have withheld warnings to Ukraine of Russian strikes that killed 6, cut power to 600,000, sources say
description: The Trump administration may have withheld intelligence warnings to Ukraine about Russian strikes that killed 6 and cut power to 600,000 people, sources say.
content: The U.S. may have intentionally withheld early warnings this week of Russian strikes on Ukraine, multiple sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine "received no advance warning from our partners" when Russia launched a ballistic missile barrage at Kyiv and other locations early Tuesday. The sources said American officials told their Ukrainian counterparts the system used to detect Russian missile launches had failed due to "bad weather." Ukrainian officials, speaking on the condition of anonymity given the sensitivity of the topic, told CBS News they did not believe the excuse, and they accused the U.S. instead of "playing" with the system. When Russia launched another wave of ballistic missiles around 3 a.m. local time on Wednesday, the sources said the U.S. early warning system appeared to be working again. The sources said the U.S. had failed to provide intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches during one previous instance earlier this year, citing the need to focus more resources on the Middle East.Zelenskyy said Wednesday that Russia launched more than 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 attack drones and loitering munitions during the overnight attack, primarily targeting energy and critical infrastructure in Kyiv and Kharkiv, killing six people and leaving some 600,000 without power. President Trump, asked Tuesday if the U.S. had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine, said: "No, we haven't. We help them, but we're really helping them get to a final answer. We want the war ended.""We are helping them, and we are sharing intel. We want the war to end, so we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end," Mr. Trump said.Russia started launching strikes soon after Mr. Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire."Earlier this week, the Trump administration threatened to stop sharing intelligence and to halt the purchase of U.S.-made weapons by European allies for Ukraine via the PURL procurement system if Ukraine did not stop deep strikes against Russian energy infrastructure, a European and a Ukrainian official told CBS News.Ukraine relies on U.S. intelligence for both offensive and defensive military capabilities, including data from satellites and aircraft sensors used to identify launches of Russian aircraft and missiles. Sources familiar with the matter told CBS News the U.S. had not ceased intelligence sharing with Ukraine overall — calling the lack of a warning about this week's attacks a specific incident. Ukrainian officials and soldiers also told CBS News that Ukraine's military had started experiencing difficulties Tuesday night and Wednesday morning with Starlink, the satellite technology owned by SpaceX's Elon Musk. In an interview with CBS News earlier this year, Ukraine's former minister of defense Mykhailo Fedorov said Starlink was one of Ukraine's most important technologies, as it allows Ukrainian soldiers to communicate and carry out strikes in environments saturated by electronic warfare. "On the night of 14 October, without warning the Defence Forces, SpaceX unilaterally restricted the operation of Starshield terminals ('military package') while in motion. This complicates UAV missions, particularly interceptors and middle-strike drones, and reduces capabilities for frontline logistics, reconnaissance and signal relay," sources in Ukraine's Ministry of Defense told CBS News. "At present, the Ministry of Defence is in contact with the United States, SpaceX and NATO partners, is collecting data from all units, and backup communication channels are being tested and put into use."The Starlink restrictions were first reported by the Kyiv Independent and the Financial Times. CBS News has reached out to SpaceX, the White House, and the Pentagon for comment. On Wednesday, as President Zelenskyy arrived in the United Kingdom to meet with Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other officials, he called for a U.S. response to the recent Russian strikes."The strike was absolutely deliberate and indicative in its scale — such a demonstrative disrespect from Russia toward America has never happened before. Russia does not consider the statements of the President of America to be strong," he wrote on X. "We ask America and EVERYONE in the world who does not close their eyes to reality to respond, and to respond harshly."

title: Florida man arrested on murder charge in ex-fiancée's 2011 disappearance
description: Michelle Parker disappeared the same day that an episode of "The People's Court" aired that featured Parker and the suspect, Dale Smith Jr., in a contentious dispute over an engagement ring.
content: A man has been arrested on a murder charge in connection with the disappearance of his ex-fiancée nearly 15 years ago, authorities in Orlando, Florida, announced Wednesday. Michelle Parker, then 33, disappeared on Nov. 17, 2011, the same day that an episode of the reality court show "The People's Court" aired that featured Parker and the suspect, Dale Smith Jr., in a contentious dispute over an engagement ring. The Orlando Police Department reported Wednesday that Smith was taken into custody on a single count of second-degree murder. Parker's SUV was located abandoned one day after she went missing, but she has never been found. Parker and Smith have two children together.Orlando Police Chief Eric Smith said in a news conference following Wednesday's arrest that Smith Jr. was "the last known person to see or hear from Michelle" on the day of her disappearance after she had dropped their children off at his home. The police chief said that over the past year, his department expanded its investigation into the case and "took a fresh, focused look at all the evidence.""We reexamined testimony and conflicting statements made by the suspect and used advanced digital forensics to uncover and analyze additional evidence," Smith told reporters. Smith Jr. has been interviewed by investigators multiple times, Orlando police Det. Phillip McMican said Wednesday, and he had also taken part in several depositions related to the investigation as well. "Very specific questions were asked of him numerous times over the years, where he gave different answers to those same questions," McMican said of Smith Jr. McMican said that advancements in forensic technology allowed investigators to "better interpret" evidence — including vehicles, electronic devices, phones and computers — than what was available to them 15 years ago. McMican also disclosed that "new evidence has been found in the last year."The exact details of what specifically prompted the arrest were not provided, however. In a separate statement, police said that although Parker has not been located, "all evidence leads to Dale Smith Jr. as the person responsible for Michelle's murder."Smith Jr. has long denied any wrongdoing.According to CBS affiliate WKMG-TV, on the night she disappeared, Parker was captured on security video dropping her children off at Smith Jr.'s home. Her vehicle was found abandoned the following day in an Orlando parking lot, WKMG-TV reports, and her cellphone was located by divers in an area lake in December 2011. Smith Jr. had been a suspect in the case since around that time. "Michelle definitely didn't deserve to have her life ended," Parker's mother, Yvonne Stewart, told CBS News on Wednesday. "And the injustice of it, that the person responsible was free."Added Parker's brother, Dustin Erickson: "I've been carrying a lot of bad thoughts for 15 years that weren't happy. They got lifted a little bit today."

title: September CPI report shows inflation accelerated to 3.7% as energy costs soared
description: Gas prices, which jumped 9.1% in September from August, accounted for more than half the monthly rise in inflation.
content: Inflation accelerated across the U.S. in September, rising at an annual rate of 3.7% as energy costs jumped, according to new government data. The latest Consumer Price Index shows that stubborn price pressures persist just weeks before Americans vote in the midterm elections.By the numbersThe CPI tracks changes in prices over time for a basket of commonly purchased goods and services. Economists expected the index to rise at an annual rate of 3.6% in September, according to FactSet.Inflation picked up after two months of holding steady at an annual pace of 3.4%. Core CPI, which excludes the more volatile energy and gas categories, rose 2.6% from a year ago, accelerating from a 2.4% rate in August and higher than economists' forecast of 2.5%.Inflation has risen sharply since the start of the year due to soaring energy prices, sparked by the war in Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine. The Labor Department said Wednesday that gasoline prices, which rose 9.1% in September from the prior month, accounted for more than half the monthly increase in the CPI report. Energy prices rose 20.4% from a year ago, while gasoline jumped 34.2%.Prices at the pump have cooled slightly in recent weeks but remain elevated. The national average for a gallon of gasoline was $4.33 a gallon on Wednesday, AAA reported, up from $2.98 before the war started. The national average for diesel, which hit a record high in late September, was $6.29 a gallon.Higher diesel prices increase the cost of transporting goods around the U.S., often leading to higher prices for consumers on everyday items like groceries. "The CPI was clearly hot, and there aren't many ways to sugarcoat it," Wall Street analyst Adam Crisafulli, head of Vital Knowledge, said in a note to investors on Wednesday. Energy played a "huge role," he added, noting that prices may not head lower anytime soon as the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine escalate."Energy prices being so high for so long is starting to seep into the broader economy," he said.One category of spending that saw large price increases last month was airline fares, which are up 22.4% from a year ago, according to the CPI report. Increases in shelter and used car costs also pushed up the core inflation figure, experts noted.Nine in 10 Americans say prices are the most important factor shaping their views of the economy, according to a CBS News poll released earlier this month.What this means for the Fed and interest ratesEconomists say the September inflation figures could put pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate later this month, as consumer prices rise faster than the central bank's 2% annual target. "Today's hotter-than-expected CPI report shows that inflation is still well above the Fed's target, and that the current rate-hiking cycle isn't likely to end anytime soon," David Royal, chief finance and investment officer at Thrivent, a financial services firm, said in an email.The spike in core CPI shows price pressures are broadening into other categories beyond energy, experts noted, a sign inflation remains sticky. In September, the Fed hiked interest rates for the first time since 2023, bringing the federal funds rate to between 3.75% and 4%. Fed officials also signaled that they expect to raise rates again later this year. The central bank has two more policy meetings this year, on Oct. 27-28 and Dec. 8-9."This is the type of move that could prompt the Fed to pull the trigger on another hike this month, rather than wait as Fed officials have recently suggested, with markets now shifting to a 50% chance of that happening, up from 20% prior to the data," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, said in a report.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar's relatives issued subpoenas as part of immigration probe
description: The subpoenas were issued on Friday, just days before Omar's home in Washington, D.C., was searched early Monday morning by investigators from ICE's investigative unit.
content: Multiple relatives of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar received grand jury subpoenas, as part of the ongoing criminal investigation into her family's history for evidence of possible fraud and false statements in their immigration paperwork, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.The subpoenas were issued on Friday, just days before Omar's home in Washington, D.C., was searched early Monday morning by investigators from ICE's investigative unit.Omar's personal cell phone was taken by Homeland Security Investigations during the search, two sources told CBS News.The subpoenas were first reported by the New York Times.The decision by the Justice Department to take those overt investigative steps so close to the midterm elections has sparked criticism. It appears to run contrary to the DOJ's own internal guidelines, which stipulate that federal prosecutors and agents "may never select the timing of any action" for the "purpose of affecting any election, or for the purpose of giving an advantage or disadvantage to any candidate or political party."Customarily, the Justice Department has operated under an unwritten, so-called "60-day rule" cited in a 2016 DOJ inspector general report. It refers to the general practice of prosecutors to avoid the public disclosure of investigative steps related to electoral matters or the return of indictments against a candidate for office within 60 days of a primary or general election.Omar, a frequent critic of President Trump's — and a frequent target of Mr. Trump and his allies — has denied any wrongdoing, and she has accused the Trump administration of attempting to "target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."Mr. Trump said Monday that he had "nothing to do with" the raid. Sources said Attorney General Todd Blanche, however, was aware of the search. The Public Integrity Section, which handles the nation's most politically sensitive criminal investigations, was consulted, the sources also said. But that section was largely gutted by the Trump administration last year, with only two attorneys remaining in its ranks. It was not immediately clear what type of guidance the section may have provided to the department before the search was executed at Omar's home.It was also not immediately clear why the government moved to execute the warrant so close to the election, since some of the documents in question date back to Omar's childhood and were completed by her late father.The warrant to search Omar's home was only approved by a magistrate judge in Washington after an extended back-and-forth discussion with Justice Department attorneys about how to address concerns stemming from the United States v. Rayburn House Office Building case, sources with knowledge told CBS News. That crucial 2007 D.C. Circuit Court case held that in a criminal investigation of a sitting member of Congress, the executive branch can't review information that is seized in a search without allowing that member to first screen it for legislative privilege under the Constitution's Speech and Debate clause.Initially, the warrant did not take the Rayburn case into account because the investigators searched the congresswoman's home and not her congressional office, but the magistrate judge ordered them to include protocols that would allow Omar and her counsel to review the materials and assert legislative privilege, one of the sources added. CBS News has not yet been able to determine who Omar's lawyer is in this case.Homeland Security Investigations, or HSI, the department's criminal investigative arm, is leading the investigation, with the Department of Justice assisting.This is at least the second active criminal investigation involving Omar and her family.Two sources familiar with the matter previously told CBS News that the U.S. Attorney's Office in Washington, D.C., is also conducting a criminal investigation into the valuation of several of her husband's businesses — which D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro confirmed during a Fox News interview this week.The businesses run by her husband Tim Mynett came under scrutiny after financial disclosures she was required to file as a member of Congress showed the value of the businesses had jumped to being worth between $6 million and $30 million.Omar later blamed the valuation calculations on an accounting error and filed an amended form that listed the couple's joint assets as being valued between $18,004 and $95,000.

title: Hayden Panettiere 911 call reveals boyfriend's brother frantically tried to save her life on day she died
description: Zach Hickerson, the brother of Hayden Panettiere's on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, called 911 and attempted CPR on the actress before she was declared dead.
content: Zach Hickerson, the brother of Hayden Panettiere's on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, attempted CPR on the actress before she was declared dead, a newly obtained 911 call reveals. Panettiere, known for her roles as a child actor in "Remember the Titans" and later the TV series "Heroes" and "Nashville," was found unconscious at her Greenville, South Carolina, residence on the afternoon of Aug. 16 by Zach and Brian Hickerson, according to a police report and the 911 call obtained by CBS News. She was pronounced dead at the scene, despite "advanced cardiac life support measures," the Greenville County Coroner's Office said at the time. She was 36. An autopsy found that Panettiere's death was accidental and ruled that the cause was the "toxic effects of" the drugs fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine.Zach Hickerson, who said on the 911 call that he had come over to the couple's home after church, told the 911 operator that Panettiere did not appear to be breathing. The operator asked if they had a defibrillator, but Zach Hickerson said he didn't know if there was one in the apartment building. The operator then told him to begin CPR and gave him instructions on how to perform chest compressions and mouth-to-mouth until emergency medical services could arrive.Zach Hickerson also told TMZ a few days later that Brian Hickerson gave Panettiere Narcan, a medication that can reverse opioid overdoses, after they found her unconscious.Panettiere had spoken openly about her struggles with substance abuse, telling People magazine in 2022 that she became addicted to opioids and alcohol in her teens. In her 2026 memoir, "This Is Me: A Reckoning," she wrote about her experience with addiction, physical abuse, postpartum depression and recovery. Panettiere told CBS News' Gayle King in May that she hoped sharing her story would help others. "I really wanted to share with the world that they don't have to be afraid. That they can live their truth. They can be imperfect," she said in the interview. Asked how she was doing, she replied, "Still working on myself all the time. I had a great therapist and I'm — I'm better, healthier than I've been in a long time."

title: Plane carrying rescue puppy lands safely in Elk Grove after engine stalls
description: ShepHeroes German Shepherd Rescue clarified that the 10-week-old puppy was not pregnant and did not have a medical emergency.
content: A private plane carrying a 10-week-old German shepherd puppy landed safely in Elk Grove Wednesday after its engine stalled, according to the animal rescue receiving the dog.ShepHeroes German Shepherd Rescue told CBS News Sacramento that the puppy was being transported by a Pilots N Paws volunteer pilot when the engine stalled.Cosumnes Fire initially told CBS News Sacramento that the plane landed at Franklin Field because a dog aboard had a medical emergency and was expected to give birth. Fire officials also said an EMS captain transported the people and animals from the airport for emergency care. ShepHeroes clarified Thursday that there was no medical emergency involving the dog. The animal was a 10-week-old puppy, was not pregnant and was not taken for emergency veterinary care.The plane landed without incident at Franklin Field on Bruceville Road.No injuries were reported.

title: Gymnastics coach who recorded girls in Mississippi gym's bathroom sentenced to 90 years in prison
description: The judge gave the maximum sentence possible to Sean Gardner, 39, who pleaded guilty to placing a hidden camera in a bathroom at a gymnastics studio in Purvis, Mississippi.
content: A once prominent youth gymnastics coach was sentenced to 90 years in prison Wednesday for secretly recording his young female students undressing and using the bathroom at a Mississippi gym, in a case that rocked the sport.U.S. District Judge Kristi Johnson gave the maximum sentence possible to Sean Gardner, ordering that he serve 30 years in prison for each of the three federal child pornography production charges to which he pleaded guilty. The sentence likely amounts to life in prison for Gardner, 39.Gardner's arrest last summer by the FBI, first reported by The Associated Press, renewed questions about whether U.S. gymnastics authorities had done enough to protect athletes from sexual abuse at the hands of an influential coach.Gardner pleaded guilty to placing a hidden camera in a bathroom at a gymnastics studio in Purvis, Mississippi, between December 2017 and April 2018 to record his students. Investigators say he created videos showing close-up images of at least 10 minors naked or undressing, which they recovered from his computers years later while investigating claims that he sexually abused gymnasts in Iowa. Investigators seized approximately 50 videos and 400 photos from Gardner's residence as evidence, according to an FBI affidavit. Gardner is allegedly seen turning off the camera in one of the videos.Several of his former students at Chow's Gymnastics and Dance Institute in West Des Moines, Iowa, have alleged to police and in civil lawsuits that he used his position to prey on them. The institute was founded by prominent coach Liang "Chow" Qiao, who is known for producing Olympic champions. Gardner coached several youth prospects and served as director of an annual winter meet that drew hundreds of gymnasts to Iowa.Gardner has not been charged in connection with any of the Iowa allegations, and police have said they would wait to determine how to proceed after the federal case concludes.One of Gardner's former students told CBS News in May 2026 that Gardner was charismatic and that she was so young, she didn't realize her coach's behavior was abnormal, especially at the end of practice."Each of us would line up to get a hug, and he would kiss us on our forehead, and pat us each on the butt," Liberty Raines, who was 11 years old when she joined Jump'In Gymnastics in Purvis, said. She added that ritual ended nearly every practice. "It was so normalized," Raines said. "I don't think any of us thought anything of it."The mother of another young Mississippi gymnast alerted USA Gymnastics via email about her concerns regarding Gardner's behavior. Separately, Gardner's boss in Mississippi said in an email that she told USA Gymnastics about Gardner's "grooming behavior" in January 2018.Gardner would later move to Chow's gym in Iowa in 2018, where he began coaching Finley Weldon, a skilled 11-year-old gymnast with Olympic aspirations. Weldon told CBS News in an interview last year that Gardner acted "weird" from the start, making inappropriate jokes and asking teen girls about their sex lives."I knew something was not really right about him," Weldon said. Weldon says Gardner would touch her inappropriately while she was stretching and while he was spotting her during her gymnastics training.The civil lawsuits against Gardner have alleged the sport's oversight bodies, USA Gymnastics and the U.S. Center for SafeSport, were told about inappropriate behavior by Gardner in 2017 but failed to take action to remove him from the sport for years. SafeSport temporarily suspended Gardner in 2022 after a Chow's gymnast alleged sexual abuse, and Chow's fired him then.SafeSport has said it learned during its investigation that Chow and other coaches had been aware of allegations of sexual misconduct against Gardner but failed to report them to the center as required by its policy.

title: Metra Milwaukee District West service halted after pedestrian hit by train in Bensenville
description: According to Metra, train movement is halted near Wood Dale due to police investigation.
content: Inbound and outbound Milwaukee District West service has been temporarily halted after a person was hit by a train late Wednesday afternoon. A spokesperson for Metra said an outbound train 2233 hit a pedestrian, described only as a female, around 5:45 p.m. in Bensenville near River Grove.The pedestrian was taken to Lutheran Hospital in unknown condition.The crash remains under investigation and no additional information was immediately available.Metra says riders should expect extensive delays and encourages them to visit MetraTracker.com for updates.

title: 6-year-old New Jersey boy celebrated as hero for helping grandmother after she was hit by car
description: A 6-year-old boy in Atlantic County was honored for helping his grandmother after she was hit by a car in Egg Harbor Township.
content: A 6-year-old boy in Atlantic County, New Jersey, is being hailed a hero for helping his grandmother after she was hit by a car."He's my best bud," Becky McCluskey said. "From the time I first saw him, we just connected. I'm the grandmother that likes to play.""We usually do a lot of stuff together, and we get to sleep over a lot," Finn Mackenzie said.On July 30, McCluskey and Finn were outside enjoying a bike ride together in Grandma's Egg Harbor Township neighborhood."He pulled up in the driveway, and I parked my bike on the side of the street, and I said, 'Do you want to keep riding, or do we want to change and go in the pool,'" McCluskey recalled.Before they could decide what to do next, a driver slammed into McCluskey, knocking her to the ground."He was right there. He came running down to me holding my hand," McCluskey said as she looked at her grandson.McCluskey didn't break any bones, but while she was on the ground in pain, Finn ran to tell his grandfather. He also went to the next-door neighbor's house and asked her to call 911. Then, he returned to his grandmother's side until help arrived."I knew 911 could help," Finn said.Last week, Finn was honored for his selfless service, courage and compassion by the mayor, township committee and the police chief."Just very calm under pressure, I mean he did something that probably most 6-year-olds wouldn't have the awareness and level of responsibility to do," Egg Harbor Township Police Chief Fred Spano said."He's awesome, I'm just so proud of him," Kate Mackenzie, Finn's mom, said.Last spring, Mackenzie said she started teaching her son how to call 911 and what to do during an emergency. She didn't expect him to put those lessons to use so quickly, but now Finn said when he grows up, he wants to be a police officer or a firefighter."Seeing them help her, seeing it in a different light, he really latched on to that. That meant a lot to him," Mackenzie said.According to police, the driver was cited for careless driving.As for McCluskey, she's still dealing with some pain but said time with Finn is the best medicine.

title: 20th anniversary tour of "Jersey Boys" coming to Denver Center
description: 20th anniversary tour of "Jersey Boys" coming to Denver Center in December, tickets on sale now.
content: As "Jersey Boys" tours the country once again, the musical is celebrating a major milestone in Denver: its 20th anniversary.Coby Oram, who plays Frankie Valli, is excited to return to the production, which tells the story of Valli and the Four Seasons and their rise to fame."The 20th anniversary is a huge moment for Jersey Boys," Oram said.This is Oram's eighth contract with the production, and he said returning to the show comes with a sense of responsibility to the performers who helped make it a hit."Now I feel like I'm representing every cast of Jersey Boys that's come before me with John Lloyd Young and the originals, and just honoring the original intent of the show, and that's a lot," Oram said.After performing in the musical across multiple engagements, Oram said one of its central messages continues to resonate with him."I would say the message to take away from Jersey Boys again. Frankie says it in the show, 'Family is everything,'" Oram said. "But to tag on to that, I think a message would be: realize what you have, and don't let it get away from you."Oram said the story also serves as a cautionary tale about the sacrifices that can come with pursuing success."Jersey Boys can kind of be a cautionary tale about what can happen when you sacrifice everything to pursue your goals, your hopes, and dreams," Oram said. "And sometimes those things might be worth holding on to."The musical features some of the Four Seasons' best-known songs, including "Walk Like a Man." During an interview with CBS Colorado, Oram even offered to teach reporter Dillon Thomas some of the choreography behind the iconic performance.Fortunately for audiences, Oram and the touring cast will be the ones taking the stage in Denver.LINK: For Tickets & Information for "Jersey Boys" at the DCPA"Jersey Boys" runs Dec. 1-6 at the Buell Theatre in Denver. Tickets are on sale now. "Come see Jersey Boys in Denver. You're the closest to (my) home. So, family, I'll see you there," Oram said.CBS Colorado is a proud partner of the Denver Center for the Performing Arts.

title: Minneapolis Amplified brings community together through dance, music
description: As Minneapolis residents and businesses continue to feel the effects of Operation Metro Surge, a new city initiative is creating opportunities for people to reconnect through music and dance.
content: As Minneapolis residents and businesses continue to feel the effects of Operation Metro Surge, a new city initiative is creating opportunities for people to reconnect through music and dance.Minneapolis Amplified kicked off its first event this past weekend, turning the parking lot outside Uncle Franky's into a dance floor.The city is partnering with My Dance Agenda to bring music to unexpected places, bringing people together while supporting local businesses."It makes me happy that they want us to come together as a community and dance and have fun," said eventgoer Alyssa Schmidt.Leo Himself, founder of My Dance Agenda, said the events are especially important after the federal immigration enforcement operation left many people afraid to go out."When the Operation Metro Surge happened, a lot of people were scared to go out," he said.He said the events offer a chance for people to take a break from the stress and connect with their neighbors."It was a moment for us to kind of forget about all the pain that's happening here and coming out together, connecting and dancing with our community," Himself said.The initiative also aims to support local businesses by bringing people into their spaces.Brian Harbour, manager of East Hennepin Auto Service, said hosting an event is not necessarily about making money."We don't necessarily earn any money off this; in fact, actually, we're shutting down our gas pumps and everything for the event, but just to let people know that we're here," Harbour said.For attendees, the events provide a space to come together and feel connected to their community."It's nice that we are holding a space for people to come together," one eventgoer said.

title: Drag performer sells bricks from Miami Beach's removed rainbow crosswalk to fund Pride groups
description: Eric Swanson, who performs as Miss Bouvee, won 50 bricks at auction and has raised more than half of his $15,000 goal for Pride organizations in Key West and Naples.
content: A South Florida drag performer is selling bricks from Miami Beach's removed rainbow crosswalk to raise money for Pride organizations across the state.Eric Swanson, who performs as Miss Bouvee, won 50 of the bricks at auction and is now selling them at auction to benefit Pride groups in Key West and Naples. Donations start at $250 per brick, and Swanson has raised more than half of his $15,000 goal."A lot of people just want a piece of our history. I think that it's something tactile. It's not just living it, you can hold it, and it's something that really means something to people," Swanson said.The state ordered the removal of all street art, including rainbow crosswalks, last year. The order prompted protests across South Florida.The city of Miami Beach reused some of the bricks from the crosswalk at 12th Street and Ocean Drive to create a rainbow-colored pedestrian area near the original. The rest were auctioned.Swanson said he picked the two organizations because smaller Pride celebrations often lack corporate sponsors. He said they are now under threat from Senate Bill 1143, which bars local governments from using tax dollars to fund or promote diversity, equity, and inclusion activities, such as Pride festivals."In Key West, this is actually financing the live performance stage. This is keeping locals employed during Pride. It's giving them a living wage so they can perform. It's financing the production," Swanson said.He said the crosswalk may be gone, but its message lives on."You can't erase us," Swanson said. "We are important; we are voters in this state. We are taxpayers in this state. We have families in this state just like anybody else. And we deserve to be seen, and visibility is our protest, so we're happy to keep going."People can learn more and order a brick via a link on Swanson's Instagram account.

title: Philadelphia police officer killing reignites pain for family of man killed in 2019
description: Christopher Williams's family said they were never told the case was flawed and found out about that possibility from a YouTube video.
content: The city of Philadelphia continues to mourn one of its protectors. Officer Shane Seiber was shot and killed over the weekend in the line of duty. New details have emerged over the past few days about the suspected shooter Eric Lewis' background.Lewis was acquitted on a murder charge three years ago. District Attorney Larry Krasner says it was because of a flawed and even corrupt investigation by the Philadelphia Police Department.Christopher Williams' mother, Darlene Brown, said their family never got justice for his murder in 2019. Brown did not want to go on camera but said she always felt like she didn't have the full story as to why Lewis was found not guilty of her son's murder. When she saw Lewis named as the suspect in the killing of a police officer over the weekend, she said she started screaming and crying.Brown said her son was shot in August 2019 after honking at a Nissan double-parked on Fallon Street in West Philadelphia. Brown said the woman in Williams' car told her they were going to a fast food restaurant at the time. After Williams honked, a man got out of his car and shot Williams four times, she said. Williams died, and the woman in his car was grazed by a bullet.Brown said after a 14-month investigation, police arrested and charged Lewis with Williams' murder. Brown said she was confident Lewis would be convicted, but the judge ruled not guilty in 2023.The family said they've been shocked and confused ever since.Then, this week in a YouTube video, Krasner said Lewis was acquitted in 2023 because of a flawed investigation by police, including an officer who allegedly provided false information from a made-up source.The Williams family said they were never told the case was flawed and only found out about that possibility recently from that YouTube video. Brown and her relatives say the fallen officer tragedy has reignited their trauma and desperation for justice.The police department has not responded to the allegations by the district attorney about police officer misconduct in the Lewis murder trial from 2023. A statement said they will address the prior investigation at a later time and right now their focus is on honoring the life of fallen officer Shane Seiber.CBS News Philadelphia asked the DA's office why they didn't charge the officers who allegedly lied about a murder investigation. We're waiting to hear back.

title: Long Beach Naples residents concerned of seawall amid coastal flooding
description: When high tides and king tides hit Naples, water spills over the seawalls in some spots nearly two feet deep, flooding sidewalks and threatening homes.
content: Naples in Long Beach is protected by a man-made seawall, and repairs are underway on the nearly 100-year-old infrastructure as part of a six-phase plan. Recent storms and king tides have raised concerns in the community as to the integrity of the seawall.The city of Long Beach evaluated the Naples Seawall in 2009 and found it to be in significant disrepair.So far, only two phases of the repair plan are complete, and there's an issue with funding the remaining four phases of the project. The city originally used oil money for the first two phases, but a 2022 state law limiting oil drilling has reduced available revenue.Residents and officials hold differing views on the immediate priority of coastal protection versus recreational infrastructure.When high tides and king tides hit Naples, water spills over the seawalls in some spots nearly two feet deep, flooding sidewalks and threatening homes. The city said that, in September, it installed and monitored seawall plugs in preparation for the impacts of Hurricane Marie."Some neighbors don't have an issue, and other neighbors' houses are going underwater, and it's pretty ridiculous to watch that in real time," resident Ben Fisher said.Fisher is president of the Naples Improvement Association and shared a video from Saturday during Tropical Storm Rachel showing water shooting through the seawall."Because everybody that has those flooding issues, they have to replace things after every flood, so that's consistent damage that happens over and over," Fisher said.Long Beach City Councilmember Kristina Duggan explained that Sorrento Trail, a public access trail along the waterway, is targeted for repairs next."The Coastal Commission wants to see that finished before we move to the next phase, but that doesn't mean that we're not working on the third phase," Duggan said. "We have to come up with alternative ways to fund the next phase. Although our design and part of the cost, the money has been set aside. We have to finish Sorrento Trail."But for residents like Fisher, the concern is what could happen when the next big storm hits."That's not a project that's risking anyone's lives or anything, with the lifestyle that's going to be taken away from them. All that project is, is a walking trail. It's not about flooding," Fisher said.

title: 84 truckloads of food donated to Philabundance during 17th annual Toyota Tundra Food Drive in Philadelphia
description: Volunteers packed food boxes for Philadelphia-area seniors ahead of the annual Toyota Tundra Food Drive.
author_name: Nikki  DeMentri, Nate  Sylves, Alan  Wheeler
content: A convoy of 84 Toyota Tundra pickup trucks made its way to Citizens Bank Park Thursday to deliver food in support of Philabundance. The Tri-State Toyota Dealers Association hosts the event, now in its 17th year. Philabundance is the largest hunger relief organization in the region and serves communities across nine counties in the Philadelphia area.Earlier this week, an assembly line of volunteers spent a morning in South Philadelphia packing dozens of senior food boxes at Philabundance."We actually distribute a couple thousand boxes to seniors across our region," Dorothy Wong, chief partnerships and strategy officer at Philabundance, said.Each box will help meet what leaders at Philabundance say is a growing need in the community."Right before the holidays, we really see that our pantries are seeing and serving more and more neighbors," Wong said.Philabundance partners with some 300 community organizations in the Philadelphia area, including Loaves and Fishes Food Pantry in Delaware County."Every month, we have probably about 60 families that have never used our pantry before, at least since before the pandemic," the Rev. Christopher Heisey-Terrell with the pantry said. The Prospect Park pantry serves more than 400 households a month, he said."I don't know how we would do this without partners like Philabundance that go out and find the resources that support pantries like ours so that we can actually spend the time in the community," Heisey-Terrell said.Events like the annual Toyota Tundra Food Drive help Philabundance and hundreds of other pantry partners fulfill their missions every year. "There's no gift that's too small right now," Wong said. "And we really appreciate that we can come together to really make the greatest impact possible."

title: Boston Public Schools employee arrested for alleged rape at Massachusetts State Police barracks
description: A Boston Public Schools employee has been charged in connection with an alleged rape at the Massachusetts State Police barracks on Martha's Vineyard.
content: Last month, the WBZ I-Team uncovered a police investigation involving an alleged sexual assault at the Massachusetts State Police barracks in Oak Bluffs on Martha's Vineyard. That investigation has now led to the arrest of a city of Boston assistant security director on rape charges. Edward J. Brown, 27, pleaded not guilty to one count of rape in Dukes County Court. The alleged rape happened on August 15, at the state police barracks in Oak Bluffs. Prosecutors say a trooper working on the island allowed Brown, his college friend, to stay the night with him at the barracks. Later that evening, a woman reported she was raped by Brown in the barracks. Police arrested Brown on Friday at Boston Latin Academy where he works as an assistant security director. In court on Tuesday, Assistant District Attorney Courtney Scalice told the judge the victim said a man at The Ritz bought her a drink and was following her around at the bar. The next thing she knew, she woke up face down naked in bed with the man forcing himself on her. Police say a passing motorist found the victim naked in the street outside the barracks and brought her to the hospital. Brown's defense attorney, Anthony Ellison, told the judge he is presumed innocent and in the police affidavit the victim said she did not want to pursue charges."This arrest followed a thorough investigation conducted independently by the Oak Bluffs Police Department, in conjunction with the Cape and Islands District Attorney's Office," Oak Bluffs Police Jonathan Searle said in a statement. "Our investigators followed the facts and evidence throughout the investigation." Brown has worked for Boston Public Schools for the past two years at a salary of more than $117,000 a year. Boston Public Schools tells the I-Team that Brown passed all background checks, and his position did not involve direct contact with students."The safety and well-being of our students is our highest priority, and immediately following this arrest, Boston Public Schools placed the individual on administrative leave," a Boston Public Schools spokesperson said in a statement. "According to law enforcement, the current charges do not involve BPS students. We will continue to cooperate with law enforcement as the investigation unfolds. Further inquiries should be directed to the appropriate law enforcement agencies."Sources tell the I-Team there is more to come and that this investigation is not over. The district attorney told the judge two former girlfriends obtained restraining orders against Brown earlier this year. Bail was set at $10,000. Brown is due back in court in December.

title: Michigan hockey players over 70 creating strong bonds through league
description: Hockey season is in full swing, from the pros to college and youth hockey. There's even a group that gathers weekly in Plymouth, Michigan, proving that it's not just a young man's game.
content: Hockey season is in full swing, from the pros to college and youth hockey. There's even a group that gathers weekly in Plymouth, Michigan, proving that it's not just a young man's game."Don't tell my wife this, but my life revolves around it," joked John Gatt, a participant and co-administrator of the over-70 hockey league.The league meets on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Fridays at the Plymouth Cultural Center and attracts people from all over and the players boast plenty of experience."We have over 100 guys in our league," said league director Rob Baase. "They're from all over Metro Detroit. We're getting them from the east side to the Brighton Pinckney area."The over-70 hockey league has 10 teams and is looking to grow to 12."The exercise, I mean it's the healthiest exercise in the entire world," said Gatt. "No. 2, the camaraderie. These are guys that we have one very important thing in common, that we love hockey.""It's competitive; they get their juices back and get a little feisty out there, but it's fun to watched," said Baase.The league also has a few women participating. Picking up a hobby in retirement is common, but for them, it's a lifestyle, and they wouldn't have it any other way."It's like living a dream," said Doug Romanski, another league co-administrator. "I'm going to be 77 soon, and to be able to play the sport you love and know that when you come out here, you're going to be protected.""I have to play," added Romanski. "If I don't play, the arthritis takes over, the body slows down, the mind slows down, so this is a young man's game with an old man's body."The organizers have talked about adding an over-80 hockey league in the near future.

title: Orange County man arrested for using Snapchat to allegedly lure 13-year-old girl before sexual encounter
description: Irvine police said the 25-year-old man used Snapchat to talk to minors, allegedly asking for sexual acts in exchange for vapes or money.
content: Irvine police are searching for more potential victims of a man who used social media to lure a 13-year-old girl before a sexual encounter last month. In a news release, police said that 25-year-old Baldwin Park resident Juan Carlos Amaya contacted the teenage girl via Snapchat and began talking to her while pretending to be 17 years old. "The two met at an Irvine park in July, where the victim had a sexual encounter with the man," the release said. Amaya was booked at Orange County Jail on October 1, and on Wednesday, October 14, he was charged with lewd act upon a child under 14, using a minor for sex acts, possession and control of child pornography and contacting a child with intent to commit specified crime, according to the Irvine PD release. "During the investigation, Detectives uncovered evidence that Amaya has been communicating with other minors on Snapchat, asking them to engage in sexual acts for the exchange of money or vapes," the release said. Police said that Amaya has used the usernames "amayaaajr" or "champagnealex_8" on Snapchat. As they continue investigating the incident, detectives ask anyone who may have had a similar interaction with Amaya or who has more information to contact Detective Robinson at MRobinson@cityofirvine.org.

title: Stoneham businesses struggling amid downtown construction project: "significant drop in customers"
description: Some establishments are seeing up to a third of their usual business, and they will have to survive until work ends in June.
content: As Stoneham, Massachusetts, works to reshape part of the downtown area with a redesign, businesses are suffering. Some establishments are seeing up to a third of their usual business, and they will have to survive until work ends in June."We have probably closed between eight and nine days," said Christine Carpentieri, owner of Christine's Sweet Shoppe. "I support the town, I support the project, I support bettering Stoneham. It's just, will we get there?"By "get there," she means to survive financially, saying the thought of it keeps her up at night. Some days, they don't open until 5 p.m. to avoid construction."The liquor store has seen a significant drop in customers and it's scary," said Carpentieri.Employees at McDonough's Liquors say their business is a third of what it usually is, and that by 1:30 p.m. on the day WBZ came by, they only made $200. Some days, Anthony's Italian Specialties says they see business cut in half. It can be hard for customers to park. The nearby public lot is partially filled with construction vehicles, while other spots have been removed as part of the project's design."A lot of time I park down at town hall and just walk, so whatever is here the customers can have," said Carpentieri, adding that another store owner takes it a step further to leave spaces open. "She lives far away and takes the train in now, which is obviously an inconvenience for her."In a statement, the town said it is working with the construction crews to limit business impact where they can. Carpentieri said some businesses have asked for financial reprieve from the town."They have asked, and so far, you know, they haven't heard," said Carpentieri.In the meantime, other Stoneham establishments are stepping up to help. "Pizza Mia, Ari Hado, he's been amazing. He gave away some gift cards over the weekend for people that came in to visit us," said Carpentieri, adding that a real estate agent also gave $5 to the first 50 customers that came in on a weekend day.The project is expected to carry on through June, with the town saying work will scale back in the winter months."Rome wasn't built in a day. It takes time to figure things out and get everything together," said Carpentieri. "I know that the customers love us, and the town loves us, the surrounding businesses want all of us to succeed."She just doesn't want to see her shop fall like the empire.

title: 2 more arrests made in Georgia block party mass shooting that killed 2, injured dozens, GBI says
description: Two more people are facing charges in connection with the mass shooting at a South Georgia homecoming block party that left two people dead and 35 injured, and police say more arrests are expected.
content: Two more people have been arrested in connection with a mass shooting at a South Georgia homecoming block party that left two people dead and 35 injured.On Wednesday, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation announced that its agents and members of the Dooly County Sheriff's Office arrested 36-year-old Kelcey Smith and 40-year-old Johntavirous Robinson.Both Smith and Robinson were residents of Cordele, Georgia, and are facing two counts of participation in criminal street gang activity, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, and tampering with evidence.The arrests come less than a week after investigators took 17-year-old Khadarius "KD" Ray of Dooly County into custody, charging him with one count of possession of a firearm/handgun under the age of 18 and one count of participating in criminal street gang activity.Authorities say the investigation is ongoing and more arrests are expected.Deadly shooting shocks South Georgia cityThe shooting happened early Sunday morning in the city of Vienna, about 50 miles south of Macon, at a party on Pine Street that spanned four blocks, officials say. Authorities estimated that more than 1,000 people had gathered to take part in the celebration when gunfire broke out.Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy said more than 50 shots were fired. The two people killed were identified as Ja'Quavion Jackson, 21, of Cordele, and Macaleb Jackson, 23, of Hawkinsville. The 35 people injured ranged in age from 14 to 51. Peavy said the festivities began Friday night, and that it had "gone well" with "respect from the community" that evening as deputies patrolled the event.But the party Saturday night was a "different story," he said."We're still working through the investigation to see what went wrong. But at large parties with people from different places, not just your locals, sometimes problems come," he said.Authorities have shared few details about what led up to the shooting and have not given a possible motive for the gunfire. Mayor Eddie Daniels declared a state of emergency on Monday, imposing a temporary curfew for 72 hours. That curfew was extended last week as well as on Wednesday and will remain in effect until rescinded by the mayor.

title: Flock Safety surveillance technology sparks privacy protests at San Francisco tech conference
description: The protest coincided with a speaking appearance by Garrett Langley, Flock Safety's co-founder and CEO, at the technology conference at the Moscone Center.
content: Protesters gathered outside TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Tuesday to challenge the growing use of Flock Safety's license plate-reading technology, raising concerns about privacy, surveillance and the potential misuse of data collected by law enforcement.The demonstration coincided with a speaking appearance by Garrett Langley, Flock Safety's co-founder and CEO, at the technology conference at the Moscone Center.Reem Suleiman, an organizer with the digital rights group Fight for the Future, held a sign reading "Flock=ICE," arguing that the technology could expose sensitive information about people's movements."They leave the back-door open with the feds by not taking our privacy seriously," Suleiman said.Flock Safety's automated license plate readers capture vehicle license plates and location data, which law enforcement agencies can use to investigate crimes.
